checks exact member keys, catalog distribution, owning group and selected bytes.
Routed members use the retained rank-local global-ID map; shared members use their
own complete ID range. A shared bank may contain more members than the routed
bank, and a foreign unit cannot satisfy validation through aggregate entry counts.

Kimi Linear and LFM2 dense and routed partition construction retain the source model
when lowering includes a parameter transform. The architecture reconstructs its
source formats from exact admitted requirements, verifies target/source semantic
addresses and local state geometry, and passes its typed source layout into the
shared runtime factory. This includes the routed expert realization and shared
bank geometry; the backend only materializes the retained source and target.

Kimi attention and LFM2 attention/convolution companions inherit their primary projection's semantic head or
output-column sharding through neutral parameter metadata. Their own physical
shapes determine the scale/bias intervals; checkpoint-name suffixes do not make
companions replicated when their primary matrix is sharded.
LFM2 routed expert ownership expands encoded logical partition units through the
shared checked range contract before deriving component and bank coordinates.

Qwen hybrid's recurrent attention now declares scalar value-head output channels.
The same ordinary, provider and parallel block drivers observe fused projected
Q/K/V, their causal SiLU convolution, control projections and the consumed
normalized/gated channels. Original/effective channel hooks precede the actual
row projection. Its read-only input evidence comes through the shared projection
observer, after any selected dynamic input transformation. With instrumentation disabled, these seams neither create path
strings nor evaluate or retain extra tensors. Channel interventions occur after
the recurrence has updated state; sublayer-input interventions occur before it.

The neutral gated-delta equation distinguishes key and value head counts and
widths and per-head versus per-key-channel decay. Qwen uses additive-epsilon L2
normalization of Q/K, contiguous head repetition, per-head decay and a SiLU output
gate. Kimi uses its declared RMS/scaling convention and per-key-channel decay.
L2 is explicitly `x / sqrt(sum(x*x) + epsilon)`. Evaluation readout directions
honor this denominator without substituting RMS or a clamped norm. Recurrent
writes with scalar component declarations no longer appear again as opaque
readout terms, while routed combined FFN contributions remain explicit.

Composite partitions retain the same immutable partition-bank selection as
routed text: bank identities, per-invocation routes, local component coordinates,
exact member tasks and selected residency. Shared member ownership follows its
catalog distribution and actual execution-unit owner rather than the routed
expert range. The common architecture construction driver binds resident or
independently cached providers to this retained selection. Native composition
supplies the shared cache and transfer mechanisms, excludes independently
materialized targets from ordinary unit loading, and retains bank handles for
bounded parameter work, atomic overlays and telemetry. Composite pipeline waves
and media boundaries continue to use their original architecture-owned schedule.
Addressable member keys identify bank invocations independently of their owning
execution unit. Runtime validates every retained parameter task against that
owner, while architecture catalogs validate the invocation and member identities.
This permits routed and shared invocations to belong to the same decoder unit.
Gemma 4's ordinary and routed TP/provider drivers translate global layer
identities through the retained partition state offset before borrowing caches.
The layer identity still selects equations, per-layer inputs and shared-KV roles;
only mutable-state access uses the local ordinal.
Its expert modules also consume the retained localized grouped specification;
router identities and cardinality remain global. This keeps EP-local storage
geometry separate from routing policy and preserves the same block construction
for resident and independently cached providers.
Muse's centered normalization derives its effective gain from the current
authoritative parameter on each invocation. It does not retain a separate gain
tensor across parameter replacement or unloading, so overlays and residency
transitions cannot reuse a stale derived parameter.

Muse component execution uses a single architecture-owned block driver for
ordinary, provider-backed, tensor-parallel, and observed calls. Its hooks expose
the actual gated attention channels and FFN units before their selected output
projections, and both sides of the separate post-projection RMS normalizations.
The postnorm acts on the complete reduced write; sparse expert contributions
must be summed before that normalization. The same architecture-owned final
readout handles tied and untied heads and retains output multiplication after
the actual vocabulary projection. Backends continue to supply ordinary tensor,
projection, sparse-unit, and collective mechanisms.

Descriptor schema 12/component schema 11 adds an explicit normalized-head
`output_scale`, token-only embedding normalization before media assembly, and
`scaled_softcap` for `cap * tanh(affine_score * scale / cap)`. The captured
assembled embedding remains the residual base. Additive score contributions
refer to the unscaled affine score, with the actual projection input and its
rounding retained as evidence. These are neutral equation declarations, not
claims of loaded support or new backend family branches.

For a complete route-weighted residual write, neutral component placement may
establish a post-normalization input from its already established output owner.
This follows the normalization's preserved axes and invocation. Admission still
requires the complete normalization axis, exact input/output geometry, and
replicated gain/bias parameters owned by that invocation; a foreign pipeline
stage's gain cannot authorize the input capture.

Muse's expert checkpoint alternatives discriminate packed and split storage by
the gate/up identities. Their shared down projection remains required by either
selected layout, but its presence cannot select both alternatives. Header-only
admission validates the complete selected layout before native materialization.

Muse load-time media quantization derives eligible matrices from its checked
architecture-owned checkpoint geometry. It selects aligned patch, position,
attention, FFN and adapter matrices, retaining dense storage where an input
axis cannot hold the requested packed blocks. Exact checkpoint format admission
remains separate. The retained selected formats drive cold capabilities, memory
plans, materialization and cache identity; backends do not repeat this selection.

`ParameterTransformConstraint::LinearIfAligned` carries the architecture's
optional packing policy into neutral realization selection. Valid requests whose
blocks do not fit retain the exact native source format; invalid requests still
fail. Muse applies this declaration to media projections after canonical recipe
finalization, so source aliases and derived outputs retain the same policy. Text
projections retain their required transform semantics.

Muse GGUF requirements derive logical shapes and canonical identities from the
GGUF text plan and, when present, its separately admitted projector. GGUF expert
recipes consume the retained prepared source. A text-only GGUF never needs a
SafeTensors vision configuration merely to enumerate executable parameters.

Mixed Muse ingress defers vocabulary-parallel text lookup until the primary text
execution group. The preceding replicated vision group performs no text lookup
collectives. A shared neutral helper declares one exact reduction shape per text
segment, excluding media positions; inactive pipeline stages consume that same
ordered schedule. Inkling uses the helper for its existing segmented ingress.
These are architecture equations and schedules, not backend family branches.

Muse canonicalization is shared by source recipes and parameter requirements,
including the generated scale/bias identities for load-time quantization. The
released source prefix is provenance, not an executable companion name. Its
optional vision root also shares one cold/loaded transport declaration; absent
projectors contribute no static vision role to text-only partition ownership.

Muse selected partition transforms retain a separately constructed, typed source
architecture and physical source layout, as the existing composite transform
contract requires. The construction driver validates execution addresses, state,
vocabulary ownership and static roles against the selected target; it also binds
the source's local expert realization. Native mechanisms consume this retained
source and the admitted tasks. They never reconstruct source geometry from
packed target slots. GGUF's learned per-head Q/K norm gains appear as replicated
architecture parameters; the Hugging Face convention remains weightless there.

Qwen3-VL's text traversal uses the ordinary Qwen decoder's component driver,
including resident and independently supplied experts, rotary embeddings and
local mutable state. Its architecture wrapper adds the assembled embedding and
final readout seams and instruments prepared DeepStack additions at the point
where they enter the residual. Disabled hooks use the same ordinary addition.
DeepStack declarations require media input and apply during prefill; they appear
as separate residual terms, with their own original and effective captures.
Traversal continues to own unit boundaries, so unit output includes the vision
addition. Family equations and semantic branching remain in architectures.

Qwen3-VL's selected transforms now use the same typed source-partition handoff:
source encodings and local layout remain distinct from packed target slots,
while execution units, state, static ownership and DeepStack roles must agree.
Optional vision packing uses the neutral alignment constraint and retains dense
matrices when the requested blocks do not fit. The shared Qwen vision format
lookup resolves relative module names and canonical checkpoint names to the
same encoding and rejects conflicting aliases before construction. Cold
requirements and module construction consume that same lookup.
The Qwen vision position table remains an ordinary dense lookup and is excluded
from transformable projection geometry, in both Qwen3-VL and conditional Qwen.
Its rank-two storage alone does not authorize affine weight packing.

Component schema 12 / architecture descriptor 13 adds two neutral relationships
for shared-state and residual equations. A read can identify the attention
component group that actually publishes its projected state; its consumer does
not acquire a fictitious local projection or a capture of historical positions.
Readout equations can reference ordered transformations of the whole residual,
including learned scalar parameters, after each layer's writes. These transform
references affect the embedding and all prior writes. They grant no parameter
query or edit authority. Older serialized descriptions default to local reads
and no additional block transformations.

Gemma4 component integration uses its existing portable dense/routed block and
shared attention cache equations. Ordinary, controlled, provider, and partition
entry points share text preparation and the same instrumented projection and
readout drivers. Native backends continue to supply generic tensor, cache,
projection, collection, and parameter mechanisms. Family topology and the
publisher/consumer and residual-scaling semantics remain architecture-owned;
Gemma4 neutral and native acceptance is recorded in the component-analysis guide.

Declared whole-residual component transforms establish complete hidden-axis
capture placement at their architecture-owned block invocation. The portable
partition builder validates the referenced layer and containing block before
propagating the existing typed transform equation; learned parameter placement
remains independently checked. Gemma4 attention-bias checkpoint admission
follows its normalized projection schedule, including shared-KV consumers and
full-attention key reuse. Neither rule is reconstructed in a native adapter.

Gemma shared attention across pipeline cuts uses architecture-owned typed
current-position key/value roles. The receiving partition declares one additional
KV history for each remotely published attention policy, attached to its first
local consumer; subsequent local consumers borrow that publication. Cold state
selection and native construction use the same replica geometry, so residency,
snapshots, prompt-cache compatibility, and copies include those histories.
Pipeline transfer scales with the current sequence length rather than the full
cached prefix. Fixed wire roles preceding their publisher are inactive and never
consumed; the publisher replaces them before any shared read. Key-reusing
projections still transport and retain both normalized value and rotary-key
payloads, since these tensors differ after their respective transformations.

Gemma attention executes through the owning cache whenever that cache retains
history outside the returned K/V tensors. Shared consumers borrow the exact
publisher cache, or the first local receiver cache across a pipeline cut. The
architecture chooses this semantic owner; the backend implements ordinary
cache-aware attention without reconstructing the layer schedule. Published
tensors may contain only the current submission, so direct tensor attention
must never stand in for reading a paged history. The neutral numerical matrix
exercises that contract against a resident full-history oracle.

A partition's additional state must enter the neutral requirements before
mechanism capability synthesis and selection. `ReplicatedTextRequirements::with_state_layout`
validates the unchanged layer address space and traversal access, then lets the
ordinary selector admit, place, and account for every declared component. It
does not relax the selected-state comparison at binding time. Gemma uses this
for its receiver histories; the subsequent TP geometry projection preserves
the selected component roles and physical storage policy.

Composite architectures also own packing and restoring their intermediate
pipeline activations. Default continuation hooks preserve the supplied tensor;
Gemma flattens its padded media batch into the admitted sequence dimension and
restores the encoder batch from the retained request geometry. Native backends
perform ordinary tensor reshaping and transfer, without interpreting media parts.

Gemma's cold and constructed media transport use one architecture-owned phase
ownership declaration. Encoder input parameters belong to the first encoder
stage and output projectors to the last. The current atomic vision static group
is also retained on the last stage when learned standardization is enabled;
the atomic audio static group is retained on the first and last stages because
it contains both subsampling and output projection. Selected materialization
accounts for these replicas. Continuation stages prepare parameter-free media
masks/rotary state and shape placeholders; they do not execute unowned embeddings
or input encoders. Only the first decoder stage performs segmented vocabulary
lookups, and the declared inactive collective waves reflect that ownership.

Component schema 13 / architecture descriptor 14 adds optional routed-bank
`write_output` and `output` boundaries. They describe the complete bank write
after route weighting and distributed reduction, and its transformed output
before combination with other branches. Architecture declarations join these
to the existing tensor-transform equations. Portable partition derivation checks
input/output widths and exact invocation ownership; transform validation still
checks normalization axes and learned parameter placement. This exposes Gemma's
routed post-normalization without inferring a bank write from a shared FFN sum.

Gemma's key-reusing publishers declare two physical cache payloads in the base
state layout as well as pipeline receiver replicas. Reuse applies to the raw
projection only: value RMS normalization and key normalization/rotary transforms
produce distinct tensors. This is ordinary neutral KV storage; a key-only state
would lose the value history and undercount storage.

Composite pipeline boundary delivery retains the semantic destination alongside
its typed payload. A result from one independent media root can arrive while a
different root is executing; only the declared destination installs that result.
An intervening group cannot consume or reinterpret the pending boundary. This
policy lives in the portable executor and applies equally to all composite
architectures and native transports.

Gemma media format selection uses the projection's logical input width in both
cold requirements and module construction. Family-wide quantization requests
retain unaligned media matrices in floating storage under the existing family
alignment policy. Logical-shape recovery expands encoded schema dimensions
only; a floating schema tensor is already expressed in logical coordinates.
Media-to-text projectors consume the same exact media format as their checkpoint
schema, including under global text quantization.

Gemma partitioned load-time transforms retain a separately constructed typed
source architecture and its exact source layout, as other composite families do.
The architecture driver checks execution-unit addresses, selected state, media
ownership, vocabulary ranges, and per-layer input ownership before passing both
source and target to native materialization. Backends consume that prepared
handoff rather than reconstructing family configuration from target tensors.

Transform source modules use the selected target's partition ownership. Runtime's
`derive_transform_source_layout` maps those exact cuts into the source encoding
with checked axis scaling, preserving logical ranges and independent expert
placements. Architecture constructors use the resulting geometry for both
source modules and prepared-source validation, including composite families and
prediction extensions. A floating source is not independently rebalanced before
conversion: for example, a 96-column matrix converted in 32-column groups over
two ranks consumes source cuts of 64/32. Native materialization consumes those
retained cuts without interpreting family equations.

Qwen3-VL, conditional Qwen hybrid, and Muse partition static roles describe
execution consumers. The final
stage retains the `output` role even when readout shares the embedding matrix.
The architecture's parameter group declares its embedding/output consumers and
selects the required replicas. Geometry validation must not replace that
consumer role with a physical parameter name when weights are tied.


Prepared prediction modules now receive the complete execution's retained weight
residency policy from the total construction driver. Physical owners remain
separate from logical depths: shared normalization/fusion modules receive one
policy and unit identity regardless of their number of consumers. The typed
materializer's invocation contract carries an equation result together with
output and changed-state dependencies even when the equation fails. Unit and
shared owners overlap until those dependencies settle. DSpark's context and
proposal loops use the same equations through this scoped module mechanism.
Backends retain native completion and parameter leases; architectures enumerate
the actual state and output roots. MLX now keeps exact bindings and unloaded
module placeholders until invocation. Target construction registers the additional
physical owners and their exact stores before initializing one common residency
manager. Queries acquire one owner through the same loan; reversible edits live
in a per-module replacement set reapplied after population. Completion precedes
unloading and bounded device eviction, including equation failure. Native
behavioral matrices verify this combined path; cold sizing is checked against
constructed modules and actual rank geometry.

Qwen3-VL GGUF companion admission uses its composite projector name translation
for both token-pending and token-bound plans. The two temporal patch slices stay
distinct exact source keys until the architecture's stack recipe constructs the
single patch-projection parameter. A physical source slice never becomes an
independent executable topology target.


The neutral residency controller can validate each physical unit against its
retained exact catalog while sharing one plan and reservation ledger. The MLX
manager retains an immutable per-unit source registry for this contract; batch
reservation, initialization, alias-owner acquisition and eviction still use the
same ledger. Identical source keys in distinct transformed stores remain distinct
values. A residency report keeps each alternate source view's diagnostics
separate because views may share physical counters. Target and prediction
construction register their units together before initialization, preserving one
weight reservation ledger.


Prediction preparation also declares whether a physical module is shared while
other units execute. This residency overlap is distinct from tensor/pipeline
parameter placement. Shared fusion, normalization and DSpark statics must be
counted alongside the largest active unit; their shared checkpoint ownership
must not force all prediction units into one resident block. The generic native
module-transfer helper retains both changed-state and output roots with the
source transfer through existing submission recovery, including equation errors.
The prediction materializer now uses this helper for both execution and scoped
parameter queries. Runtime's `AuxiliaryWeightRequirements` computes the shared
plus largest sequential owner requirement for paged execution and the complete
physical total for resident execution. Native load admission and cold support
reports use those values alongside the ordinary target window.


Cold prediction residency is represented separately from parallel parameter
ownership. Runtime's `AuxiliaryModuleResidency` is retained on parameter
requirements and selected materialization tasks. Architecture declarations assign
physical units, including Nemotron's full physical pattern and DSpark's shared
input/readout modules. Prepared module construction checks that a declared group
matches the actual module's task set and shared/sequential role. Runtime sizes
shared owners plus the largest sequential owner for a bounded phase; resident
execution counts all owners. Ordinary bounded admission now includes auxiliary
tasks as well as the target tasks. Rank-local sizing uses the same tensor-only
prediction placement as construction, counting a complete prediction schedule
on every target pipeline and expert coordinate. The caller supplies the complete
architecture parameter description. Enabling prediction can also replicate
target statics, such as token embeddings on later pipeline stages; their selected
storage ownership contributes separately to pinned bytes. A neutral numerical
fixture compares cold totals with constructed module tensor geometry across
tensor, pipeline, expert and combined eight-rank placement. Shared-phase sizing
and constructed-module roles are also checked in runtime and native fixtures;
the complete family/format paging matrices are recorded in the component-analysis
guide.

Gemma 4 primary GGUF admission maps text tensors into the complete family's
`model.language_model` parameter tree. The standalone text/assistant mapper
remains available for those construction contracts. This keeps token embedding,
per-layer input and decoder-unit ownership identical across SafeTensors and GGUF;
projector tensors retain their separately declared media owners.
The GGUF layer multiplier and routing scales map to scalar parameter identities,
including the router's per-expert scale; they do not inherit a matrix weight's
suffix or projection owner.

The component transport audit distinguishes invocation membership from parameter
storage. Ordinary hooks use `ParameterGroupOwner::is_owned_by`; auxiliary copies
are accounted through `is_stored_by` and do not add ordinary callback peers.
Prepared target hooks use the complete tensor/expert stage, and replicated
prediction hooks use the session group. With the retained pipeline-major rank
order these are connected Ring memberships, already covered by bounded member
status agreement. An arbitrary disconnected low-level membership still receives
the existing typed rejection: a world-participation wave cannot run independently
of inactive pipeline peers. No such relay is required by the selected component
execution paths described here.

Detached prompt and sampler preparation seals and observes its native submission
scope before returning. An existing operation error remains the reported cause
even if the scope also reports failed or blocked work. That error does not grant
completion: unresolved roots stay in the same recovery owner until terminal
evidence permits retirement. A generic status error is used only when the
operation itself supplied no error.

GGUF admission retains each Qwen primary tensor's exact packed format before
constructing embedding, expert and linear parameter topology. Standalone and
Qwen3-VL contexts share that resolver, using the context's declared parameter
root. Qwen3-VL and Qwen3.5 companion admission also records vision-block and
DeepStack-merger formats before constructing their composite configuration.
Facade-owned media-token binding preserves those facts. Backends consume the
resulting typed bindings and recipes; they do not infer missing family formats
from packed byte widths during native construction.

Shared architecture requirement discovery converts packed GGUF schema byte widths
back to logical coordinates using exact block geometry, rejecting partial blocks
and overflow before capability selection. Encoded storage widths never stand in
for the logical dimensions of a linear operation.

Prepared composite matrix-format handoff includes executable embeddings as well
as linear projections, preserving quantized lookup and tied-readout storage.
Normalization vectors and fixed dense position tables keep their separate roles.

Muse GGUF projector recipes flatten the admitted spatial patch kernel into the
family-declared linear patch input order. Cold requirements retain that logical
geometry, and backend binding consumes the prepared recipe without family-specific
reshaping. Both raw and canonical source names refer to the same checked layout.

Native communication uses the stream selected by the actual MLX communicator,
independently of model computation. The safe native wrapper exposes that retained
stream; backend groups share its ownership with logical groups and completion
recovery. Ring therefore communicates on its CPU transport while model operations
can run on Metal. Compatible compute streams retain caller ordering and device
affinity; singleton collectives keep the compute stream without initializing a
transport device. Initial manifest exchange uses the same stream selection and
retains its exact group through completion, before rank-local contract checks.
Native tensor dependencies order the two streams. Packing and
model arithmetic keep their compute stream, and existing communication budgets
continue to cover their owned buffers; no physical allocator-workspace guarantee
is inferred from this stream selection.

Manifest and session consensus preserve transport causes in the neutral generic
protocol error. The MLX adapter retains that exact policy/transport error through
its backend failure conversion, so application diagnostics can reach the original
native source without exposing native error parameters in facade operations.

Rank-local runtime construction also retains architecture and mechanism errors
through the typed factory handoff and final session wrapper. Partition executor
and traversal-policy constructors retain their neutral error types as sources.
Boxed errors retain the leaf itself, so a policy or I/O error without a further
source remains discoverable through the public neutral failure chain.
Vocabulary and tied-embedding readout gathers also retain the original native
exception through the neutral neural error conversion.
The replicated and composite session adapters retain typed failures during
parameter loans, state reset, snapshots, prompt-cache operations and ordinary
prediction-lane execution instead of replacing them with display strings.
If a prediction operation and its state recovery both fail, the adapter retains
both errors and exposes the recovery cause. An earlier state-preserving rejection
cannot authorize retry after that recovery failure. This does not itself prove
native completion or release pending resources.
Setup failures do
not imply native completion or permission to release pending resources.

DeepSeek V4's published FP8 default applies to linear projections. Its text and
Markov embedding tables, and target/prediction hyper-head functions, retain their
dense schema and operator semantics. Explicit separately admitted embedding
formats remain distinct from that default. Vocabulary construction derives token
ownership from the architecture-declared weight rows; FP8 companion rows index
128-entry blocks and retain their own format-derived physical placement.

DeepSeek V4's family format resolver retains published dense embedding, router
and DSpark Markov-embedding defaults, including under block-FP8 metadata. Explicit
selected per-parameter formats take precedence for admitted transformations. Cold
lowering and executable construction consume these same family-owned decisions.
The same resolver distinguishes published expert encodings from the global
projection default: mixed FP8/MXFP4 experts keep full per-row scale geometry.
Schemas, routed construction and partition placement share this decision for
target and prediction layers.

Prepared partition discovery retains an immutable index of its exact selected
tasks, aliases, companion outputs and checked parameter members. Its size is
bounded by those existing declarations, and it is rebuilt when parameters are
rebound. Queries still compile ownership and reserve the same per-call metadata
and transport costs; indexing avoids repeated full-declaration scans during
all-layer experiments. It confers no loaded authority and retains no tensors.

DeepSeek encoded expert assembly retains scale and affine-bias companions under
the same source selection, expert ordering and gate/up concatenation as weights.
Target and prediction preparation consume the complete canonical recipe outputs;
the backend does not reconstruct family source names or infer missing scales.
Independent expert residency carries these same companions in each bounded unit.
Its optional intermediate selection respects source packing and scale blocks;
pre-encoded weights and their companions remain preserved, while ordinary sources
retain eligibility for the selected load-time conversion. Target and prediction
format decisions come from the architecture's existing routed-block policy.

Native catalog preparation indexes borrowed selected output names once per query
under an additional finite host-metadata reservation. It continues to validate
each loaded slot against the retained neutral placement before publishing facts.

Muse GGUF routed recipes enumerate decoder layers independently of the composite
vision-plus-text execution ordinals. Projector recipes retain their own semantic
source roles; adding vision layers never creates text-expert source requirements.

Generic native execution-layout and unit preparation retain typed architecture
failures through the backend error source, including resident-policy conversion.
The outer public failure remains backend-neutral; preparation does not flatten
these causes into diagnostic strings.

Muse vision pipeline edges use architecture-declared flattened patch geometry
within the tower and flattened projected-media geometry at decoder ingress.
Cold continuation bounds expand the selected decoder extent by the spatial merge
area; request admission supplies the exact grid and placeholder counts. The
portable composite driver transports those declared roles, without treating
image patches as text positions or adding backend family branches.

Partitioned target readout discovery registers the actual projection-input
observation with output-invocation ownership, alongside residual and normalized
values. It remains read-only and replicated across output TP ranks; parameter
storage replicas on other stages do not grant observation ownership. The same
contract already governs prediction-scope readout inputs.

A Muse rank that has already executed a vision partition resumes the incoming
decoder activation in its retained request context. The ordinary primary-only
boundary carries no additional learned context and must not trigger a second
text/media assembly.

Muse static vision parameters use exact unit-consumer ownership. Patch/position
inputs and the grouped static norms are available on each vision partition that
constructs request context; the merge adapter and final projection are owned by
the final vision unit. Cold source selection, parameter topology, materialization
and residency sizing consume the same family decision, including replicas.

Portable partition execution preserves typed architecture, policy, state and
communication failures through the neutral neural error source. This includes
active and inactive pipeline waves, dependency completion and boundary transport;
retaining a diagnostic source does not grant completion or retry authority.

Neutral partition communication retains owned submission and completion errors
through `BackendFailure` sources while preserving operation, phase, route and
poison-domain semantics. Diagnostic-only poison notifications remain available
for borrowed failures that callers already retain. Neither form establishes
resource release; native recovery and completion still own that decision.

Composite architectures report whether retained context still contains pending
decoder-ingress collectives. Muse keeps token lookups pending through vision
execution; Gemma and Inkling resolve them at context creation. Inactive pipeline
ranks consume this semantic state when mirroring the declared primary wave.
Native backends execute the same operation order without selecting family branches.

Final source adaptation and partition error wrappers preserve owned errors as
`Error::source`, including cold model/preflight failures and non-architecture
`LayerwiseRuntimeError` variants. This changes diagnostic retention only; the
architecture/runtime layers still own preparation and residency policy, and the
native backend still establishes completion before releasing native resources.

## Bounded inference ownership

Core now declares explicit vocabulary `OutputDemand`, exact `InferenceGeometry`,
and execution-workspace components alongside existing persistent-state admission.
State geometry alone reports `PersistentStateOnly`; strict/application-budget
admission requires complete workspace bounds. Architecture code owns selection
of hidden positions before its readout equation through the required layered
selection hook and the shared `select_readout_positions`/`execute_readout` helpers.
Shared resident, bounded-unit, routed and parallel traversal carries that demand.
Pipeline transport retains complete hidden positions, while output owners select
readout and size publication values consistently. Architecture-specific retained
prediction equations remain independent of score selection, including V4 capture
concatenation. Ordinary text sessions request final-position scores; sequence
APIs and observers preserve their required rows. A distributed readout vote
propagates a sequence observer's requirement to every rank before mutation.
Runtime owns `plan_prefill`, the shared completion-gated `PrefillDriver`, and
atomic request reservations over existing and incremental managed storage.
Core submission leases can retain those neutral reservations; native completion
and recovery remain responsible for their safe lifetime. No backend family
branch, native tensor dependency in portable crates, or MLX allocator-limit
assumption is introduced. Production bounded scheduling and native workspace
bounds/reservation wiring remain in progress;
see [the implementation and validation record](bounded-inference.md).

`eredu-nn::workspace` supplies metadata tensors and neural operators that execute
the existing architecture equations without native values, devices or streams.
It retains exact projection formats, physical companions, row-block origins,
rotary recipes, attention arithmetic and recurrent-state geometry. A concrete
`WorkspaceMechanisms` supplies output allocation/alias and scratch bounds for
each invocation. The trace preserves allocation identities across views and
counts every unique output and all scratch through the completed span; unknown
operators keep the quote incomplete. Native facts must cover all strides,
numerical values, widening and staging consistent with a descriptor.

Tensor-buffer and disjoint managed-host workspace are now separate required
facts. `WorkspaceMechanisms::operation_bound` prices tensor outputs and tensor
scratch; `host_workspace_bound` prices operation-owned staging, conversion,
sorting and transfer buffers outside that backing storage. A unified-memory
mapping is counted only with its tensor root. An absent host fact is unknown,
including for views; a proved zero requires an explicit derivation. Existing
residency and untraced request preparation remain separately owned estimates.
Runtime/driver bookkeeping, allocator caches, JIT programs and unrelated process
memory are outside the managed working-memory contract, so it remains distinct
from a process-memory guarantee.

Trace reports expose `tensor_buffers` for native allocator comparisons and
`host_workspace_bytes` independently. Their main `total_bytes` and
`transient_bytes` require both domains. Host buffers remain charged across
inspection lanes and metadata completion until the explicit completed-span
boundary. Missing either domain prevents strict admission and pool reservation;
large safety reserves or smaller chunks do not supply missing facts. The current
Metal implementation supplies independent host facts for audited dense, basic,
normalization, reduction, indexing, padding, cache-copy, convolution, gated-delta,
rotary and attention operations. Shared native payloads have a derived zero additional
host charge. Rotary construction includes its Rust frequency vectors; large-row
input-score attention includes its bounded host boolean mask. Unknown formats
or equations remain unpriced in both domains. Native peak measurements validate
the tensor-buffer subreport; they do not supply missing host facts or authorize
a complete request.

Packed projection facts now follow the selected Metal mechanisms. Affine and
MXFP4 products include frontend casts, matrix compaction, the geometry-selected
quantized split-K accumulator and its possible two-pass reduction. GGML products
use direct packed kernels with bounded input/weight compaction and reshape
storage. FP8 products include activation quantization, activation scales,
weight-scale decoding and output restoration. E8M0 decoding additionally owns a
1,024-byte host lookup table, separately from its native copy. Affine embedding
promotes differently typed floating companions after selecting their rows;
the native dequantizer reads scale and bias using one dtype. Its quote includes
the selected-row conversions. Packed embedding
facts combine shared token-validation/sentinel policy with selected-row gathers
and native dequantization; GGML lookup kernels read packed rows directly.
Descriptor validation checks each physical companion instead of inferring dense
storage from the logical matrix. Observation factories, transported tensors and
other separately retained resources still require their enclosing quotes.

The metadata backend now implements the distributed neural contract with an
explicit rank and group size. Vocabulary ownership retains global validation
coordinates and local physical parameter shapes, including packed companions.
Local contribution masking, sum reduction, local readout and uneven gathering
remain distinct operations. Gather descriptors carry the exact peer widths and
axis; a local projection bound cannot silently supply a missing collective bound.
Ownership is checked before projection observers run.

Grouped neural metadata now retains learned router parameters, scoring and
precision policy, correction and coefficient scales, supplied indices, and
validated routing interventions. Original and effective decisions from an
intervened selector are distinct outputs of the same operation. Typed grouped
banks preserve packed versus independent parameters, quantization companions,
output ownership, activation and reduction policy. Tensor-parallel partials
retain the replicated down bias as a separate output, including a one-rank
parallel invocation. The ordinary explicit-group projection records its full
multiply before diagonal selection; it cannot be quoted as a smaller multiply.

Sparse grouped-unit hooks split the metadata equation before the down projection.
The logical boundary contains all selected routes and their index geometry;
native facts must cover any physical route tiling, sorting and staging. It does
not assert a numerical routing decision or native callback count. Replacements
must preserve shape, dtype and trace identity. Observation or intervention failure
retains preceding charges and prevents the finish operation. Hyper-connection
metadata likewise retains the learned projection geometry, Sinkhorn policy,
collapsed values, pre/post coefficients and stream-mixing matrix. Hyper-head
coefficient observation precedes its weighted sum. These extensions use no native
runtime. Missing grouped or hyper mechanism bounds remain unknown; geometric
metadata alone does not authorize a native request or provide tensor values to
observers that require host materialization.

Runtime supplies the metadata backend's submission adapter, preserving the
dependency direction from runtime to neutral neural contracts. Inspection lanes
share one allocation ledger and storage identity. Synchronous metadata completion
proves only that host recording finished: it performs no native work and does
not clear accumulated charges. Cross-trace dependencies and completion ordering
are rejected. The ordinary parallel layered traversal can therefore be inspected
without a second execution loop; only an explicit completed-span boundary resets
the ledger. Native transport, state materialization and whole-request budget
composition still require their own facts and retained selection.

The neural metadata backend also implements the ordinary blockwise attention
contract. Begin, accumulate and finish descriptors preserve absolute query/key
ranges, mask origin, prefix and sliding policy, sinks, and FP32 online state.
Typed options preserve Fused/InputScores and the optional positive score cap;
per-block bias is a real source operand. InputScores retains global normalization
while a second ordered value pass produces one output per block; fused/normalization
steps retain three outputs. Defaults preserve the original single-pass interface.
Ordered blocks may contain gaps for prefix-plus-window histories. Reconstruction
byte telemetry is the logical K/V input payload, not a complete scratch bound.
Each stage needs its own selected tensor and host facts; completion of metadata
recording does not release earlier stage charges or establish native completion.

Runtime owns `WorkspaceConcatStateFactory`, a metadata realization of an
explicitly selected exact-concatenation cache, including key-only sharing,
sliding tail views and architecture-declared fixed slots. Attention geometry
comes from `StateLayout`; no family names or equations enter the factory.
Retained tail views keep their full backing allocations in the report, even
when logical state is much smaller. Append publishes state and its frontier only
after all metadata operations succeed; failure preserves previous state while
earlier successful operation charges remain. Fixed components advance through
the existing runtime contract, and named-segment reset preserves their policy.
This factory must not substitute for capacity-backed, compressed, paged or
quantized native state. Those selected mechanisms still need their own metadata
realizations, allocation facts and retained-resource composition.

`WorkspaceResidentStateFactory` now composes that ordinary state with a resident
compressed-cache realization. Architecture-owned `ReplicatedTextStateProfiles`
maps the six access profiles to its typed layer state; the factory dispatches
only on the neutral `StateLayout`. The native compressed mechanism exposes its
default capacity increment as a cold fact. Runtime receives that increment,
retains padded stores and logical views, and traces initialization, padding
concatenation and exact rectangular updates. Neural metadata supplies separate
slice-update, contiguous-materialization and independent-copy descriptors,
without assuming donation or collapsing a view's backing allocation.
Restore and isolated-snapshot copies stay explicit, including any independently
copied backing and logical arrays. These mechanisms do not represent native
paging, quantized cache storage or transport. Selected tensor and host bounds
are required before strict admission can use their operation descriptors.

Native deep copy must preserve logical tensor order. `safemlx` previously copied
shape-sized bytes directly from a data pointer even for strided arrays, which
could copy padding instead of the second batch of a compressed-cache view.
Its synchronous deep-copy path now checks row-contiguous strides and compacts
other layouts on MLX's reused default CPU stream before copying data, avoiding
registration of a new native stream on every copy. The evaluated compact
source remains alive through destination construction; contiguous inputs retain
the direct path. This stays inside the existing native wrapper boundary and
adds no unsafe-code exception.

The selected Metal storage facts price a full slice-update destination plus
possible update reshapes and dtype conversion, one possible contiguous result,
and an independent deep-copy result plus possible CPU compaction. CPU and GPU
tensor allocations use the same shared Metal allocator and are counted once.
Possible view aliases preserve their original backing storage. These are
tensor-buffer bounds with a separately derived zero disjoint host-payload fact.
Enclosing preparation and retained-resource reservations are still required for
a complete admission quote.

Convolution facts follow the selected native dispatch: depthwise and implicit
kernels have no unfolded-matrix charge; explicit convolution includes unfolding,
grouped weight transposition or the actual direct-Steel split-K workspace.
Direct Steel calls retain their one-row split-K behavior, independently of the
ordinary matmul frontend's GEMV shortcut. Winograd includes its padded input,
fill scalar, transformed input/weight/output buffers and final dtype restoration.
All payload buffers use the shared Metal allocator, providing the source-derived
zero disjoint host-payload bound; kernel/shape metadata remains driver bookkeeping.

Reusable MLX convolution predicates are shared by execution and cold facts.
The transposed operator crops an expanded output when native negative padding
would incorrectly crop the undilated input. Its view retains the complete
uncropped result in the quote. Large Winograd convolutions in a Metal build
compute matching F16/BF16 operands in F32 and restore the requested output dtype,
avoiding amplified transform rounding at the cost of explicitly priced F32
temporaries. These choices are native operator mechanisms, independent of family.

Runtime `with_equation_workspace` adds the traced transient graph to the existing
state/admission report. It assigns the aggregate once to activations, documenting
that attention, projection and cache allocations in that graph are included.
Retained roots must fit the persistent-state estimate; separate preparation,
sampling, materialization and retained-resource bounds remain mandatory and
cannot be filled by trace coverage. The portable conformance mechanism validates
this composition and adaptive admission. It is not a source of MLX allocation
facts: full native quote construction and production reservation wiring are
still outstanding.

Runtime `quote_inference_workspace` composes the complete prompt/output geometry
from completed cold equation spans. It uses the ordinary `PrefillDriver` for
chunk boundaries and preprojection demand, then inspects every reserved decode
position. The callback advances a fresh metadata realization of the exact
selected architecture and cached-state projection for each candidate chunk size;
it must not prepare native input or select another execution mechanism. The
report takes the maximum simultaneous tensor-plus-host transient bound across
spans. Independent tensor/host diagnostic peaks are not added together. A missing
bound in any span remains unknown, even if a later span has a larger known peak.
The same report composes with the existing state estimate and required bounds
outside the trace before the shared pool can reserve it. Core's common context
check and runtime's exact request/geometry check run before inspecting candidate
equations, including potentially large decode allowances. This adds the shared
whole-request quote driver; production native request and resource-lifetime
integration remain required.

`PreparedInferenceBlueprint` retains the exact `PreparedModelSources` pairing
through the common executable assembler. Clones share the complete immutable
selection, artifact inspection and source graph, including readers, caches,
leases and provenance. Its private shared owner retires the outer allocation
before the payload and exposes no weak or raw handle. A unique consuming source
moves its selection and inspection; the current total-construction dispatcher
still copies those owned values when a blueprint alias remains. Those dispatch
copies, module configuration and contract validation remain separate metadata
producers; allocation-free source retention does not qualify them. The
architecture-owned replicated quote reuses `construct_prepared_execution` and typed state-profile dispatch,
then runs the ordinary equations for every scheduled prompt/decode span. Selected
host-layerwise quotation uses the same traversal with unit construction and
explicit parameter binding inside those spans, as described below.
It uses selected parameter formats and checks opening and closing state frontiers;
it does not reopen artifacts, read payloads or select a different realization.
Weight staging and other work outside these equations remain separate required
bounds, including for a selected host-layerwise or disk-streamed model.

MLX retains this blueprint on the executable that moves into the session and
captures Metal workspace facts from the realized target during construction.
Quotes use those retained facts and a fresh read-only projection of current state.
Runtime refuses state inspection during active, indeterminate or fenced
transactions. Native state/addresses stay in the backend; the architecture sees
only metadata. The current quote route covers replicated text with the selected
resident cache mechanisms. Other execution classes, pooled/paged state, prediction,
media and pre-preparation request admission still require their integrations;
this narrow equation quote is not a complete-budget capability declaration.

Configured text sampling now uses runtime's `ConfiguredTextSampler` for both
native execution and cold inspection. Standard filtering, penalty history,
Mirostat updates and speculative policy delegation have one owner. Its accepted
history uses an explicitly sized boxed U32 buffer, starting at four entries and
doubling when full. Clones preserve capacity; snapshot prices include that full
payload. Quotes include old and replacement history buffers at growth edges.
Native penalty counting uses a sorted history window with no sorting allocation,
plus exact boolean and additive vocabulary buffers. Core validates executable
filter prefixes without allocating; native expansion creates one exact mask.

`WorkspaceSamplingBackend` records the same sampling primitives in the existing
neural workspace ledger. MLX owns their Metal implementation facts: sort and
partition ping-pong buffers, probability scans, gather/scatter, masks, scalar
operands, casts, explicit random-key creation/splitting and categorical sampling.
Random-key splitting always creates new storage; retained views share that new
buffer. Existing random keys require observed allocation capacity, and unknown
capacity or a missing host/native primitive bound keeps the quote unknown.
Completed sampling spans include both old and new keys through completion.

The prepared replicated text quote can combine these sampling costs with its
equation report. The architecture supplies the actual final-position score
geometry from ordinary execution, and runtime traverses every allowed sampling
step without changing the source policy or native state. This includes the
supplied static filter payload and sampling history, but requires separate
bounds for changing constraint controllers, speculative proposals, observations,
input preparation and materialization. The composition adds costs conservatively
and preserves every unknown enclosing component. The native adapter consumes the
retained blueprint and mechanism facts; no backend family branch or payload read
is needed. Production facade admission and a complete request reservation remain
outstanding.

Runtime's `TextPromptWorkspaceReport` separately prices the complete U32 prompt
and its actual owned host capacity. Chunking limits equation workspace but leaves
the original native token buffer alive through its views. The quote uses the
selected initializer and reshape facts without token values or native allocation,
and its composition requires the exact same request geometry. Unknown backing
capacity remains unknown. Tokenizer/application strings and payload-free input
identity descriptors are outside this tensor/host-payload component. MLX obtains
the facts from the executable's retained selection. This component can be composed
with equation and sampling reports, but does not itself admit native requests.

Native disk-read batches now expose capacity bounds for their selected direct
encoded path. Direct vectored reads fill final MLX allocations without host
payload staging. MLX's `Copy` primitive shares the complete source backing even
on a different execution stream; the enclosing transfer retains its ownership
through completion and this allocation is counted once.
Every simultaneously submitted batch must therefore be charged, along with
existing resident bindings and any host-residency transfers. These facts include
Metal page rounding and oversized cache reuse. Converted/ordinary recipes remain
unknown; the older logical recipe-size diagnostic is not an admission bound.
Checkpoint metadata/read planning remains neutral, while native capacity and
stream-copy facts remain backend owned. These component bounds exclude OS caches,
driver memory and other process residency.

The ordinary source-selection gateway accepts an existing `InferenceRequest`
instead of always manufacturing unbudgeted authority. Runtime validates its exact
execution owner, batch/input shape, chunk geometry, cached frontier and output
demand before invoking the source factory. It consumes one-use authority before
that potentially allocating factory. A supplied request cannot switch to the
unquoted whole-input fallback. Unavailable ingress is a typed rejection before
state mutation, and reusing its retention handle cannot restart preparation.
The same request reaches `SessionPrefill`, native completion scopes and retained
mutable state, which continues enforcing the output allowance during decode.

MLX's owned and borrowed input views carry this internal request unchanged.
Replicated and composite native adapters validate the execution identity before
input conversion, then delegate admission and scheduling to runtime. Their cold
identity accessors do not expose a native device or recreate selection. Default
facade preparation still needs to obtain the complete quote and reserve it before
constructing these inputs; the new transport does not turn an unbudgeted caller
into a budgeted one. Sequence consumers retain their separate multi-output
`SessionPrefill` contract rather than losing earlier score chunks at this
ordinary final-position gateway.

Inference traces now seed their opening mutable-state roots explicitly.
`eredu-nn` reports the complete closing backing capacity, including unchanged
state and possible aliases, separately from new graph allocations. Opening
allocations displaced by the update remain transient through completion. Runtime
adds that overlap before selecting a request peak and checks the full closing
capacity against persistent-state admission. Primitive-only traces without an
opening inventory cannot authorize inference. Unknown existing capacity remains
unknown after the trace advances; logical view dimensions never fill that gap.

The existing `safemlx`/`safemlx-sys` native safety boundary now exposes a read-only
query for completed allocator or certified host-transfer backing identity and
capacity. It neither evaluates a graph nor polls completion. Unrecognized custom storage and
unfinished work remain unknown; allocator capacity is queried only for the
native allocator's own buffers. MLX projection deduplicates native identities
within a retained inventory, then gives portable metadata only neutral shared
storage roots and byte capacities. Native addresses stay within the adapter.
This describes existing residency, not future allocation or total process memory.

Resident compressed-cache projection imports its actual capacity buffers,
logical views, frontier and growth increment into the portable storage mechanism.
An independently copied logical view is distinct from its separately copied
capacity buffer; a compact snapshot starts from its actual compact capacity.
The adapter consumes architecture-supplied local geometry and does not replay a
prefix or branch on a model family. Paged caches still require a complete shared
manager/block projection; the resident adapter rejects them explicitly. Other
structured state projections and production quote/preflight composition remain
unfinished.

Native ordinary and hybrid resident state now project their complete layer
inventories directly. One borrowed allocation inventory spans all layers and
fixed roles, so shared keys, values or fixed tensors count the same backing once.
The borrow also prevents allocation-identity reuse during projection. Runtime
validates imported attention geometry, symbolic fixed shapes, dtypes, role
completeness and frontiers against the retained architecture layout. An absent
live fixed slot remains absent; persisted-cache presence requirements are not
used to fabricate live values. Lazy or foreign backing remains unknown.
Exact native fixed-state dtypes are checked before floating values are projected
to conservative F32 metadata; a BF16 array cannot satisfy an exact F32 role.
The native adapter verifies exact concatenation, key-only and causal-window
mechanisms before using their portable equations. Capacity-backed, legacy
truncating, paged and offloaded representations require their own complete
projections; they are not silently assigned concatenation costs. Resident
compressed layers share the same inventory, including distinct restored stores.
Projected state carries no native tensors or inference submission authority.

Native equation bounds currently cover Metal gated-delta scans, common
tensor/activation operations, reductions, normalization, dense products, gathers,
dense embedding lookup, floating softmax and the attention paths described below. Backend-owned
`MetalAllocationFacts` includes page rounding and the allocator's bounded reuse
of oversized cached buffers. `safemlx::memory::host_page_size` reads the OS fact
without initializing MLX or Metal. The scan quote uses the same internal chunk
selection as execution and prices slice/cast/contiguous copies, intermediate state,
concatenation and final conversion. Common-operation facts price initialization,
pointwise arithmetic and activations, gated products, concatenation and causal
masks. Static range slices share their input; integer-axis selection retains a
possible reshape copy. The neutral index descriptor preserves that distinction.
FP16/BF16 widening, native contiguous copies and every equation intermediate are
charged through completion without assuming fusion or donation. Causal masks
use explicit I32 coordinates, preserving exact positions beyond the F32 integer
precision boundary. Sum/mean facts include an optional contiguous input copy and
the bounded accumulator of the selected reduction implementation. Normalization
facts compose those bounds with ordinary, learned-offset, grouped and gated
equations, preserving F32 widening and parameter strides. Empty pointwise
broadcasts retain a scalar-buffer allowance even when their logical size is zero.

The pinned MLX build normalizes native view descriptors before subsequent
vector-copy or unary allocation. Empty fast-Split results use zero-length
numerical storage. Nonempty Split results retain their actual signed-stride
span, including negative axes and holes, and their signed logical offset.
Split preserves its prior positive-stride classification before applying the
new span check. Split and shared Slice mark meaningful negative strides noncontiguous even
when overlapping axes make the span equal the positive-stride extent product.
This ensures conversion uses a general logical copy and cannot preserve a
negative offset into a newly allocated buffer. Nonempty views retain the
original backing; no tensor copy occurs during their descriptor normalization.
The correction is applied through the content-hashed native patch pipeline,
without changing archive provenance or introducing model-family policy.
The generic safe Array boundary can reach all three cases. The inspected current
family projection split uses static ranges and distributed Split uses equal
sections or one boundary; an affected current family execution is not claimed.
Native regressions guard cast layout and capacity before reading values, check
both reversed siblings and overlapping slices, and compare actual cast/square
allocations with their cold envelopes. SliceUpdate also verifies that a reversed
multi-element piece is not mistaken for scalar storage. These are native
numerical-buffer invariants, not a complete host or process-memory bound.
Dense-product facts retain vector and batch geometry, dtype casts, possible
contiguous/reshape copies and one split-K partial array. They take the maximum
of applicable SIMD and NAX dispatches without initializing a device. Frontend
flattening keeps an unbatched weight matrix unreplicated; native batch collapse
is also included. Tensor linear operations price fused addmm bias, while
constructed projections additionally cover the custom BF16 row kernel and
separate bias addition. Tied dense readout consumes the same descriptor and
preserves prior selection of hidden positions. Packed projections use the
separately derived packed facts; collective storage still requires its own facts.
The tensor adapter uses explicit dimensions for batched zero-width addmm inputs;
this avoids an ambiguous inferred reshape while preserving native dtype promotion
and broadcast bias. Its reshape copies are included in the dense-product bound.
Gather descriptors retain the source axis, and metadata argmin indices preserve
unsigned 32-bit storage. Gather facts price bounds comparisons (including possible
I64 widening of unsigned indices), safe-index selection and the validation
reduction retained by the native submission. Dense embedding facts additionally
price token normalization, safe lookup and sentinel masking. Metal reads source
rows directly, so these facts charge selected rows without copying the full table.
Final-axis floating softmax uses one result/contiguous buffer; precise accumulation
does not add a widened tensor. General-axis softmax prices its complete
max/subtract/exp/sum/divide/cast equation and both reduction workspaces.
Attention facts follow the native forward-inference dispatch: supported fused
vector/full kernels, or the product/mask/sink/softmax equation. They include
Q/K/V promotion and layout copies, grouped-head replicas, split products, optional
score caps, rounded input-score query tiles, and two-pass fused scratch. Sliding
attention quotes its 256-row chunks, generated causal masks, concatenation and
head-joining reshape. Its neutral result is `[batch, queries, heads * value_width]`;
ordinary attention retains `[batch, heads, queries, value_width]`. Shared checked
sliding-history geometry rejects missing current keys and overflowing positions
before constructing native work.
The vendored native `MLX_SDPA_BLOCKS` override is now immutable after first
inspection or two-pass execution. `safemlx::fast::sdpa_blocks_override` reads that
same setting without creating a device or running runtime housekeeping. Cold
facts and native execution therefore cannot diverge after environment mutation.
Positive overrides preserve their exact count; counts must be multiples of 32
because the native final reduction otherwise drops partial groups. An unset or
nonpositive setting uses the union of device-default counts. Out-of-range integer settings return errors.
This is native configuration, not model policy. Input-score attention with key
rows above 8,192 now prices its two-pass accumulator: one query and at most 256
keys per step, with retained normalization state and finished query outputs.
Execution and inspection consume the same internal tile policy. The blockwise
accumulator uses the existing submission recovery owner to wait for successful
native callback cleanup before accepting another block. Array readiness alone
is insufficient for that storage bound. Failure still returns without treating
an error as terminality; native recovery and the enclosing request keep their
respective resources and authority. The quote takes the maximum block workspace
plus live state and query outputs, separately comparing the final concatenation
phase. Host scratch and whole-request reservation composition remain required.

Rotary workspace facts use the retained neutral specification to price native
batch outputs and concatenation, explicit input-product arithmetic, supplied
frequency or sine/cosine arrays, and the selected frequency-scaling construction.
They include the lazy first-use frequency graph, so inspection does not assume
that operator construction already evaluated it. The native kernel reuses its
result buffer for layout copies and partial rotations; explicit equations price
their separate casts, products and reshapes. Wavelength-scaled partial rotations
preserve the unrotated tail, and explicit position generation forms integer
coordinates before F32 conversion, rejecting an overflowing endpoint. These
mechanism facts add no family dispatch or scheduling policy to the backend.

Unpriced native primitives keep whole-model quotes incomplete. These
facts cover active tensor-buffer capacity, not allocator-cache residency, Metal
heaps, JIT programs, driver resources or total process memory.

The shared session transaction now accepts absent score outputs for explicitly
prepared state-only spans. Observation and publication skip absent scores;
state checkpointing, distributed phase agreement, completion and commitment
remain shared. `ReplicatedTextSessionMechanisms::complete` accepts optional
scores and must settle all mutable-state dependencies. MLX also settles active
token-validation arrays. Explicit chunk execution requires exact completion
availability and forces it before returning; the forward context remains live
through that boundary. Scheduler, semantic ingress and reservation composition
remain runtime/architecture responsibilities and are still being integrated.


`SessionPrefill` now connects the shared scheduler to that transaction. Runtime
owns reservation binding, cancellation agreement, advancement and failure fencing;
`PreparedPrefillSource` supplies architecture-owned semantic spans. The text source
in `eredu-architectures` retains host/native tokens and selects explicit query/key
mask coordinates, materializing host tokens only under the reservation guard.
Backend mechanisms provide a mandatory reservation guard before native preparation
and settle it after execution. MLX implements this with native submission recovery,
which quarantines the retained charge when completion is unobservable. Request
reservation admission through default facade preparation/decode, media span
preparation, and proved native workspace estimates remain in progress.

Runtime now attaches an exact reserved request to `InferenceStateRetention`
before span preparation. `InferenceRetention` deduplicates aliases of the same
charge and stays with retained state after the driver and completion are dropped.
Shared checkpoint wrappers attach source retention to copied checkpoints and
merge both charge sets before a fallible restore. This covers mechanisms that
replace state wholesale as well as those that mutate it. An older snapshot cannot
refund newer charges; reset releases a charge only when no descendant or native
completion owner retains it. Independent copies still require separate storage
and growth admission: cloning retention is ownership, not a new memory quote.

Portable `DeviceState`, MLX key/value and hybrid owners retain charges through
cloning, native snapshots and restore. Pooling-state construction carries the same
retention through its native copy/fork factories; hybrid segment import and
key/value transaction publication preserve imported and current charges. Ordinary
control slots move retention with state during branch exchange. Explicitly
unbudgeted requests add no retained charge metadata. Default facade admission,
shared snapshot-copy pricing and complete native quote construction remain
unfinished.

An installed reserved request also carries `InferenceStateAdmission`, a logical
decoder frontier independent of backing-charge retention. `LayeredArchitecture`
inspects prepared input dimensions without native allocation; segmented inputs
sum their semantic token spans and prepared composites use their admitted decoder
geometry. Auxiliary proposal invocations require their own quote and cannot use
ordinary decoder admission. This classification supplies semantic input metadata;
runtime owns the comparison and native mechanisms supply only state-position facts.

The shared session agrees exact batch, scheduled span length, prefill/decode phase,
readout demand and native frontier before checkpointing or executing a model.
It rejects shortened as well as enlarged spans because native workspace need not
be monotone in length. Decode is one position and cannot exceed the admitted output
allowance. A one-row sequence readout is equivalent to final-position readout.
Execution must reach the checked frontier before output observation; rollback and
branch restore recover the logical frontier while preserving every backing charge.
Restoring an unadmitted snapshot cannot erase an installed admission.

Reserved direct, prepared-input, sequence and controlled calls reaching that
session retain a native reservation scope through agreement, execution and
publication. They require exact completion. Failure to settle the scope fences
further work while native recovery retains its charge. This enforces the supplied
span contract; it does not construct the still-required complete native quote or
price independently copied state, speculative captures, or preparation outside
the reserved ingress scope.


Runtime `InferenceRequest` carries either an enforced `WorkingMemoryReservation`
or explicit no-budget authority through that same driver. It preserves consumed
start authority and exact request identity in both modes. Native guards retain
this request even when it has no memory charge. No-budget execution makes no
memory-bound claim and is never a fallback for rejected strict admission.

The prefill driver retains only request, progress and native completion state,
allowing composition to borrow its executor for each advance. Architecture-owned
`PreparedCompositeTextPrefill` also adapts pure token spans through a composite
family's existing admission rather than introducing native family dispatch.
Its owned span and admission share exact tensor identity and decoder geometry.
Media encoder ingress remains a separate architecture responsibility.

Before preparing a span, runtime compares its admitted starting position with
the retained decoder frontier reported by the selected native state mechanism.
An explicit stateless partition reports no local frontier; unknown stateful
positions are errors. All participants agree this admission before input
preparation. A stale cached-prefix claim yields `StateFrontierMismatch` and
leaves state untouched. This check uses native position metadata, without moving
family equations or state-geometry selection into the backend.

Ordinary native token-only prefill now enters runtime's shared
`try_prefill_unbudgeted_source`. Runtime owns its default span limit, retained
frontier, distributed source selection, scheduler and final score-axis
adaptation. Native direct/composite adapters supply prepared sources; architecture
code classifies token-only prepared ingress and slices ordered token segments
inside the native retention scope. Media and full-sequence observation ingress
still require migration. This explicit unbudgeted entry does not claim complete
workspace bounds or substitute for rejected strict admission.

Core's cancellable prefill submission returns an optional submission: absence
certifies agreed cancellation and safe settlement, with no score or sampled token.
The ordinary generation machine and detached continuation pass the live caller
token through this contract. Facade commitment recognizes cancellation only
after a successful no-output result; a simultaneous backend error remains an
error. Cancellation is supplied for each advance and is not snapshot state.
MLX's direct and composite adapters reuse runtime's source driver, then settle
the native operation and token-validation completion before returning cancellation.
Successful cancellation preserves the completed prefix and a healthy session;
failed or unobservable work retains the existing native fencing and recovery.

Core now owns one prompt/sampler preparation path for ordinary iterators,
borrowed controlled generation and detached continuations. `TextGenerationInput`
preserves either host token ownership or an existing opaque prompt.
`TextPreparationInput` exposes host position count and allocation capacity, or a
borrowed prepared prompt, to the backend's mandatory cold admission hook. That
hook consumes retained architecture/runtime facts; it does not move equation,
chunk-selection or memory policy into the backend.

The selected session agrees `Admission` before native prompt construction, then
agrees prompt binding and sampler construction. The machine retains its
`TextPreparation` owner through all payloads and completion cleanup. A detached
fork shares retention of the original charge; independently copied state still
requires its own reservation. Native MLX preparation carries a supplied internal
`InferenceRequest` through its existing detached recovery scope, so a failed or
unobservable operation cannot release the owner merely because startup returns.

The facade's ordinary and controlled text paths now hand host tokens to this
shared driver. Native callers without a supplied admission remain explicitly
unbudgeted: complete request quotes and shared-domain pool selection are still
required. Speculative batch preparation, media encoding, dynamic controller and
capture storage, copied state and existing native residency remain separate
integration work. The hook alone is not evidence of an enforced native budget.

Checkpoint-owned host storage is now described by `CheckpointSource::source_storage`.
`SourceStorage` retains physical owners while merging their capacities; source
views forward the complete underlying storage regardless of logical key access.
In-memory tensors include spare vector capacity. SafeTensors source caches retain
only weak payload references, so externally owned leases are charged by their
operation rather than by this source bound. GGUF supplies an explicit fixed
file-reader buffer size, and its source reserves the configured reader-cache
ceiling without opening a payload. Unknown custom sources remain unknown.

Architecture-owned prepared sources aggregate every retained source role using
that contract, including primary, companion, complete, target and prediction
views. MLX's load-time quantization overlay reports both the original source and
its retained packed host outputs through the same neutral interface. These facts
cover source-owned host payloads; native parameters, state, conversion, temporary
leases and transport still require their own bounds before shared-pool admission.
Catalog metadata and operating-system file cache are outside this payload bound.

MLX's `RetainedStorage` adds physical allocator-owned array capacities and
immutable host-transfer capacities to source storage. It keeps the actual owners
alive and merges aliases across inventories. The native residency manager exposes
its own current storage through this cold contract; inspection bypasses recovery
reaping and does not poll, read payloads, materialize or evict. In-flight or failed
transfers leave the bound unknown because their recovery resources can live
outside the manager map. Lazy or unrecognized custom-backed arrays likewise remain unknown.
Synchronous residency transfer completion finalizes each published array's
readiness before resolving its generation; this happens in native execution,
not while collecting accounting facts.

This inventory does not equate the logical offload ledger with a complete native
memory bound. Loaded module replacements, decoder state, addressable parameter
banks and escaped outputs have additional owners. Future streaming allocations
need separate workspace bounds, and shared-domain reservations must retain the
composed inventory. Metadata, allocator caches and process memory are excluded.

Residency aliases remain validated globally by the neutral controller. Native
preflight checks physical owner recipes against their exact per-unit sources;
it does not reinterpret a cross-unit alias as a new checkpoint binding. The
