native alias-reacquisition regression also verifies physical-capacity deduplication.

Retained target-module values now have a read-only traversal separate from mutable
parameter transactions. `LayeredParameterOwner` borrows its exact architecture and
policy; the shared session dispatches that traversal through replicated, routed
and partitioned strategies and rejects unresolved or active transactions before
visiting. Architecture-declared static modules use their ordinary parameter
topology. Native resident policies expose populated modules; bounded policies
expose stored overrides without acquiring or rebuilding unloaded units.

MLX projects these values into `RetainedStorage`, preserving native physical
aliases and original owners across later parameter replacement. This contributes
target modules and policy overrides only. Residency/source buffers, addressable
banks, prediction modules, mutable state and escaped outputs must still be
composed before whole-model admission. No new whole-model completeness claim or
public budget reservation follows from the traversal alone.
Both native resident-policy constructors establish the retained weight transfer's
exact completion before returning populated units. This supplies stable starting
storage without moving completion work into cold admission inspection.
Synchronous manager acquisition likewise finalizes array readiness before
publishing storage when no caller-owned transfer is returned.

The shared session also offers one guarded, immutable inspection of its native
mechanisms and current state. MLX retains the actual target residency manager
during prepared policy construction and composes its physical inventory with
current target parameters, state, and addressable-bank pools. A scoped bank
handle inventories the whole retained pool, including replacement tensors;
logical scope does not reduce physical ownership.

State inventory includes every retained paging manager as well as native layer
arrays. Sealed device blocks, immutable host buffers and buffered shard bytes
join the same physical inventory, so aliases across layers, cache namespaces and
parameter owners count once. Pending cache I/O, host demotion, retiring worker
resources and background failure keep the bound unknown. Inspection never
advances those transitions or opens a shard. Mutable tail accounting alone is
not a complete paged-state inventory.

This combined target inventory is still a component of admission. Observers,
active prediction lanes, escaped outputs and enclosing request resources require
additional composition and shared reservations. The inventory itself retains
payloads; it neither reserves their capacity nor pins the native residency ledger,
and it does not price future execution workspace.

The generic disk worker exposes cold retained-work evidence and both cache
workers retain an active-payload flag through destruction of their local roots.
This prevents completion publication or catalog retirement from creating a gap
in cache inventory. MLX's ordinary target completion also finalizes output/state
array readiness before returning. Certified host-transfer-backed arrays share the native buffer owner's identity.
The wrapper recognizes only MLX's named retaining deleter and verifies its exact
buffer before reporting charged capacity. Allocator and host-transfer identities
occupy separate opaque domains. Array/host aliases count once even across
inventory merges, and retained handles keep the owner alive after its original
host wrapper drops. Arbitrary custom storage still remains unknown. This stays
inside the existing safemlx/native FFI boundary; no native ownership token enters
portable architecture or application contracts.

Prediction executors now expose immutable resource traversal in addition to
mutable parameter control. `eredu-architectures` enumerates physical module
ordinals and the actual retained pooling/model-state prototypes for DeepSeek V3,
DeepSeek V4 (sequential and DSpark), Inkling, Qwen hybrid and Nemotron-H. The
traversal borrows these owners; it does not construct or clone a prediction lane.
MLX measures module values, placeholders, replacement tensors, exact prepared
sources, residency buffers and prototype state through the existing native
inventory. Replicated and composite sessions guard this inspection at the same
resolved session boundary. Merging prediction and target inventories deduplicates
shared backing. Active lanes and observation/output retention remain separate
owners; this contract does not itself grant submission or allocation authority.

Unloaded MLX prediction slots use completed broadcasts of scalar zeros with the
original parameter shape and dtype. The materializer installs these views before
publishing a module and saves them for unloading after each loan. This releases
constructor graphs without allocating a second full parameter set. These native
placeholders retain certified scalar backing and never replace checkpoint values
during execution: each invocation binds the exact leased parameters first.

Text preparation now consumes runtime-owned request-start authority before native
prompt or sampler construction. Reservation clones share a single preparation/
prefill state; independent wrappers of the same reservation cannot each start a
run. Preparation retains the exact startup sampling configuration. Move-only
stage permits retain the request while native construction runs, and publish
readiness only after success. A constructed prompt still requires binding; a
pre-existing prompt can enter through that binding boundary directly. Original
retention handles cannot bypass a claimed preparation to start prefill.

MLX carries the request charge in sampler-state retention and in the shared owner
of sampled token handles. Native completion can release the session's submission
lease and executable borrow while a token continues to retain its request charge.
Sampler copy/reseed and pending-input copy recovery retain those charges through
unresolved native work. Sampling restoration merges charge owners, and copied
prompts retain their chunk policy and exact request/preparation identity. This
changes resource lifetime and startup authority, not architecture equations or
sampling policy. It does not yet compose a complete public native request quote
or cover raw escaped logits and every separately allocated copy.

### Shared physical-storage registration for inference

`eredu-runtime::working_memory::WorkingMemoryPool` now arbitrates retained
physical storage and incremental request reservations under the same accounting
lock. Storage registrations use backend-supplied identity/capacity pairs, dedupe
overlapping inventories, reject inconsistent capacities, and release a physical
charge only after its last registration retires. The fixed baseline is separate
and must not overlap registered storage. Registration failures do not partially
charge the pool or increase its historical peak.

Checkpoint source inventories expose opaque owner identities with their complete
payload capacities; they retain ownership and remain independent of native
allocation and execution. The MLX inventory adapter puts native allocation,
checkpoint-source, and immutable-byte identities in distinct namespaces. Certified
host/Metal aliases retain their shared native identity. A registration owns its
inventory, preserving identity validity through model destruction. Its final
drop stages ordinary host cleanup, keeping both roots and charge alive until
destruction can proceed outside native locks.

These registrations are existing-storage accounting, not future-allocation
permits. Public session/domain composition must retain them alongside the
resources it manages and reserve complete preparation, execution, copying, and
observation workspace separately. This change does not claim that automatic
whole-request native admission is complete.

### Resident pooling and routed/composite equation inspection

Runtime validates local-key and pooling declarations for both native and metadata
realization. It owns the role, ratio, presence, overlap and shape checks. The
resident metadata mechanism tracks the native one-channel local sentinel,
partial source windows, complete pooled history and overlap views. Projection
imports actual frontiers and complete backing capacities into a shared allocation
inventory; it neither replays a prefix nor evaluates lazy arrays. Pooling mask
coordinates use checked integer geometry, with native Metal allocation facts for
its aranges, quotient, scalar and Boolean output.

The architecture-owned retained blueprint now constructs gated, ReLU-squared and
pooling routed equations, and direct/routed composite text equations. They share
the ordinary span scheduler, frontier validation, readout and sampling quotation.
Composite text spans pass the family's prepared-input admission with metadata
tensors. An inspector refuses evaluated media metadata rather than fabricating
it. Native pooling and composite adapters supply actual state projections behind
the same resolved-session inspection fence. Backend code adds no family dispatch.

These routes quote equations; selected bank/weight materialization, transport,
media preparation and retained prediction/capture resources still need enclosing
bounds. A successfully constructed route can report unknown native workspace.
Paged state, partitioned/prediction quote construction and complete public budget
admission remain unfinished.

The metadata backend's additional operator capabilities mean their geometry can
be traced, not that a native mechanism has a certified bound. Indexed/pooled
attention, pooled-position selection and mask gathering retain all participating
inputs and policies; multi-axis rotary retains its complete axis specification.
Independently cached expert execution is explicitly unpriced at every span until
its selected gather, member grouping and scatter strategy is represented. A
resident grouped equation cannot confer completeness on that execution mode.

Composite text construction also uses neutral relative-profile attention and
segmented-attention metadata. Segmented tracing follows the native slice,
transpose, fused-attention and concatenation mechanism. Relative-profile and
multi-axis rotary descriptors retain the complete geometry and policies consumed
by the native positional bounds below. Unpriced input domains remain unknown.
Empty pooled rotary history keeps its
frequency/scalar allowance without dividing by a zero sequence extent.
The native rotary adapter returns the empty input before inferred reshapes;
frequency construction remains covered by its conservative first-use allowance.

Muse attention constructs masks per layer after cache append, using the visible
key suffix for contiguous caches and absolute coordinates for blockwise caches.
Explicit full-history masks are sliced to that visible suffix. Partition ingress
leaves implicit mask construction with each layer, so full and sliding layers
retain their distinct semantics after cached multi-position continuation.

### Native pooled workspace bounds

The MLX mechanism facts now compose local/pooled attention from the selected
concatenation and SDPA implementation, and indexed attention from two selected
gathers, four batched einsum contractions, masks, shared sink normalization and
context addition. Einsum facts cover its transpose/reshape lowering as well as
the existing matmul casts, layout copies and split-product workspace. Gather
facts charge selected output storage; broadcast source views do not replicate
the complete pooled history.

Pooled-position selection includes F32 scoring, weighted head reduction and the
native partition implementation's sorting buffers. A top-k result retains the
entire partition-index allocation, even when its logical tail is much smaller.
Empty pooled history produces an empty U32 result with its scalar allowance.
These mechanisms have no disjoint host numerical payload vectors; native
buffers, including CPU/shared scalar construction, stay in the tensor domain.

Pooled masks normalize their batch/head/query broadcast geometry before joining
the key axis. Boolean masks become zero/negative-infinity eligibility when an
additive mask participates, and an absent additive mask contributes zero.
Native execution and cold facts share the shape-only normalization helper.
These are backend mechanisms, without family selection or admission policy.
Addressable expert scheduling and complete public request admission still
require their remaining workspace composition.

### Native positional workspace bounds

Relative-profile attention composes exact integer coordinates and causal/window
masks, optional logarithmic query/bias scaling, direct profile gathers, grouped
head expansion, two dense products and precise softmax. The bound includes all
child allocations through completion, including casts and strided reshape copies.
These native buffers have no disjoint Rust numerical payload. Query spans ending
at the largest supported I32 endpoint remain valid: the logarithmic coordinate
shift occurs after constructing the unshifted integer range. Contiguous and paged
attention share this native profile kernel.

Multi-axis rotary pricing follows the selected independent-axis, split-half or
round-robin layout. Native I32/U32 positions widen before offset arithmetic; I32
addition saturates as in the neutral reference. Round-robin construction creates
only the selected columns and its shared frequency vector. Column operations,
frequency copies, concatenation, angle construction, cosine/sine and possible
reshape copies belong to the tensor domain. The host domain contains one
exact-sized frequency vector at a time: the largest axis half-width for the
first two layouts, or the complete half-width for round-robin. Both returned
outputs retain their physical backing allowances, including empty shapes.

These backend facts complete the retained resident text equation quote for the
Inkling fixture, including cached multi-position continuation. This establishes
an equation workspace bound, not complete request admission or media, paged,
partitioned, prediction and snapshot/copy accounting. Native grouped
operators and selected addressable expert schedules still need their bounds.

### Native multi-stream workspace bounds

The selected MLX facts now price residual collapse, residual expansion, final
stream coefficients and the final weighted sum. Collapse includes F32 preparation,
the weightless RMS equation, learned dense projection, sigmoid coefficients,
precise matrix softmax and every selected Sinkhorn pass. One initial column
normalization and the remaining row/column pairs give `2 * iterations - 1`
normalizations. Each pass includes reduction workspace, its epsilon scalar and
the resulting matrix; quotation uses checked arithmetic without executing or
iterating through the passes.

Collapsed states, pre/post vectors and mixing matrices each retain their full
backing allowances across the sublayer boundary. Final-head coefficients remain
a separate output before the observer and weighted sum. Native casts, possible
strided reshape copies and batched products are included through completion.
Pooling and multi-stream contractions share the same two-operand einsum-to-matmul
allocation derivation. These mechanisms construct no disjoint host numerical
payload vectors.

An empty multi-stream batch bypasses RMS and Sinkhorn reductions and returns an
empty final sum after invoking the ordinary coefficient observer. This avoids
the vendored MLX empty-reduction identity-copy assertion while preserving empty
shapes and output dtype. The conservative operation envelope still covers its
scalar and empty-output backing.

These facts feed retained equation inspection. They do not price grouped expert
selection/execution, selected addressable expert schedules, materialization,
transport, media or complete request admission. Observer retention, prediction
lanes and independent copies still require their enclosing resource bounds.

### Routing outputs that share physical backing

The neutral workspace storage contract can identify an output as an alias of an
earlier output from the same operation. Backward references are validated before
the trace changes. The alias shares the complete storage root, including any
possible input roots, without adding another allocation charge. Different
logical shapes, chained views and a surviving view after its siblings are
dropped all preserve that ownership. This remains a cold declaration of native
storage behavior; it neither allocates tensors nor grants submission authority.

MLX joint selection uses this contract for selected and always-on coefficients,
which are slices of one normalized coefficient buffer. Its selected group IDs
retain the full partition-index backing. The tensor bound includes hidden
flattening, dense projection, sigmoid ranking and correction, native partition
buffers, direct gathering of unbiased logits, concatenation, log-sigmoid,
softmax, and fixed/learned scaling. Scalars use native storage; there is no
disjoint host numerical payload. Native group-count sums and zero hidden widths
are rejected by the neutral request contract before execution.

This prices the joint selector used by routed Inkling equations. Grouped expert
execution and addressable expert schedules still need their selected workspace
facts, alongside complete public request admission and the remaining
execution-path composition.

Ordinary MLX top-k selectors now compose the same dense/packed projection facts
with native input normalization, scoring, grouped eligibility, selection and
coefficient construction. Cutoff-tie detection and a possible CPU-stream
partition are both included; the latter allocates indices through the same
shared native allocator and partitions them in place. Supplied IDs preserve
their possible input backing. Scores and coefficients that are guaranteed to
share storage use the same-operation alias contract.

For routing interventions, a cold implementation of the neutral
`RoutingMechanism` executes `execute_routing_intervention`, just as the native
adapter does. The backend supplies primitive allocation facts, including row
masks, correction arrays, predicates and final dtype conversion; it does not
reimplement action or score-stage sequencing. Original-decision capture retains
both decisions. Managed host payload is the maximum live validation-count,
partition-ID, correction or keep-mask vector. Duplicate and forced-partition
validation borrow the admitted IDs instead of allocating another ID collection.
Empty routers bypass invalid native reductions while preserving subsequent
scale arithmetic and output dtype. No full routed-execution or admission claim
follows from pricing this selector operation.

Packed expert workspace facts now follow native grouped linear, gated-product
and ReLU-squared execution. They retain full sorting and gather buffers,
activation workspace, weighted output reduction and the extra bias reduction
used by the MLX tensor-parallel adapter. The gated bank's execution and estimator
share its native chunk thresholds. Every chunk's lazy intermediates remain
charged through completion, including the final concatenation. Dense and normal
packed gather kernels consume the bank directly; the group-size-16 affine path
actually gathers a packed matrix and its companions for every selected route,
and its bound includes those replicas.

Activated-unit outputs can retain the complete fused gate/up backing. Separate
unit and finish facts preserve that capacity across the observer boundary.
The selected mechanism now declares its grouped observation schedule through
`WorkspaceMechanisms`: one batch or fixed token chunks with an uneven tail.
The neutral observer driver delivers original/intervention/effective callbacks
with those exact shapes, local selection rows, absolute token offsets and total
invocation length. MLX supplies its native packed-bank thresholds; no architecture
or callback policy moves into the backend. Empty input delivers one empty batch.

The conservative Units/Finish trace retains every chunk's intermediates through
completion. Its aggregate unit metadata represents separately sorted stores,
not a physical concatenation. A metadata-only storage union preserves all
replacement and possible original owners across Finish without inventing a
native copy. An unavailable schedule raises the typed
`WorkspaceGroupedObservationScheduleUnavailable` before any callback or unit
work. Independently materialized expert providers still need their selected
member/residency execution trace; the packed-bank bound is not substituted for
that different mechanism.

Host reads inside the existing `safemlx` safety boundary now use signed native
strides. Borrowed Rust slices require row-contiguous logical storage and correct
alignment; empty arrays return an empty slice. Owned reads and native-byte export
walk logical coordinates directly, including reversed, broadcast and unaligned
views. Their Rust code allocates only the requested host result, while logical
equality allocates no payload. The selected Metal host-data access needs no
additional native staging. The shared checked geometry also rejects `as_strided`
views outside their logically flattened source and signed-offset overflow before
native construction. Independent native cloning retains its existing explicit
compaction-and-copy mechanism. These native details do not introduce a backend
dependency or unsafe-code exception in a portable crate.
Observation integer widening and routed capture/intervention coordinates consume
the borrowing logical iterator directly, without an intermediate host vector.
Native read errors retain their source through the neutral neural error boundary.
Owned vectors and widened observations reserve their exact logical capacity
before extension, avoiding generic iterator collection's extra growth capacity
for small results. The managed host payload therefore remains the priced result
capacity; allocator bookkeeping remains outside that payload domain.

Centroid-selected vocabulary readout now has a portable workspace descriptor
and shared exact geometry validation. Its mask floor is local to each decoder
position, matching the independent scalar contract across batch and sequence
partitions. The MLX realization reduces only the selected-vocabulary axis and
handles empty positions before native reduction. Its cold fact includes the
complete centroid partition backing and actual selected-weight replicas per
position, followed by dense products, per-position minima and F32 scatter output.
It assumes neither a direct indexed product nor early release of lazy children.
The descriptor also has an explicit zero disjoint-host-payload fact. These
operation facts support architecture-owned assistant traces; enclosing prediction
capture, transfer, state-copy and request admission still need composition.

The runtime memory pool can now retain a domain-capacity ceiling with each
request reservation. Every admission and storage registration observes the
strictest live ceiling under the same accounting lock. Ordinary reservations
cannot weaken an earlier live ceiling; cloned completion and state owners retain
one charge and its ceiling until their final release. Explicit completed-funding
succession, described below, requires the unique original owner's delegation.
Chunk selection uses this
atomic reservation path and includes existing residency and concurrent work.
The application request's incremental limit remains distinct from this complete
managed-domain ceiling. Native composition must still select the shared physical
domain, register its inventories, and connect complete request quotes to public
policy; these runtime contracts alone do not complete that integration.

Core now carries `TextInferencePolicy` and the cold `TextControllerWorkspace`
contract. The facade forwards ordinary/controlled chunk limits and includes them
in controlled snapshot configuration identity; finite decode allowance is checked
before coordinated native preparation. Architecture prepared-workspace composition
combines selected resident transaction copies, actual state backing, prompt,
sampling and controller payload. `RuntimeStateEstimate::selected_state_backing`
keeps physical capacity separate from logical fixed/context geometry and media.
Backend adapters supply retained projections and native facts, without selecting
family equations. Exact-concatenation/fixed and pooling checkpoints share buffers;
compressed checkpoints and rollback price independent capacity/view copies.

Runtime pool unquoted-owner leases atomically exclude complete request reservations,
including reservations charging zero bytes. Clones retain one blocker. Existing
storage registration can publish surviving certified allocations while that
blocker remains live; native completion plus complete ownership publication is
required before release. The native integration must start before materialization
and retain participation through independent inputs, copies and escaped outputs.
Public MLX managed budgets still reject unknown domain coverage; private request
reservations do not establish public whole-domain coverage. Prepared speculative
policy rejects before execution until its shared admission route is integrated.
These explicit gaps remain part of the bounded-inference implementation work.

Native model loading now enters one process-local aggregate `WorkingMemoryPool`
before communication realization or materialization. All production MLX backend
instances share that host/device domain. Its unlimited baseline is bookkeeping;
it does not claim an available-memory bound. A shared unquoted owner survives
prepared-model, executable and session ownership, and detached recovery preserves
it when loading fails or unwinds with unresolved native work. Quoted reservations,
including zero-byte reservations, exclude new unquoted loading in the same pool.

`safemlx::Array::retain_allocation_owner` attaches a `Send` owner to completed,
certified physical storage without changing its buffer, deleter or allocation
identity. Native views, lazy children retaining that backing, recovery pins and
donation retain the same owner. Independently wrapped host arrays attach to their
shared host storage. Native final release only enqueues a preallocated Rust node;
ordinary unlocked host reclamation runs its destructor. Unknown or unfinished
backing returns the original owner, and independent result allocations require
their own attachment. An attached owner must not retain its own native backing.

Session output publication attaches the model's domain owner before exposing
logits or raw output arrays. Opaque token submission owners also preserve it after
the releasable session payload is cleared. This does not yet establish complete
inventory promotion, complete quoted copy/preparation admission, observer-held
lazy intermediates, or rank-coordinated capacity rejection before communication.
Those remain prerequisites for enabling public strict budgets; the local loading
guard and native allocation primitive do not claim distributed budget admission.
Final prefill output indexing materializes its new view under the existing
request recovery scope before publication. Cold allocation inspection remains
side-effect-free and never supplies that completion evidence itself.

Existing native storage can now publish independent allocation charges while its
model remains unquoted. The runtime admits the complete inventory atomically but
returns one accounting owner per physical identity. Native arrays and immutable
host buffers attach only their own payload-free charge, so one escaped allocation
does not retain charges or address keys for unrelated weights. Source and buffered
byte roots retain their registrations at an ordinary host retirement boundary.
Complete load-time nonstate projections use this publication path; missing
projections retain the unquoted barrier. This does not register decoder state or
clear that barrier, and therefore does not duplicate state in request quotes or
claim complete model/request admission.

Native allocation identities are non-reused process-local generations. Views,
donation and host aliases preserve their physical owner's generation; exhausted
generation supply cannot become a reused identity. Checkpoint and byte-buffer
identity tokens retain weak Arc ownership, preventing address reuse while an
accounting key survives. Weak ownership can retain inline allocation storage even
after strong payload destruction. Runtime registration retirement therefore drops
the final keys outside its accounting lock before releasing their byte charge.
Reentrant destruction can observe a conservative retiring charge, but cannot see
those bytes released before the key's pinned allocation retires.


Independent ordinary prompt and sampler preparation now acquire native domain
ownership before entering their allocation workers. Reserved preparation invokes
the same workers under its one-use request authority without acquiring a conflicting
unquoted lease. Explicitly unbudgeted preparation still acquires an owner. Prompt ownership attaches to eager token backing before a lazy
view is created; wrapper clones and escaped native views retain that authority.
Reserved prompt backing retains the existing request charge even before the
separate bind stage, without retaining native roots in its attached owner.
Even greedy sampling retains an owner for its mutable host history. Submission
resources retain sampling and installed-state owners independently of the session
payload and through native recovery.

Ordinary native state capture, sampler/pending-input copies and reseeding acquire
fresh domain ownership before allocation. Completed copied prompt/token/RNG backing
retains its independent owner; encapsulated native snapshots retain it after their
payload. State exchange moves ownership with the state after the existing atomic
exchange succeeds. The initial model owner also follows displaced state, while
remaining with the model's nonstate resources. Restored sampler state merges its
retained authorities without duplicating leases or refunding request charges.
Cold estimates include added snapshot ownership metadata and do not allocate native
arrays. Empty pending input and temperature-only changes require no new allocation
owner. A live same-domain reservation rejects independent allocating work with
`WorkingMemoryError::ReservedWorkActive` before mutation. This conservative exclusion
does not implement a successful quoted-copy route or enable public strict budgets.

Speculative preparation now acquires native domain ownership inside the existing
coordinated admission stage, after validating every lane's inference policy and
before sampler or cache setup. Prepared execution binds that exact domain into
`SpeculativeExecutionStreams`; standalone contexts use the ordinary aggregate
MLX domain. Stream identity is never used to infer accounting identity. Prepared
lane and sampler owners retain the guard even when greedy execution has no RNG.
Opaque backend seed/random-state wrappers carry ownership through target/draft
splits, positional keys, reseeding, snapshot clones and recovery. A changed domain
must acquire its own authority before deriving or mutating keys.

`InferenceRetention` now retains neutral `WorkingMemoryUnquotedLease` handles as
well as request reservations. Clones of one lease deduplicate; independently
acquired leases in the same pool remain distinct. Copy, import, restore and failed
restore preserve those leases, including empty `DeviceState`. No native type or
unchecked release/promotion operation enters portable state. The architecture's
native target snapshot hook receives the complete mechanism context so the backend
can acquire from the correct domain before copying. Target snapshots retain the
neutral lease in state and attach ownership to completed native backing.

External target-cache copies and autoregressive checkpoint/restore use the same
independent acquisition and recovery rule. Autoregressive state retains its domain
for checkpoint operations whose contract has no context argument. External restore
preserves installed retention before replacing state.

Prediction-extension materializers declare a separate, borrowed `SnapshotContext`
for durable copies. The architecture forwards it through target-plus-prediction
and prediction-only snapshots and every declared prediction layer. Ordinary tensor
contexts continue to serve equations; the snapshot context retains the domain
needed for admission without introducing native types into portable contracts.
MLX uses `SpeculativeExecutionStreams` and acquires independent ownership before
copying each cache. Its resident sequential and pooling cache wrappers retain
authorities after their native payloads, including empty caches. Checkpoint, clone, clear and restore
preserve ownership; fallible restore merges both histories before touching state.
Completed copied backing carries the same ownership so raw native aliases remain
protected. Model-profile prediction snapshots reuse the target-state copy mechanism.
Cold estimates include the wrapper, shared allocation-sidecar payload and recovery
authority lists. One shared list serves all copied arrays, so growing restore
history does not create a separate list per array. These are logical payload
estimates, not allocator or allocation-registry bookkeeping measurements. Sealed
arrays inside a paging manager are outside this resident-wrapper attachment path;
the complete paging inventory and quote still require their enclosing integration.

Speculative sampling retains processed distributions in an opaque native wrapper.
Its callbacks acquire the selected domain before logits processing, capture,
sampling or commitment. Probability/residual arithmetic and verification handoff
retain source and destination authorities through native recovery. Distribution
clones keep their lazy native values with the same authorities. Sampler clones
share their authority list because custom policy and capture state can itself be
shared and retain native arrays, including from callbacks taking `&self`. No
borrow of that authority list remains active while a policy callback runs.

Complete accounting for drained host capture records, quoted-copy admission and
nonempty-state promotion remain unfinished; these ownership changes do not enable
public strict managed budgets.

Idle executable storage inspection now composes target parameters, dormant
prediction resources, blueprint-owned checkpoint sources and explicit enclosing
model/session storage. Decoder storage remains a separate identity-bearing
inventory because the execution quote includes state backing and growth overlap.
Unknown enclosing coverage, installed erased observers or uninventoried partition
communication keep the nonstate bound unknown. Zero retained decoder bytes does
not establish a zero logical frontier. Collection neither evaluates native arrays
nor changes ownership or grants allocation permission.

Session-payload composition includes parameter-overlay originals and published
replacements, with physical aliases counted once. Retained processors, native
communicators (including a target-only world) and erased test owners require
explicit coverage. Ordinary parameter visitation omits operator-owned numerical
helpers, including rotary frequency buffers. The separate read-only retained-value
traversal now covers those helpers without changing editable checkpoint parameters.
Unrecognized owners or unfinished native backing still keep the nonstate report
unknown. Partial storage publication remains protected by its unquoted owner.

Native unquoted owners now hold immutable leases. Publishing a complete inventory
can never revoke authority from an existing clone. Fresh session construction
now performs a checked transition after its initial reset has settled: the
session must be healthy, idle and exclusively own its payload, its complete
nonstate inventory must be certified, and its decoder must retain no numerical
storage. Exact loading-authority identity also distinguishes the initial reset's
local handles from any independently acquired operation authority. Registration
and native attachment finish before the executable, payload and initial reset
release their own loading handles. A local guard survives that entire transition;
escaped and recovery clones remain active. Unknown inventory, nonempty decoder
storage or a different retained authority preserves the original barrier. This
construction-only path does not periodically republish storage or authorize work.
Session operation entry checks both the retained model domain and the supplied
backend context. Additional domain authority is acquired before submission,
input construction, reset, cache I/O or observation and retained with the payload
through mutation and failure. This remains unquoted participation, not a complete
operation estimate. Direct model submissions copy retained request authority from
the completed transaction; completed output backing keeps payload-free reservation
handles alongside native ownership, independently of sampler or session lifetime.

The native wrapper also offers deferred allocation-owner attachment. A shared
array descriptor retains a payload-free authority bundle before evaluation;
`set_data` and shared-buffer publication transfer that bundle to certified native
or host backing before kernels use it. Views and donated storage retain the same
physical owner. Unmaterialized graphs retain authority until descriptor retirement;
unrecognized borrowed backing fails publication. The existing completed-only
attachment API keeps its cold certification requirements. Rust destruction still
runs through the preallocated, unlocked retirement queue within `safemlx`'s native
safety boundary. Pinned MLX performs descriptor publication synchronously during
serialized graph encoding; asynchronous workers use encoded pointers and retained
backing rather than mutating these authority lists.

The ordinary MLX observer adapter uses deferred attachment before handing native
tensors to callbacks. Its shared bundle contains only neutral request reservations
and native memory authority. Ordinary, replica, generated, routing and routed-unit
callbacks preserve lazy inputs, including geometry-only prototypes and skipped
factories; returned intervention tensors acquire the same authority. Internal
no-op prefill avoids observer attachments. Independently allocated callback payloads
that are never returned do not gain a bound through this mechanism. Retained
prediction observers and delivered host records still need complete enclosing
inventory/admission; callback storage ownership alone does not certify their peaks.

The shared ordinary text machine now acquires a move-only backend step permit
before querying its controller or constructing native decode input. Acquisition
receives the canonical preparation, current sampler/input and core-issued run,
policy-revision and attempt identities. Exact session admission remains checked
before acquisition. Ordinary emission finishes its local permit without observing
the token; controlled emission retains it through token observation, exact
completion and controller commitment. Scalar token readiness alone does not
release the native session lease before the commitment vote. Backend
completion/recovery independently retains resource charges.

The existing bounded readiness coordinator carries prediction-admission,
controller-decision and controlled-commitment votes. Local capability, permit or
callback failure still participates in agreement and preserves its original
error; successful peers do not advance after rejection. These exchanges use the
same monotone session accounting and framing as setup/delivery. Raw controller or
sampler access and host-state installation replace policy-revision identity;
restoration does not rewind attempts, and forked machines get distinct run
identities despite sharing preparation retention. Capture and intervention setup
replace policy identity before entering their mutable backend hook, since a
fallible setup may have partially changed state. Read-only phase rejection leaves
the identity intact.

Core constructs the original run context before preparation and calls
`bind_text_preparation_run` within the admission readiness result, before prompt
or sampler creation. Runtime binds that context in the existing
`InferenceTextPreparation` authority. A single mutex protects cold binding, stage
claims and run progress, so binding cannot race native preparation. Binding after
any stage claim, rebinding a clone, or binding a noninitial attempt is rejected.

Runtime's move-only `InferenceTextStep` consumes the next ordinal and one output
slot on issuance. It requires the bound run/policy, ready preparation, no active
or fenced attempt, and the exact preceding completed receipt for decode. Drop
without success fences the run permanently; restoration and cloned preparations
cannot refund work. An `InferenceTextStepReceipt` contains only preparation
identity and ordinal. It may accompany provisional output, but cannot admit a
successor until the issuing permit finishes. It retains no request charge or
native payload; completion and token storage keep those owners independently.

MLX's step permit validates session/domain, parameter epoch, prediction phase,
canonical sampler identity and the original prepared request. Resident and
selected host-layerwise token-ID admission compose the retained family equations, selected
native workspace facts, cumulative sampling, prompt allocation capacity and
controller declaration through the shared runtime planner. A private prompt
marker is set only by checked native preparation and is required both when
binding and submitting the prompt. Rebuilding or mutating input policy cannot
relabel an arbitrary input with quoted authority. An immutable private
quote records that exact configuration, request and native binding. It requires
complete published idle storage and either empty decoder state or a retained
quoted predecessor with known decoder storage and matching cached position;
unknown primitive,
processor, communication or helper coverage remains a typed rejection.

Only that private quote enables a runtime run claim before controller callbacks.
The claim validates the exact predecessor receipt and output allowance. Before
submission, the actual decision must fit the retained neutral
`TextControllerContract`: executable vocabulary, filtered/unfiltered mechanism,
final mask capacity and visible additional filter payload. Native submission
revalidates its actual predecessor receipt against the issued step; replacing the
token between permit issue and claim cannot reuse another token's permission.
The controller's
original declaration remains responsible for its opaque state and growth.
Native state validation checks every stateful layer's host frontier without
allocating tensors or consulting test-only snapshots. Decoder admission must
also retain the exact request and logical position.

Claiming the native permit creates move-only private submission evidence. The
existing submission/recovery driver retains its reservation before native work;
it never discovers operation permission from historical state charges. Raw
operations still acquire unquoted authority. Successful permitted tokens receive
an exact provisional receipt, which becomes a valid predecessor only after
ordinary success or controlled commitment finalizes the permit. Completed model
roots must retire before the next core prediction reuses transient workspace.
`ModelRuntime::validate_session_admission` is available as a read-only exact
comparison for composed backend entry; it grants no allocation or submission
permission. Reservation domain validation likewise grants no operation authority.

Strict capture/intervention setup rejects before installation until its complete
workspace is quoted. Direct sampling overrides likewise reject before modifying
temperature or RNG ownership; semantic override validation is not workspace
repricing. Neutral planner wrappers preserve their detailed estimate/reservation
errors as sources, including exact over-budget rejections. Repricing controls,
quoted reset and independent copies, raw
output/completion escape, and complete media/disk/distributed and remaining host-policy
admission remain unfinished. These are implementation gaps, not architectural
limitations of the model families.

Runtime owns exact state-revision identity independently of logical position and
retained charge ownership. Cold native continuation records that identity and
the predecessor request; equal positions after restoration do not revive a quote.
State advancement, restoration and exchange replace the revision without
refunding charges. Successful native tokens retain their producing revision as
payload-free metadata, so decode must prove both the current branch and its
immediately preceding completed receipt.

Under the existing native submission lease, the first continuation step validates
its opening state and invokes runtime's one-use predecessor supersession. Paired
run locks use a canonical order; all checks precede fencing the old run. An active
predecessor cannot be superseded, and stale handles cannot submit after successful
handoff. This transfers future execution permission separately from physical
storage ownership. Runtime can now convert a fresh, uniquely owned reservation
into request evidence and a move-only funding run. Native work takes independent
funding scopes before allocation. Publishing exact allocation identities shifts
their capacity from reserved workspace to the existing shared storage registry;
total usage and peak do not increase merely because the category changes.

The original physical funding account receives credit when an allocation retires
while its run or work scopes remain active. Once the run closes and all scopes are
certified, unused workspace is released and surviving storage retires separately.
Request metadata and storage descendants preserve the active capacity ceiling
and exclusion of unquoted work. The original ceiling remains unless an explicitly
authorized successor atomically raises it after certified completion. An
uncertified scope conservatively quarantines
the remaining bound; logical completion or an unsuccessful wait cannot release it.
Legacy reservations keep their previous lifetime semantics.

MLX publishes prompt backing during preparation and completed decoder, output,
validation and random-key backing through native recovery. The sampling event
also completes the next RNG root. Once the exact event succeeds, the completion
adapter settles every submitted array descriptor; cold inventory itself still
performs no polling or evaluation. This step clears a completed descriptor event
and cannot schedule a new graph. Model-source publications stay with the model,
while token owners retain only output/state publication metadata. A completion's
retirement guard follows its native roots and waits for outstanding recovery
tickets before certifying funding. The shared core machine drops controller,
pending input and completion owners before backend run state; native sampler
payloads in turn drop before the funding run. The same ordered owner covers
preparation agreement failure and unwind, before a machine exists. Native sampler
stage completion precedes transfer of run funding into its returned state.
Converted request evidence alone
cannot enter legacy prompt/sampler allocation workers.

A controller size witness does not prove resource lifetime. Core's
`TextControllerStorage` declares either a wholly run-owned payload or a run-owned
remainder with an exact inventory of immutable shared filters. Unknown ownership
remains the default; existing `inference_workspace_is_run_owned` declarations
forward to the wholly owned case. Shared filters must also fit the additional
host allowance, beyond the separately emitted final sampling mask.
The source inventory stays live throughout the admitted run, so its exact
capacities form a fixed part of that allowance. Runtime's
`RegisteredControllerStorage` pins the complete nonzero inventory only when every
identity is already registered at its exact capacity in the same domain. The
checked `ControllerWorkspaceContribution` decomposes the full additional allowance
into those always-live sources and remaining controller work before composing
workspace peaks. Only that fixed source component receives credit. Final sampling
masks, pre-override overlap and other controller payload remain priced. A failed
complete pin uses the full contribution; mixed registered/unregistered inventories
currently retain this conservative fallback rather than partial credit.

`ControllerWorkspaceEstimate` privately binds both full and incremental versions
of the same enclosing workspace. Architecture exposes preparation/sampling
composition before adding controller storage, while preserving its ordinary full
composition. Runtime's `IncrementalInferenceQuote` then pairs that contribution
with either full equations or the separate registered decoder-root proof. Both
routes use the same candidate planner and core admission policies. Unknown bounds,
geometry and domain checks, and ordinary reservation forgery checks remain intact.
An opaque `IncompleteWorkspace` outcome distinguishes missing numerical coverage
from invalid evidence. Runtime constructs it only after validating geometry,
domain, state-span accounting and any borrowed-root association. It retains the
candidate geometry and pool identity, but no storage pin or native payload. The
shared planner may try smaller chunks for this outcome; arbitrary unknown-bound,
identity, malformed geometry and native errors remain fatal. Complete quotes
remain the only route to reservation.
The original `Admission` remains available from reservation metadata, including
full selected-state/workspace diagnostics and the admitted incremental requirement.
That metadata holds no source, tensor or storage pin.

Successful reservation aggregates independent host and decoder accounting pins.
Funding conversion moves that custody into the run and its work scopes; dropping
a diagnostic quote cannot refund excluded sources. Preparation still attaches
charges to the actual shared owners before prompt work, including when a pin
already exists. Partial attachment failure remains uncertified and quarantines
both pins. Temporary controller quote/pin owners retire before the native retained
execution proof is published; its controller portion retains only identity metadata.

Core's `SharedTokenFilter` owns the immutable host mask and per-domain accounting
custody shared by all aliases, including aliases created before admission. Its
payload-free identity does not retain the filter. Runtime's
`ControllerStorageContract` retains only identity/capacity metadata and adopts
the existing mask from the admitted preparation envelope into its physical registry.
The charge is attached to the actual owner before prompt or sampler construction.
Mask destruction precedes its final accounting refund. Owner attachment invokes
only closed accounting operations; pool locks never invoke owner callbacks, and
accounting handles retire without holding the owner lock. Same-domain aliases
share custody; distinct domains retain separate charges.

Loaded-model composition also publishes tokenizer masks before any inference.
`LoadedModel::from_runtime` is fallible and invokes the neutral backend's deferred
shared-filter preparation hook for fingerprinting and mask construction. Runtime
obtains unquoted domain authority before invoking that factory, registers exact
mask capacity and attaches custody before releasing authority. MLX supplies the
actual session domain. A live admitted request rejects construction before the
factory runs; a model that never starts generation still contributes its mask
to later domain admission. The unquoted guard excludes concurrent quoted work;
it is not an allocation-size estimate for model loading. Standard and planned
loaders propagate the original neutral failure.

Native composition consumes this neutral contract, checking the unchanged shared
inventory before preparation and each controller callback. Decisions preserve
shared tokenizer-owner provenance and recheck it before native submission, so a
callback cannot substitute a same-sized different owner. Successful publication
survives a later preparation rejection while any loaded model, controller or
snapshot still owns the mask. Failed partial publication remains conservatively
funded. No facade controller type or grammar branch enters the backend.

The facade's text controller now shares this owner with the loaded model and
snapshots; history and emitted masks remain owned by the run. Controlled choices
price the extra pre-override mask and preserve shared provenance. Core's
`TextFilterWorkspace` now distinguishes exact filtering from optional bounded
masking. Optional declarations contain positions and allocation capacity, with no
synthetic mask or storage ownership. Runtime choice wrappers compose those bounds
without callbacks, preserving the original mask overlap through nested wrappers.
Core validates each actual decision against the declared mechanisms, executable
membership, mask extent, capacity and additional payload.

The same configured sampler trace prices each optional filter as a possible
allocation or input alias. MLX supplies the complete ordinary filtering costs and
both storage possibilities; absent facts remain unknown. Previously emitted token
and key roots remain live across every later step. Architecture inspection passes
the maximum complete backing union of its actual score rows, including possible
aliases. Sampling introduces a separate input root per step, so an earlier token
alias retains the prior score capacity instead of sharing one fictitious input
identity across all predictions. This envelope is conservative and gives no
residual credit. A bare layout passed to the lower-level sampling quote explicitly
declares packed backing; selected architecture composition uses actual backing
facts. Zero-output optional quotes construct no mask and require no optional
filter operation, while retaining independent initialization costs.

Optional filtering grants no authority to mutate an admitted controller; existing
policy revision checks remain. Grammar parser storage and dynamic control
repricing remain unfinished.

Cached requests with resident or selected host-layerwise weights obtain a separate
residual equation quote for device-resident decoder state. Native
projection pairs each actual decoder allocation with the exact portable metadata
root used by its state views. Runtime binds that bijection to an existing-only
registry pin; missing, mismatched or foreign keys reject without registering new
bytes. The neural workspace context retains one immutable borrowed-root set across
all completed spans. Residual reports exclude only those identities from the
union of opening, closing and new allocation roots, including possible aliases;
new checkpoint, rollback and growth copies remain charged. Full diagnostics stay
unchanged. No old byte total is subtracted from a maximum.

Runtime composes this residual equation peak with the same enclosing preparation,
sampling and controller costs. Core applies the same context, completeness,
application-budget, availability and safety-reserve policies to the proved
incremental requirement. Ordinary pool reservation still enforces the full-report
minimum; only a private residual quote bound to registered roots can use the
smaller minimum, through the shared candidate-chunk planner.

A residual reservation itself owns its registry pin before it escapes. It requires
private funded preparation even before conversion, preventing legacy metadata-only
allocation. Conversion transfers the pin into the run and its independent work
scopes; historical metadata does not pin all earlier cache allocations. Certified
retirement drops pins outside the accounting lock. An uncertified scope retains
one pin in permanent quarantine, which can keep its pool alive until a future
certified cleanup mechanism. Duplicate funded registrations can also retain an
old capacity ceiling on a baseline model allocation. Cleanup and ceiling lifetime
refinements remain required for the final reuse policy.

Sampling workspace inspection now retains every emitted token root across the
entire output allowance. Opening-state accounting deduplicates their actual
backing identities with random-key aliases and keeps unknown capacities unknown.
An output clone shares its backing; independent emissions each contribute their
whole native allocation. This covers serial token emission after completion
retirement. Independently retained completion objects can also retain model
logits, and raw logits require their own cumulative lifetime accounting.

Reservation retention and permission to perform an operation are separate
contracts. A retained state request currently validates executable identity,
geometry, frontier, phase, readout demand and output allowance. Those checks do
not authorize later instrumentation, arbitrary callbacks, sampling changes,
independent copies or accumulation of escaped raw outputs. Reusing one transient
reservation for several surviving output allocations would undercount storage even
when each invocation fits its span quote. Successful strict admission therefore
also requires a retained neutral execution contract and validation of each
operation against its priced mechanisms and output-retention behavior. Backends
must consume that authority through their existing submission path; merely finding
a reservation on installed state cannot replace operation admission.

Numerical storage inspection now has a read-only neural traversal distinct from
editable parameter topology. `Parameterized::visit_retained_values` visits
parameters and operator-owned numerical helpers and returns an explicit
completeness result. The default exposes known parameters but reports incomplete
coverage. Derived modules require an explicit classification for skipped fields:
descriptive metadata, a retained raw tensor, or an optional retained tensor.
Unknown children do not prevent later known children from contributing storage.
Architecture static ownership and resident/bounded policy ownership compose this
traversal through the shared runtime; physical allocation identity and capacity
remain backend facts. Cold inspection neither materializes buffers nor grants
submission authority. Mutable parameter visitors retain their existing identities
and exclude helper buffers such as rotary frequencies.

### Host-layerwise managed text execution

Architecture quotation uses the ordinary `LayerwiseRuntime` traversal with an
explicit `WorkspaceLayerwiseParameters` provider. It constructs and binds each
unit inside its executed prompt/decode span. Runtime's transactional
`bind_workspace_parameters` validates the full immutable and mutable topology,
identities, shape, normalized dtype and quote context before replacing values.
Constructor helpers and equations remain charged through the complete span.
Neural `ParameterPlaceholder` records the eager scalar seed created by an
unloaded parameter; its logical full-weight fill stays lazy and is replaced by
binding. Cloning or reshaping that metadata creates no second seed.
Workspace capability declarations also include the existing masked-output
projection trace. This permits shared construction that requires that operator;
each actual invocation still needs its selected native allocation facts.

`ExecutionUnitLayout::window_range` supplies the same group-bounded lookahead
geometry to execution and `quote_completed_layerwise_window`. The latter takes
the maximum sum of actual per-unit transfer bounds. Native execution must settle
the preceding consumer and transfer and retire their references before replacing
the window. Existing host, static and cached device allocations remain charged
separately; neither logical residency bytes nor allocator observations establish
the fresh destination bound.

MLX describes every actual ready immutable host-copy name, including alias names
that can independently allocate destinations. Selected Metal allocation facts
bound each fresh buffer. Prospective parameter backing uses the larger of source
and fresh destination capacity, covering allocation or host aliasing, without
registered-state credit. Cold metadata inspection performs no payload read,
evaluation, completion polling, residency repair or retirement. Only after budget
reservation does an atomic ready-only operation revalidate and pin those stores.
The private execution quote retains their residency pins, alongside payload-free
policy, layout, depth, allocation and parameter-epoch identity. The earlier
controller-credit metadata rule applies to the controller portion of this proof;
it does not remove these host residency owners.

The existing submission, recovery and `FundedWork` owners cover construction,
copies and execution. Final publication registers surviving decoder, output and
device-window allocations before funding certification. Failed or incomplete
publication keeps funding uncertified. This extends selected host-layerwise
ordinary/controlled text with device-resident state; other materialization, distributed, media,
speculative and instrumented execution still require their missing integration
and complete facts. No backend family branch or separate inference engine is
introduced.

### Reusable disk-read workspace metadata

Checkpoint encoded read batches and encoded recipe reads can be cloned as
metadata. Clones retain the same admitted files, ranges and tensor geometry;
reading still validates that original admission. They neither read payloads nor
pin payload-cache entries. Preparing a new read descriptor can admit headers and
update source metadata, so that preparation belongs to loading. Cold candidate
inspection must reuse the retained descriptor.

Native array metadata snapshots use a nonblocking runtime lock without
housekeeping, payload reads, evaluation or owner retirement. They report shape,
dtype, logical bytes and optional certified completed backing. Unknown backing
stays unknown, and a busy runtime returns a typed error. The snapshot retains no
array or allocation owner; keeping it cannot prevent a streamed device window
from retiring. Warm device parameters require actual backing capacity, not their
logical tensor size.

The architecture layerwise equation provider accepts both selected host and
dense disk residency through the same unit-construction traversal. This prices
equations and cumulative sampling only. Materialization still needs its own
complete source, conversion, window-lifetime and native-capacity proof before
managed admission can use that route.

MLX's prepared direct-read plan owns reusable encoded reads and an explicit
canonical binding dispatch. Its capacity calculation shares the existing direct
batch implementation. Per-unit descriptors expose the full alias-owner dependency
closure, including owners outside a requested window. A materialization retains
every batch input before fallible stream copies and retains each output before
subsequent batches. Local and external aliases reuse canonical arrays; supplied
external aliases must match the retained physical geometry before reading.

The manager prepares these plans during loading, then inspects them without
source API calls or residency changes. Device snapshots retain only descriptor
facts, and source/manager identity uses weak references: a source wrapper can own
unrelated numerical payload even when it supports direct reads. Retaining a read
plan must not prolong that payload. Warm backing uses the larger of its actual
capacity and the future direct-read bound. Host, in-flight, failed, mismatched
and ordinary-conversion branches require additional evidence.

### Foreground direct disk operation custody

The shared layerwise provider also describes selected foreground direct disk
reads. Loading retains reusable plans; a candidate uses those plans without
repeating source admission. The private receipt contains read metadata, weak
manager/source identity, policy/layout identity and per-binding capacity envelopes.
It retains no native arrays or source-wrapper payload. Warm Device hits may change
allocation identity between operations while preserving physical geometry,
canonical sharing and the admitted capacity envelope.

Each existing `SessionOperation` activates the receipt after establishing recovery
ownership and before input conversion or unloaded-unit construction. The manager
checks all acquisitions, including recursive canonical owners and ready copies,
against an exact declared group-local window plus its priced persistent owner
closure. A missing unit consumes its retained direct plan; an unexpected Host
copy cannot select another materializer. Activation rejects overlapping operations.
The guard remains until release is requested and every recovery scope settles.
Escaped token handles retain their physical charges without prolonging this route.
Guard destruction only retires metadata; it performs no native work or locking.

The admitted foreground policy completes consumers and transfers, reclaims their
references, then evicts out-of-window Device copies before initial and subsequent
refills. Logical residency capacity does not substitute for this eviction: a
roomy cache must not accumulate every new layer. Canonical owner units retained
by alias pins are priced separately from the rotating window. Eviction failures
remain errors. Unquoted scheduling retains its existing overlap behavior.

This route requires zero host-prefetch budget, device-resident decoder state and
complete direct-read/native facts. Background prefetch and ordinary conversion
still need their own simultaneous storage, funding and completion integration.
The existing equation trace, chunk planner, controller checks and core step
authority remain shared with resident and host-layerwise execution.

### Completed funding capacity succession

Runtime owns the atomic transition of a completed funding account's active
capacity. The unique `WorkingMemoryFundingRun` may delegate one move-only
`WorkingMemoryCapacityHandoff`, bound to the exact execution, weak pool identity
and a nonreused account id. Historical request metadata cannot mint it. The token
retains no numerical storage or funding-account lifetime, and its destruction
changes neither capacity nor charges. Legacy reservation and planner APIs retain
their original ceiling semantics.

The shared incremental prefill planner accepts explicit predecessor capabilities
and a successor capacity. Under the existing accounting mutex it validates every
capability, then considers only accounts with a smaller finite ceiling. Each
changed account must have a closed run, no outstanding scopes, no quarantine and
no remaining workspace. All quote, identity, geometry, overflow and capacity
checks precede mutation. Active accounts whose limits are unchanged remain
ordinary constraints; unrelated accounts with numerically equal limits never
inherit a supplied account's authorization. Fixed pool capacity remains binding.

Successful admission atomically raises each eligible account's contribution and
creates the new reservation. It preserves physical registry entries and origins,
registered bytes, exclusion of unquoted work and the remaining owners. The old
account retains the adopted ceiling even if its successor retires first. Later
succession supplies capabilities for every surviving authorized account. No
provider callback or physical-key destruction occurs inside the transition.
Rejected candidates change no charge, peak, ceiling or capability eligibility.

MLX composition keeps these capabilities in private session metadata outside the
model payload, generation state and output owners. It mints each capability from
the unique funding run before fallible preparation, and prunes retired account
tokens by metadata alone. A larger explicit managed capacity on that session's
next request authorizes succession. Core predecessor fencing and move-only text
step authority remain mandatory and independent; capacity succession cannot
restart a run, refund output allowance or certify native completion.

The capacity-policy transition commits at successful admission. A later prompt,
controller or sampler preparation failure does not restore the former ceiling: a
concurrent request may already have used the authorized headroom. Outstanding or
uncertified work still prevents any further increase. Physical storage retires
through its existing native owners and registration path.

### Immutable controller byte sources

Core's closed `SharedControllerBytes` owns one immutable byte vector. It shares
the existing filter custody mechanism and `SharedStorageIdentity` registry key;
`SharedTokenFilterIdentity` remains a compatibility alias. Identities and domain
keys retain no payload or native resources. Pre-existing aliases share later
attachments, each domain attaches once, and final destruction releases the byte
allocation before any accounting handle. No mutable or consuming raw-vector
export can detach an allocation from its custody.

`TextControllerStorage` can describe borrowed slices of shared masks and byte
owners alongside its run-owned remainder. Cold runtime evidence retains source
kind, exact identity and capacity; equal values or byte totals never imply
identity. The existing shared registry, all-or-nothing pins, fixed-source credit
and funding adoption apply to both closed owners. Byte sources do not acquire
tokenizer-mask provenance. The legacy filter-only accessor returns unknown when
a declaration contains byte owners, rather than omitting those owners.

A decision with declared byte sources must carry the complete borrowed
`controller_storage` witness after its callback. The existing native pre-submit
check validates this against the admitted inventory before any native work.
Missing, unknown or replaced source evidence rejects, including zero-capacity
owners. Filter-only controllers retain their existing tokenizer provenance
contract. Forced decisions preserve the storage witness when replacing the
final filter. This checks the callback's reported sources; controller allocation
and lifetime bounds remain required throughout the callback itself.

The neutral byte-construction hook takes a deferred, closed factory. Runtime
acquires existing unquoted domain authority before invoking it, then registers
the exact returned capacity and attaches custody before releasing that authority.
An active reservation rejects before allocation, including a zero-byte one. A
failed registration or unwind retires the new byte payload before the guard.
Portable default implementations supply no managed-domain proof; MLX only binds
the exact pool and translates errors. It owns no grammar or tokenizer policy.

Facade vocabulary preparation inspects the immutable blueprint trie without
cloning a grammar state, checks offset/host geometry, then packs u64 offsets and
decoded token bytes into one guarded allocation. Sparse slots and structural
marker stripping preserve existing semantics. Ordinary and controlled semantic
setup use the same constructor and preserve typed backend failures. Independent
compiler/trie/parser growth, semantic host state and snapshot/copy ownership still
require their own coverage; vocabulary custody alone does not admit grammar.

### Parser-owned table bounds

The pinned derivre and llguidance Rust forks are portable workspace members.
They inherit `unsafe_code = "forbid"`; llguidance's upstream C-ABI modules and
header build are excluded. Archive checksums, original file hashes and licenses
are retained under `third-party`. These packages provide facts about their own
storage and reject invalid table growth. They do not select devices, hold native
resources or decide Eredu's memory admission policy.

Derivre exposes allocation-free hash-cons lookup and checked retained capacity
for its backing vector, element vector and hashbrown allocation. Its closed
prepared table allocates capacities during explicit construction, then checks
logical and physical capacity before an insertion can mutate the table. A
duplicate requires no new space. Construction still requires the caller's
allocation authority, and actual capacity must be observed after preparation;
requested element counts do not certify a byte budget.

LlGuidance reuses lookup before allocating a new lexer state. Existing states
remain usable at the configured state limit; a missing state checks the limit
and representable geometry before interning, constructing its descriptor or
growing transition storage. Rejection enters the existing parser error path
without publishing an invalid state identifier. Transition rows grow directly,
without a separate temporary row allocation.

This bounds state publication, not all work needed to discover the candidate
state. Derivatives, expression caches, tokenizer/compiler ownership, parser
histories and copy overlap remain separate requirements. Complete managed
grammar admission stays unknown until those requirements are covered. The
shared ordinary and controlled facade drivers keep their existing typed gates.
The state cap is now installed before the DEAD/MISSING sentinel states are built.
A scalar `InvalidLexerStateLimit` rejects caps below two at the factory before
grammar compilation, and at independently callable leaf constructors before
their storage work. First-byte warming, large-lexeme precomputation, initial
parser rows and skip selection propagate a typed `ParserError` with phase context
before any failed lexer can escape as a successful parser. A successfully built
lexer and its independent copies retain their finite per-instance cap; this does
not price the copies or cap their combined bytes.

Matcher error states retain only known closed configuration/parser causes and
the existing diagnostic message. Repeated operations and clones preserve that
cause and its stop classification. Arbitrary constructor errors still retire
before matcher publication. After a caught callback panic, a nonblocking
diagnostic probe returns no cause for a busy or poisoned lexer; it neither
recovers that lexer nor infers completion. This avoids a second panic while
preserving the original failure. Native completion authority remains unchanged.

Prepared expression encoding uses explicit scratch within the hash-cons owner's
fixed backing. A scoped writer checks declared length before copying each chunk,
hashes the contiguous completed encoding, and checks duplicate identity before
new-entry capacity. New entries publish the staged words directly. Every ordinary
non-commit exit clears written scratch; a sticky write failure cannot publish a
truncated encoding. The owner also records an outstanding insertion, so forgetting
the guard fences subsequent mutations instead of treating dirty staging as free.
Committed reads and eventual owner destruction remain available.

The ordinary expression arena, checked length counter and prepared writer use
one private encoding algorithm. Raw encoding preserves tags, flags, byte order
and initialized padding. It returns a raw table identifier, not an expression
reference: reserved expression seeds, child ownership and simplifier invariants
remain the responsibility of a complete expression arena. Scratch is real
retained capacity. This primitive does not admit parser construction, derivative
scratch/caches or independent copies, and does not widen grammar capabilities.

TokenParser now builds ordinary and independent copies through one exhaustive
field-copy helper. The independent path first constructs its selected Parser
once, then clones the remaining token-level fields. It no longer clones the
complete ParserState into a temporary and immediately replaces it with another
deep copy. History, forced-token caches, timing/statistics, token allowance,
configuration and failure state retain their existing clone semantics. Ordinary
copies still share their lexer; independent copies own distinct lexer state.
This removes one redundant state copy without establishing copy admission or
changing snapshot budgets and native completion ownership.

Host preparation now has a core-owned, opaque lifetime contract:
`HostPreparationAuthority`. The backend hook validates its runtime and acquires
the existing managed domain's unquoted lease before allocating opaque host
state. Clones retain exclusion; they carry no parser payload, byte allowance,
native completion signal or permission to submit inference. Portable backends
have an unmanaged default. MLX erases only its neutral pool lease into this
contract, without acquiring a tensor, stream or grammar-specific mechanism.

The facade acquires this authority before runtime chat preparation and before
the common semantic setup used by ordinary, controlled and speculative drivers.
Runtime preparation eagerly validates a frozen tokenizer and the selected
grammar, including the existing syntax-only fallback and original-schema
completion policy. It then publishes one registered immutable recipe containing
the tokenizer configuration, selected grammar, original schemas, EOS aliases,
structural IDs/spellings, stops and activation trigger. Variable directories
also live inside that allocation; the plan retains only fixed-size offsets and
static dialect declarations alongside it. Compiler, matcher, tokenizer trie and
slicer products retire before the temporary construction authority.

The frozen tokenizer envelope preserves the special-token encoding flag omitted
by upstream tokenizer serialization. Roundtrip validation compares serialized
configuration, canonical ID/spelling mappings, normalized trie bytes and special
metadata. Unrepresentable sparse added-token mappings reject before publishing
a validated recipe. Reconstruction consumes that recipe rather than the current
model's tokenizer; tokenizer caches remain newly constructed, unquoted storage.

Explicit text setup leaves the recipe encoded. Semantic setup first acquires
fresh authority, then reconstructs mutable grammar and protocol state. Actual
tokenizer environments, grammar/controller owners and shared compiled validators
retain custody through their aliases and internal forks. Parser/pipeline payloads
retire before their authority; rebinding an existing parser retains both domains.
Backend acquisition and registration errors preserve their typed sources through
the neutral facade error boundary.

This separates registered immutable construction inputs from unbounded mutable
parser work. It does not supply finite grammar/cache/semantic-output bounds,
host snapshot destination admission, or a process-memory guarantee. Text pipeline
capacity, outer control metadata and independently escaped application values
remain separate accounting work. The existing logical snapshot ledger and native
completion/teardown obligations are unchanged.

Snapshot composition acquires host authority before allocating its destination
metadata, cursor, parser and delivery copies. The neutral continuation driver
independently calls the backend hook after pure compatibility/estimate checks,
before owned discovery/estimator construction, logical copy reservation and
