controller/capture/native copying. Retaining a caller-supplied token cannot bypass
that acquisition. A `HostPreparation` snapshot error preserves the original
neutral backend failure and does not imply native work began or completed.

Core continuations retain combined source/destination custody as a final field.
Restoration attaches it before installation can move a new payload into the
active state, while a local clone protects failure cleanup. Facade snapshot,
session and branch owners retain their own final authority; branch exchange moves
that custody with cursor, parser, lifecycle and delivery state. Existing semantic
preparation custody also covers enclosing controlled-session payload destruction.

Capture's shared identity owner now retains payload-free host custody. Checkpoint
and previously created partition handles see later attachments through that same
owner, with payloads destroyed before their final owner field. A child keeps a
distinct capture identity while inheriting source custody. Speculative activation
checkpoints preserve their separate control identity and retain the capture host
owner alongside copied plans. Attachment preserves old and incoming domains,
releases replaced tokens outside its mutex, and reports poison without claiming
settlement or recovering the lock.

These guards move rejection before previously unguarded host copies and logical
copy-budget consumption. They do not implement finite funded snapshots: the
existing MLX quoted-copy rejection remains. Generic controller/callback owners
and independently copied public plan or event values remain their composition's
custody responsibility; a borrowed DTO is not an allocation certificate. A future
funded path must quote physical source/destination overlap and bind the complete
copy to the existing managed funding mechanism.

Sampler copies now use a checked plan borrowing the exact configured source.
The runtime owns the copy of standard controls, Mirostat adaptive state and the
fixed-size history box. Its managed payload cost includes every box slot,
including spare capacity and slots retained after clearing. Ordinary backend
snapshot estimates and speculative sampler clone costs use that same plan.
Preparing a plan neither allocates the destination nor grants memory authority.

Native isolated array copies share one contiguous-then-independent-copy program
with their workspace trace. Ordinary pending-input/RNG copies and concatenating
KV snapshot copies consume that program under their existing recovery owners.
A dense cache plan borrows the stored K/V slots and preserves all frontier,
capacity and window metadata; aliased source slots still request independent
destinations. Projection observes shape, dtype and completed backing through the
nonblocking metadata snapshot API, without native housekeeping or evaluation.
Unknown backing stays unknown and inspection errors retain their typed causes.

These are component copy mechanisms. A known history payload or native operation
trace does not cover enclosing ownership metadata, controller/capture payloads,
facade state or destination execution authority. Complete finite snapshot
funding remains unavailable; existing quoted-copy rejection and logical
nonrefundable copy budgets are unchanged.

The ordinary sampler can now be constructed as an owned component of its original
funded preparation. The consuming sampling stage binds configuration, account and
execution identity and returns a finish-only token. A closed sampler scope mints
its own host-only custody; it exposes no native storage adoption or completion
operation. Sampler destruction precedes release of that custody. Native PRNG
construction and recovery retain their independent work scope.

Canonical history growth has a protected portion of the existing funding balance,
including the inline configured sampler and the largest old/new history overlap.
This adds no second charge. Native storage publication cannot spend that portion;
insufficient source funding rejects before construction. Sampling quotes compose
native and host maxima conservatively to cover the fixed retained host allowance.
A move-only sample permit checks the original output allowance before native
filtering and sampling, then delegates the existing configured sampler once.
Dropping a permit does not refund its attempt.

A sampler copy borrows both the concrete source and its authenticated custody.
Shared pool admission validates source/domain identity and all live ceilings in
one accounting transaction before copying. The destination uses the existing
funding ledger without constructing an inference admission or token geometry.
Its frozen sampler drops before its independent run; it can be the source of
another admitted copy but cannot mint a generation step. Whole native sampling
and facade snapshots still require RNG, input, state and host-copy funding.

Isolated native array copying now has a shared two-operation program in
`eredu-nn`: contiguous materialization followed by an independent copy. A sealed
workspace plan traces that program in a private context, validates the exact
imported source-root selection, and keeps all destinations live through the
aggregate. Caller-owned diagnostic reports cannot become copy authority. Missing
native or host facts stay unknown; derived metadata values cannot substitute for
imported physical sources.

Runtime associates this plan with existing-only registered source pins. Copy
admission checks the origins' health, domain, active ceilings and complete
incremental demand in the same transaction as the existing funding ledger.
The result has one work scope and closed destination custody, with no inference
geometry, run grant or scope factory. The source pin follows the work scope:
certification releases it after publication, while an uncertified scope retains
it through quarantine. Destination allocations retain their ordinary independent
registry charges after the saved component retires.

MLX binds a saved key/scalar copy to the current prepared request, completed
receipt, parameter epoch, state revision and exact borrowed slots. The ordinary
session submission lease spans cold inspection, admission and the fixed copy
worker. A distinct submission purpose skips source-model publication and retains
sources and intermediate arrays through the existing recovery tickets. Successful
settlement is followed by explicit, fallible destination publication and scope
certification. A settled read-only copy error preserves the unchanged model;
unresolved, failed or blocked native recovery still fences it. Saved numerical
components carry no source generation quote, pending-input receipt or child
execution authority. Whole snapshot composition still needs its remaining
native state and host payload plans.

Core's quiescent continuation boundary provides a copy borrow with mutable
runtime access and immutable generation state and pending input. It preserves
the source policy identity; mutable generation-state access still revises it.
The shared snapshot driver uses this borrow for capture and copy staging, then
uses the mutable boundary only when installing restored state. Copy admission
and native submission guards remain the concrete mechanism's responsibility.

Saved ordinary sampling now has one aggregate copy boundary. Runtime joins the
actual authenticated canonical sampler plan with the sealed registered array
program and checks both source owners in the same admission transaction. One
fresh account covers history plus native workspace; two private scopes split
host retirement from native completion. The canonical host payload is held
inside that account before either scope escapes, so native publication cannot
spend it. Both destination custodians use the same new account identity. Their
byte diagnostics overlap and must not be added as independent charges.

`TextSnapshotBackend` distinguishes live sampling from immutable saved sampling
and pending input. The shared snapshot driver captures that aggregate once;
restore and fork call one fallible resume-preparation hook before infallible
installation. Existing unquoted snapshots use the same shared driver. A bounded
MLX component copies Standard/Mirostat history, RNG and optional scalar input
through the existing admitted native worker without a second reservation. Saved
copies can themselves be copied after the original run advances or retires,
using their own host custody and physical roots. Old live receipts and frontiers
do not authenticate saved-data duplication.

The bounded saved representation carries no runnable sampler or pending-input
grant. Its conversion to live state rejects until fresh resumed-run admission,
initial-decode and revision binding are implemented. The full snapshot's early
host guard remains: native cache/layout, controller, decoder, capture and delivery
payloads still need a complete aggregate before whole finite snapshots can pass.

Live state-layout ownership now has a neutral immutable shared owner, separate
from cold family declarations. Runtime exposes the actual owner through the state
contract, and native key/value, hybrid and generic device state preserve that
owner when cloning checkpoints. Its retained capacity includes nested layout
vectors, shapes and names. Input descriptors use immutable sorted boxed metadata
entries with preserved lookup, JSON-map and wire ordering, enabling exact payload
capacity for shared prepared-input identities without guessing tree-node sizes.

Native retained storage can publish these closed metadata owners through the
existing registry. Each accounting key holds only a separate identity; the actual
owner retires its payload before releasing attachments. The initial idle model
inventory includes immutable layout storage separately from mutable cache arrays,
so loading authority cannot be dropped before registration succeeds. Sharing a
layout then retains the same charge through its last alias.

A closed text-input identity plan now prices its fixed descriptor, exact-capacity
fingerprints and explicit hashing scratch in the original prompt quote. The
worker binds the same immutable token slice used for native upload, streams the
canonical encoding without an intermediate vector, and publishes the actual
identity owner through the existing preparation funding scope. Shared prefill,
transaction checkpoints and control slots retain that owner without re-encoding
or copying its payload. Original unquoted or legacy reservation authority also
follows escaped metadata aliases. Replacing a reserved prompt's fingerprint
rejects before constructing another identity; measurable capacity alone never
supplies prior allocation permission. Generic media identity construction and
whole-state snapshot admission still require their own complete bounds.

Resident cache copying now has source-borrowed native programs for padded
key/value storage, compressed logical views and pooling slots. Their ordered
operand visitors and consuming workers use the same source fields. Compaction
and independent copying use the shared isolated-array program; recovery variants
retain each intermediate and result in the caller's existing completion scope.
These are native representation mechanisms and introduce no family equations or
allocation grants. A paged catalog still needs its separate complete copy plan.

Hybrid fixed state uses a private sorted boxed role table. Declared roles remain
fixed while optional tensor values change, and absent roles occupy measurable
slots. Shallow checkpoints preserve handle sharing; isolated copying produces
independent numerical storage. The box's payload diagnostic excludes enclosing
layer storage, construction scratch, bookkeeping and native arrays. Complete
copy admission still needs authenticated source and destination host storage,
one aggregate account, and a saved representation without runnable authority.

Compressed retained-state traversal also includes padded stores when they have
backing independent of the logical views, as can happen after checkpoint copies.
Physical inventory deduplicates shared allocations. The isolated copy still
consumes only its two logical operands, so complete source inventory and
destination-copy operands must remain separate concepts.

Runtime now provides move-only ownership of fixed host slot tables. Their actual
boxed payload stays outside shared locks; a separate token carries sealed inline
extent, identity and accounting attachments. Table retirement fences attachment
before destroying elements, then releases its own token. Escaped tokens retain
existing charges conservatively without retaining or exposing elements. A copy
plan still needs a borrow of the actual table; a token is not data availability
or allocation authority. Nested payload and constructor workspace remain separate.

DeviceState, native key/value and hybrid layer containers, and hybrid fixed-role
containers use those owners. Existing borrowed layer APIs and clone/restore
semantics remain intact. Native inventory publishes actual table tokens through
the existing storage registry, separately from shared layouts and numerical
backing. Idle model publication includes those extents before releasing loading
authority; final operation publication traverses the actual installed owners.
This source accounting does not certify complete state-copy construction or
issue a resumed execution grant.

Architecture-declared dormant prediction prototypes participate in the same
host-state inventory as active decoder states. Their layout and layer/fixed
owners remain distinct from the target's owners, even when numerical arrays
alias. Prototype traversal inventories those actual owners without constructing
or advancing a prediction lane.

Exact host table inventory cannot override unknown retained native storage. The
DeepSeek V4 fixture's rotary helper Copy expressions lack certified cold backing,
so its initial whole-model transition retains loading authority. Independent
publication of known table sources under that authority neither evaluates the
helpers nor upgrades the complete inventory.

TextSnapshotBackend now owns the backend contract for one immutable saved
pair containing decoder state, sampler and pending input. Runtime's shared
snapshot driver captures and prepares resume through that paired contract;
backend implementations finish all fallible preparation before returning
installable components. Saved data has no public native-slot extraction or
mutable component replacement. Logical estimates remain separate from physical
admission. MLX preserves its existing unquoted workers and separately admits
resident KV paired copies through the joint host/native program. Incomplete
native representations and fresh funded resume remain explicit rejections.

Cold replicated-session inspection can return a view borrowing the exact state
and mechanisms. The retained shared borrow prevents replacement; copying still
starts only after inspection returns and requires separate submission authority.
This lets a native copy retain the actual source payload independently of the
mutable runtime handle, without a self-referential plan or token-only data proof.

Runtime also provides a closed fixed-slot initializer derived from an actual
source table. It allocates one optional-slot buffer, fills only vacant cells,
and retains that representation through completion and later copies. Its public
plan grants no allocation authority; the allocating worker is crate-private.
Nested element resources and allocator/ownership bookkeeping remain separate.
Saved native copy preparation now binds its move-only lease to the exact
execution session, separately from a saved source's same-pool compatibility.

The existing working-memory ledger now admits a sealed sampler plan, actual
fixed-slot initialization and numerical copy program together. It validates
sampler, table or saved-host, operand and full-source origins under one lock,
then creates one account with two protected host holds and one native work
scope. The native scope carries the entire source pin bundle; host cleanup
cannot certify native work or clear quarantine. Provider keys must project the
exact table identity, and saved-slot copies authenticate their actual held
owner rather than replaying an original source registration or request.


The native resident decoder-copy adapter borrows the supported storage
representation through the neutral quiescent inspector. Static control-policy
gates are shared with ordinary control support, while its legacy logical
estimator is not invoked for this cold plan. The initial closed implementation
uses resident KV slots and returns explicit unknown bounds for incomplete native
representations. It retains actual shared input identity without reconstruction.

The joint native worker uses an independent live-payload or saved-decoder owner,
one destination session lease and the existing SessionOperation recovery engine.
Complete source-origin pins are separate from the isolated-copy operand trace.
Source and partial-array owners stay in recovery; only completed destination
arrays are published. Final frozen decoder slots contain no request, receipt or
inference-retention grant. Their destruction uses ordinary retirement before
releasing host custody. Descriptor/handle collectors remain the established
bookkeeping exclusion; their referenced buffers and semantic payloads do not.


The sampler resume prerequisite keeps cold sampling inspection in `eredu-runtime`.
Its source-bound projection borrows exact policy and advances only history length,
capacity and adaptive scalar state; it does not clone populated token history.
The numerical sampler and projection share filter ordering and adaptive updates.
A separate closed resume plan derives future host growth from actual saved
capacity. Only a fresh admitted sampling stage may copy it into new run custody;
source health and the protected host hold are checked under one pool lock.

Fixed-slot preparation can now select a destination element representation while
retaining the actual source borrow and identity. This grants neither nested copy
nor construction authority. MLX's closed resident decoder adapter also binds
actual Pooling layer tables to the existing neutral joint account and native copy
engine. Complete source retention remains distinct from copy operands. No family
policy or equation moves into the backend. Stateless table absence, nested Hybrid
state and an installable decoder for fresh resume still need their own closed
paths; these prerequisites do not authorize a complete resumed inference run.


Stateless Pooling copy now binds the actual absent-table source or saved absence.
Its closed native host/admitted variants retain that same source borrow and reject
a different same-shaped absence. The runtime supplies a sampling-copy join with
mandatory complete-source custody, reusing the existing account and native scope;
no placeholder table or decoder host scope is created. Source roots not copied by
the numerical program remain pinned through settlement or quarantine.

A separate neutral dense initializer prices and constructs one fixed `[D]` buffer
from an actual borrowed source table. Exact completion transfers the same buffer
into an immutable owner; partial errors retain it. The worker is crate-private,
and public preparation grants no allocation or execution. Native resume still
needs the closed fresh-request host hold and an atomic transfer into the actual
table's registered charge before that table can be installed.


Retained native array inventory now separates cold metadata observation from
retention. `RetainedStorage::include_array` uses `try_metadata_snapshot`, checks
identity/capacity and deduplication, and retains a handle only when needed through
`Array::try_clone_for_inspection`. The latter is a closed safe operation in
`safemlx` using its private runtime lock; it exposes no general callback and does
not reuse the release-only submission-retirement API. Neither operation evaluates,
polls, runs housekeeping or reclaims unrelated owners. Ordinary `Array::clone`
keeps its existing locking and failure behavior.

Both fallible operations precede inventory insertion. Runtime contention and
native errors keep their typed source chains; unknown backing stays unknown.
Matching the separate snapshot and retained handle still requires a settled
source without external mutation. These inspection mechanisms do not materialize
lazy model helpers or establish completion, whole-source completeness or future
execution authority.


Fresh dense decoder construction now belongs to the original neutral prompt
preparation stage. Its actual registered or funded source, mandatory complete
source inventory and exact destination account are checked together before the
fixed inline host hold is installed. Partial values, source proof and the
consumed prompt claim remain inside the host owner; a separate native scope
retains the complete source pins and follows ordinary completion/quarantine.

Only exact fill can publish a dense table. Runtime transfers its actual retained
payload from the protected hold into the existing storage registry and attaches
that charge to the real table before exposing it. The remaining temporary hold
then retires. Keys must contain independent identity data, never the table or its
metadata token. Shared and ordinary registry keys keep the same physical namespace
and existing Send-only inventory APIs. Provider key cloning/destruction remains
outside table/account locks; entry comparison precedes the transfer commit.
This owns inline host construction only. Native array work, fresh state binding,
controller/input preparation and resumed execution remain separate composition.


Prepared control-state binding now uses an opaque neutral executable-origin
token. Runtime captures and validates the existing private control identity at a
resolved, unfenced, nontransactional boundary. The identity rotates with parameter
snapshot invalidation. Binding checks it again and validates the selected layout,
then moves already constructed state and its shared prompt owner without copying,
inheriting requests, or performing publication. Existing exchange retains its
agreement and revision rules. Absent realized layouts receive a contract error.

The MLX resident KV copy adapter now uses its existing per-layer copy worker to
fill the admitted dense table. Exact host publication moves that same buffer into
a state with empty inference retention and a fresh branch revision. Native
settlement and final array publication remain in the enclosing recovery scope.
Immutable saved decoder pairs also retain their original payload-free control
origin through duplication. Resume validates pool, exact origin and parameter
epoch before destination work; this provenance check grants no new request.


Loaded MLX module values now have an explicit numerical finalization step before
initial physical publication. It runs under the provider's existing detached
loading recovery and `NativeMemoryOwner`, submits only target/prediction roots
already retained by the selected policies, including dormant prediction prototype
arrays, and waits through the existing exact completion adapter. It does not acquire unloaded units, reconstruct recipes or
make tensor constructors globally eager. Native roots and loading authority stay
in their respective existing recovery owners on failure.

The retained-storage iterator merely moves captured known/unknown array handles;
it does not query, evaluate or upgrade their inventory. Finalization is separate
work, followed by a fresh cold inventory and ordinary per-allocation publication.
Incomplete traversal remains incomplete. Helper aliases retain physical charges
after model retirement, without permanently attaching an unquoted loading owner
to those helpers. Layerwise constructor-owned host vectors still need their own
workspace facts; completing resident loading supplies no such fact.


Core exposes optional `TextResumeBackend` preparation hooks for a fresh run from
an opaque immutable saved source. Admission receives a new core context and the
final owned controller; Prompt constructs provisional payload, and Sampling
constructs sampling state and installs before readiness. Both ordinary and
resumed preparation use one private stage runner and the existing generation
machine. The backend retains source/native recovery and armed installation
custody, settles work before agreements, and binds its final quote to the actual
installed revision. Finish borrows that custody so an unwind cannot retire it
before the core-owned payloads. No concrete backend implements this extension yet.


Native resident KV inspection can project the actual live or immutable saved
source through its existing isolated-copy program. Shared exact-concatenation
validation and neutral layout import remain unchanged. The projected destination
has independent bounded output roots; source backing identities and capacities
remain in a separate temporary inventory. Inspection-only retained clones keep
this route free of native evaluation or housekeeping. It grants no allocation,
publication or inference authority.

Prepared architecture workspace inspection accepts a borrowed populated sampler and a projected random key through `BorrowedTextSamplingWorkspace`. Resident and selected host/disk layerwise inspection run the same equation traversal as configured generation. The traversal derives the actual score shape and complete backing envelope before shared runtime sampling inspection advances scalar history extents and adaptive witnesses for the full future output allowance. The original history, adaptive state and random key remain unchanged; unknown backing and foreign workspace contexts retain their existing rejection or incomplete-report behavior. The older config-based entrypoints continue to construct an empty sampler and fresh metadata seed.

MLX saved numerical provenance now retains the checked absolute decoder frontier separately from the absolute sampling observation ordinal. Authentic capture checks that frontier against the request's retained logical admission, including stateless branches; immutable array/sampler/decoder duplication preserves the same payload-free value. A private immutable quote coordinate maps absolute observation positions to request-local attempts and checks arithmetic endpoints before admission. Neither this metadata nor its read-only getter creates a request or retains a live executable.

The native saved pending-token primitive borrows an authenticated one-element Int32/Uint32 array with completed backing and rechecks its descriptor before quotation or numerical work. A single closed program runs isolated logical copy, reshape to [1,1], and an Int32-only U32 cast; workspace and native execution use the same order. Padded source capacity and aliases stay in the existing projection, while every produced native descriptor remains in the caller's recovery collector. The narrow Metal cast fact uses the pinned AsType/copy implementation, permits a new scalar allocation or same-width input alias, and includes no disjoint numerical host staging. Other cast shapes and dtypes remain unpriced.

This primitive returns only numerical input storage. It does not infer a token value, build semantic identity or host input containers, append accepted history, issue a Decode receipt, or authorize/complete resumed inference. The enclosing saved owner must establish token validity, source custody and fresh admission, and must retain the source and partial outputs until exact native recovery settles. Lazy/unknown backing is rejected without evaluation; metadata inspection failures preserve their typed sources.

Native text quotes now retain opening revision/predecessor evidence in a private single-assignment owner. Ordinary preparation seals immediately; unsealed evidence rejects runnable validation and route activation. A private future installer check reads the exact runtime and requires matching request/session/pools/epoch, settled authority, the expected frontier, empty retained authority and a changed branch revision before sealing once. The closed installer must still prove and exchange the actual admitted copy; the seal is not copied-state provenance. No production unsealed quote constructor or resume route is added. Runtime exposes a read-only semantic `InferenceRetention::is_empty()` check that includes requests, unquoted leases and admission, excluding revision-only identity metadata.


Runtime owns the closed single-token host input constructor used by fresh resume preparation. An authentic prompt completion protects a fixed host hold in the exact fresh funding account before a boxed Text/TokenIds part is allocated. Its map and extents stay empty. Shared read-only input owners retain the same box and hold; the box retires before the hold. Preparation, native entry and host fill validate the original stage and account, including closure and quarantine. The numerical payload has separate native funding and recovery; host construction does not establish native completion.

The MLX final binding adapter accepts only the published dense KV owner, dispatches by the concrete state representation and delegates exact origin/geometry binding to the neutral control mechanism. It moves the same table, fresh retention and supplied saved prompt identity; binding performs no installation or native copy. The marker proves host-table publication, while the enclosing installer remains responsible for authentic source provenance, numerical settlement/publication and readiness failure custody.

Private saved-source diagnostics project the actual immutable saved decoder, key, pending token and populated sampler. They use the shared architecture equation visitor and closed pending-input plan, retaining source pins through inspection. Installed state contributes existing-storage and semantic capability checks, not the numerical branch used for future equations. The report is a conservative full diagnostic; it is not an incremental reservation or a completed resume adapter.


The fixed F32 initialization contract keeps constructor geometry and its actual one-buffer allocation program in `eredu-nn`. Numerical realizations fill the checked buffer and call the existing tensor upload; metadata execution records a distinct operation without evaluating its scalar expression. The expression contract is allocation-free arithmetic with no native work or external effects. DeepSeek V4 retains its frequency and YaRN equations in the architecture crate. The MLX adapter supplies separate host-buffer and native seed/copy facts, with common descriptor validation and no family dispatch. Existing per-unit construction traversal accounts every invocation and conservative completed-span overlap. This contract does not price arbitrary callback resources or authorize a new execution route.


Fresh saved-source native preparation now implements the neutral TextResumeBackend hooks. The facade/core driver still owns preparation agreement, cancellation, prediction, sampling decisions and commitment. Runtime atomically validates the actual saved sampler and native custody plus complete registered source origins before full reservation and capacity handoff. The native adapter retains that immutable pair, exact controller contract, initial target revision and fresh core context; it does not retain a target payload Rc across the checked state exchange.

One original prompt claim constructs copied dense cache state, an isolated random key and the protected one-token input under existing native completion and final-root publication. The complete actual source and partial descriptors stay in recovery on failure. Typed control binding moves the published table and original shared prefix; sampling copies actual history/adaptive state under fresh host custody and moves the completed key without reseeding. The private quote remains unsealed until actual state exchange validates its new opening. An exact-session guard spans installation through shared readiness and fences a failed/unwound target without polling in Drop.


Fresh native resume now dispatches on the actual resident state representation. Ordinary KV tables and Hybrid containers whose every layer holds resident KV attention with an actually empty, zero-payload fixed-role table share the existing KV numerical leaf and architecture equation traversal. No family name selects copying or binding. The Hybrid outer table uses its actual larger slot type; copied empty children receive fresh identities under the established metadata exclusion. Both saved and fresh copies publish those child identities, despite their zero payload, before complete source inventory or runnable state is exposed. Nonempty fixed roles, compressed attention and paging require their further construction mechanisms and remain unfinished.


The compressed native copy plan supplies complete retained source descriptors separately from its logical copy operands. Its copied workspace projection reuses the ordinary native geometry validator and the existing portable compact snapshot equations. Architecture state geometry remains neutral; native stores, logical views and completed allocation identities remain backend facts. Present zero-length compressed arrays preserve their allocated-state representation through import and copying.


The neutral decoder copy mechanism supports one actual outer table with one
ordered child table per outer slot. Native typed providers establish the actual
child-of-parent relationship; runtime checks exact count, table identities and
capacities, source origin health and all checked destination terms. Source and
destination cell types may differ without changing source ownership. An allocated

Grouped immutable copy joins every table with the existing sampler/native program
in one account. Fresh construction consumes one original prompt claim, protects

Child publication attaches its exact charge but yields no prompt completion. Only
complete child publication plus exact outer fill/publication yields the original
finish-only remainder. Existing primitive initializers, table handoff and native

Native grouped Hybrid construction now consumes those exact neutral outer/child plans for KV, key-only, fixed-only, stateless and compressed attention layers. Live tables become immutable funded saved tables; saved tables can be recopied or published into fresh live state. The native representation selects this reusable mechanism without a family branch. Numerical fixed values reuse the existing isolated-copy leaf; compressed attention reuses its compact two-operand projection while retaining all possible source stores. Saved host holds are never invented as registry keys. Dense child charges attach before entering the outer table; the final state has new inference retention and retains its actual shared layout and global layer start.


Resident Pooling saved resume uses the same typed native destination dispatch as
KV and grouped Hybrid. The neutral `DeviceState::from_prepared_layers` moves the
actual published fixed table and shared layout after checking local extent, with
fresh inference retention. The existing Pooling numerical leaf and source mapping
supply isolated copies and future projection; family equations remain in
architectures. Complete retained sources remain separate from logical operands.

A registered isolated-copy program can contribute its sealed incremental term to
saved-source inference admission. NN retains exact imported roots and fixed copy
operations; runtime composes full diagnostics and the reduced reservation with
future equations, then validates saved owners, complete source origins and credited
roots atomically during reservation. Native composition supplies actual decoder/key
operands and keeps pending-token conversion independently fully priced.


The closed F32 observation destination keeps semantic output geometry in core and
host allocation/accounting in runtime. Core borrows an immutable admitted capture
selection, resolves known axes/slices without allocating, and exposes a shared
read-only tensor owner. Runtime alone constructs its exact fixed shape/data
buffers under a fresh private host-only account. No byte declaration, arbitrary
constructor callback, public funding run or native scope crosses that boundary.
Payload fields retire before final custody, including incomplete errors and alias
retirement. The hidden core retention bridge is ownership-only and cannot certify
funding. Explicit copies from read-only DTO access remain caller-owned work.

Standalone observation serialization is unchanged. A borrowed CaptureTensorWire
adapter invokes the existing capture serializer on the same protected payload,
including the capture protocol's nonfinite strings. Neither path implicitly clones
the DTO or data. This foundation changes no native capture ingress, managed capture
gate, controller policy or readiness. Actual source/transform/transfer funding and
complete ordinary/controlled capture admission remain separate unfinished work.


The original Prompt stage can continue without a decoder table. Neutral runtime
checks the exact run/reservation and complete-source registrations atomically,

creates no host table hold, table identity, account or new execution grant. The

The closed tensor-capture host destination can also be constructed inside its original runtime funding account. Exact opaque reservation/account matching and a checked geometry-derived protected host hold precede allocation; the constructor creates no native scope or request stage. Native transformations, source completeness, transfer/completion and original instrumentation permission remain separate provider obligations. Completed read-only host aliases retain their private host custody, while native recovery remains independently owned.


Shared funding quarantine now retains every failed scope source-pin bundle in private linked custody. Each node is allocated before the usage lock; linking moves ownership without provider callbacks or destruction. Certified scopes retain their existing timely pin release. The registry still charges each actual source allocation once.


Saved-source native resume now obtains populated future equations through the retained model's existing resident/layerwise blueprint traversal. One exact LayerwiseWorkspace supplies parameter roots, constructor/transfer materialization and the source identity or direct-read receipt. Following successful shared saved-source admission, ready host stores are pinned and the matching receipt is carried by the ordinary execution quote. Existing model operations activate and retire their direct-disk restriction through native completion resources; the copy-only prompt does not materialize weights. Family equations and replica/unit traversal remain architecture-owned, and no artifacts are reopened. This does not introduce a second scheduling or admission engine.


Retained ready-host inventory uses the native wrapper's nonblocking metadata inspection, preserving allocation identity and capacity without housekeeping or unrelated allocation-owner reclamation. The shared core text machine agrees cancellation at its existing Prediction boundary for both prefill and decode. Prior completions and exact session admission are checked first, so cancellation does not conceal a failure. Locally cancelled lanes create no new prediction permit or controller decision; a ready peer releases its unused permit after agreed cancellation and retains its spent attempt ordinal.


The native capture prerequisite now has one closed F32 Metal selection program. It borrows the actual settled source, checks the original admitted source axes, and uses the same ordered static-slice/optional-reshape/prefix program for workspace tracing and execution. The safe wrapper `Array::try_slice` exposes the existing static Slice operation with checked positive-range geometry; it adds no unsafe boundary. Direct evaluated F32 iteration fills the neutral protected host destination without an intermediate numerical Vec. Descriptor/shape/index bookkeeping remains in the existing exclusion, while observation shape/data and explicit construction moves remain priced.

A source-bound host transfer builder borrows its exact native funding scope, so a sibling sharing the account cannot substitute for it. Original run/reservation, active scope, complete provided source origins and host P are checked in one locked commit; pins are staged and destroyed outside locks. Constructor rejection or unwind before success restores prior scope pins. After native entry, source/intermediate recovery and all new pins remain with that scope through explicit settlement or quarantine. Host finish neither certifies native work nor publishes capture support. Original invocation/capture quota integration remains unfinished; the F16/BF16 extension is described below. All production managed instrumentation gates stay unchanged.


Core capture now has a shared tensor payload representation and a read-only SharedCapturedStep delivery owner. Both retain existing custody without issuing allocation, provenance, quota or native-completion authority. Runtime still owns the required closed frame construction/admission and one-step delivery policy; backend/facade return types and managed capture gates are unchanged by this prerequisite.


The closed native capture prerequisite now distinguishes actual F32, F16 and BF16 descriptors. Its shared metadata/native sequence performs static selection, optional Preview flatten/prefix, then an explicit native F32 cast for nonempty half output. Neutral workspace metadata still conservatively represents these types as Float32, so a separate `capture_cast_f32` operation preserves the actual allocation in the trace. The exact native signed-stride view-flag repair is a selected-mechanism prerequisite; a byte upper bound alone cannot make an incorrectly offset native output safe. F32 keeps its earlier direct read. Empty half output skips cast and F32 iteration after selection settlement; identity Slice is not assumed to normalize a preexisting empty descriptor. No new unsafe exception or family policy enters the backend.


Runtime now has a closed raw-tensor frame constructor derived from the actual immutable AdmittedCapturePlan and invocation coordinate. It protects exact record/string/shape/diagnostic capacities and explicit moves in the existing original parent account; tensor/frame holds share private arithmetic, and neither can certify native work. Shared delivery retains the whole frame and custody. Source-plan ownership, original cumulative capture quoting and backend invocation/provenance binding remain separate integration obligations.


Ordinary capture admission can now retain neutral CaptureTextOrigin cached-position metadata independently from new prompt length. Core owns checked context resolution and origin-bound immutable identity; runtime consumes that retained geometry for observation, preflight and child readmission. The origin does not prove actual native cache state or issue execution/funding authority. Native/facade binding to the actual opening remains a separate integration step.


Core SharedCapturePlan owns one immutable admitted plan and reuses the existing narrow shared-storage custody mechanism. It reports complete retained nested buffer capacities, including spare storage, without source registration or execution authority. Runtime/backend composition remains responsible for attaching the actual source charge before relying on a finite quote; no raw readmission clone inherits that source custody.


The MLX capture selection worker also exposes a crate-private metadata program derived from an admitted tensor geometry. It traces Full/Slice/Preview in the caller's existing workspace context, preserving imported source identity, full backing aliases and prior span allocations. Because Float32 workspace metadata represents actual F32/F16/BF16 sources, future nonempty selections conservatively include the explicit native-to-F32 conversion bound; the actual worker still chooses conversion from inspected native dtype, and empty outputs skip it. This uses the same closed operation sequence and creates no source allocation, reservation or execution authority. Tensor destination host custody remains a separate contribution. This component does not enable managed text capture or price capture frames, cumulative delivery, architecture observer metadata, or prefill/distributed readout.


Core capture revalidation borrows the existing opaque admission and compares its selected observation declarations exactly. Initial admission and borrowed revalidation share current schema, transform, phase-support and histogram-limit checks. Runtime preflight and checkpoint validation use that retained proof directly; semantic re-admission remains explicit when declarations change. Revalidation does not bind artifact/session identity or supply execution authority. Successful revalidation constructs no replacement plan or digest; backend estimates, record preparation and actual checkpoint copies retain their separate accounting obligations.

Core owns additive TextPreparationOptions and threads the exact SharedCapturePlan through the existing ordinary/controlled/detached preparation runner before original admission. Supporting backends quote that source and schedule in the original account, then install against the unchanged preparation/core context before one Instrumentation readiness vote. Default backends reject every supplied shared plan, including an empty plan; no source footprint, native capability, or new allocation authority follows from the options type.

Native retained storage can explicitly inventory an actual immutable SharedCapturePlan. Its checked nested retained capacity and payload-free physical identity produce a distinct CapturePlan registration; equal semantic plans remain independent allocations. Existing unquoted registration or exact funded-scope adoption attaches one per-source charge per domain through the core owner, including aliases made before publication. Successful publication drops its own plan aliases, and the source payload retires before its charge. This supplies source custody only; constructor peaks, capture-run/frame admission and original execution-quote integration remain separate.

The runtime capture host schedule now has a closed cumulative destination plan borrowing the core `SharedCapturePlan`. It derives finite ordinary frame/tensor geometries and fixed claim/control storage, protects the complete H in the original funding account before construction, and issues move-only coordinate claims to the existing fixed workers without a second hold. Completed aliases share the host-only custody. Exact native-scope transfer retains the existing exclusive scope borrow and full source pins; construction rollback restores prior pins outside Usage, while entered-work errors retain the larger bundle for settlement/quarantine. No native or family policy moved into portable code. Shared-plan source registration, actual native provenance/operation funding, original preparation installation and managed delivery remain separate obligations; capture gates are unchanged.


The closed MLX FundedWork capture worker joins a scheduled host claim to its existing exclusive native scope. It validates lazy source metadata, retains the graph before settlement, publishes actual backing in that scope, and calls the shared native selected-copy worker. Source-only publication leaves unrelated roots and completion state intact. Runtime supplies an owned terminal scheduled-tensor error that retires partial destinations and borrows but retains original host custody; source pins stay on the original native scope. Enclosing text authority, observer-aware quotation and capture policy remain separate prerequisites.

The native settled-source capture leaf can consume an existing scheduled tensor claim under the exact original native funding scope. It authenticates the actual admitted object and coordinate, pins the complete actual source backing, and reuses the same selection/evaluation/F32 iteration worker as the existing parent transfer. Scheduled construction shares cumulative host custody without a second hold. Metadata-only source-axis/dtype validation may precede lazy-source settlement, but grants no evaluation, publication or capture permission; this leaf does not itself ingest lazy architecture activations.

Portable CaptureSession and partition receipts/work now have an additive shared-source route retaining the actual core SharedCapturePlan. A private legacy/shared owner dispatch supplies the same borrowed admission to existing ledger and partition mechanisms; no raw plan copy, source registration or native authority is inferred from shared construction. Legacy raw Arc receipt APIs and dense/sum/routed behavior remain available. Source and nested receipt aliases retire before the existing final host-preparation authority. Checkpoints still copy their destination admission and separately retain an optional original source alias; source registration does not fund that copied payload. Fork creates an independently re-admitted child source. This ownership change does not move family/native policy or open managed capture.

Runtime now provides immutable shared layered observation-path sources, distinct runtime-local prepared bindings, and ordinary resident/layerwise borrowed traversal hooks. Sources contain actual fixed boxed entries and String capacities and use existing metadata custody/publication; they must be constructed and registered under loading/preparation authority before finite requests. Cold semantic rebinding validates the actual architecture declarations while sharing the same physical path payload. Mutable architecture exposure invalidates only the local binding. Prepared hooks reuse ordinary observed equations and allocate no boundary path tables/strings/shared-observer wrapper; observer/native/internal-hook workspace and source-construction temporaries remain separate obligations. This prerequisite does not yet enable managed Tensor capture or observer-aware architecture quote entrypoints.


Capture delivery now separates fallible precommit preparation from allocation-free outcome publication. A private owned aggregate retains record payload and sidecars before original host custody; an aborted frame can detach during unwind without allocating or keeping a plan/claim-row borrow. Later fallible delivery publishes only Aborted and preserves its typed cause and owner on failure. Completion remains the enclosing driver's responsibility. Ordinary observer-aware blueprint quotation cold-binds the actual shared path source, traces through the original workspace context, observes complete model.logits once, and applies the real final-row sampling index. Native ordinary replicated/composite sessions retain and publish this exact source through existing loading and idle inventory ownership. Partition path binding and selected generated-projection observation mechanisms remain unfinished.


Prepared observation is selected through a default-false neutral observer requirement propagated by transparent adapters. The existing input agreement validates the original private binding before observer preparation or mutable model state; direct resident/layerwise execution uses the existing transaction driver and borrowed hook. Explicit cold rebinding retains original path-source identity. Runtime's closed FundedCaptureSession owns the original CaptureSession ledger, one delivery slot and the unused cumulative claim bank, with a lexical observer borrowing those owners. Core's additive CapturedStepDelivery transfers either legacy records or the actual retained SharedCapturedStep. Native source provenance, completion and original-operation funding remain backend obligations; these contracts alone enable no managed capture gate.


Ordinary projection-input observation now uses a neutral checked block-FP8 reconstruction program shared by native execution and WorkspaceLinear. Selected metadata facts distinguish borrowed identity inputs from deferred GPU effective-input diagnostics. Observed FP8 prepare/finish phases expose the actual compact quantized roots and partition the existing whole-projection bound; the selected factory traces scale repetition, F32 decode, trim, multiply and shape restore in the same context. Native CPU callback semantics are preserved without claiming Metal allocation facts on CPU. The original work scope retains completion/source custody; the program grants no account or capture authority.


The native scheduled capture adapter implements the neutral runtime mechanism
using an actual borrowed MLX array and the already installed original FundedWork.
A private SessionOperation helper lends the existing executable to the lexical
funded observer; it opens no second submission/scope. Borrowed shape/dtype checks
and shared raw-count quota estimation allocate no shape/data payload. Native
snapshotting, source publication, transfers and completion remain in the existing
backend ingress. Runtime exposes only a readonly bank/account/native-scope health
check, not native types, semantic admission, source completeness or byte authority.

Generated projection observation has an additive backend-neutral retained-factory contract: private native and workspace producers borrow the same checked operator plan, visit actual compact inputs and report every generated output before subsequent work. NN/runtime/architecture forwarding preserves that contract and original typed failures. The contract grants no funding or completion; concrete backends retain roots in their existing operation owner and the observing quote must describe their actual lifetime. The actual managed NeutralActivationObserver forwards retained factories losslessly across MlxTensor/Array, and internal native retention propagation uses fixed typed signals while preserving the original error. Retained outgoing native error conversions use private fixed-Display wrappers with the original typed cause in source(), avoiding an extra copy of arbitrary diagnostic text.

Cold capture diagnostics and real funded collection share a neutral borrowed prediction policy for metadata quota, phase-aware readout, path/duplicate status and logical Skip/Fail decisions. The policy has no frame, epoch, funding or execution authority. The native diagnostic observer applies the fixed selected tensor program to actual architecture WorkspaceTensor hooks in their original context, preserving complete source backing and conservatively pricing F32 conversion under erased floating precision. Existing observed resident and layerwise blueprint traversal remains the owner of equations and parameter replicas.

The additive model diagnostic returns the cumulative closed capture host plan separately from numerical equations. Original capture/path source registration, accepted candidate identity, H composition once, physical admission, real prepared binding and collector installation remain required before enabling managed capture. A borrowed paths owner is source inventory, not proof that a live runtime binding is current.

Runtime incremental quotes can carry additional registered source accounting without changing full diagnostics, incremental bytes or controller decisions. The closed source bundle validates every pool and origin both when attached and atomically at the original reservation commit before capacity handoffs. Accounting pins follow the existing run, scopes and quarantine; native source identity, safe access and numerical lifetime remain backend obligations.


Original captured text admission now has a private closed composition over the actual immutable plan, selected architecture catalog and prepared observation-path token. Core revalidates borrowed semantic facts; runtime validates the actual prepared traversal and registered funding origins; MLX forwards those checks and composes the existing observed equation report. New shared source capacity C and cumulative capture host bank H join the original request once, before prompt or sampling preparation. Existing sources remain charged in their original registrations. The bank and source publication use the original controller-adoption scope, without a second native admission. After publication, the accepted numerical quote retires into a move-only accounting witness that is checked again before consuming the pending bank. This witness does not retrofit sources into an earlier run or certify native completion.

The retained generated observer uses the actual fixed BlockFp8 reconstruction program through the shared producer protocol. Runtime owns logical creation quota, one-use coordinate claims and once-per-hook construction. MLX validates and retains compact inputs and every generated intermediate in the original native work before later fallible operations. Cold equations retain the same roots through the complete span. The original quote/witness identities and registration-handle aggregates remain within the established binding/accounting bookkeeping exclusion; actual capture source and host destination payloads are separately charged. The core-options installation, execution and completion-aware delivery are connected below; complete public facade host custody remains unfinished.


Original captured text requests now connect the core options driver to the same MLX submission and sampling paths used by ordinary generation. Runtime validates the actual initial core context and exact live funding reservation without issuing a step or changing readiness. The backend installs the original pending bank and its registered-source witness together, then checks the actual plan, prepared traversal, source health and local prediction before every operation. Native equations execute inside the existing permitted FundedWork; core establishes completion before the retained shared drain. No family logic or tokenizer policy moves into the backend. Captured sampler/state copies currently reject with typed UnknownBound because the destination representation does not yet preserve the original capture claim/ledger state.


Scheduled prefill now announces each actual semantic chunk through neutral observer callbacks before preparing its input under the existing reservation. Callback failures enter the existing all-rank input agreement. An inline runtime guard keeps whole-prediction host evidence provisional through every chunk state commit, cancellation checks, final score indexing and reservation settlement. Its terminal notification grants neither native completion nor delivery authority; early return and unwind abort the evidence without reversing already committed chunk state. Native adapters only forward these borrowed lifecycle calls.

The funded observer retains one logical p0 epoch and a separate current native chunk epoch. It validates each contiguous prompt-relative span against the admitted source geometry, keeps metadata/quota claims cumulative, and permits hooks only inside the current prepared chunk. Final chunk sealing remains provisional until the neutral outer prefill guard succeeds. Scalar progress is included in the existing closed observer control quotation; it introduces no per-chunk frame, host allocation or funding authority. Selected whole-prompt tensor capture still requires a separate attribution implementation.


Core ordinary and detached text machines expose a closed controller termination query that delegates the existing TokenFilterController::is_complete contract without exposing mutable controller policy or revising the bound policy identity. Runtime managed continuations and both facade committed-token sources reuse it. Existing internal query/cache mutation and typed errors are preserved; querying issues no step and establishes no native completion.


Ordinary native retirement inspects every record present when it acquires the registry lock, detaches only positively settled records belonging to the current original owner thread, and destroys them after releasing the lock. This complete traversal avoids starvation when bounded completion progress rotates the same registry. Completion polling remains capped at 64 records and never destroys arbitrary resources. The ordinary pass is O(N) host work and its resource destructors may block; it supplies no new completion proof or permission to reclaim a foreign or unresolved owner.


### Facade capture delivery ownership

Ordinary and controlled facade generation drain through the existing exact-completion core delivery path. `ManagedTextContinuation::take_completed_delivery` forwards that path without allocating, granting authority or clearing failure. Internal token callbacks move `CapturedStepDelivery` and a shared event constructor preserves legacy/raw versus shared ownership.

`ObservedGenerationEvent::SharedToken` and `SharedCaptureFailure` own only a `SharedCapturedStep` alias. Their borrowed accessors do not extract a raw frame; their serializer delegates to the existing shared-frame/capture serializer. The wire tags and field layout match `Token` and `CaptureFailure`, including nonfinite tensor spelling. Deserialization creates only legacy variants and confers no custody. Explicit event/record clones share the captured frame while copying ordinary facade fields; those copies remain caller-owned work. Public exhaustive event matches must include the additive variants; ownership-independent readers can use `captures()`.

A ready terminal frame is delivered even when no token was committed. Error paths always attempt completion/drain, including empty plans, but return the original typed execution error if that drain also fails. A failed drain keeps its pending owner; successful delivery moves the original retained frame into the callback record.

This carrier is separate from finite facade admission. It does not fund provenance Strings, decoder buffers, semantic journals, envelopes or escaped output. Source preparation and existing late instrumentation gates remain unchanged. A closed original-account facade host program still must price construction, actual capacities, changed inline layouts and cumulative escaping envelopes before an options-based managed facade route can be enabled.


Core capture now exposes a closed borrowed prefill row mapper derived from the actual ordinary admitted selection and fixed inference geometry. A single declared Sequence axis with Known/Batch peers supplies placement only; it does not establish causal/full-forward assembly equivalence or executable capture support. The mapper preserves original source identity and checked cached origin, derives physical chunk coordinates and global slice/Preview destination indices without allocating per-chunk metadata, and exports no mutable payload or authority. Runtime remains responsible for ordered one-use claims, original host custody, quota and completion; native mechanisms remain responsible for actual source geometry and fragment execution. No dependency direction or managed capture gate changes.


The portable capture funding foundation separates temporary scheduled source pins from a work scope's permanent borrowed inventory. Only a scheduled claim creates the move-only association with the exact scope and schedule. Both channels keep actual registered origins and join the same quarantine on uncertified scope destruction; constructor rollback affects only its selected channel. Registration/binding bookkeeping retains its existing exclusion, while the closed H plan includes actual new inline controls and moves. No native callback, execution grant or completion certificate is added. Native per-chunk retirement still needs the existing successful chunk boundary, exact scope association and independently owned capture roots.

The neutral capture bank can construct persistent p0 host targets from an immutable admitted row-assembly plan. One initialized F32 destination per selected logical target survives chunk boundaries; a separate one-use coverage program scatters sequential scalar input using only geometry-derived indices. Exact slot/owner/writer/mapping controls and moves are included in original H, while numerical target P is counted once. Aborted frames retain partial targets with original custody. This host constructor grants no native source read, completion, source registration or execution permission; actual native fragment conversion and exact-scope temporary pins remain separate backend mechanisms.

The geometry-only prefill fragment now exposes checked read-only local axis slices from its actual admitted row mapping. The MLX adapter consumes those derived axes in a new constructor for the existing shared static Slice/optional flatten-prefix/F32 selection runner. Intersection, global Preview and destination placement remain core geometry; no family-specific math, new worker ownership or funding authority moves into the backend. The fragment constructor preserves native signed-index limits and erased-precision conversion bounds. Actual source binding, short host writers and canonical native source-segment retirement remain separate integration obligations.

The neutral short prefill transfer mechanism consumes only an actual scheduled fragment claim, joins its registered source to the exact original scope/segment, and reuses the existing single host destination. Its constructor stays private to working_memory until a canonical chunk-stamped wrapper is available. Read-only geometry and opaque fill APIs introduce no backend dependency, arbitrary writer conversion, allocation callback or native permission. The MLX wrapper exposes one purpose-built completed-record retirement attempt. `try_retire_completed_submissions` reports `CompleteSnapshot` or `Busy` using the existing native runtime lock without housekeeping. The checked-in native patch retains the full entry-time traversal, positive settled/current-owner filter, and record destruction outside the registry mutex; ordinary void callers remain compatible. Native errors remain `Exception` values. The additive FFI unsafe code stays inside the existing safemlx/safemlx-sys boundary. This method supplies no completion, callback, funding, or backend execution authority.

The neutral prefill scheduler can bind an actual scheduled capture bank to its original request, chunk and upcoming epoch before input preparation. A move-only registration becomes a one-use success ticket only after the exact model commit and existing guarded completion checks. Source-slot and fragment checks are read-only; native carrier/record retirement remains backend-owned, and no source pin release or numerical authority follows from a host frame commit. Legacy typed architecture input failures and new internal retention failures enter the same shared runner. Failed creation of a completion-agreement guard still lacks a retained distributed-failure handoff; this stage preserves the existing fence/return rather than issuing an unprotected vote.

PrefillExecutor has an additive shared-token cancellation callback whose default delegates to the existing boolean contract. SessionPrefill samples that token only after its guarded retirement callback and reservation readiness, immediately before the existing cancellation collective. Both entrypoints share one agreement body; no additional vote, scope or authority is created.

The native prefill fragment leaf now borrows the actual physical chunk and core-derived selection, retaining the full backing identity through the existing workspace projection. It uses the same native selection, settlement and direct F32 iteration worker as whole-value and scheduled capture. A narrow neutral constructor validates the canonical chunk stamp before joining source custody and borrowing the existing target; it grants no native allowance, source release or completion. The native submission registry uses constant-initialized atomic publication so first scope construction does not wait on a C++ static-initialization guard. Publication performs one load and at most one compare-exchange; losing candidates are destroyed outside locks, and the winner is never destroyed. Compile-time lock-free assertions cover the publication and scope counter atomics. This is backend-specific lifecycle bookkeeping, with no new unsafe boundary, native operation, completion guarantee or portable dependency.

safemlx exposes an additive `SubmissionScope::try_begin` with typed Busy versus the existing native-constructor Exception. It uses recovery-safe runtime try-entry and a shared private constructor requiring the real runtime guard; it performs no housekeeping, reclaim, poll, retry or new work. Its native registry prerequisite removes guarded singleton initialization. The existing crate-local FFI safety boundary remains initialized output plus owned thread-affine native scope. Backends can use private `Recovery::try_begin` to recover their exact supplied owner on failure; portable strata gain no native dependency.

The runtime exposes a ticket-gated opaque source parcel for one canonically completed scheduled capture channel. It validates exact stamp, scope, scheduled custody and complete source health atomically and transfers ownership without issuing native completion or byte credit. The MLX original FundedWork separately retains the channel's arrays/publications, requires its successful synchronous capture state and an observable completed-record retirement pass, then retires payload before pins and stamp custody outside its locks/loans. Busy or failure keeps the original recovery owner. Final publication inventories an active carrier and cannot certify through it. The carrier is not an allocation sidecar. Architecture p0 causal/readout semantics and shared fragment progression remain separate prerequisites; no backend path/family interpretation is introduced.

Runtime owns the shared p0 logical-row progression state and its private coupling to existing fixed host targets. State retains the actual immutable SharedCapturePlan by an allocation-free shared handle, so identity does not depend on address reuse or equivalent strings. The helper delegates quota to the existing CaptureLedger and checked full generated-source program; it grants no native work, fragment source release or completion. The original host plan measures actual target-slot and temporary helper controls. A future architecture-produced causal/readout companion must authorize construction before native or cold observers activate this mechanism; no backend path classification or family branch is introduced.

The native distributed GroupImpl now owns an atomic terminal submission fence shared by cached wrappers and split descendants through a direct immutable root link. Root binding occurs before a split result is published, including when marking races with native setup. Safemlx exposes an allocation-free typed preflight and no-work mark/query within its existing FFI safety boundary; backend setup uses the preflight before constructing status arrays. Existing accepted primitives and recovery records remain owned and executable under their original completion rules. This native foundation does not activate the portable guard-creation terminal protocol or add model-family policy.

Architecture-issued prefill row/readout declarations are retained inside the existing immutable shared path owner. Runtime compiles and validates that actual source; architecture discovery binds selected catalog semantics. The native adapter forwards the resulting bound companion and cannot classify hook roles from strings or infer causality from shape. No serialized discovery field/version is changed. ### Native descriptor retirement without an allocating traversal

MLX array descriptors now use closed out-of-line factories and a single
out-of-line intrusive drain. Its registry contains automatic frames identified
by the current native thread; it uses no C++ TLS, dynamic registry container or
new thread-readiness protocol. Only pointer/identity operations run under its
atomic flag. Destruction remains on the releasing thread, with the outer drain
retiring its queued nodes before returning. The spinlock is not a latency,
fairness or wait-free guarantee; signal-handler release and nonlocal escape
from an active frame remain unsupported.

Each descriptor has Expand/Finalize state. Expand retains the parent's complete
remaining fields while it clears known input/sibling edges and drains their
final releases. Finalize then deletes that parent. This preserves deferred
allocation authority across those known descendants, including against a
concurrent ordinary Rust reclaimer. Primitive-held or independently retained
graphs remain separate lifetime obligations; a callback releasing another graph
does not retroactively retain an already-released parent authority.

Array replacement runs the existing sibling cycle breaker through a rooted
temporary, and failed partial sibling publication rolls back while all outputs
remain rooted. Incoming identity, aliases and move exception guarantees remain
unchanged. Record/Scope, Data and host-transfer backing-first retirement are
unchanged. A queued descriptor can outlive its shared_ptr control block; its
intrusive fields live in the object, never in that expired control block.

The factories introduce separate descriptor and shared-control allocations;
the descriptor also contains the actual link/phase layout. This is a retirement
mechanism, not a graph-storage bound. Any later original graph admission must
price both complete allocations, allocator rounding, remaining payloads and
independent custody through each deallocation. Native Record capacity does not
implicitly pay for descriptors or arbitrary primitive/callback storage.

or full-row evidence from opportunistic tracing. An observer's

The MLX materialization adapter uses this neutral byte pin while validating its

Borrowed public materialize still performs its required caller-owned lease clone.
Original prepared recovery, cancellation and failure retain the same final lease;
no new source or submission authority is granted by the pin.

TensorView shape buffers, GGUF key/name and group-cache owners, source acquisition
request/cache allocations, uninstalled prepared read/conversion destinations,
recipe intermediates, native controls and complete stack/allocator charges remain
separate. ResidencyPopulation's complete payload fit stays unknown until those
actual mechanisms are supplied. The pin's inline layout is a component description,
not an owning-source or full-request bound.

The original neural submission bank prepares each final C array wrapper alongside

This closes the known outer clone-handle allocation in the selected neural

Cold neural clone-preparation failures retain the actual native exception in a

The source-owned report distinguishes the slot array's requested layout and actual

Composite construction keeps the selected direct and routed handoffs in separate

Prepared source-acquisition errors retain their large neutral failure behind a

The shared MLX evaluator derives its complete distinct stream population from

The selected root Event still exists before graph traversal. Other Event and

No neutral admission, public C handle layout, or safe-wrapper authority changes.

This preflight is derived from an actual submitted graph and is not a cold memory
quote. Native producer fit remains pending: graph/tape traversal populations,

Original GGUF converted-group misses now compose the neutral G1 raw, G2

### Speculative prefill intervention evidence and completion inspection

The bounded speculative collector reports span compatibility from the actual

Native conformance waits for the exact existing recovery-held session payload to

### Initial storage publication under runtime contention

Fresh-session publication is an optional conversion of the existing loading

The deterministic native fixture holds the real runtime lock on another thread,

### Explicit captured GGUF inspection

`eredu_core::inspect_artifact_with_prepared_gguf_headers` and the matching

Capture rejects changed headers on later cold reads. It does not freeze payloads,

### Prepared owned-host copy sources

The optional native owned-host copy mechanism is generic over the ordinary

It allocates no tensor backing during this cold preparation. Its native layout

Activation consumes the actual initialized `Vec<T>` without making a `Box<Vec<T>>`

The source arena retains a `Send` caller custody value with no Array, Scope,

Native final release frees arena storage before enqueueing the existing Rust

An owning refusal drops the actual Vec, then its native slot, then the arena
owner. No thread-affine observer is placed in a shared Array or source cache.

This mechanism supplies storage and copy facts, not an accepting producer-fit
or admission result. The eventual backend caller must bind the actual source,
selected copy strategy, request/role authority, source leases, current Vec

Path-based model loading retains GGUF headers from its first inspection. The

contract; generic metadata-only inspection is unchanged. Source storage facts
include each retained header payload once and each materializer's independent
parser scratch. Tensor payloads remain lazy, and this source choice does not

Original GGUF converted-group misses use the same portable G1/G2/G3 converter

The selected session projects that same witness into both original control facts
and request installation; neither portable inspection nor a materialization miss

Each existing pending ticket owns one empty source Arc and one prepared recovery
node. It contains no future tensor payload. After G1/G3 restores its original

lease alias, public failure and native source custodian retains an independent

The shared converter retains its output-name, shape and dtype checks and exact
weight/scales/biases ordering. Each actual typed Vec is consumed by an explicit

copy, rather than ordinary managed-pointer import.

A failed typed Vec, preparation arena or native slot stays in the existing pending

No polling error proves completion, and no new retry or global cache is introduced.

Known controls include the actual empty Arc, runtime witness, pending failure

bound payload size or overlapping cache consumers. Current-miss metadata

A future accepted quote must reserve the exact source layout before construction;

### Ordinary loading inventories and original refusal

A freshly loaded MLX executable now takes one explicit ordinary runtime owner

Aggregate controls, copied metadata, bounded payload destinations and wire storage

This closes the split evidence/routing mechanism previously gated by the Busy
compatibility correction. It is independent of remaining original native,

The original GGUF host-copy adapter retains ordinary cold runtime-preparation

For an attempted immutable host copy, `OwnedHostCopyError::take_native_source`

The neutral GGUF `ConversionPlan` describes the existing converter's ordered

and reservation arithmetic with the actual prepared worker; it does not claim

Checkpoint-owned `GgufConversionPlan` and `SelectedGgufConversionPlan` bind those

Exact source identity remains distinct from coincidentally equal descriptor
bytes and physical names. Unavailable or non-GGUF routes do not imply a zero fit.

These cold facts provide inputs for the original GGUF host-copy consumer; they

Ordinary MLX prefill callers now coordinate constructor access through the shared
