Installed original Model/Prefill roles retain their exact nonblocking attempt,

### Metal receipt and callback allocation custody

Original Metal dispatch validates the entered Record and its exact prepared GPU
receipt before constructing callback controls. Receipt headers, concrete handler
nodes, wait/signal entries, counted-task controls and callback-owned buffer/fence
snapshots use the existing Graph allocator. The original evaluator reserves
snapshot destinations before dispatch but retains input Data only after the
primitive's donation decision. A physical command buffer may contain ordinary
work and several original roles: each allocation retains its own immutable
quota/carrier owner, rather than rebinding a cached encoder to the latest role.
An original commit leaves no empty future Graph-owned receipt in the encoder;
later work prepares its own header. Ordinary successor preparation remains eager.

Metal's direct block overload captures only the encoder and receipt pointers.
The managed receipt owns the callback's explicit self-reference and all variable

still own that header until commit returns; its quota remains charged through
actual final deallocation. Ambiguous registration/commit or a callback that
never arrives retains the real receipt and encoder; a polling failure does not
release them. The callback and commit exception paths share one atomic counted
task token and can decrement the existing scheduler only once.

An enforced managed-memory cap differs from successful-workspace feasibility.
The physically prepaid Graph and Record arenas cannot grow or fall back when an
allocation does not fit. Once every relevant allocation and refusal/retirement
transport is closed, those finite arenas can prove their managed cap without an
exact cold reconstruction of every reachable DAG or its minimum successful peak.
Their full allocation/header costs, population and custody still enter admission;
fragmentation may cause earlier typed refusal. A selected capacity is not thereby
a Complete estimate of required successful workspace. Required external/native
workspace that is unknown still rejects before work, and feasibility reports
must not present a chosen arena size as a proven successful requirement.

This receipt unit does not close persistent encoder resource maps/sets, fast
Fence buffers, caches, ordinary exception production or all other managed
outside-arena resources. Their variable counts, capacities and retained ownership
remain explicit pending obligations. Opaque OS/driver implementation bytes behind
Metal objects and the runtime block are outside the documented managed guarantee;
our fixed block captures, receipt/header controls, containers, buffer capacities,
resource populations and callback payloads are not hidden by that exclusion.
No native-fit acceptance or backend activation changes accompany this unit.

The two native `array::set_data` Data/shared-control constructions use the actual
entered Graph domain, including an active Record's retained birth domain after

required but incomplete original role refuses before choosing control storage;
ordinary calls without a Graph keep their existing `make_shared` construction.
Existing ordinary graph-only scopes continue to use that same Graph domain.
The shared control keeps its immutable allocator through Data destruction and
final weak-reference deallocation; neither later scopes nor shared aliases
rebind it. No extra Data or Array references precede donation decisions.

This closes these two Data object/shared-header allocations in the Graph arena,
not the native buffer allocator or a whole-request fit. Actual control layout is
the supported standard library's `allocate_shared<Data, GraphAllocator<Data>>`

The existing by-value `std::function` Deleter entry, its Data constructor-parameter
and member copies, arbitrary deleter captures/destructors, deferred allocation
owner storage, and thrown-exception allocation remain separate obligations.
Their current error and copy order is preserved; the incoming-buffer guard frees
once if a body-level construction/copy failure occurs. A by-value argument

The original converted-group miss consumes the neutral, source-owned

The shared worker keeps ordinary conversion as its default. Its original
producer reserves a separate final typed Vec only when the corresponding dense
or affine cast is reached, then writes without growth and moves that same Vec

Weight creation still precedes affine scale and bias transformations. Existing
name, shape and dense-width checks retain their order; a stored source-plan

transform refusals retain the actual encoded/bits input and any allocated

Box. The compact public error retains the actual typed cause and independent

Requested layout and actual returned Vec capacity are distinct facts.
`try_reserve_exact` and a no-growth write loop do not bound allocator charge
before work. The current miss still constructs plan/name/shape metadata and its

Persistent runtime/platform owners and original native Graph/Record fit also

### Persistent Metal encoder resource ownership

The shared Metal encoder's resource membership, prior-output and waiting-fence
indexes use fixed intrusive headers and separately owned entries. Each original
entry is allocated through its actual Graph quota and retains that same quota
through payload destruction and physical storage return. Replacing an old
request's fence never changes the old entry's allocation owner. Membership stores
buffer identity and flags only; it adds no Array/Data references before donation.
Barrier and concurrent-output transitions require no allocation.

Before `end_encoding` mutates resource membership or encodes fence waits/updates,

and callback-detached nodes are released outside the output mutex. A callback
removes a prior output only when both its pointer and shared control still match

and that partial state becomes sticky rather than retried.

Temporary registration remains after the primitive's dispatch/donation point.
It stores an inline Array or adopts the actual incoming vector allocation with
its original allocator; duplicates and row order remain intact. A batch and its
vector can retain different admitted requests. A failed batch allocation leaves

and unclaimed names. A fixed checkpoint-owning compiler consumes retained
resolution and mapping, then moves that same catalog into the existing source
builder. Runtime can precharge its qualified node, clone, scratch, shared-owner
and failure requests through the existing cold source account. The catalog's
private origin is recognized only in its original pool; arbitrary generic
custody and ordinary catalogs do not establish admission.

The private handle exports no Arc or Weak. Its concrete final retirement frees
the shared block, indices and nested storage before releasing the original
account. StoreInner drops readers and materializers before its catalog, preserving
that order even if the consuming reader construction reuses the compiler's input
Vec backing. Leases retain the actual source/catalog; a stale source identity
retains only the separately unclosed StoreInner shell. G4's copied entries keep
their independent request accounting.

The explicit architecture catalog-pool entry follows the same cold primary and
companion driver and consumes its retained resolution. This closes catalog birth
and alias ownership only. The open recipe cache, checkpoint/header baseline,
reader and StoreInner/PAL construction, source wrappers, architecture graph and

and model-fit admission remains unresolved.


### Shared process Scheduler initialization

The original host materializer now constructs the shared Device (where required),
process Scheduler, and input allocator in that order, each through the same
managed pool's existing shared-native source comparison. The Scheduler contribution
contains its actual empty object, safe custody node and named native/C/Rust
constructor controls. Its native winner retains that source account permanently,
matching the existing process-lived Scheduler. Ordinary callers borrow this same
winner; an existing ordinary singleton cannot acquire admitted provenance. A
successful predecessor stays owned if a later initializer fails.

The Scheduler's dynamic constructor qualification is separate from constant
module storage. On the narrow Apple arm64/non-PAC libc++210106 ABI1 C++20 path,
a read-only comparison checks the actually bound C1/C2 shared-mutex constructor
instructions against the audited 68-byte store-only body. The query takes no
runtime lock, initializes no first-caller thread identity and calls no loader API.
Directly bound function addresses are interpreted as permanent readable libc++
text under that ABI; each read stays within a 4-KiB subpage. Different code,
trampolines, boundary-adjacent addresses and other ABIs return typed unknown;
no runtime patching, PAC stripping or loader search broadens the proof. Actual
compile/link validation must confirm the alias and constructor import identity.
CUDA's distinct cache-initializing constructor remains unknown. Ordinary
Scheduler construction and public stack-owned Scheduler semantics are preserved.

The module's slot, generation, publication pointer, instruction constant and
existing first-caller thread-id/guard are counted once, separately from the
admitted dynamic object. The pure static quote does not depend on the loaded
constructor matching. Raw allocation prefixes and the enclosing safe Box retire
before their source custody on refusal. Successful native publication transfers
custody once; neither a dropped safe witness nor a later failure refunds that
permanent native owner.

This closes one process owner, not worker-table growth, StreamThread/native-thread
startup, stream directories, encoder/queue/resource populations, caches or selected
workspace. All MLX/Eredu-owned capacities remain in scope. Allocator-private
rounding/bookkeeping, compiler-runtime guard internals and OS-private lock storage
are outside the managed-object bound. Whole-model native fit remains pending.


The MLX prepared stream-copy boundary copies only the existing native Stream
value into one exact C wrapper. It never constructs or promotes a native worker,
queue, stream directory or TLS mapping. Its private no-Weak Rust owner and
preallocated retirement node are priced through the existing qualified host
storage producer and source-initializer comparison before allocation. Final
retirement frees the Arc block and scalar C wrapper, then queues the node;
unlocked reclamation frees that node before releasing its original account.

Ordinary Stream cloning and the public materialization context retain their
independent mutable C-handle behavior, including existing const accessors. Only
the private supplied-cache manager context owns the explicitly immutable prepaid
pair. Shared recipe/acquisition helpers consume a synchronous borrowed view;
there is no second materialization engine and no borrowed view escapes in native
work. The manager's separate ordinary stream fields, workers/queues, recursive
recipe workspace and total model fit remain separate obligations. Requested
wrapper/header extents are managed storage; allocator-private rounding/caches
remain outside that definition consistently with other producer boundaries.

The native shared binary materializer prepares copied strides and its fixed
deallocator before requesting output backing. Its five allocating branches use
the existing owning adoption worker, which releases incoming backing if capture
or `Data` construction fails and preserves the prior output. Donation retains
its existing predicate and alias order. This closes the raw-buffer argument
construction gap without issuing new memory authority or completing the pending
whole-operation fit.

The same existing owning adoption helper also protects shared unary and Select
output allocation. Copied strides and fixed-deleter preparation precede native
allocation; all existing donor short-circuit ordering and output byte equations
remain unchanged. This bounded cleanup guarantee does not establish a complete
producer fit or change compiled-transform/custom-buffer admission.

The existing selected-plan cache-identity control quote includes the private
manager context borrow and its concrete three-reference materialization view.
Recipe call-depth controls remain in the pending selected recipe envelope.


### GGUF reader-source construction and prepaid inventory

The supplied cold GGUF source driver consumes the exact admitted immutable catalog and admits its reader/source constructor in the same pool. Ordinary prepared-reader sources use the same concrete worker and retain ordinary origin. The constructor owns the fixed reader bank, materializer coordinate and parser scratch storage, LRU/touched rows, initial empty recipe-cache controls, and shared source/checkpoint shells. Concrete fresh-reserve and shared-layout qualification precedes allocation; failed construction retains the original catalog, untouched checkpoints and completed materializer prefix.

Private source handles propagate the constructor custody through leases, captured metadata, retained source storage and weak source identities. Strong/weak allocation references retire before custody. Source accounting holds only a weak pool reference, so a canonical registry key cannot create a strong pool cycle. The original charge remains once through the last retained identity; pool teardown cannot create new credit.

Canonical source registration keeps the full physical inventory and recognizes only the new backing prepaid by an authenticated constructor in that same pool. It charges the original captured-header residual and ordinary rows, preserves canonical alias origins, and charges the full inventory in another pool. It never promotes an ordinary row. Prepared namespace/row owners ensure comparisons precede structural commit and key/custody retirement occurs outside `Usage`; normal and reset-layout retirement share the residual-charge rule. Source-inventory coverage is distinct from mutable and immutable native-buffer birth coverage.

Original checkpoint construction, future arbitrary recipe/validator entries, source/context wrappers, file/stream and selected-thread initialization retain their separate coverage obligations. Registry preparation still has its existing ordinary cold-control contract. This source component does not enable aggregate model-fit admission.

The explicit `PreparedMaterializationSourceStream` constructor now admits a new

The module registry/guard/publication extents join the existing fixed native

This is a completed registration contribution, not worker readiness or complete

### CPU worker directory publication

The Scheduler now owns one fixed intrusive `WorkerEntry` per created CPU worker.
Its integer-index links and inline optional `StreamThread` are one physical

a second lookup under the exclusive loan elects the same serialized constructor.
Only that winner starts `std::thread`. Publishing its already-owned entry cannot
allocate or throw. A losing empty candidate is destroyed after the loan ends.
This removes the former unordered-map node/rehash allocation after thread start.

The existing thread constructor, FIFO queue, counted-task acceptance/completion,

This is an allocation-strategy prerequisite, not an admitted worker-launch

or erase `missing_worker`/other typed original-context refusals. A later source

The supplied GGUF source path also admits the actual primary/companion union
before constructing its child-vector backing, cloned key buffers, prepared

Nested storage and private custody shells retire before that charge.

This union contribution covers neither the public outer `Arc<dyn CheckpointSource>`

### Qualified CPU worker startup is a separate source owner

An explicitly registered materialization CPU stream can prepare one process

The native recipe is available only for the qualified compiler/library layout

A retained checkpoint root may now use the neutral `RetainedCheckpointSource`

Clones and opaque `CheckpointSourceIdentity` values retain the same outer

Prepared source graphs, architecture visitors, MLX materialization and residency

Original MLX array operations now share the existing C destination setters and

remain separate prerequisites.

Valid depthwise convolution uses the shared native convolution worker with inline owned axes. Its resident recipe covers both input promotions and compactions and the output, while the architecture owns causal history and padding. Public native vector interfaces and deferred CPU ownership remain compatible.

The resident constant-pad recipe follows the shared default-zero tensor worker:
one eager I32 source, two cast candidates and the two-input Pad. The native
primitive retains Shape axes, and ordinary vector APIs/C calls use one borrowed
axis worker. Pad's CPU/GPU copy passes explicit shape, strides and offset to the
existing copy worker instead of constructing an alias descriptor. The actual
primitive size and constructor transports feed the resident Graph query. Safe
width controls are admitted only through their owning inline-capacity query
(currently rank at most four), and contribute to the existing request controls.
Edge padding and heap width destinations remain unqualified; ordinary behavior
remains available through the same implementation.

Text quotes borrow identity from the same retained original source workspace. Legacy
and saved-resume quotes instead move its existing identity and retire the snapshot;
no copied identity or new manager/disk-cache lifetime is introduced. Owning layout
and declaration queries price the retained ready-host vectors, metadata shapes and
keys once in the enclosing host term. Direct-read metadata remains separately
unqualified. Cold device inspection uses the existing scalar stream snapshot
instead of constructing a temporary Device shell.

The initial original ready-host pin now waits for the quote's accepted control
guard and uses the same immutable-owner pin worker as operation installation,
before any native producer or arena allocation. The enclosing host term prices
this one pin separately from the operation-bank pin. Deferred leases and escaped
fixed failures retain independent raw custody, so either can outlive the quote
without refunding the other's storage. Legacy and saved-resume pins keep their
ordinary path; cold snapshot construction and shared manager owners remain open.

Grouped projection recipes include the shared helper's concrete BF16 configuration,
result and shape owners once per possible projection call, using owning Rust/C
layout queries. Scalar stream inspection avoids temporary Device allocations.
The existing packed chunk destination retains raw metadata custody through native
concatenation and failure. Kernel construction, persistent TLS/cache ownership and
native generated-source text remain separate obligations; these per-call controls
do not certify them or provide an independent grant.


The original resident packed dense gated-bank worker derives its complete chunk
population from the shared 64-token threshold and 32-token loop. Before graph
construction, the existing original submission ingress prepares a finite output
directory and exact Array destinations under its admitted metadata custody;
chunk calls consume those destinations without growth. Their custody survives
partial fill, concatenation and scope retirement. The native ArrayVector element
backing remains Graph-owned, while its C header and named transport controls are
separately included through the actual owning layout query. Validation, both
projection alternatives, every chunk and final concatenation enter the selected
recipe; router tie handling, sequential reduction and other unclosed producers
remain independent requirements.

Ready-host cold inspection now lends source declarations and validated recipe metadata through the neutral checkpoint/residency contracts. Direct bindings reuse the retained catalog loan and the ordinary selection validator; derived bindings inspect the same cached result after releasing its mutex. Native shape validation iterates that loan, including packed four-bit lowering, without cloning the recipe or constructing conversion vectors. Custom catalog fallbacks, cache misses and owned errors retain their existing behavior and remain separate constructor obligations; these borrowed inspections neither grant source custody nor close the shared-manager baseline.

The resident grouped recipe keeps graph and physical-buffer facts separate from
custom-kernel host readiness. Nonempty grouped SiLU still requires owned kernel,
TLS, configuration, and generated-source storage. Dense selected projections
whose widths admit the BF16 row worker additionally require actual native dtype
or those same owned kernel facts: the neutral Float32 descriptor includes BF16
and cannot prove that worker absent. These cases leave the enclosing retained
workspace unknown and cannot supply a completion recipe. Empty or geometrically
ineligible Identity projections do not acquire this prerequisite. Component tests
with explicit prepared operation controls do not certify whole-request host fit.

Selected finite resident Eval recipes now impose an early necessary submission-tracking capacity before prompt/native preparation. Each nonempty constructor request uses the native RecordQuota allocator's own block/back-offset/alignment arithmetic, and the maximum covers every known prefill, decode and shared-sampling constructor. Undersized configured arenas return neutral `WorkingMemoryError::SubmissionTrackingCapacity` with exact required/configured bytes. The separately exposed sum describes known constructor storage only; concurrent retention, wait Records and other users remain separate fit obligations, so passing this comparison grants no complete-fit guarantee.

The shared cold prefill candidate search treats the typed submission-tracking capacity refusal as a smaller-chunk candidate failure. The backend passes the exact neutral required/configured fields through that search; an exhausted search returns the final typed refusal, while source, identity, native and arbitrary unknown-bound errors remain terminal. Candidate retries create no prompt/native work and do not imply that a decode or other fixed constructor minimum can be reduced.

Ready-host snapshot construction now reserves its final unit and copy vectors from the exact locked selected stores. Copy rows live once in a flat destination; unit ranges and dispatch ordinals let in-place sorting check duplicate units and conflicting allocation capacities, then restore the original requested-unit and host-name order. No BTree scratch or separate identity index is allocated. The existing retained-layout query prices these actual vectors, including their control fields, while canonical aliases, borrowed recipe dimensions, source pins and error-prefix ownership keep their existing semantics. Shared manager/source births and other cold constructor owners remain separate obligations.

The fixed custom-kernel invocation borrows bounded template names and output
shape descriptors through the same native Metal kernel worker. Rust and C keep
its configuration and result slots inline; no config object, template strings,
output-shape vector, or Rust result vector is created. Native output descriptors
use the existing Graph allocator and shared sibling-publication rollback. The
ordinary owning APIs retain their signatures and feed the same worker. This
configuration mechanism supports multiple outputs for reuse by other kernels.

F32 pointwise SiLU/Sigmoid consumes that invocation without changing the
`stable_exp_f32` source or rounding. Its exact invocation controls feed the
resident recipe, but kernel/TLS captures, generated source and persistent source
and library caches remain separate unqualified owners. Direct and grouped
pointwise traces preserve graph/payload facts while refusing complete host fit;
a passing numerical component test does not establish whole-request admission.

#### Resident dense router CPU tie branch

The backend's ordinary `largest_indices` path keeps its existing GPU partition,
value-only CPU tie fallback, global crossing-tie predicate and eager ordinary
branch. Original execution borrows a previously admitted process CPU source,
worker and immutable Stream copy, constructs both existing partitions lazily,
and chooses their IDs with the same global predicate. The CPU result is sliced
on the execution stream, so only the partition itself runs on CPU. No model
family, routing policy or alternative tie comparator is introduced.

The source, worker and wrapper use the existing shared native initializer and
retain their own actual birth accounts. Selector construction may prepare them
only outside an original Scope and only after the admitted process Scheduler
exists. The worker is the last fallible constructor. A failed extra preparation
leaves ordinary selector behavior intact, keeps original qualification missing,
and records a sticky failed attempt so repeated selector construction cannot
accumulate failed process registrations. Quotes never initialize these owners.
Original borrowing authenticates the same accounts and preserves retryable native
Busy separately from unavailable ownership. Worker birth does not price later
mutable error diagnostics or certify worker health.

Rank-two last-axis CPU ArgPartition shares its real value-only callable with the
ordinary worker. Fixed Eval physically reserves, from the existing Graph arena,
the cleanup task, empty Data-reference slots, output/tracer invocation backing,
output Data shared control, the two weak-view descriptor/descriptor-control/Data
sets, exact bound FIFO TaskNode and original mutable buffer birth.
The bank and its finite pointer slots retire with the same Graph references;
there is no second arena, fallback or post-dispatch allocation of these owners.
Invocation aliases, donation, dispatch, cleanup filling and task-count update
retain their prior order. Other CPU primitives retain their existing path.

The native Fence/Event producers expose their actual shared-control allocations,
CPU wait/signal tasks and GPU handler nodes. Slow Fence Event creation and fast
Fence U32 backing remain separate alternatives; each selected router contributes
at most two fast backing births. The per-router receipt ceiling includes the two
actual stream Events, two possible slow-Fence Events, CPU input wait/output update
and final signal, and corresponding GPU handlers. Opaque platform Event creation
and failure remain distinct from managed Graph requests. Neither these facts nor
the CPU query create runtime state or grant admission. Non-Metal receipt producers
report unknown. The take-along-axis ignore list now borrows inline Shape through
the existing synchronous broadcast worker; public vector interfaces and the
owning dynamic-tracing callback remain unchanged.

The selected resident recipe consumes these controls for dense F32, unpartitioned
Softmax/SelectedSoftmax routing without supplied IDs/intervention, input transform,
learned coefficient scale or explicit selected normalization. Its actual flatten,
projection and score prefix is at most 16 primitives/17 edges; largest selection
is 8/9 without a cutoff fallback or 46/53 with it, including the final lazy Select.
Gathered scores, selected-only Softmax and coefficient cast add 6/7. Biases and a
nonunit scalar coefficient add their actual binary/scalar producers. The physical
routing emitter includes both partition backings, Select promotions/result and
fast-Fence payloads. Normalized routing remains missing because `f32_sum_last`
uses its own cascade-sum custom kernel and owning configuration; ordinary Reduce
is not substituted. Partitioned/intervened and other dtypes retain their distinct
missing producer facts. These local Graph/Record/payload facts do not complete
whole-model fit, persistent kernel/cache ownership, platform-event storage or
post-start diagnostic growth, and available arena bytes are not a completeness
proof.

The router Softmax paths call `safemlx::ops::softmax_axis` directly through the C
wrapper to native `core::softmax`. They do not call the backend
`arithmetic::softmax_last` TLS custom helper used by attention. This distinction
does not close the native persistent kernel/compiler/cache owners.


The original Metal pointwise worker borrows one immutable kernel definition
created by the cold input-runtime path through the existing shared native
initializer. A qualified native request covers its fixed header and exact copied
name/body/header bytes in one allocation; the safe owner frees that allocation
before releasing its original accounting custody. The fixed attribute catalog,
source literals and initialization coordinators belong to the shared domain's
static baseline. Later borrowers share the same completed owner and domain;
ordinary TLS kernels are never promoted. Both representations call the same
native source generator and preserve explicit FP32 exponential rounding.

This closes the pointwise definition's constructor and alias lifetime only.
Generated primitive strings, template/source-generation controls, and persistent
source/library/kernel cache entries remain separate unqualified owners; the
shared custom-kernel prerequisite continues to prevent complete-fit admission.

The loaded facade's additive managed plain-text entry compiles a consumed tokenizer
file through the existing original source account, then authenticates its complete
supported configuration against the selected loaded tokenizer by borrowed component
comparison. Vocabulary, merge ranks, added-token policy, preprocessing and decoding
must agree; execution-cache storage is not tokenizer identity. The public source has
no raw tokenizer or funding exit. Controlled startup and uninterrupted generation
both use the existing original plain session, lend `GenerationPlainTextEvent` text,
and return the same retained text/ID storage. Fixed startup failures remain by value;
backend failures retain their neutral classification and source. Existing prepared
chat/semantic APIs keep their contracts, and unknown native/host producer bounds
still reject before prompt construction. Loading the model, opening the source file,
chat rendering, capture, snapshots and speculative generation are separate scopes.

For the selected resident original path, Record arena sizing now sums every fixed
Eval constructor attempt across the retained equation and sampling rows, including
all successful and failed prefixes without taking early-retirement credit. Prompt
upload and the observed empty sampler preparation issue no Eval; resident Roots
completion, SamplingEvent synchronization and TokenScalar use scoped observation,
so they issue no consumer WaitRecords. Cross-stream Event/Fence work stays in the
same counted fixed Eval. Missing rows never produce complete Record fit. The native
allocator adds its actual minimum splittable tail to the complete extent sum: while
requests remain, a fresh arena retains a large enough contiguous tail even if earlier
blocks retire or first-fit reuses holes. Checked native alignment/overflow rules
remain authoritative. This is a Record-domain fit, independent of Graph, payload,
queue, kernel and broader host/disk obligations. Original tracking facts retain the
exact requested ceiling for preparation identity and separately charge/allocate the
source-derived capacity within that ceiling; legacy facts keep both equal.


The MLX automatic target creator can now create its physical Metal execution
stream through the existing shared native initializer and StreamRegistry. Its
account covers the exact stream entry, encoder, birth record, encoder shared
control, initial submission-state/receipt shared controls, independent C wrapper,
safe custody node and named constructor controls. The account follows each actual
initial shared control through physical deletion, including a callback's state
alias after the idle frontier; ambiguous completion retains the encoder and its
birth together. Stream registration publication is last and nonthrowing. Ordinary
local/global encoder maps keep their existing constructors and never become
original authority merely because an entry already exists.

The backend retains those exact initialized owners and the existing separately
admitted CPU materialization stream/worker owners. Strict original text quotation
checks their actual native identities and source-pool accounts before prompt or
recipe construction; the quote itself initializes nothing. Factory compatibility
falls back only for an explicitly unsupported producer or an ordinary prerequisite
predecessor. Budget, busy, allocation and platform constructor failures propagate.
Caller-supplied ordinary streams are preserved and cannot pass this readiness check.
Ordinary Stream cloning and its independent mutable C-wrapper semantics are unchanged.

Queue/buffer/autorelease handles and their platform failure paths are owned and
released by the actual shared constructor. Private Foundation/Metal allocator,
compiler and driver internals are platform storage, outside Eredu-managed memory;
the query reports their handle populations without inventing internal byte bounds.
Requested MLX buffer backing and later task, receipt, kernel/cache, diagnostic and
TLS owners still require their own producer contributions. Debug queue-label
formatting remains unqualified. This birth owner does not certify total process
memory, later work, or whole-model fit.

The admitted FP32 pointwise kernel uses a finite prepared source family. Its
shared native initializer admits the immutable definition block, six exact
source/cache slots (two operations and the scalar, small constant-pointer and
device-pointer input signatures), copied generated source and one retirement
node before construction. Input length is the dispatch grid, so changing length
does not grow a cache. The ordinary and admitted paths retain the same explicit
`stable_exp_f32` arithmetic and source generator.

Each slot compiles lazily using the ordinary framework compiler worker and owns
its library/pipeline handles under its own mutex. It never enters the unbounded
ordinary source/library maps. Native primitives and retained compiler failures
keep the same source family alive. Final native retirement releases all handles
and both blocks before queuing the original custody for unlocked host release;
no request Graph, Scope, Record or physical-output grant is retained by this
persistent owner. Querying a declared layout is independent of warming or cache
contents. Undeclared signatures refuse before source generation or publication.

The bound includes Eredu-owned strings, slot/alias/synchronization controls and
requested tensor backing. Foundation/Metal private allocator, shader-compiler
and driver storage remain excluded platform storage under the Device contract;
this is not a process-memory or total-native-memory bound. Other custom kernel
families, including the BF16 grouped projection, still require their own source
constructors and remain explicit admission prerequisites.

`CustomKernel::state()` keeps its ordinary serializer tuple and copying behavior.
Only native export/state extraction calls it; the admitted no-capture resident
Eval and Metal execution paths borrow prepared source directly and do not invoke
export inspection. Export's copying owners are outside this admitted route.

The reproducible RMS, row-sum and attention-softmax helpers now share the same
finite Metal source-family owner as pointwise arithmetic. Two non-scalar
address-space signatures per helper cover all admitted row dimensions; the
existing input shape metadata and dispatch grid supply width and row count.
Reduction order, precise square root and stable exponential equations are
unchanged. Each actual source family has its own once-admitted account, with
no request Graph in its persistent cache. Normalization quotation includes
the possible row RMS invocation and its fixed controls; missing qualification
remains a typed admission refusal. Wider attention/router paths retain their
existing incomplete bounds. All three focused row checks pass: declared families
at multiple dimensions against scalar equations, independent BF16 normalization
rounding, and the existing independent sigmoid/coefficient fixture using row sum.

Ordinary stream synchronization now shares the existing Completion wait boundary: after a successful native wait, observe and retire submission records outside original/scoped observation control. Waiting alone did not refresh the final record and could retain its primitive/source family indefinitely. Failed waits and scoped/original execution preserve their explicit recovery/retirement boundary; retirement-only polling keeps its existing semantics.

The original resident Graph capacity is selected from all attempted native constructor requests, not from the requested arena ceiling or mutable tensor bytes. The selected executable must retain `FullyResident`; every equation and observed sampling phase must have a closed native dispatch population. The backend combines the exact eager prompt, prefill/decode root buffers, resident construction banks, fixed Eval Synchronizer and prologue banks, sampling event and worker requests. Generic tensor-handle clones are counted by the shared neutral metadata driver independently of backing identities; native shell costs remain backend facts. The native allocator supplies block/alignment extents and its actual fresh-arena split tail. No early retirement credit is taken. The original Graph policy ceiling remains in preparation identity; only the selected allocation and its controls are charged. Unsupported source materialization, parallel workers, kernels and incomplete dispatch populations remain explicit gaps.

Public managed plain-text requests use the genuine original token-ID claim to request complete native planning even when auxiliary Graph/Record policy ceilings are omitted. The backend authenticates that claim and the retained stream sources before inspection, derives both arena sizes from complete selected populations, and charges them against the one managed-domain budget. Explicit auxiliary values remain ceilings. Neutral arena facts preserve the original optional policy in preparation identity; configuration is never rewritten. Ordinary Vec-input sequence diagnostics retain their existing omitted-component behavior. Prepared-media and incomplete producer routes keep their typed refusals.


Resident dispatch Graph ownership now joins the neutral semantic tensor-handle
copy population to the actual `PreparedInputArray` shell class in the existing
physical construction bank. Named backend aliases are additional source-derived
terms. No shared mutable C handle or replacement clone mode is introduced.
Scalar/source seeds also reserve their actual original-buffer birth metadata.

The first complete worker profile covers the single admitted GPU stream used by
dense resident equations and greedy sampling. It sums actual descriptor/Data/birth,
collapse and GEMM-stride growth, temporary-vector, resource/fence-candidate,
encoding-cleanup, receipt and Event requests. Encoder intervals come from Eval
thresholds, input Event waits, signals, finalization and recovery; unique buffer
keys and concrete shader argument populations bound resources. It charges fresh
vector allocation attempts and lifetime overlap through the existing GraphQuota
fit query, preserving failed-prefix owners. The standard pipeline cache and
prepared custom source families retain their independent shared/request owners;
private Metal allocation internals remain excluded platform storage.

Grouped/router, convolution, recurrent multi-output and larger-rank worker
profiles still have explicit absent complete bounds. Their existing tensor and
host-construction facts remain independent. A partial worker description does
not authorize a complete Graph fit, host fit or original request. Ordinary native
execution and public clone semantics are unchanged.

Public managed plain-text source preparation installs its requested domain ceiling
through the existing neutral PendingAccount/AccountTicket ledger before stop
compilation or tokenization. The fixed account is charged before its node is
allocated; source compilers retain their own independent measured charges. The
backend supplies the authenticated source pool and actual selected execution
identity. This budget owner grants no native or inference authority. Successful
startup establishes the request's own ceiling before the preparation owner retires;
failed startup keeps that owner after its by-value cause so partial source storage
retires first. Pending, published and physically retiring accounts constrain all
concurrent domain work through the existing shared capacity calculation.

The GPU concatenation worker retains its prefix-size array under the existing Graph allocator. One exact input-count-plus-one reservation replaces ordinary vector growth; the resident worker recipe independently counts its requested integer slots and constructor attempts in addition to ArrayVector and copy destinations.


### Admitted default-library pipeline destinations

An original resident request constructs its native pipeline destinations only
after accepting its host controls and Graph arena. The actual selected worker
population supplies a checked shader-lookup count; each lookup claims one
preallocated row before entering the platform compiler. The row retains the
actual default library and resulting pipeline. Exact function names, constants
and linked-function loans are consumed synchronously by the shared compiler
worker. No ordinary cache entry provides admission credit. The first realization
compiles once per lookup, even for repeated names; bounded reuse is a subsequent
performance optimization.

The same Graph retains this independent cache through completion, failure and
alias retirement. Cache custody contains only the accepted raw host owner, with
no Graph, Scope, Record or physical-partition backedge. Native rows and framework
handles retire before that raw custody. Installation refuses an already shared,
used or configured arena and preserves both owners. Finite rows cannot spill
into the ordinary maps. Ordinary map lookup also avoids insertion under its
shared read lock.

The build includes the existing precompiled Metal instantiations alongside the
ordinary JIT configuration. Original selectors branch before source builders;
the admitted shared Device owns the actual embedded library bytes. Dense
embedding's contiguous axis-zero gather has additional instantiations of its
unchanged gather_front worker. KV overwrite SliceUpdate uses the existing copy
worker and returns before reduction-source construction. Other local JIT
indexing/reduction builders remain refused in original execution; absence of a
complete selected worker profile keeps quotation unknown. NAX coverage remains
conditional on the actual SDK, deployment target and selected Device.

Managed host storage includes the row block, safe retirement node, actual
libc++/fmt-qualified selector name and constant-vector populations, and native
constructor/error/handle transports. Metal/Foundation private allocation, shader
compiler and driver internals retain the existing excluded-platform boundary;
this is not a claim about total process memory.


The gated-delta Metal worker now uses four originally admitted source families for scalar/vector decay and decode/prefill. The generic finite family supports 64 distinct source signatures, covering all non-scalar address-space combinations of the actual six F32 inputs without specializing model dimensions. Existing input shape metadata supplies key/value width, sequence length and heads; recurrence order, initial state, chunk thresholds and F32 accumulation are unchanged. Original invocations borrow fixed six-input/two-output configuration and retain source/cache custody through both sibling descriptors. Multi-chunk outputs consume the existing prepared host destination bank, and cold quotation includes its exact population, Stream scalar query, fixed invocation controls and explicit missing-source prerequisite. Ordinary Metal uses the same equations with its existing ordinary source ownership; CPU/CUDA workers are unchanged. Private Metal compiler/driver storage remains platform storage; owned managed handles and finite text/cache slots remain charged.

The resident GPU worker population now admits the existing prepared recurrent scan and exact separable depthwise-convolution lowerings to the common descriptor, Data, temporary and resource classes. The grouped dense/packed route forwards its supplied stream into gather/scatter index broadcasts and shares the actual native Int32 sort planner to fund every merge/copy dispatch and cache lookup. This preserves the separate `Bf16Projection` and `GroupedIndexed` source prerequisites; neither a Graph population nor a sort bound supplies the missing kernel source/selector owners. Router cross-stream Fence dispatch remains a separate producer.


The BF16 row-projection helper shares one source definition between ordinary
execution and a once-admitted finite Metal family. Its 32 signatures cover the
actual two non-scalar address classes of the BF16 input, BF16 weight and I32
index vector, together with the existing grouped/four-lane flags. Width comes
from the input shape loan and output columns from the dispatch grid; changing
those dimensions creates no new retained source key. Both FP32 reduction orders
and final BF16 rounding are unchanged. Fixed borrowed invocation and a bounded
local final-shape buffer replace the original path's configuration/result/shape
vectors; original ranks beyond 32 refuse before index preparation. The same
shared-domain source initializer funds generated text/cache slots before any
invocation, with typed failure prefixes and native output aliases retaining its
custody. Ordinary TLS construction remains ordinary and receives no credit.

This closes the BF16 source prerequisite of the quoted grouped producer and
joins the same host-control query to eligible dense PhysicalLinear projections,
whose existing primitive recipe already counts the ungrouped zero-ID seed. It
does not close the independent grouped indexed gather/scatter prerequisite. The batched attention
helper's constructed host index vector and other unqualified producer populations
remain separate requirements; source readiness alone does not certify them.


The private original chat ingress now retains a move-only preparation containing
its rendered prompt and the caller's shared-domain source ceiling. The ceiling
is installed through the existing runtime account ledger before rendering and
remains live between rendering and startup, including failed render/encoding
prefixes. Startup requires the same capacity before compiling stops or encoding
and transfers enforcement to the ordinary request admission. Error fields retire
startup resources, then rendering, then the source ceiling; cancellation follows
the same ownership order. No separate registry or native submission authority is
introduced. This extends the existing private chat route; public chat tools,
grammar and template-policy integration remain separate work.


The shared BF16 batched matrix producer creates repeated I32 group IDs directly
in the final native input buffer through the existing array iterator constructor.
Its safe immutable geometry plan checks the range, I32 shape, byte extent and
iterator difference limit before any descriptor or view construction. Native
publication keeps the existing Graph descriptor/Data/C-shell and original failure
carrier contracts; there is one eager native source generation and no numerical
host ID vector. Cold matrix geometry consumes that same plan, retaining the
existing native source/copy/validation terms. Explicit-attention host facts include
the named fixed input-producer controls, reused across its sequential products and
tiles. This producer adds no model-family policy and does not certify the remaining
custom-attention lowering, kernel, dispatch or lifetime prerequisites.
The resident sampling recipe retains the shared configured sampler's TopK,
TopP and MinP operations even at greedy temperature. It counts Partition/Slice,
reductions, sorted GatherAxis, Softmax, Scan, overwrite ScatterAxis, casts,
broadcasts and actual scalar seeds. Multi-block sorts consume the existing
source-derived additional-dispatch query, while the request owns every pipeline
attempt and named selector control. The prepared library supplies the unchanged
floating-point/U32 GatherAxis and overwrite ScatterAxis kernels for both offset
widths and all contiguity classes. Ordinary JIT and all numerical filter rules,
including ties and nonfinite values, remain unchanged. Other scatter reductions
or index dtypes do not inherit this source qualification. Valid-path scatter
axis controls use the existing Shape/AxisView workers instead of allocating a
prefix string or independent axis vectors. Sampling traces now retain their
first missing operation just as equation traces do; an unsupported policy cannot
be confused with an observed empty preparation.

Resident sampling now reduces the shared repetition, frequency and presence penalty
worker from its neutral history-window and policy flags. Its eager mask/scalar
uploads, binary/Select children and adjusted-logits handle enter the same selected
Graph/Record and physical populations as the filters. The existing host quote
funds the exact Bool/F32 vocabulary buffers and contiguous sorted history suffix;
the owning worker supplies their fixed transports through the sampling control
quote. Zero windows preserve the shared worker's configured graph, and token
values or out-of-vocabulary history entries never substitute for a population
bound. Built-in source/cache qualification remains required; stochastic and other
unclosed sampling operations remain explicit missing lowerings.

Original ready-host and foreground direct-disk transfers share the same prepared
publication rows. Their existing per-window transfer bank reserves the final
row vector and two canonical unit-ID destinations before activation, using the
manager's unchanged closure and accepted raw host custody. One ID moves into
the transfer application and the other into the publication row; active work
neither collects these IDs nor grows the row vector. Original materialization
borrows the retained immutable binding declarations, while ordinary acquisition
keeps its existing clone behavior. Capacity and source identity are checked
before consuming destinations, and a failed construction keeps its actual partial
slot. The local publication owner retains raw custody until its vectors and any
unpublished native rows have retired; publication moves the existing named-array
owners into manager storage. This closes these shared host publication controls,
without qualifying the separate manager/source baseline, direct-read metadata,
or layerwise Graph/Record producer requirements.


The original resident native budget converts the existing Metal emitter's total
requested-byte bound with the actual retained allocator's page quantum. Ordinary
small buffers may occupy less than one page; original backing rounds every
positive birth separately. The selected equation and sampling capacities therefore
include at most `maximum_births * (page_size - 1)` additional bytes, with checked
arithmetic, before their generations replace the earlier workspace peaks. The
single eager prompt source already reports its exact physical capacity and is
not converted again. This pure C/safe query invokes the same linked physical
rounding worker as original allocation, performs no initialization or allocation,
and supplies its fixed controls to the original provider. CPU header rules remain
separate; unsupported retained allocators cannot gain a Metal population proof.

The loaded portable facade exposes managed text-chat source compilation and
start/run composition using the same original J/H renderer, tokenizer sources,
source-budget guard and controlled plain cursor. A source retains original C/J
and authenticates the current loaded tokenizer plus actual template source and
selected name on each startup; named-template matching allocates no selector or
fingerprint. Public request/error/preparation/result representations enter the
same H/S/E/I/R consumer layout, and translating a native startup error preserves
its source through BackendFailure while H retires before its caller ceiling.
No new admission authority or backend semantic branch is introduced. Message
and source-file opening ownership remains caller-side, as in existing APIs.


Direct explicit attention now supplies its own resident lowering from the actual
shared worker. It covers finite rank-four grouped-head geometry below the
worker's existing blockwise InputScores branch, including score caps, boolean or
additive masks and learned sinks. Both BF16 batched products account for their
final-owned I32 IDs, deferred safe-index validation roots and actual prepared
projection family calls; the first product preserves its width-rejection prefix.
Row softmax borrows the existing prepared family, and sink-column removal uses
the fixed rank-four Slice bridge instead of constructing general host indexing
vectors. The physical product bound includes the original deferred validation
alternative alongside ordinary eager validation. Source qualification, original
scope ownership and typed refusal remain mandatory. Sliding/blockwise accumulator
and host-output-vector producers remain distinct; this does not certify them from
the direct worker's graph or source facts.

Standard positive-temperature sampling retains the same explicit-seed native
random worker and Gumbel/argmax equations as ordinary execution. Its observed
U32[2] seed is an eager preparation with one physical birth, a prepared Graph
constructor block and no Eval, Record submission or shader lookup. The existing
Sampling preparation Scope installs that block before calling the shared state
constructor. Each subsequent step counts RandomBits, the separately traced key
views, uniform arithmetic and scalar sources, both Log/Negative pairs, addition
to logits and the actual ArgReduce or unit-axis zero branch. The compiled default
library already contains both contiguous and strided-key random kernels; the
request-owned pipeline rows handle their actual lookups. Named native/C/safe/Rust
controls are consumed by the same cold recipe. Per-birth physical page conversion
remains in the selected original buffer producer. Mirostat cutoff/probability
requirements remain separate; no global default random sequence or alternate
sampling engine is used by this path.


Originally admitted resident KV reset now uses the existing neutral
`SessionResetPreparationBackend` boundary. Its closed MLX readiness owner holds
an exclusive session borrow, rejects live payload/recovery aliases, authenticates
the retained prepared source worker and execution encoder, requires the existing
complete borrowed census of actual nonstate and decoder storage, and observes their
terminal frontiers without a new task, command buffer, wait or global reap.
The GPU check also rejects an open unsubmitted receipt and current encoder work.
Consuming readiness uses the same prepaid table/publication constructor and keeps
displaced arrays and their memory custody together until ordinary retirement.
The following request observes the newly published table through the existing
source-registration path; no state-copy allowance is inferred. Live work returns
Busy. Ordinary/unqualified streams and nonresident/parallel selections remain
unfinished integrations with typed rejections; ordinary reset and snapshot/fork
behavior are unchanged.

The same neutral resident table constructor also supports nested fixed-state
slots. It borrows the actual outer and child tables, validates the selected
component policies, and prepares exact dense destinations under one reset
account. The MLX hybrid adapter supplies inline empty attention policy and moves
funded child tables with their role keys and absent numerical values; it does not
copy a tensor or reconstruct model-family state geometry. Every child, including
an empty table, retains its own metadata. Existing child source pins are acquired
before construction, and failure retains completed children and all source pins
until their owning error retires. The account records the exact new table keys
and capacities without retaining predecessor tables or its own custody.

A following request binds the actual typed KV or hybrid state source and must
find its exact outer table in the complete inventory. Each original child is
independently checked for pool, published membership, capacity and liveness,
then shares the same constructor account instead of a second registration.
Provider identity projection runs outside the accounting lock; existing-only
lookup and retirement reuse the normal typed registry mechanism. Key-only,
compressed and paged hybrid reset constructors remain separate unfinished
profiles. This extension provides no numerical copy, fork or snapshot authority.


Sliding and InputScores query tiling now borrow fixed rank-four Slice bounds
and consume the existing prepared output destinations instead of constructing
independent Rust array/reference vectors. Their resident recipe recursively sums
the actual direct tile lowerings, window-mask constructors and concatenations;
output-bank call counts and maximum tile capacities flow into the same original
metadata ingress, including nested query tiling inside sliding windows. The
shared worker's 256-query tile and 8192-score-row branch remain the selection
source. True key-block recurrence still keeps its per-block Recovery/evaluation
frontier; its first evaluation can reach the enclosing decoder prefix and needs
a prepared nested completion join before this original profile is closed.

Original Standard sampling carries its advanced PRNG key into the existing
SamplingEvent's second root slot. The same fixed traversal completes both split
views before later sampling imports that key; no additional physical tensor or
native event is created. A pre-admitted C clone slot retains the key descriptor
under the same original host custody, including setup failures and final event
retirement. The recipe derives two roots from the actual SplitRandomKey trace;
greedy sampling keeps one. Shared local sampling now accepts that retained PRNG
state, while collective sampling still requires its own closed producer.

Original input-score attention with key blocks retains the shared two-pass
recurrence and completes each block before constructing the next. The retained
resident Graph bank declares a checked finite number of nested completions before
its first constructor. A synchronous native guard temporarily detaches only that
bank, submits fixed roots using the same accepted Scope and prepared traversal,
waits for actual callback progress, drops the event and retires settled records,
then restores the same bank. Failed attempts remain spent; unresolved work keeps
its original Scope ownership. There is no replacement authority, quota refill,
new TLS mode or lazy retention of all key blocks.

The cold producer follows the real 256-key blocks, both passes, masks, sinks and
head replication, including original all-true scalar/Full masks and backend C
handle clones. The first nested Eval may reach the enclosing decoder prefix;
each allowed attempt therefore uses that authentic enclosing row's complete DAG
ceiling, including roots and input leaves. Traversal and Record populations
include every such attempt with checked arithmetic. Request pipeline rows count
the complete equation DAG once: completed descriptors are not executed again at
later frontiers, and the fresh Synchronizer has no shader lookup. The resident construction
bank is counted once, and physical payload still follows the unchanged shared
workspace emitter's live-block peak plus retained finished query outputs and
actual original per-birth padding. The generic nested-completion mechanism also
accepts smaller fixed root sets from other callers with the same declared
traversal; it does not certify their operation or source populations itself.

Original Mirostat V2 consumes the shared sampler's actual cutoff, categorical,
intermediate token read, and probability update. One finite nested completion
settles token and advanced random key inside the existing Sampling Scope,
suspending and resuming the same prepared Graph bank. The final SamplingEvent
is consumed once for probability and retained token. Failed waits preserve the
same recovery owners; only successful exact completion permits continuation.
The complete observed trace bounds both Eval frontiers. Record and frontier
controls include both attempts; pipeline rows count the same observed sampler
DAG once, including its actual temporary, copy and sort kernels. Construction
and tensor births are charged once. Two prepaid C clone shells retain the key and token under the
existing raw host custody. Ordinary and original probability selection share
Softmax plus a borrowed static Slice and scalar reshape, preserving the same
coordinate without general-index buffers. The managed library includes the
existing Bool/UInt32 ScatterAxis overwrite worker for the best-token fallback;
cutoff ties, nonfinite values, explicit random splitting and the neutral mu/history
update use the unchanged shared policy. These facts do not certify speculative
or distributed sampling, other indexing reductions, or platform-private memory.

An already admitted CPU worker may authenticate its immutable Scheduler,
registered stream and worker-birth identities inside a valid original Scope.
This read-only loan creates no worker, task or source authority. The cold
Scheduler borrow/constructor still requires an empty submission context, and
ordinary scoped borrowers remain refused. The same original controls and
concrete worker identities are checked before router construction; no source
is replaced and no ordinary stream is promoted. The worker source layout also
includes the native binding and Scope-loan controls used by this validation.

Nested completion authenticates the explicit resident-bank kind supplied only by
the actual resident constructor. Worker-prologue exclusivity is a separate
allocator property and cannot identify resident banks. Pointwise and worker
banks never acquire the resident tag; existing allocator routing is unchanged.

The checked chat source constructor now feeds the existing bounded VM from the
shared full-template parser, instead of requiring a particular template text.
The first source-codegen profile covers text literals, message role/content
items and attributes, text addition/inequality, short-circuit `and`, conditional
blocks and nonnested iteration over messages with the actual declared local
name. Ordinary and checked codegen share jump patching, and both renderers retain
the shared instruction dispatcher. The checked path keeps its existing concrete
three-operand/one-loop measurement workspace; wider expressions, nested loops,
filters, calls, macros and other unimplemented operations return typed source
profile errors. These are unfinished compiler integrations, not template or model
limitations.

The text adapter retains the actual UTF-8 source or validated JSON selection.
Its decoded-byte iterator is allocation-free; source byte counts bound shared
parser records, continuations, copied spelling bytes and instruction/location
arrays before runtime admits original J. Decoding and every AST/codegen reserve
occur under that allowance. The temporary syntax and continuation buffers retire
before compile returns; success owns the decoded source and output arrays, while
a failure owns its completed destination prefix until the same source account
retires. Selected-name/source authentication and the caller's preparation ceiling
remain in the existing facade/runtime source driver. No backend or native grant
is introduced by this portable compiler mechanism.

Exact replicated-text source binding now has a cold entry accepting neutral
architecture/lowering destination descriptions before any native module exists.
Both that entry and ordinary native module traversal feed the same provenance,
alias, companion, placement and coverage driver; traversal lends its descriptions
without a second map. Cold descriptions are not native binding authority: the
retained loading plan must validate actual typed destination slots before binding.
This extraction is ordinary allocating planning, not an original memory grant;
source/manager constructor admission remains a separate required integration.

Bounded-policy neural submissions consume the existing accepted equation recipe. The selected execution layout adds each actual initial/group/final call to the enclosing span's finite nested Eval population before Graph and Record selection. Each group's traversal uses the full equation DAG as a conservative ceiling; the request pipeline population counts its once-executed descriptors, and physical backing is not duplicated and asynchronous execution is preserved. The single-GPU native submit helper suspends the resident constructor bank only while synchronous Fixed Eval/prologue construction runs, returns an owning Event, and restores the bank before host construction continues. Pending GPU callbacks retain independent existing allocation/custody bindings. Consumer waits use their exact WaitRecord layouts plus the enclosing equation's bounded encoder/resource cleanup envelope, and the same registered Scope authenticates every operation. Ready-host materialization still requires its distinct original-copy Graph/Record producer before whole host-layerwise admission can activate.

The original ready-host manager can now consume a neutral residency constructor
plan that borrows the actual OffloadPlan, unit declarations, selected source
catalogs and declared window names. Its single requested amount includes deep
input String/Vec/Box clones, sorted unit/alias ordinal rows, iterative alias
scratch, finite ledger rows and shared plan controls. Cloning and all destination
reserves occur only when the source initializer consumes that plan after
admission. Existing source declarations are not relabeled as original births.
The backend keeps its independent manager source account through every strong or
weak manager owner, escaped plan-source alias and constructor error; core/runtime
contain no backend or native accounting owner.

Controller alias lookup and the original operation closure share the retained
ordinal rows, so neither constructs temporary tuple/string keys. Ledger named
windows share one transition implementation: ordinary callers may add names,
while an original constructor retains only its actual supplied names and finite
per-unit host/device flags. An undeclared name returns a typed refusal before
state mutation. The current ready-host operation path does not create named
windows; direct/dense producer support must pass its own genuine names when
those mechanisms become qualified.

Checkpoint recipe validation for this constructor borrows authorized metadata
from the actual selected source and executes uncached inference in explicit
finite action/result destinations. It never clones a recipe merely to infer it
or adds an ordinary inference-cache entry. Direct selections, reshape,
transpose, concatenate/stack and output byte validation share their ordinary
semantic helpers. Missing borrowed catalog support remains an explicit
constructor-qualification refusal. The input tree determines every shape,
continuation and error-prefix allowance; native tensors, device selection and
complete neural-producer qualification remain the backend's separate contracts.

The source-layout prepass is allocation-free and borrows the caller-owned recipe
tree, catalog and planning stack. Its query transports are named in the amount
used by construction, but that amount is not authority for earlier planning and
does not claim a whole-thread stack bound. The finite worker's possible owned
recipe errors are the real permutation axes copy and unsupported-dtype text;
selection, reshape, join and byte-count failures retain fixed scalar causes.
Those exact children, together with controller identifier/name diagnostics, are
included in the constructor's failed-prefix allowance.

Cold replicated binding destinations are projected through the total prepared-execution driver with WorkspaceBackend and the ordinary selected-format architecture and unit constructors. Physical packed slots and quantization companions come from those modules; logical checkpoint shapes are never substituted for native destination shapes. The projection retains the exact prepared contract and canonical unit order, reads no payload, and grants no memory authority. Backend scalar compatibility and intrinsic lowering remain in the exact binder adapter; actual native slots must still match before publication. This metadata planning step precedes the ready-host source constructor, whose clone/read/native allocation and alias lifetimes require their own admitted source account. Other execution classes retain explicit route refusals until their projections are supplied.

Ready-host loading passes its optional prepared source manager by move from the backend provider, before NativeMemoryOwner acquisition, through the total materialization driver and typed replicated visitor into the existing policy construction seam. It does not enter global or thread-local storage. Native binding declarations are checked before adopting the prepared manager. An unqualified ordinary source plan keeps existing ordinary loading and remains unknown for strict admission; after a qualified source account starts, preparation failures propagate without falling back or promoting unquoted work.


Prepared encoded recipe reads reuse the checkpoint-owned admitted spans through
one borrowed batch worker. Its finite group, span and vectored-I/O scratch is
quoted from those exact spans before the backend creates any host destination;
immutable plan cloning has a separate owning storage/control query. Source
payload diagnostics use flags over the already admitted shard set, so reading
never grows a path map. Both ordinary and prepared calls share shard ordering,
disjoint destination splitting, file-version validation and short-read handling.
Prepared failures retain fixed batch/shard ordinals and the original I/O cause;
the backend keeps source plans, invalid output prefixes and their source account
through failure translation. These facts cover neither initial source/header
admission nor OS-private file operations, and never grant a native transfer or
turn an unclosed source constructor into an admitted original source.


A prepared encoded-read collection can detach its exact admitted metadata into a
new finite source owner after source admission. It copies the selected file
versions, paths, tensor/output metadata and spans, with independent fixed
telemetry/path flags; no ordinary cache, file-identity or telemetry Arc survives.
This is a metadata constructor, not source discovery: payload reads still open
only the retained canonical path and use the same before/after file-version
checks as ordinary reads. The move-only collection exposes borrowed metadata and
the shared read worker, with no owning recipe/Arc projection. Caller source
custody retires after all detached storage, after any partial constructor prefix,
and after an escaped read error's original I/O cause. Initial ordinary source
preparation is not retroactively reclassified as original construction.

The neutral completed-layerwise-window calculator now accepts borrowed per-unit byte facts and performs no allocation. The ordinary reporting API uses that same numerical worker while retaining its descriptive assumptions and unknown reasons. A source-accounted ready-host manager prepares one immutable copy snapshot plus a separate metadata-only identity; later candidate inspection shares them and validates locked source identity rather than rebuilding metadata. Legacy identity-only retention does not retain host buffers. Constructor layouts include the actual shared owners, deep metadata clones and fixed failure transports; detached recipe outputs and source-constructor metadata avoid fallback inference or native metadata allocation in the original snapshot builder. This source construction does not itself certify repeated binding, native materialization or whole public request coverage.

Ready immutable host sources use the shared host-transfer worker under the existing original request scope. Each actual copy has a fixed native Eval; the selected residency window then submits a separate scheduled-root Synchronizer and its finite consumer waits. The prepared C Event retains Graph-bank suspension through root construction, and the safe guard restores it under the same runtime loan before any deferred retirement. Source metadata and the retained canonical window closure supply output births, parameter handles, Graph/Record populations and cache attempts; ordinary transfers retain their existing path. The immutable source account remains distinct from request destination storage, and does not become submission authority.

The borrowed residency constructor plan exposes canonical alias declarations before owned construction. Cold lookup and the actual controller share alias identity, traversal and byte-agreement validation; cold lookup uses finite borrowed scans and returns no owned diagnostic. Native source constructors consume these neutral owner loans for exact physical shape and alias-slot planning, without rebuilding alias naming policy or acquiring a catalog/source owner.

Generic retained checkpoint erasure can now move a concrete neutral catalog into the same closed source lifetime owner used by typed sources. Its exact constructor query names one private source Arc, one custody Arc and fixed erasure/identity controls; source payload remains the caller's independently admitted responsibility. Strong aliases keep the source alive and opaque weak identities keep its allocation and constructor custody alive after source destruction. The generic variant supplies no typed prepared acquisition owner and never forwards a custom qualification callback. This lets a prepared backend policy keep its detached catalog without retaining ordinary cache/header roots, while checkpoint ownership and native materialization remain separate.

Original ready-host managers construct their scalar operation-window source once inside the same admitted source account as the immutable host snapshot. Its pre-grant producer names closure scratch, final window rows, the qualified shared owner and fixed constructor/error controls; later request Q does not charge those allocations again. Policy/operation plans share an opaque window owner retaining independent manager-source custody, and cached reuse authenticates the existing host snapshot layout, depth and selected unit order. Ordinary policy preparation uses the same population worker; an original manager without its prepared cache cannot fall back to ordinary source construction.

Prepared host-layerwise parameter binding borrows retained source names into one
finite row vector. The same neutral binding worker performs immutable validation,
mutable topology validation, and infallible publication for ordinary maps and
prepared rows. Selected native leaves provide direct mutable physical fields and
borrowed parameter declarations, so this path reconstructs no parameter maps or
metadata names. The accepted per-unit source population bounds row storage and
fixed traversal controls; actual imported Array handles consume the existing
request Graph shell population. Initial immutable-source imports instead consume
the source owner's declared native alias slots. Neither operation promotes an
ordinary source or grants admission authority to a scalar count. Legacy custom
populators and active replacement maps retain their separate readiness obligation.

Original ready-host source planning captures the selected primary and per-unit catalogs through the existing metadata/provenance APIs as owned cold inputs. After source admission, measured clones form finite shared catalog owners; each alias retires its data before independent manager-source custody. The detached policy preserves the primary logical key universe, exact provenance and contract/materialized-key metadata, while per-unit catalogs preserve their selected source overrides. Detached read leaves do not replace that logical catalog, and ordinary source/cache roots do not survive in the prepared manager. Payload acquisition remains on the existing prepared manager/read worker, separately from this metadata-only view.

The borrowed residency constructor exposes the same finite canonical unit closure
as the retained controller. Initial host/device publication selects roots from
the actual plan tier and supplies one caller-owned closure slot per declaration;
the shared fixed-point worker also includes alias owners assigned another tier.
Cold resolution borrows the constructor's existing alias validator and original
unit declarations, performs no catalog or native work, and grants no residency.
The source initializer prices and consumes the resulting per-tier populations.

Ready host-layerwise source construction now measures the retained neutral
controller, selected catalogs, detached encoded reads, immutable native host
buffers, static array aliases, and cached window metadata before their shared
source account is accepted. The constructor reads into the final native buffers
and publishes the same canonical per-tier closure used by ordinary residency.
The policy receives the detached selected catalog rather than retaining the
ordinary store's header/cache roots. Source-local file identity checks and
metadata/provenance remain unchanged.

The neutral residency lease accepts an additive owner-handle parameter, with
its existing weak-manager handle as the default. The MLX handle retains raw
source custody through manager weak aliases, host buffers, static native array
aliases, cached snapshot identities, and escaped construction failures; it
cannot acquire a new grant. Ordinary materialization retains its existing
worker and source behavior. This source join does not certify unrelated
transforming or direct-disk producers.

Rejected allocator, Metal Device and Scheduler initializers cancel only their
unadopted safe preparation shell before public error erasure. Their exact typed
native cause and original shared-source custody remain in the error; successful
initialization and native retirement ownership are unchanged. This uses owner
conversion rather than an unsafe cross-thread trait for native preparation nodes.

The runtime span plan distinguishes the actual forward count for generation
starting from prefill scores from the conservative equation record population.
The latter includes one extra decode for workspace coverage. Native host-copy
and neural submission validation consume the runtime count; the complete records
and their memory bounds remain available to scoring and verification consumers.

Ready-host request payload qualification authenticates the cached host snapshot
and operation-window owners against their original source manager and detached
