catalog. The source account owns their construction and aliases; the request
account owns its finite controller, transfer, binding and completion banks.
Ordinary lookalike metadata and disk descriptors cannot supply this qualification.

The runtime's `original-custody-test-support` feature exposes only a read-only
last-owner observation on an existing original metadata custody handle. Backend
conformance tests retain exactly one such handle after real completion, then
verify that every other alias of the same request has retired. Graph and Record
arenas, native buffer partitions, Scope/Roots/recovery and publication owners all
retain that raw custody. This detects request leaks independently of unrelated
pool refunds; it grants no completion or allocation authority and exposes no
Arc or Weak that could outlive the custody of its control allocation. Normal
backend dependencies do not enable this test support.

Original GPU consumer waits submit their paid command buffer inside the same authenticated WaitRecord dispatch before returning. This remains asynchronous: it performs no host wait and progresses no unrelated stream. The selected host/neural wait population already includes the full encoder-resource, receipt, handler and cleanup controls; the existing accepted-dispatch allocation path preserves the resident constructor bank. A failed commit remains owned by the same Record and receipt and is never treated as completion.

At a completed original layer-unit handoff, the existing unlocked payload-release
boundary destroys the module and then targets that transfer's application owner.
Only a settled, resolved transfer with no consumer children and sole application
ownership can bypass its deferred queue and drop its existing pin collection.
Shared, failed or unresolved owners retain their original deferral; no global
queue sweep, extra completion, allocation or admission credit is introduced. The
unit source recipe includes the fixed teardown transports. This permits the next
bounded layer window to evict the completed unit without retaining stale pins.

The foreground disk descriptor source uses the ready-host producer's shared
borrowed read-source plan and detached catalog owner. Its source account precedes
final catalog, unit-definition, canonical-index and exact read cloning. Descriptor
aliases keep that source custody without retaining ordinary provider/cache roots.
This metadata component neither reads tensor payloads nor activates disk execution;
read destinations, native transfers and publication must close their own bounds.

Cold descriptor consumers validate their exact unit identifier domain through the same neutral residency-controller checks as ordinary construction. The borrowed check preserves refusal priority without constructing a controller or granting source/native authority; alias, recipe and byte geometry remain separately validated.

The source-bound chat compiler lowers argument-free string `trim` through the same filter dispatch used by ordinary MiniJinja. Ordinary evaluation still resolves the environment's registered filter and argument rules. The bounded storage adapter shares the builtin Unicode whitespace boundary and retains borrowed slices, including flattened concatenations; measurement and filling use the same finite operand and atom populations before render admission. Filter arguments and other unclosed filters retain the typed source-profile refusal, without substituting an ordinary renderer or recognizing model-template literals.

Each original residency transfer retains its one prepaid consumer-observation
node inline, outside the shared resources that the observation keeps alive.
Nonblocking transfer polling retires that exact child only after successful
native completion and record retirement; pending work, contention and errors
retain the same node. This releases the consumer count without a global reaper
or a host wait at submission. Abandoned transfers preserve existing quarantine,
and a second original consumer is rejected before another submission.

Completed original transfer teardown consumes both the sole application node and
its independently boxed lease-return payload at the same unlocked boundary.
Native/consumer completion precedes both; their existing custody remains last.
Cold catalog and read authentication preserve `WeightRecipeError` as a typed
source-recipe cause instead of allocating a fictitious binding diagnostic.

Foreground disk materialization borrows a validated contiguous subset of the
exact detached source. The shared checkpoint reader validates every destination
before I/O and keeps source custody in an escaped failure. The backend prepares
all final host-source buffers under the exact accepted reservation and source
domain before reading. Before I/O, its copy adapter also authenticates the actual
manager/unit catalog and every empty canonical destination using the same
predicate as publication. Each copy array and event enters the existing transfer
recovery owner before fallible alias/publication work. Separate measured host,
page-rounded source backing, output and copy populations feed the existing
request admission; this component alone does not activate the disk policy.

The prepared foreground disk manager shares its detached descriptor/read/catalog owner with the existing immutable source constructor. Only the actual initial Host/Device canonical closure allocates source buffers or publishes completed static aliases; every other disk payload remains unread. Cold adoption authenticates the full offload plan, selected bindings, primary/override provenance and admitted streams before moving the manager through the existing loading transport. It creates neither a ready-host snapshot nor disk request authority. Public disk selection remains unchanged until finite per-attempt read destinations, Graph/Record/native workspace and original transfer dispatch are joined; the explicit cold provider handoff is available for that integration.


Foreground disk request storage uses the existing selected-operation bank. Each
actual canonical window retains an independent two-attempt unit reader, matching
the shared whole-unit retry limit; source-owned ready-host units do not consume
read slots. Cold planning retains only declaration ordinals, exact native read
layouts and admitted descriptor aliases. After the original request compares the
complete control amount, the same reservation precedes final buffer, vector and
slot construction. Each read consumes its slot before payload I/O, and failure
keeps the request and source custody through the unsuccessful prefix. Host source
backing is charged with the read constructor once, separately from native device
output births. The operation registry loans its exact accepted reservation along
with the authenticated current observer; neither that loan nor the storage bank
creates native permission. Complete disk activation still requires the independent
source/controller, Graph/Record and shared execution joins.

The foreground disk request join passes the model session's actual memory pool through
private native composition. Cold descriptor/allocator planning occurs only after
native inspection and policy loans end. Selected read slots are keyed by canonical
unit and retain the exact registered request reservation; a selected refusal never
enters the ordinary disk reader. Their outputs and completion events move into the
existing resident transfer owner before fallible publication, preserving the shared
completion and cancellation boundary. Source-controller/workspace and native fit
must all join before this route reports complete managed coverage.


The foreground disk native recipe consumes the accepted read-slot plan and retains the exact immutable descriptor owner. Its per-forward and request populations must match again when the operation bank is installed. The shared source-copy recipe still funds all canonical window copies, including initial host sources; the disk-only read subset never reduces that bound. Device logical outputs receive the existing per-birth native padding once, while prepaid disk source backing remains in the read-bank host/source charge. Copy Eval, aggregate completion, consumer waits, Record storage, Graph allocation populations and kernel attempts use the existing host worker machinery.

Foreground transfer borrows the registered request's actual reservation; it creates no new funding scope. Before payload I/O, the worker matches its guard to that reservation, its descriptor to the manager's retained source, its observer to the current registered native role, and every empty named destination to the manager/unit. Existing recovery resources retain both output and completion before fallible clone/publication. Fixed typed read/native/named/domain/cache errors retain custody without a recursive or boxed transfer error. This source and recipe join does not grant the unfinished disk controller, workspace, or public capability.


Foreground disk sources prepare dense telemetry groups, activity rows, mutex
backing and the controller Arc within the same accepted source constructor as
static native arrays and detached read/catalog metadata. Opaque controller
handles retain that source custody through policy aliases and completion guards.
Telemetry reads the authenticated neutral ledger through a borrowed iterator;
ordinary report construction and original execution share the same aggregation.

An original foreground policy uses its request-owned transfer/read bank and keeps
ordinary mutable dense-window vectors empty. Ordinary sessions and forks on the
same prepared source still use the existing scheduler; its window storage is
created for that session and dropped at the settled forward boundary. Exact
ordinary protection names are declared by the shared scheduler before the source
grant. Source-owned foreground window identity and canonical persistent-owner
rows are consumed without recreating catalog receipts. These source constructors
do not substitute for request read, native Graph, or Record admission.


Foreground disk workspace geometry and canonical parameter rows are constructed
once inside the admitted manager source owner. The backend borrows exact
retained descriptor metadata and the neutral controller's alias closure; it
shares the selected layout and operation windows without creating a legacy
disk activation receipt. Existing pinned Device backing is excluded only from
future materialization, while cross-unit disk owners remain covered and
persistent. Request source custody authenticates the same domain and source;
the already-bound native recipe and complete capacity gates remain separate.


The foreground disk source bank reserves finite metadata for each permitted attempt and a shared backing capacity for the maximum live canonical window, rather than constructing every forward's payload buffers in advance. Each selected read authenticates its source and both custody handles against the registered request, acquires the complete unit's actual page-rounded backing before allocation, and splits that charge into the final native source quotas. An immutable admitted allocator identity supplies a fresh thread-local borrower at consumption; this never initializes or promotes an ordinary allocator.

Within the existing safemlx unsafe boundary, a closed quota retirement callback can refund only its fixed byte permit before enqueuing the ordinary ownership node. PreparedInputAllocation frees physical backing before its quota block; HostTransferStorage's shared allocator pins the source quota through that destruction; GraphQuota frees its final arena before invoking the callback. The callback zeroes the permit before publication, so later queued destruction cannot refund twice, and runs no arbitrary destructor. Failed construction retains the exact unspent owner/permit. Request custody still outlives the counter/permit and queued node; the counter is not funding authority. Per-attempt metadata remains fully charged even when physical backing has recycled. Successful original window retirement observes Metal handler/receipt destruction before the published terminal frontier, allowing reuse without a global reaper. Device output copies and their existing Eval/Graph/Record ownership are unchanged. Private framework allocator internals remain the documented platform boundary.


Foreground disk request banks retain finite metadata per actual attempt while
final source-buffer construction is deferred to the consumed read. One exact
request-bound native retirement capacity covers the maximum canonical window,
including the permitted whole-unit retry. Every constructor/control remains
priced cumulatively. The shared original driver drains the previous transfer
before another window; native buffer handlers retire before terminal receipt
publication. Capacity is returned only by final native quota destruction, while
original Rust custody may remain queued. Neither an event observation nor a
custody clone grants reusable capacity, and no global reclamation is required.


The shared checkpoint encoded-read compiler also admits declared byte views, same-dtype casts, and axis permutations that preserve the relative order of all non-singleton dimensions. It proves this from the existing admitted metadata and validates the complete recipe byte count; equal shapes or element widths alone do not authorize a data permutation/conversion. These recipes reuse the same detached exact file ranges and fill final host-source backing directly, so foreground source capacity and native copy populations remain unchanged. No backend family or source-format branch participates in this decision. Arithmetic conversions and permutations that change byte order continue through their existing materialization mechanisms until their own admitted producers are joined.


Managed chat character-set trim reuses MiniJinja's ordinary Unicode scalar
membership/range helper and shared filter dispatch. The source compiler accepts
one borrowed text argument on a borrowed message field or literal, including
chained trims; both source and render plans price the actual operand and helper
controls before construction. No character vector, normalized string, or second
renderer is introduced. Character trimming of concatenations remains a typed
source-profile refusal because the allocation-free measurement pass retains only
whitespace boundaries for those values. Ordinary filter overrides, argument
conversion and safe-string propagation continue through their existing adapter.

General numeric tokenizer-config validation uses an owned/shared scalar parser
seam with ordinary serde_json conversion, boxed failure storage and qualified
float-roundtrip scratch. The source J account precedes those constructors; the
original finite-range validation and error ordering remain in the same parser.
Optional arbitrary-precision retained strings require their own producer.


An admitted input allocator may be borrowed during an active original role:
the existing native slot only attempts its mutex and validates the immutable
completed initializer identity before lending facts. Allocator initialization
still requires an empty submission context, and borrowing neither constructs a
fallback nor grants backing storage. Deferred foreground read attempts include
the C/native borrow frames and safe current-thread loan controls in their own
pre-admission host amount, separately from the retained source initializer.


The existing funded saved decoder/sampler/key copy worker now admits its measured
root-collector contribution before constructing the collector. The same checked
source-plus-two-results-per-operand plan supplies both the diagnostic amount and
the accepted account's exact Vec/Rc storage and fixed constructor/error controls.
A recoverable reserve refusal retires the host-only destination prefix, certifies
only the untouched native scope, and retains the original allocation cause with
that copy's custody. Native work, partial-result recovery, and the shared
SnapshotBudget's nonrefundable cumulative-copy accounting remain unchanged.

This closes the collector constructor, not complete managed snapshot admission.
The original public cursor still needs a coordinated decoder/stop/output copy
contract and a consumed snapshot-budget connection to saved native components
and fresh continuation. Complete original native copy fit must also cover its
clone/primitive, traversal, publication, and failure owners before that public
path can activate; the existing ordinary snapshot/restore/fork driver remains
the shared behavioral mechanism.


The shared continuation snapshot driver now consumes a prepared borrowed host-copy
contract for capture and restore. The ordinary facade binds its complete active
decoder, UTF-8 assembly, stop/parser frontier, canonical cursor, semantic delivery
prefix, prompt and snapshot metadata through that contract. Source inspection
and scalar identity selection allocate no destination; the existing SnapshotBudget
reservation precedes metadata formatting and every host destination copy. Restore
also prepares the prompt before native exchange, leaving host installation as
moves. Failed copies still consume cumulative copy allowance, and restore never
rewinds delivery sequence, epoch, transport, or capture consumption.

The contract is a logical copy transaction, not a new native or physical-memory
grant. Existing ordinary capture and restore callbacks delegate to the same
worker. An original fixed decoder/stop/sequence provider must additionally bind
its actual retained sources to an independently funded destination, preserve
its complete progress and terminal-text state, and compose complete native
copy/resume roles before a public managed snapshot can activate. Current original
provider custody is not permission to allocate a second mutable provider.


The neutral background prefetch lifecycle accepts a concrete move-only failure type while preserving the ordinary String interface. The MLX adapter now retains its actual residency/source error through demand and cancellation, and the concrete operation lives directly in the worker thread instead of an erased closure Arc. Typed panic payloads use a safe neutral mutex wrapper; no native observer is transported to the worker. The existing fixed ordinal FIFO, coalescing and generation policy remain shared. All discarded typed failures leave the lifecycle mutex before destruction, including cancellation's sorted first-error drain and completion/rollback failure paths.

This used transport prerequisite does not grant original-background readiness. Worker/channel/thread/synchronization/error-storage construction, request-bound read-slot jobs, host-ledger publication, and capacity covering real host lookahead/cancellation must still be supplied under the existing source/request owners before background options can activate. Demand-side device copy remains in the registered native role.

Fixed collector exhaustion reports a neutral `WorkingMemoryError::CollectorCapacity` with the actual collector kind and occupied/consumed slots against prepared capacity. It does not fabricate a native failure, grow a constructor, or grant another attempt. MLX Work retains its first concrete collection/publication/certification error and moves that owner to the first returning caller; a separate permanent failed bit prevents extraction from reopening collection, publication, or certification. Internal preparation observation puts its exact error back instead of discarding it. Existing native roots, refused inventory values, and source/control custody keep their prior ownership and drop ordering. Actual `sizeof` control queries include the new state and error transports.


Managed chat tokenizer-config numbers use the same pinned serde_json scalar
parser as ordinary config loading. Cold borrowed JSON validation exposes only
actual numeric slices and quotes the dependency-owned private error allocation
and scalar controls. The source compiler invokes numeric parsing after its
existing J admission, before template construction or deferred selection errors.
Successful scalar results own no heap payload; the first numeric failure retains
the original typed serde error and source allowance through teardown. Config
maps and numeric strings are never reconstructed. The float-roundtrip producer
reserves the ordinary digit scratch to the token length and derives two lexical
Bigint backings from the owning float/cached-exponent limits. The same exact
iterative multiplication and limb-shift workers prevent temporary product
allocations or growth within this profile; conversion and rounding are shared
with ordinary parsing. The source J account includes these synchronous buffers
and controls before invoking the parser. Scratch retires before success/error
returns, while an escaping error retains the existing source custody. This
qualifies the real facade feature union without disabling float_roundtrip or
preserve_order. Optional arbitrary-precision Number string ownership remains a
separate unfinished producer with a typed pre-admission refusal.

Settlement callbacks retain the first owned publication or certification failure in the work owner. Infallible completion callbacks preserve its source and custody for the next fallible caller, while a permanent fence prevents subsequent work after the cause has been consumed. They neither replace it with a generic fence nor allocate a new diagnostic owner.


The retained generation provider has a prepared host-state copy mechanism. Core
owns borrowed lifecycle reassembly (committed prefix, preparation phase and finish
reason); the runtime checks its concrete provider and the original consumer type,
then independently admits its destination through the existing pending account
and ticket. The source request guard and the destination ticket occupy distinct
private ownership variants. No source account is reused as destination credit,
and the copied provider creates no native scope or fresh request authority.

The text-owned decoder and stop workers copy their full fixed buffers and
pointer-free progress under that destination account. Tokenizer and literal-stop
programs retain their exact original source owners and nonce; source programs are
not recompiled or replaced. Partial allocation errors retain their original
TryReserveError and destination custody. Account refusal remains a typed,
allocation-free host-admission error. Token-result aliases retain the independent
copy account after the mutable provider and original request retire.

The private retained consumer adapter composes this worker as PreparedTextHostCopy
and preserves its failed/finish flags. It is ready for the same nonrefundable
SnapshotBudget transaction consumed by ordinary capture/restore. This does not
activate public managed snapshots: original capture still needs its complete
native/controller saved-state and fresh-resume join in place of the ordinary
host-preparation and Unquoted native branch. Unique caller-owned compatibility
decoder programs also need an independent source-clone producer; their missing
copy profile remains unknown. These are unfinished integrations, not model limits.

Model and sampled-output completion recheck retained publication failures after retiring their final native recovery scope. The first owned callback cause enters the existing cached observation before another decode can begin; a later generic poisoned-session or account fence cannot hide that earlier failure.


Prepared disk host results use the same opaque named host owner as ready-host source copies. The admitted per-attempt read layout owns canonical name bytes, final row buffers and each actual shared control before construction. Only completely initialized immutable buffers become host results. Request-born host aliases retain raw original metadata custody after their shared storage; each native source buffer separately retains its accepted live-capacity permit and original request through physical backing retirement. The shared original copy helper authenticates the current native observer and arms both output and event in existing transfer recovery before a fallible alias or destination publication. This adds no source selection, native authority or background admission. Background worker birth, cancellation/result rows and lookahead live-capacity composition remain separate owning producers.


The neutral prefetch worker's notification uses its existing lifecycle Mutex/Condvar and fixed wake/shutdown fields. Its ordinary and selected FIFO share this same executor; no dynamically growing notification channel remains. Logical worker exit wakes waiting consumers but does not certify physical thread or native completion. Nonjoining ordinary Drop retains its operation until that worker returns. Source-funded background construction still needs its own thread lifetime, finite payload/result/cancellation storage and accepted lookahead capacity; the fixed wake is not an admission or adoption mechanism.


A prepared source-backed device value retains its real immutable host source in its existing canonical Array cell. Cross-unit aliases retain the same cell and source; the source is removed with the last device/canonical alias, not by promotion into Host residency. Borrowed manager inventory exposes those actual host owners alongside their arrays so the shared publication validates both physical identities and capacities. Canonical cell layout and fixed source-row population are measured before admission. This explicit owner witness does not itself mint a prepaid source origin or certify a background worker.


Managed plain snapshot capture borrows the same completed generation machine as
ordinary continuation capture. The portable snapshot transaction reserves its
logical count/storage/copy budget with an inline pending lease; only after the
actual retained-provider host destination accepts its separate physical account
does it allocate the shared reservation lease. The provider prices that lease,
the complete cursor/decoder/stop copy, the enclosing snapshot/error controls, and
its payload-free destination custody. Native decoder/sampler/pending-token copies
consume the existing independently bounded saved-component mechanism. Partial
host/native failures retain their own custody, while failed logical attempts
release retention without refunding cumulative copy work. No unquoted host token
or old request authority substitutes for these destination admissions.

The resulting managed plain snapshot keeps immutable tokenizer/stop source
aliases and independent native/host state after its source request retires. Its
read-only core source carries the existing run identity but creates no detached
driver identity. This gateway captures completed decode/terminal boundaries;
pending prepared prompts and original observation checkpoints retain explicit
unsupported results until their bounded copy producers exist. Capture does not
activate restore/fork or issue a fresh prediction: those still require the actual
fresh-resume and independent destination-session contracts.

The MLX gateway's original preparation hook deliberately remains unknown until
its projection/registry/program metadata producers have complete bounds. Both
the facade plan and shared runtime gate query that owning hook before any
original copy. The host account will cover the returned exact preparation
amount; a closed retained-error wrapper keeps that same account with any escaped
native planner/error prefix. This hook does not certify the native implementation
merely because the shared capture path is now connected.

HostPreparationAuthority now keeps a private exact-type retirement function with
its erased shared owner. Final release downcasts and uses Arc::into_inner before
dropping the payload-free custody token, so an account cannot refund the same
shared shell before its allocation/header retires. No raw strong/weak handle is
exported; cloning remains allocation-free. Original provider preparation uses
the owning retention_bytes query for this actual shell and retirement frame.


Native existing-array projection now uses one sorted Vec row representation for
both borrowed and retained witness inventories. Known physical identities occupy
a sorted prefix; unknown witnesses remain distinct and can never certify complete
coverage. The first witness and exact portable root for each allocation are
preserved across aliases. Finite snapshot planners reserve the source-count row
capacity once and refuse a new root/unknown witness before it exceeds that count.
The owning ProjectionInventoryLayout includes both real Vec extents during the
borrowed-to-native-clone handoff, rather than treating that safe conversion as an
in-place type change. Saved sampling/decoder copy preparation consumes this same
constructor and reserves its exact operand-vector count. Portable metadata roots,
workspace graph/registry/program owners and native clone shells remain separately
priced producers; the inventory change alone does not qualify original snapshot
preparation or remove the native gateway's unknown hook.


The shared isolated-copy planner validates exact borrowed roots directly against
its ordered source slots and compares each destination with the retained source
and previous destination slice. Its closing buffer reserves the checked 2N
extent once; it no longer builds three additional owning identity sets. This
preserves duplicate source requests, zero-byte root identity, and independent
destinations. The private operation trace and report still require their own
preparation bounds before original native snapshot admission can be enabled.
Pending-token validation now borrows the native descriptor under the existing
inspection loan rather than allocating a shape snapshot.


The foreground disk source path now uses the existing neutral host-source construction/publication transaction with a separately selected live backing peak. The immutable source descriptor owns the stable producer identity used by both cold quotation and request installation. The accepted source bank binds that selection once to the actual native retirement-capacity owner before any child banks split. Each constructor authenticates and consumes exactly one split permit from that owner; cumulative constructor and publication storage stays separate from the reusable physical backing allowance.

The neutral transaction supports an owning begin/finish boundary. Begin debits constructor storage and moves the source receipt plus permit into the native quota before allocating final host backing. Pending results expose only the selected producer's unforgeable initialization owner. The existing detached batch reader validates all destinations and preserves its grouped shard I/O and failure ordering. Finish requires the actual immutable host observation before publishing and attaching the canonical prepaid-host origin. Cancellation and failures retain each constructed prefix and its custody; native physical release refunds the permit before queued arbitrary owner destruction, without refunding cumulative constructor storage.

The device publication retains the real host owner and validates host/array identity and capacity. An explicit source inventory may reuse an already canonical immutable prepaid-host row only for the same original publisher. A missing row remains ordinarily charged; neither a raw key nor equal bytes creates prepaid coverage. MLX Array backing classification and ordinary checkpoint/source behavior remain unchanged. This closes the selected foreground source-origin accounting join; background worker admission remains separate.

Workspace source registration has a finite constructor separate from allocation
authority. The neural metadata crate owns a Vec-backed borrowed-root selection,
its requested constructor layout and fixed validation causes. Ordinary selection
shares that validator and preserves first-occurrence root order. Runtime owns
physical-key/root bijection validation, input-count reserves and the existing-only
registry pin. Its source-count layout qualifies the pinned host allocator before
claiming Vec/Rc/Arc extents; provider key payloads, comparisons and input-iterator
construction remain separate source facts.

Prepared binding moves provider keys and preserves sorted physical-key root order.
No BTree map/set scratch is constructed by this route. Ordinary public storage
pins retain their pre-lock key Clone callbacks and share the same all-before-commit
registry validation with prepared owned inputs. Every capacity, missing identity,
overflow and domain-ceiling check precedes owner increments; provider keys retire
outside Usage and no new physical bytes, namespace, scope or account is created.
These metadata owners must remain under the enclosing admitted planner lifetime.
Their layout does not qualify native snapshot capture or the independent private
copy trace/program/report constructors.


Snapshot source pinning now carries originally constructed decoder tables and
prepared-input descriptions in a finite source container. Each table validates
its completed constructor and pool before being retained; each prepared input
validates its existing original residence. Duplicate aliases consume one row.
Association with an existing-only registration validates every source and rejects
overlap with ordinary keys before publication. Reported capacities do not create
new charges. The container retains the enclosing accepted host-preparation
authority after its Vec and source tokens, including construction failures.

The shared snapshot driver passes that existing host authority to the same
paired native-copy worker. Prepared storage-pin groups preserve it through nested
pair/aggregate wrappers and quarantine. Their closed Arc retirement releases
the shared shell before child pins/Vecs and then the authority. This is lifetime
propagation only: it neither supplies a byte grant nor proves an arbitrary group
was included in a plan. The MLX original preparation hook still requires the
complete collector/projection/private-copy-program bound before activation.

Saved decoder inventory construction uses the existing retained-state and idle
auxiliary visitors for both its count-only pass and final finite collector.
Original snapshot preparation retains the actual decoder owner and source pool,
counts all emitted rows before construction, and prices the existing Vec inventory
plus prepared native clone handles. Aliases may lower the final retained count;
they never permit another unplanned allocation attempt. Ordinary saved copies use
the same visitors directly instead of constructing and merging two inventories.

The finite inventory distinguishes accepted text metadata custody from snapshot
host preparation custody. Both validate the same source attachments against their
actual pool. Snapshot custody only retains the independently accepted host account;
all native publication entrypoints reject that variant before registration or
attachment. Rows and unfilled/filled clone shells retire before their final host
token, including failed construction. The source-bound plan exposes its known
collector contribution for aggregate admission; no byte grant is inferred from a
lifetime token. The managed native snapshot hook remains unavailable until the
complete source visitors, projection/context, private copy trace and native roles
are qualified and their amounts are composed before this constructor runs.


The neural isolated-copy preparation can now use a finite metadata producer before native snapshot construction. An allocation-free accumulator accepts borrowed layout views one source at a time and queries the retained WorkspaceFactMechanisms through the same isolated_copy program used by construction. This avoids requiring a WorkspaceContext or projected tensor merely to quote the private copy metadata. After host admission, exact imported source selection and actual populations are validated against the prequoted layout. Fixed fact destinations populate a flat graph, which uses the existing WorkspaceReportWorkspace equations; final operation/layout/assumption metadata is moved into its diagnostic report without ordinary mechanism fallback or report cloning. Source projection, selected-provider custody, allocator-private overhead and native copy execution remain separately owned and priced by the caller. The compatibility preparation path remains available, and missing facts retain incomplete diagnostics rather than enabling a native snapshot capability.


The owning residency inventory and borrowed cold visitor both enumerate immutable host sources retained by device publication cells. A request-born foreground disk source does not become a Host-tier cache entry: its actual host owner accompanies the device array into publication, where the existing paired identity/capacity check and canonical prepaid source transaction apply. This closes the collection join without weakening native backing classification or charging the same source backing again.

Snapshot source projection now has a cold component plan over the actual borrowed decoder operands, sampler key and pending token descriptors. Native rank/dtype/backing inspection creates no shape copies or native handles; the plan prices the source context, imported roots, logical shapes, finite projection rows and fixed descriptor-clone controls. Its admitted host path consumes the same source selection through shared native identity and portable import constructors, retaining partial-failure custody with closed error ownership. Physical source aliases remain shared and unknown backing refuses before construction. This component does not include retained-source inventory/pins, registered binding or the private copy program, and does not enable the original snapshot preparation hook by itself.

Snapshot source association now has an owning finite pin plan derived from the
actual retained census. The plan prices source-carrier slots, entry/key storage,
the final registration and ordinal arrays, and their closed failure transports.
Construction uses the existing all-before-commit registry validator with moved
keys and a qualified exact reserve; it creates neither a namespace nor missing
physical entries. Original table/input tokens retain their genuine source account
while the separate host preparation authority covers only these new constructors.

Copy-source wrapper populations follow the same native Registered/Funded table
branches as host_copy. Empty registered tables count; funded tables do not create
a registered pin. The actual neutral two-source, optional-third-source and grouped
joins use finite counted vectors when their complete source carries preparation
custody. Ordinary joins retain their existing behavior. Quarantine retains this
same closed bundle; its already-priced scope wrapper is not charged a second time.
The source-bound collector query composes this pin plan and the source-selected
wrapper layout before aggregate host admission. Registered table binding and
initialization, grouped progress/scope vectors, and native copy arenas remain
separate unfinished planner contributions; this change enables no native snapshot
hook and claims no complete copy fit.

Ordinary execution on a manager retaining detached foreground disk descriptors consumes those same validated reads into final host-transfer buffers, then uses the existing device transfer, alias closure, completion and publication workers. The metadata-only detached catalog is never used to reacquire payloads or reopen artifacts. This ordinary allocation path grants no managed request capacity or original storage authority; managed execution still requires its separately admitted read slots and capacity.


Managed snapshot pre-grant logical estimates use the neutral
`TextSnapshotBackend::original_snapshot_estimates` contract. Its default is
unknown and it cannot delegate to ordinary estimators, which may allocate host
inventories or diagnostics. Original capture consumes the three complete fixed
facts before its nonrefundable logical reservation and independent host grant.
Missing facts produce the existing typed `UnknownEstimate`; this contract is
neither a physical-copy certificate nor submission authority.

The MLX implementation preserves the ordinary logical cost equations while
borrowing actual decoder arrays through direct layer visitors and no-hooks
native descriptor loans. The shared replicated driver adds the same retained
prompt identity and control metadata. Session/target/policy checks construct no
owned diagnostic, and paged-cache auxiliary costs use a nonblocking loan and the
ordinary catalog summation. Sampling retains the shared fixed-history equation;
pending decode input uses the same scalar condition from borrowed shape facts.
Ordinary support diagnostics and snapshot estimates retain their existing path.
Pending original prefill and incomplete physical/native preparation remain
separate unfinished producers. Native/TLS control qualification, complete
constructor/error populations, private-copy fit and actual completion owners
must still join before enabling the original saved-components preparation hook.

The adjoining native preparation-size hook also returns fixed neutral
`WorkingMemoryError` causes. Both facade and runtime map these directly to host
admission refusal before any backend error erasure or diagnostic allocation.
Backend failures from actual construction remain behind accepted host custody.


### Finite snapshot table construction

The runtime's closed decoder table-copy worker now has a finite preparation component. It binds original reset tables through their authenticated existing source carrier; actual ordinary sources retain the existing-only registration path. Both paths retain the enclosing host preparation, and an original-source refusal cannot fall back to ordinary registration.

Prepared destination metadata and its independent diagnostic identity retain host preparation through escaped aliases. Registry keys remain payload-free. Private table and attachment mutexes are initialized before sharing and their concrete PAL allocations enter the same cold layout query. The existing decoder copy scope continues to own only its exact inline slot payload and value temporaries.

Grouped preparation prices its actual counted child, progress, hold, source and scope arrays. Taken children retain progress construction independently of the coordinator. Destination identity creation occurs before copy-account admission, so exhaustion cannot quarantine an untouched native destination. These are shared table constructors, not a second decoder copy engine or a complete native snapshot capability; account, numerical execution, recovery and publication remain separately composed.


The saved-component host preparation now retains one borrowed finite component
plan for native projection, existing-root registration, the complete source
inventory and its pin wrappers, and the shared isolated-copy report. The same
plan consumes those constructors under host preparation custody and supplies its
quoted flat-copy layout to the existing two-operation copy program. Physical
aliases remain distinct requested copies; only their source roots are deduplicated.
The ordinary worker retains its existing adapter and copy semantics.

The cold inventory query reuses native state and slot-metadata collection before
backend error erasure. Session boundary and native metadata refusals retain fixed
causes without constructing diagnostic IDs or exception boxes. Saved sources use
one borrowed metadata/array visitor for counting and filling; cache census reuses
the actual nonblocking manager traversal and preserves incomplete worker evidence.
The component sum is not total snapshot admission: table/account constructors,
remaining enclosing/native copy controls and their actual authority joins must be
covered before enabling the original native snapshot preparation hook.


The backend now lends the saved-copy worker an `OriginalCopyEnvironment` from its
actual admitted execution/source stream owners and same-domain allocator
initializer. This is an immutable, fixed-error query: it neither clones native
handles nor enters a new scope, initializes a runtime, or reserves copy bytes.
The consumer revalidates the allocator when borrowing its input runtime, uses the
model's existing completed runtime witness, and separately admits the native copy.
The environment cannot promote an ordinary predecessor or establish source
quiescence. Its borrowed stream owners remain alive throughout the caller's loan;
completion and saved output still need their independent copy-account custody.


Prepared snapshot copy account constructors now have a neutral, side-effect-free
`WorkspaceCopyAccountLayout` contribution. The retained single-table, grouped or
stateless source selects the actual sampler/table/native scope topology. The
existing host preparation query includes the execution identity Arc, one fixed
account node, closed shared copy owner and named commit/retirement/scope controls;
the accepted host path consumes that same topology before these constructors.
The existing numerical copy account still performs its own source, capacity and
copy-budget admission. The constructor contribution changes neither B nor the
native Graph/Record limits. Table/group vectors, source pins, projection rows,
destination attachments and native work keep their distinct owning producers.

`WorkspaceCopyRetention` shares the existing copy execution and funding run with
native resource owners; it has no native scope, source-credit or budget methods.
Its last closed Arc alias deallocates the shared shell before the execution and
run retire. Prepared execution clones and the ledger's execution Weak each keep
their host preparation alive. Terminal account retirement takes that token out,
deallocates the node and Weak outside Usage, then releases the token; the existing
retirement guard drains any resulting terminal host account. This remains active
when the caller has dropped every external pool handle. Abandoned native scopes
preserve their existing quarantine and nonrefund semantics. These constructor
facts alone do not activate original native snapshot capture.


Saved native snapshot source preparation shares fixed cache validators with the
ordinary decoder-copy adapters. Its cold construction query borrows actual
sampler, decoder, target and idle-authority facts without formatting backend
errors, acquiring a submission lease or constructing table bindings. Full
request, frontier and receipt authorization remains mandatory in the existing
post-admission driver. The host-selected path queries the actual destination
slot peak directly, then constructs each prepared table binding once at copy
admission. Prepared plans and escaped errors retain the closed host preparation
authority after their metadata. This source component does not establish native
execution, recovery or full original snapshot qualification on its own.


The host-prepared saved decoder and paired sampling result retain preparation
through their actual returned owner blocks. The frozen decoder's existing closed
Rc retires before its ordinary-retirement node is queued; the node destroys its
Box before native/metadata payloads and the final host token. Paired saved-data
and resume consumers share an opaque `CopiedTextComponentsOwner` rather than a
raw Rc/Weak, so the last pair block is deallocated before payload destruction can
release preparation. The source query prices these two Rc blocks, the existing
one-node retirement constructor and named return/provenance controls. Existing
source identities are shared, while table, sampler, numerical and account payloads
keep their original independent charges. No native snapshot capability changes.



The MLX saved-copy native producer uses the existing neutral isolated-copy
program and the existing original Scope/Graph/Record machinery. An allocation-free
descriptor census derives its finite Contiguous, eager-copy, handle and nested
completion populations. The consumed plan constructs native quota, buffer,
pipeline and failure owners only after the registered copy admission, retaining
the same accounting-only WorkspaceCopyRetention through actual native aliases.
Each Contiguous root completes under the original bank before the shared eager
typed deep-copy initializer reads it; no second family copy equation or runtime
initializer is introduced. The physical Metal birth bound composes by maximum
with the shared numerical copy bound, while constructor H remains separate.
Source registration, finite destination publication and the facade's complete
snapshot capability remain enclosing mechanisms, not consequences of this
native component's layout query.


Saved-copy completion uses fixed status errors in the shared session finalizer. It preserves the original copy failure without allocating a redundant diagnostic string; failure or unobservability never releases a pending source or submission lease. Native settlement and resource retirement remain independent requirements.


The host-selected saved decoder copy composes its actual borrowed-source projection,
registered storage, finite copy program, table/account constructors, native copy
plan and destination publication plan before construction. The native physical
requirement joins the numerical copy requirement by their maximum; only the
positive difference enters the existing copy account reserve. Recovery retains
all source handles, but publication visits copied logical operands once, including
compressed storage aliases. A local construction guard retires the native bank
before recovery on both normal return and unwind, while the execution budget
survives destination publication. An empty native program uses the same host copy
and finite publication without opening a native scope. This caller composition
does not by itself enable the public original snapshot preparation hook.


### Finite saved-copy destination publication

Saved-copy publication has a distinct finite origin in the existing canonical
storage publisher. Its prepared transaction authenticates the actual admitted
`WorkspaceCopyCustody` against the same `WorkingMemoryFundingScope` before
constructor allocations, and again before canonical commit. Completed array
identity/capacity and destination child-table metadata debit that copy's existing
B account. H retains the source-count vectors, registry nodes, shared output
registrations, attachment slots and failure controls; it creates no native
partition or original-text permission. The source-only snapshot collector still
refuses publication. Ordinary publication retains its existing behavior through
the same validation, commit and attachment workers.

The backend prepares one inspection clone per actual destination operand, one
finite inventory, and one terminal publication transaction before native work.
It checks native budget witnesses against each inventory row both before commit
and immediately before attachment. Prepared child metadata reserves its actual
single attachment slot under H and uses the existing lifecycle gate and provider
worker. Construction failure cancels only the untouched copy scope; failed native
or publication prefixes retain their original recovery and funding. Canonical
registry/output/namespace shells retain H until after their allocation and keys
retire. Successful publication preserves the existing explicit unlocked backend
retirement boundary for its remaining non-native collector owner.

The cold `SnapshotPublicationPlan` adds only incremental finite constructor and
attachment amounts; the existing `RootCollectorPlan` continues to price the common
FundedWork/submission/capture controls once in B. Source and destination counts
come from the selected decoder representation. Compressed destination storage
and logical views intentionally alias, so publication uses its logical operand
visitor while source recovery retains the complete source visitor. This component
alone does not activate the original saved-copy hook or supply native completion.


MLX now supplies the original saved-components preparation hook from that consumed
source-bound aggregate for no pending input, one decode token, or one complete
prepared plain-text token matrix. The shared
original snapshot driver admits the reported host preparation before entering the
same bounded copy worker, and its logical SnapshotBudget reservation still precedes
independent destination admission. Unqualified source/native facts return fixed
neutral refusal before construction. Plain pending prefill uses the shared exact
quote/request/chunk binding validator and requires the unadvanced opening plus
one complete integer token matrix with no media, metadata, or extents. Its copied
matrix enters the same projection, native copy and publication workers once;
encoding is not repeated. The logical estimate shares the ordinary prompt
inventory with borrowed descriptor facts. Saved prompt geometry and cache
identity remain immutable data, with no source quote or request transferred.
The pending-kind tag prevents even a one-token prompt from entering the existing
committed-token resume worker. This activates immutable capture only; it does not
grant restore, fork, a fresh generation request, or snapshot-copy admission.



The admitted disk read descriptor contains only transferable immutable source/request ownership and finite metadata. Mutable native host-transfer transactions are constructed and retired on the thread executing the shared read worker; only frozen attached buffers or precise custody-bearing errors leave it. Its cold layout prices those execution-local controls and allocations before admission. This typed boundary supplies neither physical thread construction authority nor a background lookahead allowance, which remain separate prerequisites.


Saved pending-token resume preparation borrows fixed native descriptor facts and retains no shape allocation before host admission. The existing shared scalar copy/reshape/cast program gains an original-mode finite collector refusal and a second genuine nested completion for its tail. Its source-derived native population composes with the fresh resume request's Graph, Record, source, pipeline and physical-backing admission; it supplies no saved-account grant. Ordinary scheduling remains shared and original resume remains gated until the fresh request and publication producers are joined.

Complete paired snapshot source validation now distinguishes the accepted host-copy handoff from standalone native-component copying. A paired source retains the enclosing host preparation token through every source revalidation, and permits an original sequence only after its bank has moved into the facade-owned sequence. Pending banks and capture ledgers still refuse. Standalone native array copying keeps its existing sequence rejection. This prevents the former blanket sequence guard from rejecting a complete independently funded facade snapshot; it grants no resumed execution authority.

Each original isolated-copy operand now establishes its one real nested completion and obtains a borrowed completed view before the eager deep copy. Destination inspection uses the same read-only completion witness. It does not call Array::deep_clone through into_evaluated or schedule another evaluated call on the already completed result; those redundant scopes exceeded the finite single-operand tracking population. Ordinary calls retain their existing evaluation behavior. This keeps native work equal to the source-derived completion recipe instead of enlarging quotas to hide duplicate work.


Original managed snapshot restoration and branching use the same core fresh-resume
preparation/readiness machine and the same controlled/plain cursor. A cold
backend hook supplies fixed constructor and logical facts from the immutable
saved pair and exact controller. The concrete runtime host provider independently
admits its destination, then the backend must admit the complete fresh execution
and native roles for the newly issued core context. Saved-copy custody and host
preparation lifetime do not authorize that run. Default original resume hooks
refuse without invoking the ordinary allocating planner. The copied cursor remains
original after its sequence has been extracted; restore never reclassifies it as
an ordinary sequence. Native original resume qualification remains a separately
consumed backend producer, not an inference loop or a family policy in runtime.

Resume consumes the immutable snapshot's existing cumulative SnapshotBudget.
Pending logical reservations allocate no lease shell before host admission. The
same retained-generation provider account publishes and owns the closed lease
before constructing any copied payload, so both machine host custody and escaped
token/text output aliases retain it. The lease owns only the scalar budget, never
its physical account. Its shell and payload retire before the provider's physical
ticket; no independent return value can release the branch charge early. Budget
and lease sharing use closed Arc owners for Send/Sync output storage. The budget's
caller-owned constructor eagerly initializes its scalar mutex before any cold
reservation. Dropping failed or completed destinations refunds retained counts,
never cumulative copy usage. Source token IDs, decoder histories/progress, pending
stop state, terminal delivery status and remaining output allowance remain under
the existing shared host-copy contract. The facade validates loaded tokenizer
identity and permits shortening, but not extending, the saved output allowance.



Original saved-text resume reuses the architecture-owned borrowed-sampler equation driver with an actual equation trace observer. The MLX backend derives copy/preparation populations from immutable saved array descriptors and composes them with the selected native equation/sampling recipe, preserving decoder/key source credit through the same sealed fresh request span. A retained-tokenizer controller constructor authenticates the original source/filter and requested maximum without issuing another sequence owner. Native Graph/Record/physical/pipeline/preparation banks come from the fresh request, never the snapshot account. The copy physical population replaces only its already-priced numerical term's required padding; cumulative native generation replacement remains in the existing named span mechanism. The public original resume route remains gated until its finite cold metadata and actual prompt/table/publication producers consume these owners.


Saved-resume source metadata can consume the same finite source-census, projection, moved-key registration and isolated-copy constructors as saved capture. The complete registered source contains decoder, random-key and pending-token roots. Only decoder and key operands enter the sealed credited copy program; pending-token isolation/reshape/cast remains a full numerical contribution. The finite constructor retains the accepted host preparation through the registered complete-source carrier and through escaped errors. Ordinary resume keeps its existing worker. This component is not a complete host-preparation bound: the dense destination-state projection, its subsequent shared equation trace and enclosing quote constructors require separately closed layouts before original resume admission can be enabled.


Workspace state projection stores architecture-declared fixed roles in a finite sorted key vector with a parallel mutable-value vector. The declared role universe bounds both destinations and the import duplicate-mark vector. The ordinary and prepared projection paths share this worker; iteration remains in role order, unknown/duplicate/missing roles retain their previous refusal precedence, and fixed dimensions are resolved through the existing borrowed dimension kernel before shape/dtype comparison. Saved-resume source preparation includes this policy-derived component. It does not claim the remaining state-table, equation-operation or trace/report constructors as covered.


Saved pending text now uses one source-bound isolate/reshape/optional-cast program
for both committed decode scalars and complete `[1,N]` prefill matrices. Immutable
pending-kind metadata prevents a one-position prompt from being mistaken for a
decode token. The native mechanisms validate exact geometry, dtype and completed
backing before work; copy and cast populations scale with actual logical bytes.
The packed text cast shares its numerical and host predicate, and prices the
whole logical output. The composed native request still owns its graph, record,
physical-buffer and recovery populations.

Runtime prompt completion can protect one prepared text part matching the fresh
request's exact input count and valid chunk size. It neither derives token values
nor supplies cache identity. The MLX composition preserves saved prompt identity
and chunk coordinates. Original pending-input host metadata retains the accepted
host preparation alongside its numerical payload and uses closed shared ownership:
the last alias retires the Arc allocation before the payload and its host authority.
The additional cold control query covers that concrete shell and fixed transports;
the existing independently protected part/move payload is not charged twice.
This producer does not by itself qualify fresh resume's complete planning metadata.


Fresh original saved-state resume uses the existing dense decoder host worker
under its genuine prompt claim and new request funding. Its cold table query
covers actual source binding, per-table prepared metadata, ordered group arrays,
source-pin wrappers and finite host-registration/attachment constructors; dense
payload P, pending input construction and native Q work remain distinct owning
contributions. The shared dense initializer retains the prepared identity through
partial finish and uses it only for the exact completed table. Registered and
funded source branches retain their actual source identity without creating new
source credit. Group children remain ordered, and only the outer table returns
the original prompt completion.

Prepared dense host transfer uses the same canonical registry and exact protected
host-hold debit as ordinary transfer. Its registration, one-row batch, namespace
and attachment destination are allocated under the accepted constructor lifetime
before any attachment or Usage lock. All identity/capacity/origin checks precede
counter commit; linking the prepared row then allocates nothing. Unused namespace
and rejected prefix owners retire outside both locks. This table is an ordinary
funded destination of the fresh request, not an original-source or native prepaid
origin. Numerical publication separately consumes that request's original native
bank and already prepared Work inventory. The erased installed control-state box
and pending host input have separate constructor/retention plans; table metadata
custody alone does not certify their enclosing allocation shells.


Saved-resume host preparation composes the actual dense-table constructor controls, pending-input source controls and fixed admission-owner controls with the finite source/copy metadata. Original preparation obtains the dense initialization peak directly from the borrowed selected source through the same fixed dense dispatch; it does not construct and discard an ordinary source binding merely to obtain that peak. These host controls remain separate from protected table payload and native/request budgets. Ordinary resume preserves its prior construction path. The full original resume hook still requires the remaining equation trace metadata producer.



Original saved-source resume prompt execution consumes the same newly admitted text request and named Prompt/Sampling roles as ordinary preparation. The native adapter reuses the existing prepared Recovery, finite Graph/Record banks, resident nested completion and shared dense/key/pending copy workers. It binds the exact registered saved source before native construction and publishes completed destination arrays/table metadata through the fresh request's finite work collector. Retained source views determine the finite recovery Rc/Vec producer; cold layout and construction share checked root arithmetic and construction rechecks the native recipe population. The original branch uses completed witnesses without repeated evaluation. Its resident construction bank retires before outer recovery seal on success, failure or unwind. Sampling resumes the actual saved host state and key under its consumed fresh role. Fresh H follows returned pending parts and escaping preparation errors; old snapshot accounts remain source custody only. Complete finite equation metadata preparation is still required before the public original resume cold hook is enabled.


Fresh saved-input native population binding now validates the actual pending position
count against the request. The same ordered decoder/key/pending census handles
scalar decode and complete prepared prefill matrices, including the full signed
cast backing. Runtime admission includes all cached plus input positions. Prompt
construction preserves the saved cache identity and selects a valid chunk no
larger than the saved chunk or the caller's requested limit. The key and pending
trace roots use their fixed optional/array containers rather than growable Vecs.
The nonzero matrix mechanism check passed for signed and unsigned token sources
with full output equality and actual MLX backing coverage. This does not qualify
unmigrated planning metadata or enable an unsupported public resume hook.


Original saved-state resume prices the actual returned native control-slot type
at its typed adapter. The completed published state is moved through the shared
portable origin/layout binding worker and boxed as the same
`ReplicatedTextControlState<S>` used by ordinary exchange. Its enclosing native
slot retains fresh host-construction custody after both the erased Box and the
native memory-owner list. A provisional prompt returns that closed slot, and
installation preserves its allocation provenance when the previous installed
state is exchanged into it. Fixed original diagnostics share validation and
vote/swap logic with ordinary diagnostics; no family policy or second inference
loop moves into the native adapter.

The original installer also consumes a finite preparation for the displaced
state's actual ordinary memory owners. A cold borrowed plan counts the distinct
existing state, model, and operation authorities in ordinary merge order without
cloning them. After the constructor amount is admitted, the same borrowed worker
reserves one exact-capacity vector and retains those existing authorities. Before
mutation, installation verifies the exact target, settled session boundary and
unchanged owner union. The common typed exchange performs its usual distributed
preparation vote before the infallible state move. The prepared vector then moves
to the displaced slot; the previous metadata retires only after all its
underlying authorities are retained there. This path neither grows the model's
ordinary owner vector nor runs global native/ordinary cleanup. It does not make
source accounts into destination credit or infer completion from destruction.

These contributions cover the typed Box, local fixed diagnostics, finite owner
rows, and their constructor/return/installation controls. Native copy execution,
all-rank agreement resources, pending input, semantic source planning, and final
inference still require their actual independent producers and fresh request
funding. Host lifetime custody alone establishes none of those bounds. Sampling
and installation failures retain the same host admission through the backend
error source, including when callers use the low-level shared resume driver.


Original saved-resume copy sizing compares the original per-birth physical
capacity P with S, the new-tensor allowance from the exact registered decoder/key
copy and pending-input reports. Those reports already include their selected
allocator allowance and compaction scratch. The fresh request therefore adds
only max(P,S)-S and gives the native preparation partition max(P,S). Old source
backing and host work remain in their existing terms; the same registered copy
is then consumed by source-credit composition. Unknown new-tensor reports refuse
qualification, and checked sums preserve full-source overflow diagnostics.


Workspace trace-state metadata now shares fixed-role declarations and value snapshots. A clone retains the same immutable slot and tensor-layout owners; mutation first reserves a new value vector and shared shell through the participating WorkspaceContext. A failed reservation leaves the prior state intact. Projection duplicate marks use the same fallible metadata allocator. StateError retains the original neural metadata construction error as its source rather than formatting it into a new String; errors with retained sources no longer promise value equality.

The shared-layout workspace DeviceState constructor accounts for its layer vector, final boxed extent, metadata identity, and initialized table/custody mutex controls before creating them. The quote-only branch constructor uses that same table producer and immutable layer handles. It does not copy native request admission or revision authority into a metadata simulation. Native state cloning retains its separate semantics. Architecture text and media quote workers and live/copied native state projections use this participating constructor.

This closes participating constructors, not the complete initial admission problem. Initial ordinary cold equation tracing still occurs before a complete planning-metadata reservation; its resulting census is an input to saved-source resume accounting. Initial factories now use a closed source-layout clone query and the shared typed table constructor. Remaining semantic error formatting and equation/application temporaries still require their own producer accounting. No overall bounded-resume capability may be inferred from the presence of a partial metadata census.


### Pooling metadata shares declarations and charges mutable branches

The portable pooling workspace mechanism and native projection consume one
allocation-free declaration/stream validator. The ordinary geometry API remains a
Vec-returning adapter to that same validator. Its accepted overlap configurations,
stream ordering, duplicate declaration selection and validation order are
unchanged. The workspace path retains one admitted immutable policy with ordinal
component references, and admits policy shapes, stream rows, projected component
rows and mask layouts through the Context metadata producer. Stream checkpoints
share their existing metadata. A later stream mutation admits a new row vector and
Rc before replacing the shared branch; reset prepares that copy before changing
local keys or frontiers. Imported dimensions use the shared checked iterator, so a
shape mismatch cannot hide a later dimension-conversion failure.

Pooling diagnostics use the same Context string or retained-source producer;
`StateError::WorkspaceConstruction` preserves an already admitted workspace cause.
The fixed pooling-mask geometry check is also shared with the ordinary constructor.
These controls are cumulative across metadata checkpoints and do not grant native
execution or refund snapshot budgets. Initial public realization from an owned
`StateLayout` still uses its separately unqualified layout clone; this component
alone does not qualify the complete original snapshot/resume host estimate.


Portable workspace tracing has shared metadata constructors for operation facts, participating vector/shared-root producers and report storage. Original initial and saved-resume equation traces reserve participating allocations through their actual runtime planning account, without refunds at span boundaries. Completed reports move their diagnostic storage and reuse the ordinary scalar reducer. These controls remain separate from native graph, record and buffer bounds. Constructors that have not joined the account remain explicit qualification gaps; a prior trace does not provide their allowance.

Native dense-copy metadata projections now share a counted source-root constructor and reserve each later destination-root insertion through WorkspaceContext. Completed copy spans use the consuming report producer, retaining the existing ordinary-context report behavior. Typed state failures are carried by a counted source wrapper; an existing workspace construction failure is moved directly without another allocation.


### Initial workspace state-layout clone participates in metadata construction

Initial concat, resident and pooling workspace factories now copy the supplied
`StateLayout` through one private borrowed construction plan before invoking the
shared workspace table driver. The plan counts the exact existing clone's boxed
layer schedule, nested policy tensors and shapes, component groups and shapes,
and segment-name bytes, using destination lengths rather than the source's spare
capacity. It also counts the actual shared layout/identity allocations, metadata
custody, initialized private attachment mutex and fixed result/error controls.
The same source borrow is consumed after the Context metadata debit. No policy is
reselected or component inventory rebuilt; the existing clone copies all values,
including named segment lifetimes and processed-token offsets. Ordinary shared
layout construction retains its prior lazy attachment behavior.

A generic error adapter around the existing table constructor preserves factory
policy errors while converting allocation failures exactly once into
`StateError::WorkspaceConstruction`. The constructor does not create native state
or a new host grant. This closes the initial layout allocation's participation in
the context census; the complete pre-admission original snapshot/resume quote
still requires its separately composed source and full-sequence metadata bound.


Initial workspace layout cloning selects its original ordinary constructor before
any qualified layout query when the Context does not record checked metadata.
Checked contexts consume the exact private clone plan. This preserves ordinary
platform availability and lazy attachment initialization; the mode test uses the
Context's source fact selection rather than an optional census result.

The assembled metadata migration compiles across neural/runtime/native/facade targets. Focused runtime checks pass for exhausted checkpoint-copy metadata capacity without state mutation and for pooling checkpoints over uneven chunks, restore and reset. Source projection queries and the outer planning/report constructors still require their final combined admission join; these results do not qualify the complete public resume path.


The retained dense snapshot/resume projection queries its metadata constructors
through the same closed native representation that selects the existing worker.
Runtime owns the exact concat and pooling role, declaration, stream and diagnostic
populations; compressed state owns its inline import/geometry controls. Empty
fixed declarations allocate no role owners, while duplicate declarations retain
the constructor's unique value count. Pooling counts both actual local-state
constructions and the exact declared native component rows. The native adapter
adds the actual shared state table and its selected layer constructors without
inferring a mechanism from role names. These queries create no admission authority;
source tensor imports, operations, native clone shells and trace/report storage
remain separately owned components of the cold resume plan.


Prepared replicated text equation projection consumes the execution graph and canonical unit layout from its existing validated module/contract pair. Portable runtime retains and borrows that move-only geometry through shared resident/layerwise execution; this metadata conveys no source readiness or admission authority. Arbitrary architecture exposure invalidates retained topology and produces a typed stale-geometry refusal, while the shared restricted tensor-slot workers preserve it. No backend reconstructs architecture group names or scheduling policy for this handoff. Initial declaration construction, composite/media carriers and observation declaration preparation remain separate owning producers.


Saved-resume preparation separates its exact retained-source copy plan from construction of the future equation schedule. The first uses the actual native roots, isolated-copy operands and pending-input program. The second reserves its actual metadata allocations through a fresh runtime planning account. The obsolete saved semantic census and source-envelope query have been removed: a changed chunk schedule is charged as it is constructed. Neither preparation mechanism grants native execution or bypasses unknown native bounds.


The portable inference quote scheduler accepts an existing WorkspaceContext for cumulative metadata construction. It uses the same PrefillDriver and decode schedule as ordinary quoting; the Context does not create native authority. Checked request, cancellation, span-plan and diagnostic owners debit before construction, and fixed/paid errors remain typed. Downstream report composition and initial cold planning admission remain independent qualification boundaries.


The portable neural workspace accepts an actual caller-owned host metadata account through `WorkspaceMetadataFunding`. Its fixed refusals allocate no diagnostics; participating Context and fact producers reserve before allocation or destination mutation. The closed shared owner retires its Arc and concrete account Box before the account can refund host admission, with no execution/native grant or raw/weak escape. Context retains the account last, while callers must independently retain the same funding with metadata outputs and errors that outlive it. Ordinary and finite-envelope equation workers remain shared; no original execution capability is inferred from this hook alone.

Runtime workspace planning now uses the same shared domain ledger as inference admission. A host-only account reserves each participating constructor before allocation, checks all live capacity limits under the usage lock, and retains its cumulative charge through the last closed planning owner. It grants no tensor or submission authority. Initial native quotation is being joined to this mechanism; the remaining admission/report constructors and escaped diagnostic owners must participate before that path is qualified end to end.


The initial native resident-recipe entry can now construct its existing shared
workspace trace under an independently admitted host-planning account. Runtime
owns that cumulative account; the backend supplies retained mechanism facts and
uses the same recipe worker as cold diagnostics. The actual finite registered
root constructor and closed diagnostic erasure reserve their own controls before
allocation. The returned generation workspace, root registration, native recipe
and Context travel with an independent funding handle, retained through enclosing
candidate/report composition and any escaped error. This account neither admits
native execution nor supplies a missing native bound. Ordinary diagnostic calls
