keep their existing construction and error behavior.

Planning errors preserve existing neutral classification and native state-preservation
status while retaining the original cause through the existing closed shared
backend-failure owner, with planning funding last. If that incremental diagnostic
cannot fit, the cause retires while funding is still live and the backend returns
an inline funding refusal. Public conversion uses the existing static prepared
request rejection, preserving capacity/overflow/unavailable classification
without allocating another diagnostic shell.


Original saved-resume diagnostics now reserve their second workspace Context's
metadata through a fresh runtime planning account. The constructor executes the
same dense projection, pending-input program and complete future equation and
sampling schedule; each participating producer reserves before allocating.
Neither the old saved semantic census nor its former report count supplies this
new allowance, so a smaller prefill chunk is charged for its actual additional
reports and operations. The original idle-storage check uses the existing
allocation-free census visitors, preserving domain and unknown-source checks.
Ordinary resume keeps its prior Context and owning inventory construction.

The first sealed decoder/key-copy Context and its registered saved-source plan
remain covered by the separately admitted host-copy preparation. Their native
source credit is unchanged. Only the former second-context source envelope,
old semantic envelope, and second Context constructor were removed from that
host amount; those constructors now reserve on the new planning account. The
prepared diagnostic retains planning funding last, its surviving span plan and
pins retain their construction owners, and native admission carries an explicit
planning alias into the final text quote. Failed diagnostic or later admission
construction retains that account through the existing closed error owner. This
join grants no native work and does not enable the public original-resume hooks;
logical copy estimation and complete enclosing admission construction remain
separate integration requirements.

A native recipe now retains its actual planning account when its recorder used funded metadata construction. The subsequent native-request control estimate excludes that already-reserved recorder/recipe shell and its two vector destinations; query populations and future native controls remain explicit. Ordinary diagnostic recipes retain their existing full control estimate. This is ownership-based composition of distinct constructor terms, not a discount of an execution peak. Other original host-control overlaps still require the same audit.

Saved-resume admission report construction uses the actual dynamic planning
account retained by the second diagnostic Context. The portable admission worker
still compares the same borrowed state, incremental requirement and context
facts; runtime constructs the owned state/report and rejection text through
`WorkspaceReportMetadata` before allocation. Core supplies the shared fallible
rejection formatter so ordinary and counted diagnostics preserve the same
variants and text. The native original caller retains that planning account
through every report and paid error, and the sealed future span plan passes the
same account to the existing saved-source reservation. Source-copy H, native Q,
source credit and atomic reservation validation remain separate. This closes
those report constructors without enabling the aggregate original resume hook.

The neutral NeuralBackend contract exposes an optional construction_metadata destination. Its default is absent; WorkspaceBackend borrows the same WorkspaceContext already driving equations. This hook creates no account, native permission, source credit or separate dispatcher. The ordinary replicated architecture handoff consumes a typed prepared-contract entry point, preserving a participating constructor's nn::Error through ReplicatedTextDispatchError and PreparedExecutionError. The legacy contract API continues to return its existing String diagnostics; unrelated routed, partitioned and media preparation remains on that route.

The shared contract parameter validator stages borrowed name/shape/owner rows and expected names in exact requested-capacity vectors. Checked contexts debit these requests before allocation. Duplicate detection, selected catalog comparison, executable shape equations, owner refinement, derived metadata pairing and translated provenance cardinality keep their previous order. The resulting companion catalog retains indices into the one original ArchitectureParameterDescription; comparison no longer clones companion recipes or provenance that it never used. Indices sort without heap scratch, diagnostic lists format borrowed iterators, and the common output-companion identity predicate remains shared with the owning constructor. The source description remains alive through task comparison; every reference stays within that lifetime.

This closes the validator's row, companion-index and packed-shape temporary producers, not the entire initial quote. The existing source selection/inspection dispatch copy, normalized family configuration, architecture parameter-description construction, lowering descriptor, selected task duplication, addressable catalogs, prompt-cache identity and geometry constructors still require counted or retained-source construction. The enclosing Context/account must retain all returned errors and plans; these borrowing helpers do not claim independent lifetime custody or complete host qualification.

The saved-resume H0 source query includes the existing source-counted prompt
preparation controls. That owner prices the dedicated recovery-root vector and
its Rc, the consumed resume driver/provisional return values, and their escaped
failure controls. These are separate from fresh Q's FundedWork/submission/native
controls and from its numerical buffers. The same retained decoder/key/pending
source determines the query and the actual prompt constructor. The aggregate
public original-resume hook remains gated independently.
The H0 source plan no longer adds fixed-role projection rows: its first sealed
copy program imports arrays directly and has no role-table producer. Actual typed
state projection participates in the second Context's planning account.

Checked plain prepared contracts now borrow the authoritative selected materialization-task sequence during validation and retain a marker instead of a second deep task vector. The existing task-presence predicate is shared with the owning materialization helper. Public task inspection still returns the same ordered slice; quote geometry consumption drops the marker without cloning. Ordinary/native contract preparation keeps its owned task vector, and a later native consuming split of a marked contract explicitly constructs the same owned sequence. This does not claim that consuming split as a checked metadata producer. Empty addressable exclusions bypass the redundant selected-name catalog and companion-name expansion; nonempty exclusions retain their existing single-pass semantics and constructor path. No task, format, source identity, exclusion or readiness decision changes.

Span-plan diagnostics continue to report their full allocated record capacity. Reservation control estimates include those records only when no retained planning account has already reserved them; the same span-plan owner holds that account through the records' lifetime. Newly constructed reservation, sealing and native controls remain separately charged.
The original MLX saved-resume logical estimate borrows the immutable funded decoder/sampler/pending pair before host admission. It shares the existing logical snapshot equations for native layout/arrays, sampler history, one-part inputs, and the portable control-state header and prompt identity. Native fixed preparation supplies exact source descriptors and destination representation without constructing a new state. The logical estimate grants no source, copy, or execution authority; original preparation and fresh native admission remain independently qualified, and physical Q or the saved copy account cannot substitute for logical copy work.

Original saved-resume prompt, sampling and installation retain constructor H
through their entire driver phase, including prompt target/phase validation and
post-copy binding. All three use the same closed core failure owner, which
releases its allocation before the nested cause and final H. Prompt construction
no longer adds a nested wrapper, so the existing single whole-phase error
contribution remains exact. Ordinary errors, native recovery and state mutation
ordering are unchanged; this correction does not activate the preparation hook.

The shared replicated-text contract validator now borrows exact selected lowering
source and physical/logical shape metadata. The ordinary owning lowering query
uses the same geometry/axis validation before producing its owned descriptor;
checked inspection does not clone encoding names or shape vectors. Invalid source
geometry and missing source facts retain the same diagnostic text and precedence.
This closes lowering inspection only; selected config and architecture parameter
description construction remain separate metadata producers.

The shared equation visitor constructs opening observation-root vectors and appended diagnostic assumptions through its existing WorkspaceContext. A failed reserve precedes insertion or cloning; later callbacks cannot add roots after that failure. Entry geometry, span frontier, score consistency and missing-output diagnostics use the same message policy with a counted destination for checked contexts. Ordinary messages and forward/sampling order are preserved. Immutable score-layout clones share their existing shape owner and add no allocation. Observation declaration and architecture reconstruction remain separately owned producers.

The checked replicated-contract worker charges its temporary partition layout
through the runtime-owned nested Clone recipe before allocation. Final prompt
identity consumes the actual architecture identity strings and constructs the
policy schedule, prefix offsets and segment names through the same Context.
Portable cache validation uses one shared diagnostic callback and prior-slice
role/segment checks, preserving validation order without scratch sets. Ordinary
constructors use that same validator with their existing diagnostic variants.
Architecture-owned creation of the initial model/family/fingerprint strings is
still a separate producer: this runtime join does not substitute an expected
fingerprint or claim that those upstream producers are already bounded.

The plain shared decoder description now transfers its emitted parameter groups,
execution graph, and unit layout into the validated description when using checked
workspace metadata. Its authoritative expected list is the same emitted group
sequence, so the previous deep duplicate is unnecessary. Validation borrows sorted
target and owner rows under the actual Context destination, preserving duplicate,
owner, missing, and unexpected-target ordering. Owner validation scans existing
roles and consumers rather than building sets or a temporary consumer vector. The
ordinary independent-expected constructor uses these same validation workers and
retains its typed errors. Checked owning rows, owner names, and diagnostic buffers
are paid before construction; their enclosing quote retains the Context custody.

This is description assembly and validation, not a bound for the upstream parameter
group producer. Module parameter paths, group/member shapes and companion metadata,
family config/format ownership, and initial graph/layout constructors still require
their own participating producers before the complete native preparation hook can
be qualified.
The total prepared-execution driver retains the admitted source selection/catalog owner through typed construction. Visitors that need only the target architecture borrow it from that same immutable graph; floating-state dtype selection uses the retained target plan and original catalog through the existing shared selector. Visitors requiring an owned full inspection materialize that view at their existing typed entry without reopening the artifact or changing source-format policy. This removes an eager metadata duplicate from plain replicated equation construction. Remaining owned selection/configuration/geometry and full-inspection producers are still required to participate in metadata funding before original resume preparation can be qualified.

Parameter-description validation collects borrowed rows with their original source
ordinal, then sorts once by target and ordinal. Duplicate diagnostics select the
earliest second occurrence from the source traversal. Owner validation stops at
the first invalid owner; duplicates in its completed prefix still take precedence.
Missing and unexpected targets remain lexicographically selected. This bounds row
ordering work to O(n log n) without allocating owned target names.

The saved-sampler native recipe worker and local saved-resume diagnostics now use the same paid closed error destination as initial planning. The actual planning account reserves each escaping diagnostic before its shell is allocated and stays alive through its cause. First source-copy construction retains its separate H controls; these local changes do not qualify unconverted upstream architecture constructors.
Original saved-resume logical estimation authenticates the saved decoder's exact executable origin through the shared runtime control-origin comparison. A matching parameter epoch alone does not establish executable identity. The fixed origin loan checks the existing resolved boundary without inspecting the current decoder, allocating a diagnostic, or granting construction/execution authority; admitted original resume planning uses the same typed comparison.

Static shared-decoder parameter groups now have a checked producer using the
existing strict borrowed parameter-source visitor. It counts actual named members
without cloning traversal metadata, pays the final member vector, then revalidates
its count while filling the same source. The shared ordinary/checked member worker
preserves shape conversion, supplied sharding, companion identity, and row-layout
metadata. Checked names, shapes, companion names, group vectors, callback controls
and errors use the actual Context destination before allocation. A changed or
incomplete source refuses with its typed borrowed-source cause; partial groups
remain under the enclosing quote's Context custody.

Ordinary group construction and the checked producer share validation. Duplicate
target checks use borrowed prior rows; chunked-partition geometry is checked through
borrowed extent iterators, without temporary target sets or chunk-length vectors.
The architecture uses the same static embedding/norm/output group worker for both
destinations. Per-block projection/segmented groups and upstream config/graph
construction remain distinct producers requiring the same treatment.


The shared plain and partitioned decoder identity path now accepts the actual
workspace metadata destination through `ArchitectureParameters`. Its seven
`Config` implementations use the same ordinary/checked fingerprint producer:
borrowed field names, exact sorted key/value hashing, unchanged float-bit and
nested-identity encodings, counted string/sort storage, and a fixed digest writer.
K2's complete configuration debug field worker is shared by ordinary formatting
and its map-normalized fingerprint; it does not clone the configuration or build
an ordered tree solely for identity. Attention schedules likewise format directly
from their retained policies. The runtime still compares this actual produced
identity with the independently selected identity. It never substitutes the
expected string. Copied strings, fixed identity controls, and diagnostic transport
consume the enclosing metadata account, whose retained planning owner covers the
returned contract. This closes these constructors, not blanket architecture
qualification: `Config::validate_config` retains its existing validation/error
producer, and non-layered fixed/compressed architecture identity overrides must
join the same metadata contract separately. Neither gap changes public support
or admits native execution.
The authoritative replicated-text selection is immutable after the shared cold selector validates main and auxiliary materialization tasks. A closed shared owner retains its exact requirements, graph, unit layout and task metadata across typed construction, without exposing mutation or allocation/execution authority. The total driver borrows the selected branch; plain replicated branch cloning shares the retained selection rather than copying a metadata tree. Validated execution geometry remains move-only and retains that same selection. Resident and layerwise workers consume its borrowed graph/layout through their existing shared equations, preserving ordinary graph construction for callers without a prepared contract. This does not qualify remaining configuration, declaration or routed/partition metadata constructors.

Workspace layerwise acquisition reserves the actual unit Box and its return/error transports before building the unit. Address validation uses the same paid diagnostic destination as the surrounding equation Context. Unit payload, parameter-source construction and later numerical execution remain their respective producers.


Fixed and compressed replicated families now implement the same actual identity
metadata hook as the shared decoder. LFM2, both Kimi mechanisms, DeepSeek V3,
Nemotron-H and Qwen hybrid retain their existing family dispatch and validation,
while ordinary and checked identity entry points share each fingerprint worker.
Sorted configuration sets/maps use counted storage; layer schedules and Qwen's
compact JSON values write directly from immutable policy. FP8 exclusion sorting
also borrows its strings. Nemotron's identity layer count visits the same validated
MTP policies as ordinary collection without constructing a temporary policy Vec.
DeepSeek's identity validation uses a shared diagnostic destination and the same
fixed scalar encoding/rotary predicates, preserving its diagnostic text and
ordering on failure. All returned identity strings and typed error transport use
the enclosing planning account. These hooks qualify their own identity producers;
separate configuration cloning, construction/validation, parameter enumeration,
and native execution still require their own participating producers. No source
identity substitution or aggregate support activation is introduced.


Prepared geometry validation now receives the same metadata destination as the
rest of the contract. Actual plain/partitioned decoder and fixed/compressed target
shells expose a borrowed graph declaration and static transport-role declaration;
the ordinary owning graph/transport APIs consume those same source declarations.
The selected graph is only compared against the actual source name, dependencies,
order, output and transport fields. Group-count errors and geometry diagnostics
use the checked destination. The generic contract adapter forwards a retained
fixed `WorkspaceMetadataError` cause without trying to allocate another diagnostic;
ordinary error text remains unchanged. This closes graph/transport comparison for
these target shells, not the separate state-layout constructor. The compatibility
owned-graph/default hooks and appended-prediction shells retain their existing
producers and do not gain a metadata qualification from this interface.


The shared layered decoder's dense per-block parameter declarations now carry
an optional `WorkspaceContext` metadata destination through the existing
attention, normalization, and feed-forward placement workers. Checked module
collection uses the strict borrowed parameter source visitor, counts its exact
member destination, and debits names, shapes, companion identities, segment
ranges, and group vectors before allocating them. Projection placement, GCD
partition selection, fused segment validation, and encoded tail chunk equations
are shared with ordinary declarations. Chunk conversion borrows the complete
unchanged source group, computes its widths in source order, and moves existing
member and segment owners into the result. Duplicate-target validation sorts
only counted indices and still reports the first repeated source ordinal after
any earlier member error. Config-specific value-format and optional normalization
name companions use the same borrowed name components as their ordinary methods.

The checked producer is consumed by the existing dense `BlockFactory` variants;
it does not establish a bound for other factories that have not supplied that
producer, or for module/config construction before parameter collection. Those
remain distinct prerequisites of complete original quote qualification. The
metadata account remains the enclosing Context/quote's custody; the returned
parameter declarations do not grant native execution or reopen prepared sources.


Architecture state geometry now has a shared counted layout constructor. Core
policy/tensor constructors expose the same validation with caller-owned diagnostics,
and policy component expansion writes the same actual declarations into supplied
vector destinations. Runtime `StateLayout` uses that producer for both ordinary and
metadata construction, preserves policy/segment validation order, and validates
duplicate segment identities against the prior sorted slice without an allocating
set. Counted construction reserves each nested component shape, segment string,
constructor frame and retained diagnostic before birth. Already-owned partition
layouts use their existing exact counted clone worker. These are constructor
mechanisms, not grants or whole-architecture qualification; family geometry callers
must supply their actual policy schedule under the same retained metadata context.


The actual replicated architecture geometry validator now supplies its retained
metadata context to state-layout construction. Shared plain decoders, LFM2, Kimi
Linear, Nemotron-H, DeepSeek V3 and Qwen hybrid derive their original policies
through the same geometry workers used by ordinary and rank-local constructors.
A private destination supplies ordinary or counted vectors, symbolic shapes,
policy schedules, segment names and typed diagnostics; numerical geometry and
validation remain family-owned. Counted schedule conversion also pays a possible
Vec-to-box payload replacement before that handoff. Partitioned plain decoders
copy their actual retained architecture layout through the existing exact clone
worker. No selected requirement is substituted for an architecture declaration.
Fixed/compressed construction contracts require the actual metadata hook, and
metadata refusal is propagated without formatting it into a new definition error.
Compatibility defaults for other architecture implementations retain their original
behavior and do not qualify those constructors for complete original admission.


Standard layered decoder module construction now uses the neutral backend's
existing construction-metadata hook before producing its attention, dense MLP,
and block metadata. One private destination carries the caller's Context through
the same constructor order, parameter alias policy, formatted names, companion
naming worker, fixed normalization validation, and diagnostics. The checked
configuration companions explicitly preserve absent aliases/normalizations and
share repeated-layer source names with ordinary construction; an unimplemented
checked Config companion refuses instead of implying a bound. Ordinary contexts
continue to use the ordinary constructor destination.

The neutral fused projection and linear-format constructors now share their
owned validation workers with checked variants. Segment names and indices are
admitted before allocation, duplicate errors retain original source-order
priority, and already-owned companions and segments move into their final
specifications. Missing capability names and rotary configuration kinds are
borrowed rather than copied into temporary collections. The rotary parser uses
the same scalar/geometry validation with a caller-provided diagnostic destination.
Repeated-source format fallback uses its existing lookup sequence with a checked
name destination; group tail/alignment callbacks preserve any resulting refusal.
These mechanisms do not establish bounds for other block factories, initial
static-module/config preparation, or later native realization; those producers
remain separate. Metadata lives under the enclosing Context and quote custody,
with no new native permission or source grant.

Capability reports now retain one closed immutable `CapabilityEstimate` payload.
Cloning the report shares its existing model capabilities and state schedule;
consuming report transformations preserve the old independently owned result
semantics when another report retains the original. The closed last owner frees
its Arc shell before retiring the report payload. State-memory conversion moves
the actual validated runtime layer schedule instead of cloning the schedule.
The core `StateMemoryLayout` diagnostic callback runs the same field and policy
validation with caller-owned error construction.

An exact prepared source retains the capability report published after its
ordinary architecture contract succeeds. Later replicated workspace construction
authenticates the same selected requirements owner and borrows that report.
Its handle and result controls are charged before retaining the alias. A checked
workspace with no completed report refuses before entering an ordinary allocating
capability producer. Workspace-only inspection does not publish this completed
construction witness. The retained report carries no execution permission or
source-storage credit; the actual architecture geometry is still validated by
the shared construction contract. These changes close report reconstruction,
not the remaining static-module constructors or the public fresh-resume gate.


Replicated dispatch's normalized plan-identity check now consumes the actual
configuration's counted fingerprint and state-layout producers. Its single-group
graph and complete unit-address/submission layout compare borrowed author
declarations without constructing duplicate vectors. State-access classification
walks the same actual layout already validated in that check. Checked failures
retain the typed metadata error; ordinary diagnostic wording and comparison order
remain unchanged. The existing normalized eligibility selectors still decide
which configurations reach this replicated driver. Their Nemotron sparse-policy
predicate now uses the same MTP visitor without allocating a temporary policy
vector or malformed-policy diagnostic; invalid policies retain the original false
result. No native mechanism, source authority or execution-class gate is added.

The shared static text-module constructor now uses its existing borrowed
`StaticModuleSpecView` and construction-order worker for both ordinary and
Context-backed metadata. The owning view adapter pays for the three exact names;
the concrete sink pays for parameter declarations, encoding companions,
normalization/head specifications, and fixed validation transports before their
owning producers. Embedding creation still precedes normalization, and output
ownership validation remains after both; failures retain the existing local-owner
retirement order. The ordinary destination retains its existing error conversion.

Plain decoder configuration names and embedding encoding lookup use the same
metadata destination. The exact Config lookup hook defaults to a fixed unqualified
cause; current configurations forward their actual lookup, including the shared
repeated-parameter source-name worker where that lookup needs a String. This does
not infer embedding quantization from a different head-format policy. The hybrid
target-group constructor uses the same checked validator; its group identities
remain borrowed static strings. These are portable architecture producers and
introduce no backend branch, native authority, or source reopening. The enclosing
prepared owner remains responsible for retaining Context funding. Upstream plain
configuration/block validation and prediction-group construction are separate
producers; this component does not declare the complete original resume hook
qualified.


Fixed and compressed replicated-family static-module declarations now return
borrowed `StaticModuleSpecView` values. The six actual family implementations
retain the same names, scalar geometry, tied-head policy and format lookup; the
shared counted conversion owns every resulting name string before the existing
static-module constructor runs. Ordinary DeepSeek V3 callers consume the same
view through the ordinary conversion. Qwen hybrid FP8 exclusions compare borrowed
prefix/rest aliases from the same declarations used to construct checkpoint alias
strings, so a static format query creates no temporary alias vector or string.
This covers the upstream static-spec producer; family configuration validation,
execution-group owners and downstream module constructors retain their own
construction/accounting responsibilities.


Fixed/compressed replicated construction now passes its actual metadata context
through the shared family configuration validator, profile checks and layer-count
conversion. LFM2, Kimi Linear, Nemotron-H and Qwen hybrid ordinary validators
delegate the same predicates to a diagnostic callback; DeepSeek V3 uses its
existing callback. Selected encoding failures use fixed causes before writing the
original diagnostic. Nemotron validates MTP through its existing visitor without
creating and discarding a policy vector. Qwen's validation feeds the shared rotary
normalizer from the actual borrowed JSON scalar lookup, preserving typed-map
conversion, selection and error precedence without cloning a temporary map.
Ordinary owning RoPE conversion still moves its strings. Checked metadata refusal
stays typed through the caller; the validation change grants no native authority.

The checked plain-decoder parameter description now materializes its actual
single-group declaration through the shared `ArchitectureExecutionGraph::Single`
storage worker. The Context destination pays the group name and graph row
vectors; ordinary Single materialization uses the same worker. General graph
validation, `ExecutionGraph::chain`, and scheduling are unchanged. The ordinary
and checked unit-layout constructors share their existing group-major loop;
checked construction borrows the declared counts and pays group identities,
ranges, and each address-vector reserve before allocation. This replaces the
previous description-level `sizeof` allowance around ordinary owning graph and
layout constructors. The resulting owners move into the existing validated
parameter description under its enclosing Context funding.

A checked decoder parameter-group hook that returns `None` now returns fixed
`WorkspaceMetadataError::Unqualified` before the ordinary group producer is
called. Ordinary callers retain that producer. Replicated unit construction and
its group/index failures use the same ModuleMetadata diagnostic destination as
module names and specifications. The shared storage loops, validation order,
source ownership and selected parameter semantics are preserved; this does not
create native admission, completion, or publication authority.

The shared plain decoder constructor now selects explicit checked configuration
and block-policy validation adapters before constructing its static modules.
Llama, Gemma 2, Nanbeige, Qwen, K2 Horizon and GPT-OSS adapters use the same ordered
validation predicates as their ordinary entry points, with diagnostic formatting
and error ownership supplied by the actual workspace metadata context. The
operator requirement check uses the same ordered capability predicate. Unknown
custom checked adapters return the fixed metadata qualification refusal before
calling an ordinary allocating validator. This is constructor participation, not
an independent execution or snapshot support declaration. Ordinary configuration
errors retain their existing types and text; GPT-OSS normalized RoPE validation
borrows the actual stored type string instead of cloning it.

The MLX original saved-resume host hook now queries the same immutable funded pair with fixed source-origin and constructor-layout checks before H0 admission. Explicit arithmetic overflow remains a neutral `WorkingMemoryError::Overflow`; other missing fixed bounds reject without diagnostic allocation. Source/table/pending/error preparation is separate from the independently funded dynamic equation context and fresh native request, with no source-credit refund or ordinary construction fallback. The shared runtime provider continues to own copied controller and facade state.

The final plain/fixed module and validation destinations, exact prepared-source reuse, and native saved-resume entry are integrated. Public dense/hybrid restore and fork regressions pass for both saved pending prefill and a committed token boundary; no broader family or mechanism support is inferred.

The saved-resume copier finishes its independent copy report before opening a
new model-construction span for parameter placeholders. The ordinary shared
driver then opens inference state spans from the actual projected saved state;
this transition does not reset cumulative metadata funding. Live captures retain
the parameter epoch already authenticated by their source witness, including
before the first prefill initializes the live sampler epoch. Resumed copies keep
the same strict origin checks. Native model destruction still queues semantic
payload retirement; the copied host account and logical branch lease survive
until the existing ordinary retirement boundary destroys those completed owners.

Media equation intervals now consume one complete span report and share its
immutable payload with the existing inference reducer through a closed, paid
owner. The retained encoder cut uses the same scalar reducer without consuming
the active span; decoder and rollback work therefore remain in the first
interval. Root, checkpoint, rollback and interval destinations reserve through
the actual WorkspaceContext before allocation. Success and partial-failure
results retain source/table custody, the ordinary lease and an independent
planning-account alias until their owned metadata retires. Finishing the media
source after its report only advances the retained traversal phase and releases
its prefix values; the next scheduled span opens before further equations.
This shared diagnostic ownership grants no native admission or completion and
does not change managed-media qualification.

The shared layered scheduler retains executor-fork, graph-submission, dependency
ordering and terminal-finish errors in the neutral `BackendFailure` source owner.
Replicated session conversion and error widening move that same owner instead of
formatting it into a contract string. Native error types remain inside the
backend source chain, including their actual admission custody; this conversion
does not certify completion or change unresolved completion teardown. Resident
strategy inspection borrows only its already-installed policy, with no fallback
to bounded policy or new source of execution authority.


The resident MLX policy now participates in the same prepared group-boundary
submission worker as the bounded policy. Its cold plan counts the actual selected
execution graph's initial and group frontiers, excluding the bounded policy's
separate final-output submission. The accepted equation recipe closes those
frontiers before admission; the genuine request claim subsequently constructs
finite clone/completion slots and an exact scope registry. Resident conversion
transfers the loader's existing installation owner rather than allocating a
second installation owner. Each completion and retained failure keeps the same
request control custody; no copied-state account or TLS observation grants work.

The neutral layered driver permits a policy to consume a prepared choice to use
its supplied executor for every group. MLX's original resident and bounded banks
make that choice only after validating the current request/scope and the exact
stream value captured from the selected execution mechanism. This matches the
accepted single-stream native recipe and creates no per-group queue or stream.
The default continues to fork executors. The same group scheduling, state,
observation and completion drivers are used; this does not qualify distributed
execution or manufacture missing native bounds.


### Source-selected floating workspace representation

Initial resident recipe planning can project exact completed parameter dtype and
row-contiguity through the existing borrowed native parameter source visitor.
The portable workspace retains only paid immutable parameter names, logical
layouts and optional scalar representation facts. These facts grant no source
credit or native permission: the containing quote retains its existing selected
execution and parameter-epoch checks. Logical layout equality and its conservative
Float32 storage convention remain unchanged. Unknown sources and unaudited
operation propagation retain the generic dtype/stride union.

The MLX fact provider propagates concrete precision only through individually
inspected workers, including real F32 scalar promotion and the recurrent
FP32-state/query-dtype-output boundary. A completed row-contiguous BF16 weight,
proved BF16 activation, and the existing Metal row-kernel geometry select the
smaller physical projection bound. It still includes possible input compaction,
result/reshape storage, the scalar group seed and separate bias work. Other
inputs retain the existing cast/copy/GEMM union. Dense tied embedding readout now
tries the same BF16 row helper as an ordinary dense projection and preserves its
matmul fallback. This changes the applicable BF16 reduction implementation;
released-checkpoint numerical and token comparison remains required evidence.
Native graph, completion, publication and request-wide physical lifetimes are
unchanged by this descriptive refinement.

Initial native recipe planning may attach descriptive floating representation
facts to its private WorkspaceContext from the exact idle resident executable.
The fixed session inspection and selected-policy loan retain the static modules,
unit layout and loaded transfer during strict parameter visitation. Each row's
name, shape and container is paid before construction; a completed descriptor
loan supplies element type and row contiguity without evaluation or tensor
cloning. Unknown backing and unobserved strategies keep conservative facts.
Only a complete traversal installs the table, and the enclosing text quote keeps
its existing parameter-epoch validation before submission. These facts neither
register storage nor create reusable native allocation or execution authority.


Generation preparation diagnostics are borrowed from the actual backend-retained
request through the core `TextPreparationReport` contract. Ordinary iterators,
controlled generation, and managed plain-text sessions use the same hook; a
backend without an accepted-admission report returns `None`. The loan carries the
selected inference geometry and the existing `Admission`, without cloning a
report or reservation or granting native work. The selected prefill chunk can
therefore be distinguished from its requested cap. The historical incremental
requirement includes any proved source-storage credit and must not be presented
as measured peak memory or current managed-domain usage. The managed memory probe
copies only those two scalars before consuming the common run/advance driver and
preserves them if a later execution step fails.


The retained media equation source now constructs its dependency-prefix flags,
retained-cut flags, and per-group outcome slots through the same worker used by
ordinary media sources. The workspace entry reserves each actual graph-sized
vector before initialization and reserves the diagnostic request owner before its
construction. It retains an independent metadata-funding alias after the source
payload; constructor failures retain that alias after their typed cause and
closed error shells. Empty slots are created before any traversal can clone a
retained group output. Dependency validation, inactive outcomes, encoder-once
behavior, and the commit boundary are unchanged. These paid source tables do not
qualify the architecture's ingress-plan/graph constructors, nested prepared decode
admission, or native media submission; those remain separate consumed producers.

Successful original prefill roles now release their exact operation-registry
observer after the existing Recovery finish has retired the role's root payload.
Failed, blocked, pending and reentrant retirement paths retain that alias. A
separate cumulative registration count remains spent when an observer is removed;
neither the role population nor the request's native partition is refunded. This
shortens completed Scope/control ownership without claiming that escaped state or
output arrays have died. Native equation capacity remains the conservative full
generation sum until selected carryover and next-construction bounds are joined.


The shared workspace report now records the complete possible backing population
of its actual closing roots: backing bytes and the maximum positive allocation
count travel together through alias unions and collapsed score-source envelopes.
The ordinary byte equations are unchanged. Equation observation supplies current
state and semantic-output populations; shared sampling observation supplies the
advanced RNG key and all emitted token roots. Byte-only legacy sources retain
unknown native count evidence rather than acquiring a packed-storage assumption.
MLX applies its existing source-owned physical rounding worker and retains those
components, the whole prepared-input contribution, and complete native producers
of the retained prefill validation results in the selected native plan. These
are descriptive carryover facts, not successful-retirement proof: the original
all-generation capacity, cumulative births/publications and admission gates stay
unchanged. Closing state does not include a still-live rollback checkpoint; the
current complete construction population continues to cover that overlap.

Media workspace construction now consumes the same validated module/contract
pair as plain text. The existing resident/layerwise unit worker receives the
contract's retained execution geometry, and retains the optional source-format
architecture until runtime retirement. The media cut copies that runtime's
actual validated graph through the same worker as ordinary `ExecutionGraph`
cloning, with each name, adjacency vector, and order vector admitted through the
current metadata Context before allocation. Constructor failures keep the source's
existing closed funding custody. This eliminates graph redeclaration during
runtime and cut construction without creating another topology validator. The
shared media traversal's per-span architecture graph comparison remains active;
its repeated declaration producer, ingress-plan diagnostics, and nested decode
admission are separate remaining metadata work. Native media qualification is
unchanged.


The original speculative completion's final C clone handles are constructed by
its existing `PreparedNeuralSubmission` before activation and are included once
in that producer's control quote. Filling those slots consumes the actual source
under the current original role. The shared exact handle-size query now also
supplies speculative diagnostics; it contributes no additional charge and no
source-independent Graph/Record permission. The remaining pending requirements
are the reachable verification DAG, its evaluation/receipt Record population,
and outside-arena stream/event/queue owners. The selected target/draft source and occurrence bank below supply equation
roles; validation, copy and sampler producers remain required before activation.

The shared media invocation now obtains its graph through an architecture loan.
Ordinary architectures retain the same declaration producer. The workspace
composite adapter instead aliases the exact immutable selected owner from its
closed, validated module/contract pair before the runtime consumes that pair.
Both first-span and received-span validation compare every graph field through
the existing graph view; no names or adjacency tables are rebuilt. An arbitrary
public mutable borrow of the underlying prepared architecture invalidates that
carrier, and later media entry rejects it with the existing foreign-graph cause.
Private trusted forward/module workers retain the pinned topology. The carrier
creates neither a fresh selection nor native execution authority; source-format
modules remain retained by the matching runtime. This closes repeated graph
construction in that consumed workspace path while leaving ingress diagnostics
and nested decode preparation as explicit producers.


The independent-model speculative worker now shares its canonical/optimistic
proposal geometry with a finite fresh-request occurrence contract. The typed
executor can retain a move-only cursor outside cache and checkpoint state; each
actual prefill, proposal, verification and replay claims its source/pass/width
at the inspected state frontier before decoder work starts. Failed or discarded
work never refunds these counters. The same source domains convert to ordinary
single-invocation equation geometry with complete sequence logits for decoder
calls and the existing target/draft prefill demands. Actual alternatives must be
traced; no largest-shape monotonicity or complete native fit is inferred.

The optional contract is a source-bound scheduling component, not original
admission. Its current MLX inspection accepts one prepared plain token part;
media expansion remains an additional selected producer. Target/draft epochs, cumulative metadata funding and exact native equation
roles are retained by the source/request bank below. Rollback/snapshot copies,
sampling, validation ingress and original public speculative installation remain
required joins. Existing ordinary scheduling and completion continue unchanged.


Original media workspace plans now enter a shared constructor that charges the
actual family plan, return transports and closed error shell through the current
metadata Context before consuming the projected input. The same family
`from_original` worker handles ordinary and checked construction; its geometry
check uses the existing fixed validator, preserving the rejection order without
constructing a discarded diagnostic. Successful plans retain independent
planning funding after their input, tables and source owners; failures retain it
after the exact original semantic cause and table custody. The shared traversal
and cut constructor select the checked plan/graph diagnostic companions when a
workspace Context participates. Compiled input count validation uses the same
borrowed comparison with either the ordinary String destination or the paid
error destination. Ordinary native media entry is unchanged. This does not yet
close projected input/identity buffers, composite contract construction or the
native whole-request contribution; original media qualification remains gated.


The selected original resident program now composes a successful-prefill native
capacity envelope from the actual shared-driver equation schedule. Each row keeps
its whole rounded construction population, including checkpoint and rollback
copies, through the sealed prefill completion. The ordinary report reducer also
exposes the complete seeded opening population, including the initial resumed or
session-existing state; possible aliases contribute their full backing capacity.
Across successful chunks the envelope retains the current state plus every
potentially escaped readout and all prior validation-producing native populations.
It includes both construction-time overlap with the opening state and the closing
state/output/validation frontier. The final frontier remains covered through the
unchanged summed decode and sampling populations and full prepared-input term.

The native provider consumes this closed schedule reduction in its existing
selected storage plan. It may replace the prefill generation sum only with a
complete smaller envelope; missing population facts or candidate overflow retain
the original sum. The candidate conservatively includes full initial state without
issuing new source credit. The fallback remains the existing native-generation
bound with its existing preparation/source coverage. A test-injected component
trace without an enclosing retained-root census also preserves that fallback.
No admission, publication, graph, event, or scope counter is refunded, and all
controls still cover the complete request. Failed, blocked, or unsettled prefill
stops advancement and retains its resources. Primitive outputs remain pinned
through their actual completion, so this change does not reuse storage within an
equation and does not reduce the one-chunk generation bound.


The original media slot projection now consumes the validated source parts
through a shared runtime mapping/descriptor worker. It reserves the complete
part, metadata, extent, descriptor and shape destinations before projecting or
copying values, and constructs canonical fixed maps without temporary trees.
Ordinary prepared-input descriptors and checked descriptors use the same worker
and the existing core validators. The concrete MLX adapter reserves its borrowed
projection inventory from the actual payload-plus-metadata slot count; it neither
clones native tensors nor evaluates them. Recomputed ordered descriptors must
still exactly equal the original source identity, and physical aliases/unknown
backing keep their existing projection semantics.

Projected inputs retain their own planning funding through final payload and
identity retirement. A later ingress plan or error retains both that source
account and its own constructor account, even if they differ; ordinary entry
with an already funded input debits its existing account rather than escaping
to an unquoted error constructor. This closes the projected input's host
producers while preserving its actual original source and ordinary inspection
lease. It does not turn that lease into original native request authority or
supply the still-required composite contract and whole-request native plan.


### Independent speculative equation source and recipe

The optional independent-decoder occurrence schedule accepts only an external
strategy with its empty target-feature capture contract. An uninstalled schedule
keeps the ordinary worker unchanged. Installed calls permanently consume a
move-only claim before preparation; the same once-only callback wraps the
existing prefill/decode worker. Claims keep the exact request identity, role,
frontier and attempted ordinal outside every cache checkpoint.

The native source pair retains the existing target and draft control-origin
owners, which change on parameter publication. Empty-cache construction records
its assigned role and available origin; checkpoint/restore preserve both.
Preparation validates request identity, role and current model/cache epochs,
then retains exclusive model/cache loans through actual equation tracing and
payload preparation. A source address or logically equal shape cannot replace
these checks. The native mechanism retains the existing `Executable` at its
shared caller, preserving access to the actual blueprint.

The source producer validates the actual plain `[1, N]` token descriptor and
uses its real chunk cap, the shared default, and token dtype. Decoder inputs are
Uint32, matching the native `from_slice::<u32>` worker. A zero generated-output
count still runs the requested input equation: decoder verification/replay is
one full-width sequence-logits span, while prefill uses its ordinary chunk
worker. The initial adapter requires the selected ordinary-unit strategy and
resident parameters. Prefill/Decode attribution stays explicit; routed/provider
and partition strategies need their own actual execution-pass producer.

The equation-only recorder reuses the existing source-plan validation and
reducer without inventing a sampler. Each source pair owns one cumulative
participating metadata account. The original request separately reserves a
finite ordinal bank, then accepts each actual role's complete physical, Graph,
Record and control requirement through the existing atomic pool-account worker.
Roles remain retained outside checkpoint state; failed preparation and rollback
cannot recycle either a claimed group bank or an accepted charge. Native arrays
and arenas retain a closed account-only alias, without a plan/source backedge.

The existing resident slot can install the distinct speculative role and uses
the same generic prepared neural submission/completion producer. Decode uploads
its exact eager Uint32 input before opening the resident host construction bank.
The bank stays active through model and row-view construction, then closes before
the exact parent, readout, cache and assertion root completion. Lexical cleanup
closes the bank before Scope recovery on return or unwind. Successful scope
retirement precedes returning the output; later verification consumes its closed
completion witness rather than submitting another Eval. Ordinary completion is
unchanged. The previous unused metadata-funded outer verification bank is removed.

The same fixed validation and grouped-output storage accepts the distinct
speculative role, retaining it after each exact vector and rejected prefix.
Assertion counts and grouped destinations come from the actual one-equation
recipe. The native callback completes parent/readout/state/assertion roots while
the shared sequence transaction still owns its checkpoint. Assertions consume
same-scope completed scalar receipts without another Eval; failures retain the
original semantic cause and role. The existing completion agreement, rollback
and commit worker handles both ordinary and callback-driven sequence execution.

Host metadata funding refusals belong to the portable core error boundary.
`HostMetadataFundingError` carries exact required/available bytes or a fixed
layout/unavailability cause inline in `BackendFailure`; even exhausted accounts
need no error-source allocation. `eredu-nn` reexports the same type as
`WorkspaceMetadataFundingError` and depends on core solely for this neutral
contract. Core has no NN dependency. This conversion preserves typed source
inspection and delegates snapshot retry and native settlement decisions to the
existing drivers; it grants no host or execution authority.
Dense host-copy callback errors and fixed funding wrappers expose their immediate
typed cause through `Error::source`. Their display text is unchanged. In
particular, transparent display must not skip a source-less funding leaf before
an outer copy owner or the executor can inspect its exact required/available
values. This changes no allocation, authority, retry or retirement behavior.

The completed output clones its already prepared stream owner. Independent
execution carries typed backend failures through the shared driver. Existing
neutral source owners move directly; exact metadata funding refusals remain
inline. The same completion and sampler workers adapt their error type without
new numerical work, policy or intermediate Exception source allocations.

Each original sequence invocation prepares an independent copy of its exact
lane before mutation. The backend reuses the saved-source projection worker,
registered workspace-copy program, native isolated-copy plan and final
publication/recovery mechanisms. Fixed host destinations reserve through the
same planning account before each allocation and retain preparation custody;
partial construction stays with copy recovery. This is a separate copy admission,
not a text or invocation grant. Native backing retains only copy/account custody.
The erased destination box retains host custody until its shell retires.

The existing sequence checkpoint agreement accepts that settled copy. Rollback
moves its state through the shared restoration worker; it does not submit a
second native copy. Empty-to-empty retention merging skips transient revision
construction while preserving admission and final revision invalidation.
Ordinary checkpoints keep their existing copy/restore mechanism. Both paths loan
the existing erased lane box across state exchanges, and the original path uses
the planning account for typed exchange/recovery error transport.

Independent external checkpoints and restores consume that same admitted copy
worker. Startup retains only the actual initialized copy prerequisites; each
copy obtains its own numerical admission. The saved wrapper closes its Rc so its
allocation retires before the native state, prepared stream and metadata account.
Restore checks saved role/origin, schedule, domain and actual prepared stream
before copying; the shared driver installs target and draft only after both
copies succeed. Source epochs remain subject to actual-model validation at every
invocation. Copy failure is retryable, uses a prepaid owning diagnostic or exact
inline funding refusal, and does not fence snapshots or recycle spent attempts.

The shared `PrefillDriver` can retain an original speculative role directly,
without constructing a text request. Starting the driver and claiming each exact
recorded span are monotonic operations on that role's existing account. Aliases,
cancellation and state rollback cannot restart it or return a consumed ordinal.
The same step/run loop retains cancellation and completion ordering. Native span
handoff checks the exact role and actual lane frontier before borrowing the lane.

The shared session transaction accepts the span's LastPosition/StateOnly demand,
caller-prepared rollback copy and exact completion callback. It uses the existing
output publication, all-rank agreement, rollback and commit worker; draft spans
create no vocabulary result. Its concrete callback/return frames are charged to
the same metadata account before the transaction.

The original native prefill callback now consumes these contracts. The actual
whole prompt is copied by the existing registered pending-input program before
its U32 equation trace. Each recorded span adds the same static input view via
the existing native recorder. Its Graph, Record, physical, validation and group
controls use the ordinary reducers over that exact row; the role admits their
cumulative sum. The shared driver claims a row before any span work. Its rollback
copy completes before the span opens the same Scope/construction/recovery worker
used by decode. Static input indexing then runs in that bank. StateOnly completes
all state/validation roots without scores; LastPosition supplies the target seed.
A private settled completion is created only after exact native completion,
recovery and Record retirement. Cancellation and rollback never refund either
the span ordinal or its one group-bank construction. The closed controller owns
the copied source, equation reports and planning funding through all callbacks.
This bank currently requires the selected single-stream resident source; a
partitioned/distributed strategy or parallel layout is refused before native
construction because its agreement and transport producers are not in this bank.

Shared speculative proposal, history, verification-input and optimistic-prefix
buffers use a fixed retained host destination when the actual executor supplies
original metadata funding. Core constructs that destination itself after the
native hook charges its exact buffer/control request and the existing closed
HostPreparationAuthority token. Ordinary Vec conversions remain ordinary; no
operation attaches custody to a previously allocated Vec. Retained destinations
cannot grow or export their Vec, and owning iteration keeps custody until the
buffer and unconsumed elements retire. The same acceptance bookkeeping moves its
round commitment destination into publication rather than copying it. Optimistic
promotion discards its consumed first proposal in place. No proposal/verification
schedule or sampling policy changes.

Canonical speculative sequence construction and transactional copies use the
same GenerationSequence rules and existing RetainedGenerationStorage protocol.
The selected native adapter pays the concrete fixed token/EOS buffers, closed
Arc/Box provider and host-authority controls before construction. Every retained
copy uses the exact provider loan and shared copy-complete validator; ordinary
storage stays ordinary and unknown retained providers cannot fall back to an
unpriced clone. Snapshot/restore invokes that same copy hook before native state
mutation. Cancellation changes only the published scalar state, avoiding an
unnecessary token-buffer clone. Neither sequence custody nor its constructor
query grants native execution authority.

The terminal driver moves the sequence's existing immutable token owner and
statistics through the runtime result adapter. It no longer copies the committed
prefix into an unowned Vec. Only ordinary token storage can yield a raw Vec;
retained iteration and aliases preserve the closed provider until all payloads
and shared shells retire. The native initial preparation keeps typed paid errors
through its batch boundary while ordinary exception semantics are preserved.
The actual prepared-lane, request-table, terminal-row, scheduler-fact, candidate,
timing and returned-output destinations now use that same fixed host-buffer
hook. Known lane counts reserve their request and terminal destinations before
prefill; incremental growth prepares both replacement buffers before moving
existing rows. Coordination mutates the same borrowed slice and returns its
original container, so retained storage never passes through a raw Vec or skips
the existing participant agreement. Every added readiness exchange uses the
existing monotone per-attempt preparation account.

Request identity has a closed shared shell whose final alias retires the shell
before its host authority. Statistics separate copyable scalar telemetry from
the owned acceptance history. Verification prepares exactly the current prefix
plus one next-round slot before taking pending work; snapshot/restore prepare
the exact current prefix before native mutation. Final results move these
owners. Managed history has no infallible Clone, batch request extraction returns
the retained buffer, and appending to that buffer is fallible. The CLI consumes
its existing statistics owner after reading timing and termination.

Controlled snapshot and branch lookup now use counted sorted live-row buffers.
Identifiers remain monotone and handles retain the exact scope identity; row
removal never rewinds it. Growth allocates a complete replacement before moving
old rows. The shared saved-state owner closes its Rc, and both the snapshot
budget and logical reservation close their Arcs before releasing their host
custody. The budget retains its initialized Mutex/PAL separately, before the
last host token. Existing reserve/refund rules remain shared: failed copies
release retention while cumulative copy usage stays spent.

The neutral speculative host-metadata hook admits the actual shared-owner and
reservation queries before construction. Its ordinary default has no managed
authority; the native adapter validates the actual source pair, charges that
same planning account and rejects unknown storage. Snapshot and branch logical
estimates consume these concrete shell and table-growth queries instead of a
fixed map-node allowance. This is host custody, not numerical copy permission.

Controlled proposal, verification, step and branch-info arrays now use immutable
`SpeculativeValues`. The same borrowed proposal selector supplies ordinary and
counted construction. Managed construction copies or moves rows into a newly
paid driver buffer, then admits its closed shared shell before publication;
it never attaches custody to an existing source Vec. Retained record clones
share the payload without cloning nested capture rows. Copy-valued consuming
iterators retain the source, while other rows remain borrowed. Serialization
and deserialization keep the existing JSON array fields; deserialization creates
ordinary storage with no managed authority.

The controlled step compares borrowed proposal views and applies the existing
accept/reject/discard rule. New preparation failures are agreed before scheduler
work, and post-action record failures use the existing final delivery agreement.
The raw prediction-capture field now uses the existing `CapturedStepDelivery`:
legacy frames preserve ordinary copies, while retained frame clones share the
actual closed source owner. Serialization remains the previous nested frame
object, and deserialization creates legacy storage. The sampler drains an actual
`SpeculativeBuffer`; the controlled step preserves that buffer and admits only
its immutable shared shell. It never adopts an ordinary Vec into H or copies a
retained frame into an unfunded raw DTO. Activation rows retain their existing
paid destination worker. Role, logical position and tentative/accepted disposition
remain independent of capture storage and native completion.

The controlled
entry consumes its already-owned activation and raw-logit plans into the existing
installation calls; it no longer deep-clones either plan before installation or
an existing typed rejection. Their source allocation remains caller-owned until
the actual collector qualifies any new retained destination. Branch exchange
prepares the returned prefix from the exact incoming saved state before native
restore or slot mutation. Record allocation does not provide completion evidence
or refund snapshot, capture or transport allowances.

Request submission now moves ordinary EOS configuration unchanged or copies its
actual IDs into the funded immutable driver destination before prefill. Scalar
settings and proposal geometry use the same worker. A retained snapshot/restore
shares that immutable EOS allocation; no raw Vec clone escapes its custody.

Controlled sampler/RNG and semantic-state copies now have distinct constructor
queries and paid-copy hooks. The shared snapshot/restore worker obtains host
custody from the actual executor before calling them. Existing logical snapshot
size does not certify a constructor: unknown managed callback state refuses
before Clone/fork, while ordinary copying preserves its previous values. The
built-in plain semantic constraint has no allocated state. A qualified sampler
must retain custody in every escaping sampler/RNG alias and allocating error;
an enclosing snapshot alone is insufficient. Host funding grants no native copy
or completion permission, and logical copy budgets remain monotone.

Incoming caller-owned lane values, capture/sampler source queues, concrete native
sampler/RNG snapshot constructors, caller-owned semantic callbacks, enclosing
callbacks and encoded transport-failure storage still require their actual
producers. Native sampling retains its separate qualification. These container
joins preserve the public original speculative gate.

Public original speculation remains gated. Remaining joins include selected
sampling/probability work and complete enclosing lifecycle metadata/error producers. The typed sampler error adapter changes no sampling
qualification. External snapshot containers and generic pre-invocation refusal
transport still require their enclosing original owners; this copied-state
producer does not qualify the whole request.


Successful original equation advancement now requires an exact terminal Record
retirement pass in addition to completion evidence. Each configured prefill role
retains an authenticated observer independently of optional group registration.
After the existing Recovery finishes and its root payload retires, that observer
drains only the same role's completed native Records before the registry alias is
removed. This also covers a single-group equation with no neural group bank.
A busy or failed pass returns through the existing terminal-fence boundary; it
does not authorize the next chunk or refund any cumulative population.

For cached decode, model completion clones the already authenticated observer
from its concrete ModelExecution owner before taking execution Recovery. It
preserves validation and publication ordering, then performs the same exact drain
before caching successful completion. The shared text machine resolves and drops
that completion before another state-mutating decode. Escaped score/token aliases
and current state remain independently owned; the pass does not claim those
backings are gone. Native errors retain their original carrier, and failure or
unobservable cleanup poisons/stops the session. Ordinary completion is unchanged.
The new fixed observer/query transports enter the actual prefill-role and decode
collector control queries. No new scope, allocation budget, inference loop, or
per-unit synchronization boundary is introduced.


Composite media construction retains the actual immutable Qwen configuration in
`SharedCompositeConfig`, the same closed owner used by effective text
configuration. The constructor moves its configuration into that owner; model
access and nested decode admission share it without copying its maps. The shared
shell is admitted before allocation and retires before the configuration and its
metadata funding. No mutable configuration alias or new source selection is
exposed.

The direct composite handoff consumes the existing metadata-aware prepared
contract worker. Its prepared wrapper forwards the inner architecture's checked
graph, unit-count, transport comparison, state-layout and state-identity methods,
so validation still compares the actual constructed architecture with its exact
selection. It never treats the retained selection as independent evidence for
itself. Selected-state and source-transform diagnostics use that same worker's
metadata destination and preserve ordinary validation order and messages. Module
construction failures preserve their typed metadata cause through dispatch and
the existing media report's closed funding owner. This handoff does not qualify
unconverted family declarations, dispatch configuration producers, or native
media storage by itself.

The same selected native envelope now has an explicit completed-decode mode.
For the original no-capture resident text driver, both prefill and model/decode
completion require exact successful Record retirement before another equation.
The capacity reducer therefore considers every actual prefill/decode record with
its full opening state, whole current construction, and cumulative prior score
and validation-producing populations. It also covers each closing frontier after
adding that record's full score/validation populations. Keeping every score
backing conservatively covers escaped sampled tokens that may alias an earlier
score; scalar output shape is not a physical-capacity assumption. Sampling's
whole generation sum and full prepared-input population remain unchanged.

This replaces the equation-generation sum only when all carried facts are known
and the complete envelope is smaller. A late unknown decode population preserves
the original complete sum. The initial seeded state includes decode-only resumes,
and all existing source credits stay unchanged. Ordinary and prefill-only
construction contracts remain available with their previous behavior. No storage
is reused within an equation: native primitive outputs remain protected through
their actual complete submission. The pinned Metal producer's
`CommandEncoder::complete_receipt` destroys its EncodingCleanup handlers and
receipt payload before publishing `state->finish`; terminal Record progress
requires that completed receipt frontier. Exact equation retirement then removes
its remaining primitive/current/synchronizer owners. Failed or unsettled cleanup
prevents the shared driver from advancing.


Composite graph construction uses the ordinary `ExecutionGraph` validation
worker with an explicit metadata destination. Borrowed sorted name/index rows
replace temporary copied lookup names, resolved dependency rows detect duplicates,
and a prepaid min-heap preserves the smallest-ready-group topological order.
Reverse reachability marks each group before pushing it, so pending storage is
bounded by the actual group count. Ordered dependency lists, exact graph errors,
and disconnected-group diagnostic order retain the original semantics. Every
owning graph row, diagnostic name and working vector is admitted before birth.

Both Qwen media architectures construct their actual vision/decoder/prediction
declarations through this worker for checked contract and parameter-description
construction. Ordinary execution shares these same declaration methods. Group
unit counts preserve their source validation with paid diagnostics, and transport
comparison borrows the exact declarations used by ordinary transport ownership.
No selected graph substitutes for the architecture's declarations, no schedule
or native submission authority is introduced, and the enclosing media result or
error continues to retain its metadata funding.


Checked Qwen composite state declarations use the same geometry destinations as
ordinary construction. Qwen VL preserves its first-layer scalar position delta
and each actual attention/KV-head policy; conditional hybrid delegates to its
existing ordered hybrid state worker. Parallel geometry clones use the shared
counted layout copier. The actual ordinary forward state checks select those
same destinations when a workspace Context participates, retaining exact state
comparisons and paid mismatch diagnostics.

Composite parameter descriptions reuse their already constructed graph when
building the group-major execution-unit layout. Counts come from the actual
family worker and the existing counted layout constructor owns the names and
rows. Conditional description no longer rebuilds an ordinary second graph just
to obtain that layout. These changes preserve source and state policy; they do
not qualify remaining configuration identities or native media capacity.

The source-bound Metal dense projection facts also distinguish actual F32
activations with completed row-contiguous BF16 matrix weights. For non-singleton
`[N,K]` weights, the selected shared projection transposes their strides to
`[1,K]`; native AsType's vector copy preserves those strides, and Metal matmul
accepts the resulting column-contiguous matrix directly. The same geometry
worker therefore excludes only a second full weight compaction. It retains the
full at-most-F32 casts for both operands, input and reshape copies, result,
geometry-selected split-K population, bias, and existing custom-kernel ceiling.
No primitive lifetime, birth count, completion or cumulative budget is relaxed.

The refinement requires both exact scalar representations and the actual source
layout already retained by the accepted parameter-epoch contract. Missing,
conflicting, noncontiguous or singleton weight evidence, general matmul, and
other projection mechanisms keep their generic union. Counted and owning fact
adapters use the same producer and diagnostic destination. The focused source
regression uses the real scalar-widening and shared projection constructors to
check this mixed case, retain cast costs, and preserve unknown/singleton fallbacks.


The native fixed kernel families memoize their pure source-qualification result
for the lifetime of the binary. These facts depend only on immutable source
definitions, finite signatures and the compiled native ABI/platform layout;
they do not observe devices, request shapes, shader initialization or cache warmth.
This avoids repeating source-layout counting for every operation in a cold
equation trace. The existing process baseline includes the fixed memoization
cells. Actual constructor layout queries, admission, realization and per-call
source/shape validation remain in their existing owners and run as before.


Composite cache identity uses the same counted fingerprint machinery as text
identity. Qwen vision schedule and format fields, VL text/vision/token/position
fields, and conditional text/vision/token fields are emitted by one ordinary or
counted producer with unchanged serialization. Model state-identity hooks consume
those actual configuration fingerprints and the shared scalar placement checks,
then move the paid strings into `ModelStateIdentity` through its existing
validator. Direct dispatch also uses these producers for its expected cache
identity and effective model label. No expected selection fingerprint is used as
a substitute for actual configuration evidence. The enclosing media result/error
owns the metadata funding and shared model configuration remains immutable.

The original resident recipe now consumes standalone exact and approximate GELU
operations through the same native equation receipts used by the shared activation
workers. Exact GELU counts its four binary calls, Erf and three eager scalars;
approximate GELU counts seven binary calls, Sqrt, Tanh and five eager scalars.
Each binary retains both possible casts, both broadcasts and its result; each
unary retains its cast and result. The already supported gated approximate GELU
adds its final up multiplication to that same activation receipt.

Both paths use the supplied stream and the existing standard unary/binary native
worker. Their original physical and numerical-host emitters remain authoritative;
there is no custom kernel/cache shortcut, fusion assumption, lifetime reduction,
source credit or new grant. The same recorder derives complete Graph, Record,
worker and birth populations from the receipt before native preparation. Unknown
activation kinds and unrelated missing operation receipts still prevent a complete
native program. This closes an operation used by shared unary decoder and media
MLPs without asserting support for an otherwise incomplete execution path.


Workspace report reduction keeps one prepaid, sorted identity index alongside
its stable node/edge destinations. Lookup uses binary search while node insertion
and traversal order stay unchanged. Residual accumulation consumes that same
identity order, avoiding repeated full scans and insertion sorting during cold
long-prompt inspection. The index has exactly the declared node capacity and
is included in layout, constructor, retained-prefix and failure accounting.
Short index storage refuses before mutation just like the other destinations;
source aliases and unknown/overflow precedence retain their existing semantics.


Prepared composite construction retains the actual composite requirements already
validated while preparing its source graph. The existing closed source owner
owns those declarations; its aliases borrow the same selection, inspection,
