format requirements and physical source graph without rebuilding a cold execution
class or copying the inspection catalog. The declarations retire before their
source graph, and no declaration points back to its enclosing source owner.

The total composite route authenticates the retained selection and reuses the
existing exact target-store validation witness. Its handoff retains a closed
source alias through construction and admission; checked metadata pays the
control transports before retaining them. Public construction from owned
requirements uses the same dispatch and validation worker. This changes no
semantic branch, source recipe, processor choice or native admission gate.


A successful prepared composite handoff retains aliases of the actual effective
target and optional source configurations held by Qwen VL/conditional models,
together with that handoff's actual capability report. One inline completion
slot in the existing source owner publishes this pair only after full contract
validation. The slot contains no source alias and cannot form an ownership
cycle. It retains the same closed configuration/report payloads rather than a
second configuration or capability cache.

Repeated prepared construction authenticates the same immutable selection,
configuration family and source-transform presence. It consumes those owners
through the same model constructor and still validates the resulting contract;
it does not rebuild selected format maps. Checked reconstruction refuses a
missing completed owner before ordinary format/configuration producers. Fixed
control destinations are charged before retained aliases and nested constructor
work. Standalone owned construction preserves source-before-target validation
and failure order. Nested static-module metadata and complete native media
receipts remain required before the original media admission gate can open.


Conditional Qwen construction borrows its retained text configuration into the
same decoder constructor used by an owning hybrid model. It consumes the
resulting pinned modules directly, avoiding a full configuration clone and a
temporary owning model. Operator/configuration checks, integer geometry, static
modules, prediction-group validation and shared MTP extension still run in their
original order. No group validation is inferred from the parent model.

The shared constructor emits static parameter names, prediction path tables and
MTP module specifications through the existing Context metadata destinations.
Every prediction row/string is paid before birth; the ordinary and checked group
constructors use the same loop and diagnostic predicates. The existing enclosing
media result/error retains funding through these modules and failures. This adds
no native admission, equation, configuration selection or additional grant.
The same index marks borrowed roots once in the existing byte-sized mark buffer.
Only identities already in the report union are marked; unused borrowed roots
and their descendants do not enter that union. Residual exclusion then reads
that bit, avoiding a full borrowed-root scan per node without another allocation.


The selected affine and MXFP4 projection receipt consumes the native supplied
stream through the existing quantized-matmul frontend. Affine activation,
scale, and bias promotion now pass that stream explicitly; validation and dtype
promotion order remain shared with ordinary calls. The original precompiled
quantized-kernel wrappers bypass unused JIT template construction before it
allocates. The shared selector layout query includes the literal-derived
quantized names, all 18 recursive concatenate arguments, and wrapper controls.
Ordinary JIT construction remains unchanged. The ordered
`mlx-quantized-supplied-stream.patch` participates in the native source identity.

This closes a one-stream projection receipt for the existing affine and MXFP4
formats. It retains every cast, up to four compactions, split/reduction buffers,
output bias, and the floating replacement alternative (including its BF16 source
controls). It does not reduce physical population or extend packed embedding,
block-FP8, or unrelated operation receipts. The component regression supplies
actual cold reports to the existing original request admission before native
Graph/Record creation. Nonzero witnesses compare exact/approximate GELU and
quantized input/companion casts plus MXFP4 with the same ordinary workers and
check escaped-output account retirement. Native execution of these new witnesses
is a required integration check; source/patch validation alone is not a native
qualification result.


Prepared local neural submission now carries its existing generic account
custody through native submission, consumer waits, completion, and owning
failures. Native methods still require the actual `OriginalScopeObserver` and
preserve current/retained observer equality before cloning or submitting roots.
The custody type does not confer native authority. Exact slot/control queries
measure the selected custody and observer types, including both owning error
transports; the default remains the original text control guard. This permits a
separately admitted speculative role to retain its own request account through
the same completion and retirement worker. The pointwise plan remains specific
to its existing text control quote. No speculative admission gate or native
receipt is activated by this generic lifetime join.


The closed shared configuration owner can internally retain an immutable member
projection of another actual configuration owner. A private typed parent alias
and field-access function replace a copied child configuration. Its exact Box
and Arc representations and controls are charged before allocation or alias
construction; no raw Arc, Weak, mutable field or public projection capability is
exposed. On the final alias, the Arc shell retires first, the erased projection
Box retires next, and the parent alias retires before the new metadata funding.
The ordinary owned-value variant keeps the same value semantics.

Qwen VL and conditional construction use this projection for VisionStatic's
vision policy. The shared vision module remains independent of its parent family
types, and static-module Clone now shares the same immutable policy rather than
copying its schedule and format map. Public owned vision constructors and
composite projected constructors use the same vision construction worker. The
actual merger-width vector is also emitted through the Context metadata
destination. Vision validation/spec/name producers still require their existing
metadata completion before original media admission can be qualified.

The report identity index builds sorted binary runs rather than shifting a
complete sorted vector for each new identity. Equal-sized runs merge through
the already prepaid DFS frames before traversal begins; remaining runs merge
once after graph discovery. Lookup during discovery searches those runs, and
subsequent report traversal uses the final sorted index. Stable node/edge order,
exact identity comparisons, arithmetic error order and five heap destinations
are unchanged. The actual merge cursors are included in control sizing.


Vision geometry validation uses one worker with ordinary or Context metadata
destinations. The exact merger-index vector and format-prefix Strings are paid
before construction; the sorted merger indices are compared directly against
their ordinals rather than allocating a second expected vector. Scalar, mode,
schedule and per-format checks retain their original order and diagnostics.
The fixed encoding validator supplies the same diagnostic without constructing
an intermediate ordinary error. VisionStatic and both composite constructors
consume this checked worker during funded reconstruction. No stored selection
or parent configuration is treated as a substitute for actual validation.


Constructed rotary receipts include the actual still-lazy wavelength frequency
ancestors: Arange, fifteen shared binary workers, two where workers, reciprocal,
and twelve distinct scalar constructors. Input-product rotary adds its retained
reciprocal for wavelength/proportional algorithms. Nontraditional wavelength
rotary retains its actual explicit-product path; traditional rotary retains the
existing batch-wise fused operator. First-use physical frequency buffers remain
in the existing rotary emitter. No family label supplies a missing operation
fact, and caller-provided cosine/sine or multi-axis paths retain their separate
requirements.

The same source accounting includes the fused wrapper's exact output-vector
extent and the explicit worker's fixed output arrays. General static indexing
borrows its actual declarations through the existing slice/reshape worker;
gather-owned suffixes retain their existing construction and validation. The
index-control profile applies only to no-array/no-ellipsis operations with at
most four axes/indices, checked by the rotary source geometry and the inline
container layout. These queries describe constructors and confer no allocation
or native authority. A staged component witness constructs wavelength and
proportional frequency ancestors inside the genuinely admitted native graph,
compares nonzero outputs with the ordinary shared workers (including partial
rotation and both pair layouts), and checks escaped-output retirement. Its
native execution remains an integration requirement; a receipt alone does not
qualify an entire model or an unrelated preexisting source graph.


The shared Qwen vision module constructors emit their actual rooted parameter
identities, selected format companions, block activation strings and merger
vector storage through Context metadata destinations. LayerNorm, PatchEmbed,
linear projections, attention, vision blocks, mergers and VisionStatic use the
same construction order and backend spec workers for ordinary and checked
contexts. A borrowed rooted-name formatter avoids an intermediate name where
only the final ParameterSpec needs ownership. Format lookup retains the existing
relative/full-name precedence and pays its fallback prefix before construction.
Composite capability and missing-vision failures also use the existing paid
diagnostic adapters. Shapes, equations, selected formats and native admission
remain unchanged; the enclosing media result/error retains constructor funding.


Composite parameter descriptions consume the canonical graph, unit layout and
actual emitted parameter groups through the runtime's shared owning validator.
The complete-group constructor validates the same expected targets and owners
as the separate-authority constructor without duplicating each name, shape,
companion and placement record. The composite Context pays destination vectors,
static-role strings and execution-group owner copies before those births; it
remains retained by the enclosing prepared equation through description use and
failure. Partition-global reconstruction borrows the original hybrid text config
and projects vision config from its closed immutable prepared owner. It preserves
the checkpoint-global declarations even when the executing modules are local.
The separate-authority validator remains available for callers comparing an
independently supplied expected group set. Inner routed text and hybrid group-member
construction remains a separate metadata boundary; this ownership transfer alone
does not qualify native managed-media admission.


Shared Qwen vision parameter-group construction now uses one ordinary/Context
worker for block norms, fused QKV segments, MLP projections, patch/position
modules and main/DeepStack mergers. The runtime's existing strict parameter
visitor and placement validators remain authoritative. The metadata route pays
names, member containers, QKV segment copies, output vectors and pinned-unit
consumer owners before constructing them; complete composite descriptions call
that route directly. Placement predicates, consumer units and traversal order
are unchanged. A plain group-only result consumes each owned group instead of
copying its payload. Routed text and hybrid/MTP member builders remain distinct
pending producers, so this does not change native managed-media qualification.


The Qwen routed parameter-group hook now uses the same ordinary/Context worker
as its public declaration API. Shared decoder attention and dense-MLP groups
reuse their existing paid workers; routed experts retain the exact gate/down
name predicates, rank checks, quantization alignment and fused segment placement.
Names, segment copies and group-vector growth are charged before construction.
The composite VL description and routed block factory consume this hook directly.
This completes these declaration destinations, not the separate routed numerical
constructors or native media admission evidence.


Conditional hybrid parameter groups now use a shared metadata destination for
norms, recurrent and attention projections, dense/routed/shared experts and MTP
pinned modules. Placement reads the exact borrowed primary/companion declaration
from the existing parameter visitor. FP8 segment conversion therefore keeps its
owning-weight format and alignment validation, without creating temporary owning
metadata. Names, segment buffers and every MTP consumer copy are reserved before
birth. Ordinary APIs use the same worker and error variants. The composite
conditional description consumes this path; native managed-media qualification
still requires the remaining equation and continuation/output destinations.


The shared vision continuation path reserves its actual configured DeepStack
container through the participating Context before construction, and checks any
later growth before creating a captured feature. Final output moves that same
container. Replacing transported continuation tensors now reuses the supplied
vector by draining the two rotary roots instead of collecting a new suffix.
Prepared encoder table checks retain their original/projected owner loans and
route diagnostics through the Context before error allocation. Ordinary inverse
permutation and its metadata companion share one validator; original/projected
inputs continue borrowing their already-prepared inverse tables. None of these
changes repeats encoder work or changes the native media qualification gate.


Original native publication control storage distinguishes retained per-row owners
from sequential worker call frames. Every possible sidecar heap node, observation
vector, prepared clone slot, and native clone handle remains charged for the
complete admitted row and publication populations. Inspection/preparation/attach
frames are charged once per publication, and clone preparation/fill/drop frames
once per actual inventory or Work: those closed loops reuse the same call frame
and retain only their separately priced results. Failed handoffs retain the
existing original custody and full failure-owner allowance; no publication count,
row capacity, native payload, or cumulative budget is refunded.


The independent speculative decoder now uses the existing eager original
U32 `[1,N]` input constructor when its explicit invocation owner supplies the
accepted input/view plan. Its exact prepared-runtime input facts enter Graph,
physical birth and control requirements once: the equation recorder already
excludes the architecture's exact token-placeholder ordinal. Ordinary calls keep
their existing source constructor.

Proposal and verification readouts use the same static sequence-position index
as ordinary execution. The actual index trace is reduced by the existing native
recorder and appended to the sole equation receipt before admission. Completion
unions retain additive primitive, root, edge, CPU, grouped-output and nested-work
obligations, and recompute the combined native worker layout from its retained
birth/sort populations; separate worker sizes are not assumed additive. All
fallible combinations precede mutation of the accepted source recipe.

The original decoder constructs the finite row views while that exact invocation
is current, then completes parent logits, row descendants and the independent
cache/validation roots through the enclosing role's existing completion worker.
The output owns once-only completed row slots and retains the same role after
the callback returns. Later sampler readout moves an existing row without a
new native scope or allocation. Fixed wrong-role/input/consumed-slot refusals
retain the observer's existing failure carrier without diagnostic construction.
This join supplies input/readout producers; request roles, checkpoint copies,
sampling and public capability acceptance still require their own complete
admission and lifetime joins.

The native exception boundary also has a paid retained-source constructor. It
stores the already-custodied Rust error in one closed erased Box without
formatting a diagnostic String; its exact generic layout is charged before
construction. The erasure frees that Box before destroying the typed cause, so
its final account cannot retire ahead of the error allocation. Source downcasts
remain available, and ordinary exception construction retains its old behavior.

The prepared request pipeline cache is sized from the retained recipe's complete
native kernel population once per single-GPU equation and sampling row. Fixed Eval descends
only into unscheduled descriptors, marks a primitive and its siblings evaluated,
and detaches ordinary completed graphs before the next frontier. Nested group,
attention and adaptive-sampling completions therefore partition shader work;
their fresh Synchronizers issue no shader lookup. Both the allocation query and
cache constructor consume this same count. The cache still preallocates and
monotonically spends one concrete pipeline row per possible lookup, retains every
platform handle through its final graph/error alias, and releases raw metadata
custody only after those rows retire. Actual host copy/reload/transfer and saved
resume-copy descriptors keep their independent populations. Failure never
refunds a cache row or permits another request attempt. Selector string/control
requests remain cumulatively priced for every admitted kernel attempt.


The original resident Graph quota composes a single no-tracing descriptor DAG
across its actual nested and final completions. The native fixed evaluator skips
non-unscheduled descriptors, marks each successfully dispatched descriptor and
its siblings evaluated, and detaches them before another completion. The recipe
therefore charges primitive prologues, temporaries, buffer-routing owners and
kernel resource registrations once. Every fresh Synchronizer, its root storage,
fixed-Eval construction bank, event owner, consumer wait and possible encoder
cleanup remains cumulative. The shared native worker query takes explicit
completion and wait populations; it derives interval resources from actual
kernel argument registrations across those frontiers. It does not use a peak
instead of a constructor sum, refund quota, or grant a replay after failure.
Mixed CPU/GPU rows retain their previous conservative repeated worker bound.
Record traversal reservations and independent host/source-copy producers remain
separate. Native parity is exercised by the existing nonzero key-block attention
case, which performs 66 prepared nested completions plus final evaluation under
the request's derived quotas; the cold frontier regression also checks ordinary
single-Eval parity, new owner growth, and overflow refusal.

Mixed CPU/GPU pipeline rows retain the complete per-completion kernel ceiling.
Although a completed descriptor does not execute again, a fresh GPU Synchronizer
can first consume an unscheduled CPU result and create an additional fence-shader
edge. The single-GPU once-per-DAG reduction does not claim that mixed frontier
composition. Copy/reload/transfer and resume-copy counts remain independent.

Qwen composite prepared-input assembly uses the actual construction Context for
its metadata destinations. The ordinary public constructor and counted internal
entry share the same ordered token, projected-value and encoded-media worker.
Token/kind/projected vectors reserve from the exact prepared part count; pixel
and optional grid vectors reserve from the borrowed encoded-part count, and each
retained grid reserves before copying its actual entries. Placeholder tensors,
source aliases and pixel concatenation preserve their existing order. Borrowed
model-input part vectors likewise reserve before the shared layered callback.
Hybrid semantic-token preparation uses the same checked destination before
constructing any token. These containers remain under the enclosing prepared
media/quote funding through success, partial failure and drop. The media-plan
input loan uses the same identity/count validator for ordinary String errors and
Context-paid errors, avoiding an allocated intermediate diagnostic before the
paid path. This changes no source selection, encoder scheduling, numerical
equation or native media qualification gate.

Media ingress validates runtime state against retained local geometry without
cloning existing TP or hybrid partition layouts. When Qwen VL needs a PP slice,
the shared StateLayout slice worker admits its exact policy/vector/segment
copies before construction; full unretained layouts use the existing counted
family state constructor. Ordinary slicing and counted slicing preserve the
same range rejection, intersecting segment identities, lifetime, rebased ranges
and processed-token frontiers, followed by the same component/partition
validator. Full-layout and sliced-policy cloning share the same exhaustive
nested-policy allocation query. Ingress source/pixel/frontier failures use the
current metadata destination and remain under the enclosing prepared-media
funding; no layout comparison grants native state or execution authority.


Independent speculative state and completed output retain a shared prepared
stream when startup is original. Cloning that closed owner does not clone the
native C Stream wrapper or create a queue. Ordinary stream cloning keeps its
existing behavior. The prepared stream retains the exact startup host account
through its wrapper and shared/retirement shells; native operation authority
continues to come from the separately admitted speculative role.


Original independent-draft startup now consumes the runtime request's once-only
target/draft startup ticket before constructing an actually empty canonical
resident cache. The shared resident-table validator checks the existing selected
layout, component placements, local range and concrete storage policy; an
additional state-owned predicate requires every numerical slot and frontier to
be empty. The same fixed dense-table producer builds independent outer and child
tables from that source. The ticket is retained by the closed host-preparation
authority, whose actual owner bytes are included alongside the tables, erased
typed state box and supplied-stream wrapper. State/output stream aliases and
table metadata keep that account until their final allocation retires; typed
constructor errors retain it through the paid source/error bridge. No native
invocation role is created by this host-only startup.

Ordinary startup continues to fork the canonical cache, including restored
prompt state. Original startup selects the same host-only empty constructor when
the actual source is empty; populated sources instead consume the independently
admitted resident copy described above, preserving all actual cache contents.
Both keep the selected source role/origin and the prepared stream. External
controlled checkpoint/restore constructors remain a separate join, and public
original speculative support remains gated.

Media decoder spans reserve their ordered-part, projected-slice and DeepStack
containers through the active workspace metadata context before cloning or
constructing their contents. The shared ordered-input and multi-axis rotary
workers keep ordinary validation and tensor equations while accepting counted
host destinations. Position construction borrows the admitted axis slices;
encoder outputs remain retained once and are sliced for each decoder interval.
The enclosing media report/failure owner retains planning funding through these
destinations. This metadata join creates no native operation or submission
authority and does not qualify an incomplete native media recipe.

The media equation's decode input follows the same descriptor, repeated-identity
check and family part-admission workers as ordinary prepared input. Counted
inspector companions reserve actual descriptor shapes and metadata-read buffers
before constructing them; ordinary-only inspectors refuse before entering an
unaccounted constructor. Qwen policy views and output-plan materialization are
shared between both destinations. Errors retain their portable causes and use
the enclosing media planning account, which remains live through the complete
report or failure. No saved shape is treated as tensor identity or native
authority.


The native graph arena resumes allocation search after its last successful block
instead of rescanning the entire live prefix for every prepared node. The cursor
is an arena-owned offset under the existing allocator loan; splitting advances
it to a valid successor, and coalescing repairs any cursor whose block header is
absorbed. A failed search still visits every current block exactly once. Block
geometry, full-scan exhaustion, allocation ownership, and final retirement are
unchanged. The arena's queried header size includes its cursor and scratch offset;
the fresh-capacity bound still counts every allocation attempt without reuse
credit, independently of which free block fits first.

The resident media decoder continuation uses counted part, grid, position and
DeepStack containers in its existing family forward worker. Global position
construction shares the same validate/emit traversal with ordinary input and
reserves each complete axis before writes. The continuation preserves the
persisted position delta and exact local state-layout validation; it does not
re-enter the vision encoder for a text decode step.

Native prepared-buffer allocation serializes with the concrete allocator's existing mutex, including concurrent completion retirement. The original physical allowance retries only its atomic counter comparison when another debit or refund changes that counter; it rechecks capacity before the successful debit and performs the physical allocation once. Allocator waiting creates no extra capacity or work attempt. Graph allocation releases its loan before entering the physical allocator, and physical free releases the allocator mutex before returning Graph storage and refunding the allowance. Genuine allocator refusal still follows the existing partial-construction rollback.


Original prepared media now reaches the same funded workspace and native recipe
recorder used by actual text preparation. The native adapter authenticates the
completed input, selected session and current parameter epoch before projecting
its existing backing, then runs the retained architecture's encoder-once and
decoder intervals plus shared sampling equations. A prepared-source interval
explicitly has no synthetic token initialization to remove; later decode
intervals identify their actual initialization operation. Native lowering and
capacity arithmetic remain in the existing recorder.

The projection constructor shares the ordinary source worker and accepts the
actual retained workspace metadata account without creating an unquoted lease.
Source table aliases, projected state, trace reports, native recipe and Context
remain inside a closed result with funding last. A failed partial trace retires
its non-Send intervals before transporting the original typed cause, completed
source table owners and metadata custody through the existing paid error owner.
Ordinary media diagnostics retain their original lease and use the same traversal.

Public original media preparation still refuses an incomplete native request.
After fixed source/capture preflight, it reports the first actual equation or
sampling operation missing a receipt. If operation reduction is complete, the
request still requires source registration, full native Q sealing and execution
control installation; descriptive media output geometry does not grant those
resources. This change does not run the encoder or promote diagnostic metadata
to native completion evidence.


Original strict packed embedding now consumes the existing selected-row affine
or MXFP4 worker when its input rank is at most two. The source geometry and
companion validation stay in the shared physical operation facts; the native
receipt adds the actual flatten, row gathers, companion promotion, dequantizer,
F32 result cast and reshape on the supplied stream. GGUF custom-kernel and
block-FP8 producers retain their separate qualification requirements.

The Metal dequantizer's retained fallback object is constructed through the
accepted Graph allocator before the primitive is born. Its shapes and scalars
occupy the actual shared allocation; the pinned libc++ small-buffer function
holds only a shared pointer. Both allocation and allocator retain the arena
through destruction of the callable and its shared shell, without a Scope or
primitive back-reference. The native Graph census names the concrete callable
and Quantize control layouts. Ordinary CPU and Metal calls keep the same
fallback equations and ordinary allocation path. The original receipt covers
the Metal inference worker, whose native evaluation does not invoke that
fallback; it does not qualify automatic differentiation or CPU execution.

A nonzero component regression constructs affine and MXFP4 parameters through
the ordinary quantizer, then compares the selected-row worker under capacities
derived from its actual operation report. It includes differing floating
affine companions, all supported affine bit/group descriptors in the cold
query, and retained-output account retirement.


Prepared multi-axis rotary now has a source-derived original Metal receipt for
the existing borrowed-frequency worker. The actual native entry validates the
same inline owner profile as the cold query before constructing array owners:
input rank and axis count at most four, with round-robin selection additionally
limited to four half-width entries. Independent-axis and split-half widths are
not capped. Signed coordinates retain their widened saturating addition and
minimum policy; unsigned coordinates use the same conservative native envelope.
The recipe includes frequency/scalar copies, indexed columns, casts/broadcasts,
layout concatenations, both trigonometric branches and output reshapes.

Actual Rust row/output-shape owners use SmallVec; qualified original branches
stay inline. Prepared frequencies remain the supplied immutable source and are
copied through the accepted native Graph/buffer domain. Typed original errors
retain the existing failure-account carrier through closed neutral error shells
without adding a Scope or graph back-reference. Ordinary calls retain their
frequency generation, equations and error messages. Larger original profiles
remain implementation work for a paid row bank; this finite profile is not a
model-family limitation or an eventual integration cap.


Prepared-input workspace projection is now a shared runtime mechanism. The
architecture retains the actual A/B semantic comparison, while the runtime
visits the genuine original prepared owner through its backend tensor projector
and checks the resulting ordered descriptors. Only that constructor can create
the closed source witness: its exact complete metadata root selection is paired
with an alias of the original B account. Unknown backing never becomes credit.
The witness retains metadata and accounting; native tensors stay in the caller's
completed input owner.

Native publication retains that same accepted source profile in Work, including
prepared work before activation. Cache metadata must share the exact B
materialization account and pool; equal host inputs, semantic cache values or
another B in the same pool do not match. One shared entry builder authenticates
the original table and prepared source before adoption, then omits their already
funded metadata from new registrations. The existing publication keeps actual
original cache owners in its non-native inventory. Missing profiles and foreign
sources remain rejected; no unquoted lease, new source account, native root
backedge or completion shortcut is introduced. Saved-state publication still
requires its own actual source profile.

The existing registered-root constructor can combine those prepared roots with
registered decoder roots before the first equation. Its separate closed
RegisteredPreparedWorkspaceStorage result cannot expose the combined selection
as a registered source-copy certificate. Controller/residual composition uses
the existing traversal and arithmetic, then retains the registered decoder pin
and the original B account-only pin through the incremental quote, reservation
and run. B is neither registered nor charged again, and no scalar is subtracted
from a peak. The native media recipe adapter consumes this binding before its
actual media trace; public native admission still requires complete receipts,
source-aware native carryover, Q sealing and execution installation.

Prepared media native carryover uses the same exact borrowed-root selection as
its residual admission. The shared report reducer emits opening and closing
backing populations after excluding those identities, counting possible aliases
and collapsed backing populations in its existing traversal. No aggregate byte
subtraction supplies source credit. The prepared native recorder requires that
selection and seeded populations; ordinary text observations keep their complete
opening and closing populations. The score observation uses the residual only
for native carryover, while sampling still receives the complete score backing.
Completed input custody and the planning account remain with the closed prepared
source/report owners. These descriptive populations do not issue native work or
make an incomplete media recipe executable.

Native request quotation borrows one completed equation/sampling observation in
its shared post-trace assembler. That assembler owns the existing controller,
residual, native-population and sequence-seal composition; text tracing does not
repeat those policies. The generic sampling-to-vocabulary report addition lives
with the runtime sampling report and remains the same worker behind the
architecture text helper. Borrowed reports never replace their enclosing source
or planning-account custody.


Prepared spatial rotary uses one finite native row bank for independent axes,
split halves and round-robin sections. The same numerical worker expands an
independent row before appending it, so it retains one row population. Ordinary
execution keeps its local row vector. Original execution allocates both the bank
header and its exactly reserved `ArrayVector` backing from the accepted Graph
allocator, after checking the explicit current observer. Append cannot grow;
concatenate checks the same role and supplied stream and consumes the bank once.
A local allocator reference survives row destruction, backing release and final
header deallocation. The bank retains no Scope or Record back-reference. The
resulting graph keeps its normal descriptor/input and physical-buffer owners.

The source-derived rotary receipt uses the actual row count for maximum operands
and adds one checked resident control envelope for the concrete bank header,
backing and borrowed output-shape copies. A native layout query proves that those
allocations fit the existing accepted classes before qualification. Replacing
only the final dimension of a borrowed source shape uses the ordinary native
reshape worker and Graph-owned Shape storage; no Rust shape vector is created.
There is no fixed four-axis, four-column or rank-four qualification cap. Count,
shape and allocator-layout failures remain checked refusals; prepared frequency
source validation, the full numerical primitive/temporary populations, and the
existing completion/retirement requirements remain in force. Component cases
cover larger axes, a 32-column round-robin table and rank 12 with derived Q,
Graph and Record capacities and the neutral scalar rotary reference.

The prepared-media consumer now passes its exact completed input/source binding,
actual equation and sampling reports, and retained layerwise source selection to
that same native quote assembler. Completed input is an explicit preparation
profile: its B witness owns the existing leaves, descriptor graph, canonical
parts and cache identity, so no token upload or repeated identity constructor is
requested. Its physical roots are excluded only through the already validated
residual selection; the account-only B pin survives in the resulting proof.
Logical media-state diagnostics still use the retained semantic position facts.

When numerical receipts are complete, this path selects the actual Graph/Record
and buffer populations, composes the existing controller contribution and seals
the shared sequence quote. It still refuses before reservation/native execution
until the actual media installation path is connected. Original token-domain
controllers use their existing authenticated source worker; empty source
inventories reuse ordinary validation without a map allocation. Other shared
ordinary controller inventories remain an explicit missing original-controller
producer, rather than being adopted during original request planning.


The native text quotation installs an accepted candidate through one consuming
worker shared independently of the input's quote producer. It moves the existing
reservation, observed recipe and source selections into the unchanged sequence,
Record, Graph, native-storage and preparation banks. The handoff makes no second
reservation or source clone. Its concrete control representation is included in
the accepted quote, and lexical decoder-source cleanup is re-established before
any fallible pin or funding conversion. Completed prepared-media input continues
to require its exact source witness and prompt handoff before public activation;
this shared installer does not reinterpret completed B as a token upload.


Completed native media quotation carries its actual prepared-input account
witness through the same candidate, reservation and accepted quote owners. The
portable witness compares the original materialization account by private owner
identity; equal source contents, shapes or logical byte counts cannot substitute
an independently materialized input. It retains accounting and workspace-root
metadata, with no native tensor or completion backedge.

The backend's shared prompt binder authenticates this witness against the
completed packet and its canonical parts/cache before moving the input. It then
uses the existing one-use InferenceTextPreparation binding transition and
attaches the same accepted request and quote. This transition explicitly permits
already constructed inputs: it does not claim an upload Scope or reconstruct
encoder input. The original media packet remains available to the same encoder
and chunked decoder driver. Token input and saved-resume routes carry no media
witness. Full media admission remains conditional on complete native quotation
and the corresponding source-specific ingress checks.


The original native GPU receipt distinguishes descriptor shape rank from the
rank used by numerical workers. Prepared spatial rotary performs arithmetic on
its actual two-dimensional flattened positions and restores the two output
prefixes with the shared reshape worker. Its high-rank reshapes, and ordinary
reshape/concatenate operations, now include a native source-rank supplement for
SmallVector growth, contiguous-dimension collapse, cast candidates and temporary
slice Shape/Strides. The supplement queries the existing workers; their numerical
equations and Graph allocators are unchanged. Every allocation still consumes the
entered accepted Graph before construction and keeps that allocator through
member destruction. Initial, nested/final, and combined completion recipes retain
the supplementary extents while keeping the full host-graph shape rank. Other
high-rank mechanisms retain their existing qualification requirements. Larger row
counts and high-rank strided input have separate numerical component cases, each
using the actual derived physical/Graph/Record capacities and scalar reference.
The borrowed-prefix reshape also exposes its closed host-control query for other
shared native operators; its Shape backing remains part of the source-rank Graph
population.


Ungrouped block-FP8 projection keeps the shared PhysicalLinear equation and
its ordinary floating replacement. Managed Metal execution consumes finite
prepared activation-quantization and tiled/scalar projection kernel families,
with runtime dimensions taken from the actual rank-two native operands. The
existing shaders are shared by ordinary and prepared definitions. Quantization
keeps both sibling outputs; each invocation prices descriptor, copy, metadata,
scale-lookup, optional bias and completion populations. Observed prepare/finish
and grouped/segmented projections need their own retained operation receipts;
the ungrouped receipt does not authorize those paths.

Unsigned E8M0 scale decoding borrows one immutable process-owned 256-value
lookup table. Its fixed bytes belong to the shared native-domain baseline,
while each native upload and gather remains in the operation tensor bound.
No per-projection Rust lookup vector remains, including ordinary grouped and
observed use of the same decoder.

Completed prepared-media input now enters the same native candidate planner as
original token input. Fixed source and capture authentication precede inspection;
the candidate borrows the planner's validated controller contract and retained
parameter selection, then carries its actual prepared-input source witness
through completeness comparison, reservation, installation, and prompt binding.
An already completed input contributes no new upload destination. Numerical
receipt gaps remain typed refusals, and incomplete workspace reports retain the
shared planner's retry classification. Successful binding retains the accepted
Q and planning account without executing prefill or rebuilding the supplied B.

The accepted prepared-media source retains the actual funded workspace Context
that produced its winning quote. Its native input view lends that Context with
the existing request and completed B. The shared media source factory pays the
validated graph copy, cut flags, retained-value slots and fixed source controls
before their births. It retains the same cumulative ledger until its source
containers retire; no new Context, census or account is synthesized. Ordinary
media still rejects a managed reservation, while the explicit counted entry
requires funded metadata and the actual bound source/session/cache relationship
before using the shared one-use prefill driver. Escaped native source errors
retain account-only custody, preserving before-mutation classification. This
source-construction join does not change numerical receipt coverage or authorize
a second media upload.


Original speculative prefill copies the actual immutable native token matrix once
through registered workspace-copy admission and the existing original pending-
input program. That program isolates the source, reshapes the full matrix and
casts signed tokens through the ordinary unsigned conversion; token validity is
still checked by the shared sequence transaction. No host token reconstruction
or text request authority is introduced. Source registration retains the actual
constructor funding in the copy account's execution identity, so native buffers
and later static views retain both numerical and host custody after source pins
retire. Completion and publication precede the prepared input's return; failed or
unsettled work follows the existing copy recovery and quarantine rules.

Each admitted speculative prefill span borrows a static range of that completed
copy. One shared range declaration drives its workspace trace and native slice,
and the trace adds no Initialize or second upload. The speculative span compiler
composes this actual view receipt and its caller controls with the model equation
before opening the span's scope and construction bank. The source-copy account
remains separate from the model role, preserving cumulative domain accounting
without charging the full copy again for every span.

The bound native media plan now shares the accepted source's actual planning
Context with vision continuation and decoder-span state. Original encoder-table
validation, DeepStack vector construction/growth, ordered decoder assembly,
position helpers and span temporary containers use their existing counted
workers with that explicit loan. Vision and forward owners retain it after their
paid containers. The native numerical context stays separate; neither a new
workspace Context nor thread-local accounting authority is introduced.

Independent speculative verification now retains its exact host token input
before invoking the decoder. The shared runtime uses the existing immutable
GenerationTokenIds contract; the native constructor pays its actual vector,
shared shell and error transports from the source pair's cumulative metadata
account. Every cloned token owner closes retirement through the concrete Arc
payload, freeing that shell and token backing before the account can retire.
A funding refusal therefore precedes cache mutation or verification submission.
This does not qualify the remaining scheduler history or sampling producers.

The prepared-media vision continuation lends its existing metadata Context to the
neutral segmented-attention companion. The Workspace and MLX implementations
reuse their respective ordinary segment loops; MLX reserves the actual native
output-handle vector and fixed controls before constructing those destinations.
The borrowed prepared segment lengths and numerical equations are unchanged.
Other backends do not gain a counted-construction claim from the default
companion: checked calls require an explicit implementation. The enclosing media
source retains the same funding through execution, error transport and container
retirement; this metadata loan supplies no tensor or submission authority.


Observed ungrouped block-FP8 uses the same original quantization and projection
kernels as whole projection. The native recipe now follows the actual callback
boundary: prepare retains compact values, block scales and decoded weight scales;
the shared neutral reconstruction records each selected view, scale expansion,
ConvertFP8 and product; finish consumes those original prepared operands. The
compact U8-to-F32 conversion is the ordinary MLX unary worker with a Graph-owned
primitive. No reconstruction, extra source copy or observer selection is inferred
from a model family, and unselected factories create no reconstruction graph.

The prepare receipt pays the enclosing callback and typed failure transports
before native construction. The shared PhysicalLinear producer predicate also
selects that error path before quantization, covering failures before the factory
is offered. Retained callback errors cross the native adapter using a fixed
original propagation carrier, while closed typed Exception/NN source owners keep
the actual accepted domain through shell and cause retirement. Ordinary error
behavior is preserved. Grouped and segmented FP8 still need their separate
receipts; this join qualifies only the actual ungrouped prepared operands.

Cached decode after original prepared media consumes the accepted quote's existing
metadata Context through the one-use text operation and the native erased decode
entry. Its text part, actual tensor descriptor and architecture admission use the
same validators and paid constructors. The decode-only adapter no longer builds
or evaluates a token fingerprint that the caller discarded; committed prompt-cache
identity remains in the session. A borrowed PreparedCompositeInput carries this
metadata loan into the existing direct forward worker, whose state-layout, part,
ordered-assembly, position and DeepStack destinations now consume it. Forward
owners retain the Context last, and returned failures retain its funding through
the existing paid error adapter. Ordinary direct callers share the same equations
without gaining original execution authority.


The original Metal grouped-linear block-FP8 producer consumes contiguous
`[groups, output, input]` banks through the same sorting, projection, bias,
activation and weighted-reduction worker as ordinary execution. Its six finite
prepared kernel families borrow the ordinary tiled/scalar shader bodies: three
actual decoded scale dtypes each retain 32 input-class signatures, within the
existing 64-specialization family limit. Input,
weight and scale shapes supply every shader dimension, including the contiguous
row-block origin; sorted group IDs retain their actual signed representation.
The existing admitted shared-native initializer owns these families and their
source/signature storage before use. Each call uses the accepted Graph/Record
and buffer domains, the supplied stream, fixed argument/output controls and a
closed typed error transport that keeps its paying custody through destruction.
The recipe records the actual quantizer/projector nodes, scale decoding, safe-ID
assertion, possible operand compactions and common grouped equation. It does
not substitute the dense projection receipt. The nonzero component fixture
compares the real grouped operator with ordinary execution using report-derived
capacities and checks escaped-output custody and final retirement.

This producer currently closes nonempty contiguous grouped linear with 128 by
128 FP8 blocks, floating or UE8M0 scales, identity/SiLU and summed reduction.
Packed gated-product banks additionally consume their retained independent
row-block layout. The original shader receives rank-four views of the actual
weight and decoded scale bank, so every component starts at its selected scale
origin without a new specialization or host-scalar upload. Contiguous banks use
the same worker with one partition. Native source checks validate exact shapes,
dtypes, scale encoding and address/grid arithmetic before construction. The
physical and Graph queries include both views and their possible copies.

The existing packed chunk worker now composes two actual FP8 quantizers and
projectors with its shared routing, activation, bias and weighted reduction.
The recipe derives chunk count and tail from that worker's 64-token threshold
and 32-token chunk width; it retains the single outer selected-ID assertion and
the existing output-container/completion custody. Typed failures cross the
shared closed Exception/NN transport after its controls are admitted. The new
nonzero fixture covers independent 137-row components, both scale encodings,
and a 65-token tail case, using only the actual report's capacities and checking
escaped-output custody through final retirement.

Standalone segmented FP8 has no production neutral operation descriptor or
caller; no unused original receipt is manufactured for it. Other reductions and
tensor-parallel grouped original execution retain their separate completion
requirements. These are implementation gaps, not model-family limitations.

Packed gated-product observation uses the same dense or FP8 chunk worker, split
at its actual callback. Units prices routing, first projection and activation;
Finish consumes the effective observed units for the second projection and
weighted reduction. Chunked Units describes separately owned stores without
constructing a native concatenation. Observer-created operations remain explicit
in the shared trace. The complete result and selected capture use the existing
original completion roots and native account custody.

Each quoted Units invocation adds one move-only failure slot to the existing
prepared grouped-output directory. Its expected shape has the batch contract's
two dimensions; its actual-shape capacity is the maximum rank of that accepted
trace, including actual callback operands. The slot is prepared before native
work and extracted only by the same original Scope observer. An in-capacity
shape mismatch moves exact copied dimensions into the ordinary typed
GroupedUnitError, retaining the raw control account after its buffers. A foreign
larger rank refuses before either copy rather than growing an unpriced diagnostic.
Callback failures preserve their original source through the paid shared bridge.
Slot consumption never refunds or reissues capacity. Ordinary callbacks retain
their unrestricted existing diagnostics and execution order.

The shared layered traversal now accepts an explicit metadata destination from
its actual forward owner. Prepared media forwards the existing Context through
its architecture wrapper; ordinary callers report no destination. Output,
completion, dependency and retained-reference buffers reserve against this
Context before filling. The two media families and native mixed state lend their
existing fields through ordered visitors, so completion does not first create
unaccounted nested vectors. Each subsequent push still checks capacity before
mutation; a counting pass is not authority for an unchecked allocation.

Execution-group scheduling uses fixed ready slots in declaration order. The
same worker serves ordinary and counted construction; successful transitions
lend releasable dependencies directly, and failed pending descendants close in
validated topological order. The schedule retains only the paying Funding after
its slot vectors. The traversal's Context survives policy cleanup, while existing
native boundary controls and the closed media/decode error adapter retain any
escaping failure. No new budget, execution grant, or native gate is introduced.

Saved composite continuation keeps its newly funded resume Context through the
existing diagnostic-to-quote handoff. An explicit typed native adapter accepts
that construction destination only after the saved source's executable origin
has been validated. The quote stores it separately from completed prepared-input
source evidence: a resumed token receives no B binding, source credit or previous
request authority. The existing execution loan reaches later composite input and
forward constructors, while non-participating adapters retain ordinary behavior.
The continuation Context retires before the quote's final planning-funding owner.

Checked tensor gather uses the same native take-axis implementation in ordinary
and managed execution. Its backend recipe counts the existing signed-wrap bounds
assertion, safe-index selection, gather cast and axis views, scalar seeds and
reduction temporaries. Intermediate rank includes the indexed singleton before
squeeze. Tensor storage remains owned by the existing physical indexing emitter;
empty indices construct no validation graph. No family-specific branch or new
execution authority is introduced.

### Resumed composite text ingress metadata

A post-commit media resume carries the second, funded continuation Context from
the exact saved quote into its first-token prefill source. That pending Decode
row uses the same selected text admission as cached decode. It preserves the
committed prompt identity already retained by the copied session; it does not
encode media, hash a replacement prefix, or claim completed-input B credit.

`PreparedCompositeTextPrefill::from_prepared_text_with_metadata` consumes the
actual prepared token handles. Its ordinary and counted routes share geometry
validation, span slicing, and architecture admission. The counted route reserves
source/chunk vectors before constructing their contents, borrows the selected
immutable admission-config owner through a neutral hook, and pays the borrowed
input view before the infallible forward loan. Source and chunk keep the actual
Context last; escaping native errors retain an account-only funding alias after
local cleanup. Backends without the counted config/inspection hooks keep their
ordinary constructors and cannot silently enter an allocating checked fallback.

This closes post-commit token continuation construction. An unadvanced media
snapshot still needs its distinct pending prepared-media ownership/copy join;
this route does not reinterpret such a pending encoder input as a Decode row.

The counted neutral multi-axis rotary helper prepares its actual frequency table
through the supplied WorkspaceContext before invoking the existing prepared
Tensor operation. The same neutral frequency equations supply both the traced
and native calls. Concrete backends receive borrowed frequencies and retain their
existing graph/dispatch recipe; they do not create an unaccounted host table.
Ordinary calls continue through the same backend numerical worker with its
ordinary frequency producer.

Caller-supplied rotary embeddings use the existing shared apply-rotary equation.
The backend derives its native recipe from batch/head views, the two half views,
negative-half product, concatenation, cosine/sine products and sum. Its actual
indexing and concatenation controls are priced alongside native descriptors;
source frequency generation remains the neutral producer's responsibility.

Original speculative sequence completion uses the collector's prepared scoped
completion once. That worker submits, waits and validates with the same retained
authority; it must not then call the ordinary wait/validate APIs, which reject
original collectors. Token-validation roots still receive their existing explicit
completed-value check before the invocation is marked complete.


### Original speculative deterministic numerical phases

The portable speculative runtime owns the fixed normalization, probability
selection, and positive-difference/correction equations. The ordinary MLX
sampling adapter and its Workspace adapter execute those same primitive workers.
This does not certify an arbitrary sampler's `process_logits` callback, capture,
intervention, categorical draw, or PRNG derivation.

The independent native producer receives only a closed completed numerical
value. Its initial sources come from the actual once-only completed decoder row
slot, or the final selected prefill output after the shared span driver has
established completion. The ordinary row accessor and numerical accessor consume
the same slot. The prefill adapter preserves target-output and draft-state-only
semantics. No raw Array plus role constructor can manufacture this provenance.
Subsequent values are created only after this numerical worker's exact successful
completion. Values distinguish logits, probabilities and internal correction
differences, and share an already-prepared stream owner without a new C wrapper.

Each actual deterministic program obtains a move-only numerical phase through
the existing original request/PendingAccount/pool admission worker. Sources must
match the request's original header account, pool and schedule; equal schedule
identities alone do not equate two separately prepared requests. The request
retains every accepted phase using an iteratively retired paid fixed link, while
native budgets retain only that phase's account. Completion and rollback do not
refund cumulative admission or rewind attempts. Link, Arc, native domains and
error owners are priced before construction; their closed destruction frees the
owning shell before its paying account.

A selected sampler-input capture can join that same numerical phase.
The source loan authenticates the exact previously published capture C owner
or the closed newly compiled original capture source; an ordinary plan or
matching shape is insufficient. The same host claim-table
producer receives the numerical account, and each tensor, token-score or candidate
claim checks that exact phase account before the shared native worker reads it. The existing
ProcessLogits compiler traces the one-row reshape and selection, reserves its
physical/Graph/Record domains and nested completions, and runs capture before
the existing mask/policy worker. Identity policies still execute an installed
capture. Selected outputs settle under the existing Scope; shared frame delivery
leaves the producer only after the same recovery and Record retirement succeed. On an
execution error, a separate borrowed destination can receive already sealed host
evidence while the original error and Recovery retain every unresolved native
owner. A failed observation remains Aborted; a capture completed before a later
policy error remains Untracked, matching ordinary callback timing. This failure
drain neither certifies native completion nor commits speculative output. A
secondary host-sealing failure preserves the primary execution error and all
spent claims.

The request's numerical retentions own the cumulative capture ledger, matching
ordinary speculative sampler clones which share LogitCapture. Replayed logical
positions consume new numerical ordinals and cannot rewind capture spending.
The frame's Untracked outcome is ordinary logical speculative attribution;
its shared payload retains original H through escaped delivery. Text grants and
text checkpoint destinations cannot consume this numerical custody. Fresh-request
saved-lineage import remains unsupported. Initial C now uses the existing
original source compiler account and a shared core DTO count/copy worker: it
reserves before every fresh String/Vec/shared-owner birth, copies the actual
admission without readmission, and keeps C on every plan alias. Caller buffers
remain ordinary inputs. The context-bearing instrumentation hook installs that
source and a closed shared queue. Each required queue growth allocates a fresh
exact destination under the authenticated source-pair H before numerical work;
drain moves the retained buffer into existing step delivery. Sampler snapshots
share this source/queue, preserving the ordinary cumulative-ledger semantics.
The existing controlled facade entry and its continuous observed wrapper consume
these producers. Full/Slice/Preview, TokenScores and TopCandidates use the
existing F32 ProcessLogits source. TokenScores reuses the shared scalar program's
exact root/control/completion population; candidates reuses the finite-check,
sort and bounded readout program with its three internal frontiers. The completed
numerical source needs no text publication or extra source completion. Every
intermediate remains in the existing phase recovery/final-root owner. The fixed
plain controller lends its authenticated pre-force domain; forcing and sampler
truncation do not alter score normalization or domain membership. Unknown
controller projections, other transforms, internal activation producers and
fresh-request capture-lineage import retain their explicit refusals.

The compiler executes the actual Workspace primitives, then reduces each trace
through the shared native physical, Graph, Record and kernel-population machinery.
It preserves whole-primitive temporary populations and source backing custody.
Correction prices two cuts before native construction: precise F32 softmax on
both sources, positive difference and total mass; then logarithm only if the
completed mass follows the existing epsilon/NaN branch. It does not construct
logarithms speculatively or replace the observed mass with an assumed result.
Each cut uses the existing prepared Scope/recovery engine and supplied GPU stream.
The prepared root-completion entry already submits, waits and validates under
that scope; ordinary collector wait/validate are never fallback operations.
The collector is retired by the recovery payload, then successful advance requires
exact `CompleteSnapshot` Record drainage. Pending, failed, blocked and future
unknown retirement states remain refusals with original custody retained.

This is a consumed native numerical producer, with separate callable original
prefill/row handoffs. The public speculative sampler still uses its ordinary
Logits carrier until the enclosing adapter selects this producer; no aggregate
original-speculation support claim follows from these fixed phases alone.

Independent speculative numerical operations borrow the actual target's retained
PrefillRootsRuntime and workspace mechanism facts from their source-pair header.
Those fields and constructor results are funded before the queries. The accessor
returns a borrow and copied facts; it creates no replacement runtime, stream or
submission authority. Each numerical phase still validates its source account,
stream and completed-value meaning before admission and execution.


The shared media span lifecycle authenticates its exact prepared request and
current state revision in the existing reservation vote. Successful first-span
admission may replace the branch revision before any input operation; the same
closed lifecycle moves the source to that actual admitted revision. It does not
rebind the completed media source, ignore a stale revision, or relax executable,
control, frontier or parameter identity. Later chunks retain the existing
commit-to-source revision transition, and ordinary span adapters use their
unchanged admission worker.

### Pending prepared media in paired snapshots

Before the first media prefill, paired snapshot capture validates the pending
input against its exact bound request and completed prepared-source owner. The
immutable completed B payload and semantic owner may then be shared into an
explicit saved-media variant. This preserves the canonical parts, cache identity,
source identity and historical B custody without repeating upload, constructing
new array handles, or retaining the prior generation quote. Decoder, sampler and
PRNG state still use the existing independently admitted copy driver.

The snapshot's host-preparation query includes the actual saved-variant/control
layouts before these aliases are constructed. Logical SnapshotBudget allowances
still use the existing complete-input descriptor policy; the physical copy plan
contains only values actually copied and grants no fresh B or generation Q.
The packed-token resume constructor deliberately cannot interpret this media
variant: resumed media must consume it through the prepared-source recipe and
fresh request installation, which remains a separate join.

The speculative numerical-phase compiler also consumes a closed immutable
projection of the actual default, standard, or Mirostat logit policy. The
portable projection freezes scalar controls, current adaptive `mu`, supplied
temperature, and the actual history extent; it copies no policy, history, or RNG
storage. Its ordinary and prepared paths call the same penalty/filter/temperature
workers. Arbitrary callbacks and constraint controllers have no implicit
projection. This projection covers processing only: random selection and adaptive
commit remain separate producers.

The native processing adapter accepts only the existing closed completed logit
carrier and the same request/source/stream binding used by numerical phases. It
traces the selected worker with `WorkspaceSamplingBackend`, admits physical,
Graph, Record, pipeline, host-payload, and error-owner requirements through the
existing request account, and constructs under its retained original scope.
Penalty uploads own their payloads before the borrowed history returns. The
actual F32 sampler receipts qualify nonempty processing; other numerical dtypes
remain an implementation gap until their selected receipts are supplied. An
actually empty processing trace returns a retention-only alias without creating
a native phase. There is no raw array escape or text-role substitution.

Mirostat cutoff is a pure graph constructor. Its existing intermediate token
observation is attributed to the exact recognized full adaptive sampling step,
which retains the same one nested-completion allowance. A cutoff-only numerical
phase uses its real final completion and does not manufacture an intermediate
observation. Successful values retain their phase account; failures retain the
typed cause and the same funding through closed owner retirement.

Known default and standard speculative policies expose a separate closed
projection for their actual greedy choice and inherited unchanged commit.
A processing projection alone does not certify either callback. The greedy
program constructs the existing backend argmax at exact zero temperature, from
one actual F32 score row, with no RNG argument. Its Workspace trace and source
handle clone enter the same numerical-phase physical/Graph/Record/host admission;
only the exact completed U32 token is read before successful retirement. The
request retains the accepted phase charge after scalar return.

The unchanged-commit adapter authenticates the same completed logit carrier,
request, stream, source shape and token domain, then consumes the known no-op
projection without invoking a callback or constructing native state. Mirostat's
mutating commit, arbitrary overrides, and stochastic choice retain separate
producer requirements. No absence or presence of a random-state handle implies
that a stochastic producer has been admitted.


### Saved completed-media equation and copy composition

The native saved-source quote now selects the explicit captured media variant.
It projects the immutable completed B through the same input projector and runs
the same media equation traversal with the actual saved sampler/history/key.
The future decoder is the projected independently copied saved state, never the
current live frontier. Exact captured execution/revision/frontier and control
origin plus the current parameter epoch authenticate the source pair. No media
encoding, upload, prompt selection or sampler reset is repeated.

The copy population names only real decoder/key operations when completed B
replaces a token tail. Its zero-input case has no invented token, cast, reshape
or completion. Completed B enters its own registered equation-root association;
the shared residual composer combines that association with the separately
sealed isolated-copy proof. Both account pins survive the resulting admission.
Full diagnostics remain source-inclusive, and neither a byte discount nor the
new copied decoder can substitute for the existing B witness.

The returned media generation report is moved, not deeply cloned, and the fresh
quote retains its actual source projection and constructor Context. Ordinary
text resumes continue through the same copy/report worker. The public original
resume preparation query still requires the token constructor until the pending
media prompt-completion and authenticated copied-state installation join lands;
this intermediate unit does not claim pending-media restore/fork is enabled.


The independent-draft adapter now carries logits as an opaque ordinary/original
sum through the existing generic speculative driver. An original prefill uses
the same bounded worker and returns its completed numerical owner; decode moves
one settled row through its existing one-use slot. Before that move, the adapter
checks the exact request account and stream and admits the actual enclosing
result representation. No raw original Array leaves that ownership boundary.

The shared MLX sampling adapter accepts the actual associated logits type.
Original policy preparation, normalization, probability lookup, correction and
greedy choice use the admitted numerical workers; qualified unchanged commit
uses the same source validation. Outer consumers check placement and account
identity before work and fund only their added controls and distribution wrapper.
The inner numerical owner retains its existing authority. Ordinary distributions
under an original context are rejected before fallback. Native errors remain
inside backend contracts and retained original failures keep their neutral source.
This joins the numerical consumer; arbitrary callbacks, capture queues and the
complete public managed speculative request constructor still require their
actual producers and retain explicit refusals.

Original speculative sampler construction now consumes a closed, source-bound
host-copy witness from the known Default/Generation/Configured Standard policy.
Runtime reuses the actual full history-box copy worker; no existing unpriced
payload is adopted. MLX pays the concrete enclosing controls before construction
and keeps the copied policy immutable in a closed shared owner. Ordinary sampler
callbacks and Clone behavior stay unchanged. Original aliases allocate no new
history or callback-memory owner; snapshot copies without RNG use fresh supplied
host custody and preserve policy/history independently. The outer owner and any
escaped capture-refusal alias retire their shells and payloads before custody.
Numerical processing/unchanged commit borrow the same closed policy projection.
This does not qualify ConstrainedSampler: its facade controller's committed-token
history, tokenizer domain and prospective forcing/filter work remain the next
source/copy join. Adaptive mutable commit, RNG snapshot copies and capture remain
explicitly unqualified by this host-copy witness.


Original saved-controller admission now accepts the same complete empty shared
inventory as initial original-input admission. This supports already copied,
run-owned controllers such as an all-token filter without fabricating a tokenizer
domain. An actual original tokenizer still requires its exact domain witness;
unknown or nonempty ordinary shared inventories still reject. The existing
source-preparation worker validates the empty inventory and real request funding
without adoption, registration or source credit. Snapshot host copying remains
responsible for constructing and retaining the controller itself.

Original speculative PRNG construction uses the same numerical-phase account
and Scope engine. The explicit configured `u64` seed is a zero-input typed
program; it creates the ordinary two-word native key only after complete native
and host admission. Its immutable stream copy is captured from the actual
original environment and realized under that phase's account-only custody.
A closed key owner retains the completed array, prepared stream, phase account,
and planning funding, without a public raw-array/key conversion.

Key advance consumes the existing native split-two worker; the retained current
key and returned next key both enter exact completion. Draft-position derivation
uses the existing split(`position + 1`)-then-static-select equation. The shared
SplitRandomKey metadata and native receipts therefore use the actual positive
`[count, 2]` U32 output shape and its entire allocated backing, including when
only one row escapes. No independent per-position RNG algorithm is substituted.

Known categorical policies have their own closed projection, separate from
processing and commit. The phase takes the actual completed F32 score row and
completed request-owned key, constructs the same native state split and
categorical worker, and completes the token plus advanced key before scalar
observation and state replacement. A failed attempt preserves the caller's
previous key; its accepted phase remains cumulatively charged and recovered by
the existing owner. Immutable key clones support isolated replacement without
new native allocation. Raw caller seed arrays still require their own admitted
copy handoff, and mutating adaptive commits remain separate producers. These
producer APIs do not by themselves certify the outer public sampling flow.


### Completed media follows the actual copied-state exchange

Prepared original state exchange now returns an optional opaque media binding
receipt from the same shared validation, distributed vote and infallible swap.
The source control/execution owner and the actual copied-slot frontier are checked
before mutation. The receipt contains the source binding and the fresh installed
revision; raw position or same-origin matching cannot create it. Ordinary state
exchange keeps its existing behavior.

The original route prepares the installed revision under its existing metadata
Funding before the exchange. A closed revision Arc retains that exact account
through the last alias and destroys its shell before releasing funding. A failed
validation or vote preserves the old installed state and drops the provisional
revision through the same error path. There is no second installation driver.

The existing installed-opening boundary authenticates the receipt against the
actual target and seals rebound semantics into the accepted media source owner.
The borrowed input then lends those semantics to the same prefill constructor.
Immutable B, canonical parts, cache identity and prepared media stay shared; no
encoding/upload or historical source mutation occurs. A later unadvanced snapshot
retains the effective rebound semantics with B, so repeated restore/fork does not
fall back to its first historical revision. Escaped semantic/revision aliases keep
the constructor charge independently of the quote's lifetime.

Pending-media prompt-copy/completion and the public pregrant query remain the
next consuming join; this transition alone does not activate public resume.

Copied media restoration checks the copied control slot's captured execution and
revision before returning a source-to-installed binding receipt. This private
provenance travels with the existing completed-copy origin/binding worker and is
cleared when a slot is exchanged. Executable/parameter `same_origin` comparisons
retain their ordinary meaning and survive state advancement. Fixed origin loans
only clone an established revision; they never allocate a missing identity.

Pending original-media restore/fork consumes the shared saved prompt claim and
copied decoder/key program while retaining the exact completed B parts and cache
owner. It constructs a fresh request/chunk input through the same canonical B
wrapper as initial binding, without token substitution, encoder replay, upload,
or prior generation authority. Exact source semantic revision/frontier checks
precede H0 admission. H0 prices the actual prompt/control wrappers; logical copy
estimation shares the existing descriptor-based SnapshotBudget equations.

The prompt worker uses the same dense table fill/publication and final state
binding for tokens and media. A media source with no decoder/key arrays performs
only host construction, inventory publication and the original prompt completion;
it opens no submission lease, Scope, Graph or Record. Nonempty decoder/key copies
use the unchanged native recovery/completion worker. Returned input aliases keep B,
while the independently admitted request and state controls keep their fresh Q/H.

Original media and saved-sampling quotation use the same resident numerical trace
as initial original token quotation. The retained selected `LayerwiseWorkspace`
separately supplies materialization, source copies, and future unloaded-unit
construction. Its authoritative requested-unit rows are visited by logical ordinal,
including repeated uses of shared owners and every alias-named binding. The
existing source constructor rejects incomplete exclusions and replacement sets;
