shell before the allowance. This bounds downstream auto-trait expansion without
erasing source identity, adding custody constructors, or changing compiler debit
and settlement. Account queries include the actual fat-pointer control frames.

Original speculative ProcessLogits Histogram capture consumes the same fixed-edge
selection and bin builder. The actual numerical occurrence authenticates the
claim before its edges/count storage is born and again before delivery; failures
retain partial bins under their paying custody. The borrowed immutable capture
source supplies edges, and its exact Workspace trace prices selection, flatten,
comparison/mask/sum and scalar reads. Only the already-completed input's source
settlement is omitted. All produced arrays remain in the same numerical
Graph/Record scope and Recovery owner, without a second source publication or
capture account. Ordinary and controlled speculative sessions use the same
observation driver and cumulative ledger.

The original numerical capture transaction now has an activation hook using the
same declaration-order selector and logical intervention ledger as ordinary
capture. Source-bound claims admit each operation once, retain charged failures
in the paid outcome destination, and pass the effective logits to the existing
mask/policy worker. Its cold path resolves actual axes and slices into paid rank
destinations through shared validators. MLX consumes the shared static activation
program and retains every emitted root, including unused selection intermediates,
until the numerical phase settles its complete root union. Applied records are
provisional construction evidence until that enclosing completion; failed phases
retain native recovery and may drain only sealed host evidence. The public install
gate still requires the loaded-declaration and session-authenticated source handoff.

Original static intervention evidence uses immutable Preview/Summary companion
declarations copied once inside the same paid SharedInterventionPlan. Core owns
the borrowed layout and copy census; runtime owns operation/side/phase claims,
child record destinations and the existing logical capture ledger; the backend
consumes the existing selected-output and scalar reduction workers. The
companion's zero logical limits describe geometry and grant no independent
quota. Before/after metadata and values are reserved from the enclosing ledger.

The original numerical worker retains every action and evidence root in its
existing final completion/Recovery union. After-edit tensors may still be lazy:
Preview completes its selected output, and Summary completes its selected flat
value before scalar reads, evaluating that edit's dependencies. The source
settlement omitted by these phase-local workers is not a proof that an edit was
already evaluated. Host evidence is provisional until the enclosing transaction
completes; failure preserves attributed aborted evidence and consumed quota.
No per-step selection/path/point declarations or replacement account are made.


### Original speculative static edit installation

The loaded MLX session lends its existing `PreparedModelDiscovery` owner and
constructs a fresh, source-funded session-identity copy before taking the model
operation guard. The resulting private declaration owner retains the actual
replicated model origin and the same request metadata funding. The source pair
accepts it only for its exact target origin. Both role wrappers use that target
session discovery, as ordinary speculative intervention admission does; every
numerical invocation still checks its own actual role, source shape and dtype.

Runtime projects primitive support once through a shared worker with owned and
borrowed destinations. Architecture-owned validation resolves only an already
cached artifact identity and compares the actual selected declaration projection.
Core canonical digest validation takes fixed byte destinations, so it allocates
neither a discovery clone nor a formatted artifact identity. No caller discovery
DTO, host token or matching semantic digest creates a loaded-source witness.

The existing controlled intervention method now supplies an explicit context to
borrowed source validation and installation. Native installation prepares exact
rank scratch through the request's H, runs the shared schedule/geometry/estimator
and per-step/cumulative budget arithmetic, and invokes the existing immutable C
source compiler for each role. Four rank destinations are reused without growth;
no caller Vec or action payload is adopted. Both candidate slots must succeed
before the sampler replaces its fixed role array. Its closed holder retains the
actual installation H until both C aliases retire. Refusal preserves the previous
installed sources, and empty replacement clears them through the same boundary.

The original sampler sends those source loans into the existing ProcessLogits
capture/invocation worker. Static activation roots are settled by the already
admitted numerical completion and its recovery owner. The policy receives the
effective logits only through that completion path. Snapshots alias immutable C
sources while independently copying mutable policy/RNG state; the existing shared
capture lineage preserves spent observation/transport budgets. An explicit empty
capture plan still constructs its C/ledger owner because attributed intervention
outcomes require that budget even without selected tensor payloads.

This installation initially accepts the existing static model.logits actions with
`InterventionEvidence::None`. Preview/Summary companion installation is a separate
producer being joined through the same source copy and claim workers, not an
architectural restriction. Routed edits and unselected declarations retain typed
refusal. Ordinary discovery, control replacement and sampling behavior remain in
the same drivers.


### Original hyper-connection worker qualification

The reusable MLX hyper-connection worker now supplies original receipts for
`HyperCollapse`, `HyperExpand`, `HyperHeadCoefficients`, and `HyperHeadSum`.
The existing neutral declarations validate stream/hidden geometry and exact
parameter shapes. No model-family selection enters this native mechanism.
Ordinary and original execution use the same RMS, projection, sigmoid and
Sinkhorn operations. The two fixed contractions use batched matmul with the
same stream-axis order as their former einsum expressions; fixed slice/reshape
operations replace parser and indexing-plan construction. Standalone ordinary
Sinkhorn splitting retains its arbitrary leading-rank behavior. The original
profile is the actual rank-four residual cycle with F32/F16/BF16 sources.

A tensor-free counter executes that same worker to obtain descriptor edges,
scalar seeds, returned handles, reshape copies and native temporary births.
It counts one shape-preserving normalization step and scales its checked
population for the selected Sinkhorn iteration count, so cold inspection does
not loop over arbitrarily large iteration declarations. Existing conservative
physical storage envelopes remain in force, including output/retained
coefficients, casts, matmul compactions/partials and reduction temporaries.
Logical floating storage remains a four-byte envelope; output representation
comes from the actual cast/source relationship.

The head retains its actual widened input across the borrowed coefficient
callback and consumes that tensor in the final sum. Original validation and
callback failures retain the paying domain through typed error sources, with
the concrete wrapper/control layouts included before execution. Empty RMS and
normalization aliases use the existing prepared clone worker; empty head
output uses the same ordinary zero constructor. Completion and failed-prefix
retirement stay in the existing scope/recovery machinery.

The focused native component case
`original_hyper_cycle_preserves_sinkhorn_contractions_and_borrowed_head`
compares the full nonzero collapse/squared-sublayer/expand/head sequence with
the former einsum worker and an independent host calculation. It covers F32,
strided BF16, F16, one stream, multiple Sinkhorn counts and the borrowed head
callback, using the actual prepared GPU domain and original escaped-output
retirement harness. The existing cold geometry test also checks large-count
completion and overflow, and empty-span alias populations. Native execution
validation of this new packet is pending the integrating run; no broader
model-family completion is claimed by these primitive receipts.

Original static intervention installation now builds each candidate immutable C
source before its evidence preflight, then borrows the source-owned companion
inventory through the existing scratch/schedule/budget worker. The real capture
plan supplies all per-step and cumulative limits. Metadata and selected Preview/
Summary estimates include both sides and each actual scheduled occurrence. Both
candidates must pass before the existing fixed role holder is replaced; failures
retire candidates under their original H and preserve installed sources.


The embedded prediction startup destination now consumes the exact loaded
`MaterializedPredictionExecutor` through `PredictionStateStartupFactory`.
Architecture code supplies its existing sequential slot count, pooling prototype
slice, or model-state prototype; MLX does not select a family or reconstruct a
state layout. `MlxModelSession::prepare_original_prediction_lane` authenticates
an idle actual executable and its `OriginalSpeculativeSemanticPreparation`, then
retains that same cumulative metadata funding. Fresh Vec storage, erased state
Box, host authority, and failure transports are paid before construction.
Sequential slots use the existing inline empty constructor. Pooling sources are
proved operand-free before the existing leaf-copy worker runs; its policy,
frontier and scalar fields are preserved. Populated model prototypes use the
existing independently admitted resident-copy program, including completion,
publication and discarded-prefix retirement. The destination keeps state/Box
before source provenance and H, with no infallible Clone or raw owning exit.
Physical extension depth and selected proposal capacity remain distinct.

This producer does not issue model invocation authority or enable the public
Embedded path. Its next consumer is the shared embedded cache/occurrence driver:
it must bind this exact prepared state and target source, qualify its target
capture and prediction phases, and use paid checkpoint/rollback and observer
containers. Populated or paged per-layer pooling prototypes still require an
admitted cache-copy adapter; they refuse without resetting or ordinary copying.
The existing independent External schedule is not an Embedded substitute.


The original chat context is a borrowed text-layer projection of the real
message input, tokenizer-default map and caller-override map. Facade code keeps
tool/reasoning policy, selects the ordinary base → defaults → caller precedence,
and supplies that projection to the same neutral source/render admission worker.
Loop locals shadow external values. Both layout measurement and admitted
execution borrow the same immutable maps, including reserved-key replacements.
The backend only supplies its existing pool and validates the original J/C
sources; it does not merge maps, select templates, or reconstruct policy.

The shared MiniJinja worker now formats the selected scalar population through
its existing allocation-free formatter, preserving integer, finite floating,
negative-zero, boolean and null spelling. External text operands retain only
map-entry indices and byte ranges in paid stack/concatenation destinations; no
caller reference enters a returned render or partial error. Their six original
render buffers, widened operand/instruction layouts and actual formatter/context
controls are queried before H construction, and H/J/C retirement is unchanged.
Structured formatting/access, arbitrary loops and remaining compiler operations
are still explicit profile gaps. This borrowed scalar-context connection is not
an assertion of complete arbitrary-template support.


### Original selected implicit convolution

The shared native convolution mechanism supplies an original construction and
worker receipt for nontransposed 1D/2D convolutions whose actual Metal dispatch
selects the aligned implicit GEMM or separable kernels. This closes the same
channel-mixing conv1d and stride-two conv2d mechanisms used by portable codec and
audio-subsampler equations without introducing a family selector in the backend.
The compiled cold query consumes exact input/weight shapes, stride, padding,
dilation and groups. Dispatch and inspection use the same alignment/Winograd
predicates. Query refusal remains in force for Winograd, explicit unfolding,
unaligned implicit-general, transposed and 3D construction until those complete
receipts are supplied; their existing ordinary physical facts remain intact.

The conv2d entry uses the existing fixed-axis constructor, eliminating temporary
host vector construction. Its two possible dtype casts and one convolution
supply three descriptor nodes/four edges. Native input and weight compaction
contribute at most two additional physical births, alongside the cast candidates
and output. The existing four-byte floating storage envelope covers F32/F16/BF16;
no unfolded matrix or guessed algorithm workspace is added. The common native
contiguous helper also canonicalizes singleton-axis strides before forming the
implicit worker's signed input jumps. This uses the same existing copy path and
its already-counted destination, preserving the ordinary convolution equations.

Inspection checks the actual signed constructor, output-tile, reduction and input
jump arithmetic before admitting the source. Exact native parameter structs,
axis/array transports, selectors, seven-constant depthwise alternatives and
retained typed failure wrappers feed the existing control query. The original
source guard runs before any native cast or convolution descriptor is created.
The selected GPU scope, graph/record banks, physical allocation owner, completion
and failed-prefix retirement remain the existing shared producers. The ordered
native patch extends the current compiled-source receipt; no JIT fallback is
qualified.

The new focused original-domain component case
`original_implicit_convolution_preserves_stride_groups_and_compaction` uses six
nonzero 1D/2D cases, uneven strides, dilation, grouped/separable channels,
F16/BF16, strided inputs/weights and a row-contiguous singleton-axis view. It
compares ordinary and admitted execution with an independent host contraction,
then exercises escaped-output retirement through the existing component harness.
Native compilation and this new case remain pending the integrating run.

Prediction-prefill alignment is a neutral core coordinate contract declared by the actual architecture extension, independently of sequential/fused scheduling. The existing captured-prefill driver and occurrence planning share checked hidden/token pairing and prediction frontier arithmetic. Runtime's prefill control plan exposes the same physical chunk geometry used for its scope roles; no second chunk scheduler or backend family branch is introduced. These declarations do not establish source identity or grant execution/memory authority.

The shared speculative executor copies optimistic draft state through an explicit
fallible `copy_draft_state` operation. The coordinator agrees copy failure before
any rank enters independent proposal work. Embedded state erasure forwards that
operation instead of requiring infallible `Clone`; prediction transactions use
the same fallible copy worker for checkpoint and advanceable replicas. Ordinary
implementations retain their existing clone behavior. This seam does not certify
original Embedded cache construction, tensor copies, or erasure allocations;
those producers remain required before public Embedded activation.

Embedded speculative occurrence plans consume the selected architecture's physical prediction membership, core hidden/token alignment, runtime shared prefill chunks, and core canonical/optimistic proposal counts. They keep target prefill, prediction seed, sequential/fused proposals, verification and both replay calls distinct. Attempt counters share the same monotonic spending worker as independent drafting and stay outside rollback state. Restored futures add new finite slots; no model snapshot returns spent capacity. These cold descriptors and claims are not native work authority: the exact source, state-copy, host-storage and completion producers must still be bound before enabling managed embedded execution.


### Original independent prediction-cache copies

Native sequential compressed and pooled-attention cache copies now use the
existing typed leaf copy workers with a supplied fallible copy callback. The
ordinary and original paths preserve the same slot order, optional presence,
frontier, capacity and pooling metadata. Compressed caches copy their logical
latent/rotary views once and retain the returned arrays as both stores and views;
local key/value and five-slot pooling streams preserve their existing stored
operand behavior. The original path supplies paid `PreparedArrayClone` inspection
slots for the compressed aliases after numerical copy completion.

Each populated leaf goes through the existing registered-source isolated copy
admission, original execution, recovery, completion and publication worker. The
actual complete backing must already have a legal registered source. This join
adds no raw-array adoption, ordinary allocation owner or synthetic source credit.
A new paid account-only holder retains every returned copy custody and the actual
metadata funding after the destination cache. Empty caches use the same
representation worker without inventing numerical operations. Errors retain the
paying host account, and earlier completed destinations retire before their
custody if a later leaf fails.

The loaded embedded prediction startup uses this producer for resident pooling
prototypes, including populated ones. Its source/header, idle-session and stream
authentication remain in the existing composition entry. Per-cache host custody
is aggregated behind the prepared lane; provisional cache rows retire before
those tokens on failure. Native representations stay below architecture-owned
prediction-state dispatch, and the same typed producer is available to that
dispatch's independently prepared cache-copy provider. Paged local caches still
require the distinct existing manager-copy mechanism; no ordinary clone fallback
is introduced. Snapshot/copy limits and cumulative accounting remain the shared
controller's responsibility, not permission granted by this representation copy.


Borrowed structured chat context now uses the same GetAttr/GetItem dispatcher
for JSON map members and signed array/message indices, including arbitrarily
deep member chains within the existing expression-stack profile. The ordinary
index normalization worker is shared. Equality, boolean negation, numeric
negation and the defined/undefined/none tests also enter the common dispatcher;
ordinary custom test lookup, cache, call, error and truth conversion remain in
the ordinary storage adapter.

The original engine keeps input references only in three operand-side registers
and one transient result register, corresponding to its actual three-operand
workspace. Push normalizes handles to their operand positions; pop preserves them
only until that instruction consumes the values. No reference is stored in paid
operand, loop or concatenation arrays. The accepted source profile has no JSON
local assignments or duplicate-value opcode. Any borrowed text atom retained by
concatenation is copied into a seventh source-measured byte destination under the
same H allowance before its fragment is persisted. Two measured/admitted runs
share those exact transitions, copied-byte counts and peak destination capacity.
Errors retain actual allocation prefixes and original source custody without
caller-reference escape or post-hoc adoption. Structured formatting/deep equality,
JSON-container iteration, string indexing and unimplemented filters/calls remain
explicit profile gaps; facade tool/reasoning semantic gates remain independent.

The embedded invocation workspace descriptor keeps the canonical target coordinate separate from the prediction-local frontier read from actual state. Target readout demand comes from the shared invocation; prediction demand comes from the selected architecture equation and observation path. Seed spans compare against the shared exact seed frontier. Accounting compares the complete descriptor with the completed workspace report, while the native consuming binder still authenticates source identity, state revision, and selected producer. Coordinate equality is not source authority.

Prediction module completion takes ownership of the architecture invocation's existing root destination. The native materializer no longer clones every root into a second vector before handing it to the same transfer/completion owner. The equation outcome remains provisional through that owner's unchanged completion/failure/teardown protocol. Original-domain destination preparation remains a separate obligation; moving an ordinary root vector does not qualify its allocation.

Original embedded prediction startup now retains the actual prepared stream,
copy environment, exact executable origin and authenticated host preparation.
Its fallible saved-lane copy dispatches architecture-owned current state
membership to the existing registered compressed/pooling/resident copy workers;
it never recreates a prototype. Per-member copy custody outlives destination
arrays, and native resident variants move into their exact typed state without
an extra erasure allocation. The closed lane also retains architecture-declared
physical occurrence shape and prefill alignment separately from requested width.

These copies run at settled boundaries outside an active numerical scope. Target
copies can consume the existing completion-bound resident source witness. New
prediction role births still require their actual source publication before a
subsequent registered copy; identity alone supplies no source discount. Public
original Embedded execution still requires the shared cache/erasure constructor
and occurrence/native invocation joins; this copy producer does not open that
gate or change the independent External strategy.


Original Embedded speculative requests now use the existing request/account
acceptance, native budget custody and cumulative retained-slot worker. A private
tag distinguishes Embedded schedule identities from independent AR schedules;
no External realization or second pool is synthesized. Each retained role keeps
its full equation plan before its original account. The additive Embedded role
entry compares the exact consumed invocation and the complete workspace geometry
from the architecture's observed local frontier/output descriptor. That
comparison is accounting, not native source/state/epoch permission: the consuming
backend must still authenticate those actual owners before construction.

Target and prediction startup accounts share the existing once-only constructor
worker and retain exact schedule, issuance-ticket and pool identity. Embedded
prefill is already split into exact occurrence spans, so each accepted occurrence
uses the same one-use native-bank issuer; AR keeps its existing per-prefill-row
claims. Numerical values and completed-source copies retain the same original
budget classes through the private tagged request identity. Continuation reserves
actual replacement storage through existing metadata funding, then moves every
old plan/account and spent ordinal without refund; cursor limits install only
after success. This closes the portable account producer, while native Embedded
invocation/completion integration remains independently required.

Prediction state copying and workspace source projection use one architecture-owned
`PredictionStateSourceFactory` dispatch over actual current sequential, pooling or
model state. The compatibility copy entry point delegates to that same visitor; a
backend cannot infer lane membership from scheduling depth. Embedded target workspace
descriptors preserve the admitted invocation coordinates while permitting observation
readout to widen (never weaken) the required vocabulary demand. These descriptors
remain geometry, not source identity, completion evidence or submission authority.

The embedded target equation quote consumes the retained target projection and
validates its original selected prediction/source pairing through the same
prepared construction driver. Its private target-only purpose neither constructs
a prediction extension nor changes the selection or placement. The shared
layered capture-retention hook exposes the architecture's actual target hidden
value independently of vocabulary readout; quote observers receive both roots
and their complete backing union. A source-explicit invocation observer supplies
its real logical prediction coordinate even though the equation itself requests
no future generation. These are metadata mechanisms, not native admission or
completion authority; source binding, auxiliary state and prediction execution
remain separate obligations.


Prepared embedded cache copying uses a neutral closed provider in
`eredu-architectures::speculative_execution`. The provider retains only immutable
copy prerequisites and paying-source identity; each target or prediction state
retains its own completion/source evidence. The native producer must validate that
evidence against the actual supplied state and run the existing independently
admitted copy/completion/publication worker. Neither a provider identity nor an
evidence carrier certifies a later mutation. Completed isolated-copy payloads may
instead retain their actual registered-copy custody.

Provider and evidence erasure pay their exact host shells before construction.
Closed typed retirement frees each shell before its final host/source authority;
no raw `Rc` or weak handle escapes. Cache checkpoint, prediction fork, success
commit and restore copy actual current payloads fallibly, and construct all
replacement metadata before replacing live state. Error rollback consumes its
already completed checkpoint. The existing ordinary callbacks remain the ordinary
path. Shared capture validation accepts either the existing owned lane identity
or a sealed borrowed view, so prepared callers do not clone selected/input strings.
This mechanism is a preparation/copy boundary, not an inference-role grant; native
Embedded invocation and per-state completion installation remain separate consumers.


Prepared prediction extensions expose a borrowed `PredictionStateSourceLayout`
from their selected architecture construction. Sequential and pooling profiles
retain exact ordered state-layer ordinals and complete rank-local cache policies;
model profiles borrow their existing full `StateLayout`. Compressed prediction
policies come from the authoritative local geometry before it moves into the
executable, so an empty native cache never supplies guessed latent/rotary widths.
The descriptor grants geometry only: native current-state projection must still
validate every actual member and retain its original source evidence. It grants
neither native execution nor copy/completion authority.

Native prediction workspace projection consumes the actual typed current lane and
the selected architecture's explicit per-member policies or model layout. Sequential
compressed, pooling and model-state profiles reuse the same native state projection
workers as ordinary execution, with one shared allocation-identity collector per
lane and fallible retained-source handoff. Empty compressed geometry comes from
prepared architecture policy, never guessed arrays or scheduling class. This
metadata projection supplies no independent source/revision or execution authority.


The closed chat VM now accepts the ordinary built-in representation tests
(string, sequence, mapping, boolean, number, integer, float, iterable, true and
false) through a shared lazy predicate worker. Dynamic values retain their
existing kind/integer/boolean queries; iterable retains the actual ordinary
iterator call, including custom-object refusal. The closed adapter supplies
facts from the actual borrowed JSON, scalar, message and loop representations,
without creating dynamic values or iterators. Scalar float/integer and false
boolean versus numeric-zero distinctions are preserved, including ordinary
empty iteration for undefined and none. Built-in names require that mechanism
feature; no arbitrary registered callback is accepted by the closed source.

Short-circuit `or` now uses the same instruction dispatcher and jump-patching
worker as ordinary execution. It retains a truthy left operand and does not
execute the right operand; ordinary strict-undefined errors, custom tests and
opcode source locations are unchanged. The existing three operand registers
remain the full temporary-reference domain. A branch-selected borrowed string
is copied into the existing ContextText destination only if concatenation
persists it. Source and render controls include the actual new opcode, action,
predicate-fact and result frames before construction; both measured/admitted
variants consume the same source and context. This expands expression support,
not JSON-container loops, arbitrary filters/calls, structured formatting or
facade-owned tool/reasoning controller support.

Completed target and prediction state roots use the same native source capture and
binding worker. Capture follows terminal successful completion and recovery; each
branch retains the actual native budget and neutral model-role custody for its
current backing. Individual prediction cache copies now consume that same completed
source binder. Roots absent from completion evidence still require existing exact
registry pins; neither projection identity nor a polling error creates completion.


Original speculative numerical sources are independent of a model occurrence
strategy. The closed native `OriginalSpeculativeNumericalSources` consumes the
existing request (including its private AR/Embedded schedule tag), verifies its
retained execution against the actual target, and retains that target's existing
roots runtime, native mechanisms, exact origin, optional loaded intervention
declaration and cumulative host funding. It creates no alternate request account,
model scope or inference permission. The neutral request comparison checks exact
execution identity, never geometry/capacity equality.

The AR source pair owns this common value while keeping its AR schedule, draft
epoch and active model occurrence slots separate. `original_execution()` remains
the typed AR model consumer. Shared sampling, numerical programs, capture,
controller/RNG snapshots and paid host destinations consume `original_numerical()`.
Its checked borrowed binding validates the exact pool and stream pair and rejects
an existing binding or ordinary native-memory owner. A future Embedded model
binding supplies its own actual role/completion producer alongside the same
numerical context; it does not enter the External schedule. Existing numerical
phase reservation, provenance, completion, recovery and escaped-value ownership
are unchanged.

Speculative model invocations share one native domain-construction worker for graph
and record quotas, physical buffers, pipeline cache, failure record and retained
completion roots. Independent execution consumes it directly; it is also available to the pending
embedded integration after that path establishes its exact source/role admission. The helper owns no
family dispatch, schedule conversion, source authentication or completion policy.


Prediction workspace materialization consumes the same architecture-prepared
extension and physical-module order as native materialization. Its generic
`WorkspacePredictionParameterSource` lends actual source/executable modules,
selected tasks and local layout to a native parameter projector; it does not
reconstruct a model-family dispatch or certify generated placeholders as source
storage. Source-format modules and full backing aliases remain retained through
trace consumption. Current sequential, pooling and model state must match the
selected policy and actual metadata trace, including empty cache members.

The shared materialization worker admits final module/state container destinations
before filling them. The metadata adapter uses counted current-state copies and
root containers; it preserves cumulative metadata spending across failure and
retirement. Its escaped failures retain the same host account after the cause.
Ordinary native materializers keep their existing invocation dependency collector
and completion/poison semantics. These mechanisms supply metadata equations only;
they neither grant native occurrence authority nor settle actual native work.
The retained prepared extension's source construction, native parameter projector,
and final original quote/installation remain distinct, required producers.

The native Embedded equation wrapper retains its full checked target/prediction
workspace descriptor and one actual trace. It uses the same completion, Graph
and Record reducer as independent speculation, without constructing an independent
draft invocation. The wrapper is descriptive: the consuming native adapter still
authenticates current state, parameter sources and request identity, and reserves
the complete role before construction. Input creation, copying and sampling remain
separate actual producers rather than implicit allowances in the equation report.


Original Embedded cache construction now has a context-bearing neutral factory
and a checked native one-use startup slot. The slot authenticates the existing
numerical request, target origin and host preparation before the shared session
preparation boundary. Runtime keeps the same commit resolution, exact selected
layout comparison and rank agreement; its prepared path carries the existing
fixed inspection-boundary error directly, while ordinary construction keeps its
legacy error mapping. Copying occurs in that mutation-capable preparation callback,
never inside read-only source inspection.

The native provider copies the actual canonical target through the existing
completed/registered source worker and moves the paid prediction-lane Box into
its exact architecture-selected state type. It verifies physical depth, occurrence
shape and alignment separately from requested proposal capacity. Every later
copy authenticates each state's optional CompletedResidentSource; a foreign
witness fails before copying, while completed independent copies retain their
registered source custody and clear the prior model-role witness. The immutable
provider holds only copy prerequisites and source identity, not a mutable current
state or completion witness. The initial target witness is consumed only by the
startup copy, and failed startup does not reopen that one-use slot.

The typed factory and final DynEmbeddedCache retain actual host custody through
payload and Box destruction. Concrete shared controls and provider/error shells
are paid before construction; generic session failures use the existing retained
planning-error worker, which pays its own exact shell. Context-bearing construction
returns BackendFailure directly, preserving unresolved native error ownership.
The no-context ordinary constructor remains available. This is not an original
Embedded invocation grant: the subsequent native executor still uses its
Exception error domain and session_failure conversion, and its remaining
invocation/output destinations require the original role/completion consumer.
Those joins must preserve retained typed failures rather than use ordinary
Exception formatting. Independent External execution and its scheduling remain
unchanged.

Embedded model invocations use the existing token-validation ingress and grouped
output storage worker. Its additive entry validates the exact Embedded role,
invocation and completed equation plan before allocating the declared validation
slots; the retained validation batch keeps that same role through native completion.

Embedded prediction equations use one architecture-owned `PredictionEquation` driver for prefill, sequential proposal, fused proposal and committed replay. Cold projections and native invocations lend the same operands; scalar token construction is inside the invocation. The full mechanism context reaches the shared prediction phase, while the tensor context is borrowed only for existing equation/completion workers. Unobserved fused execution still borrows the immutable lane, and observed fused execution retains its existing fallible prepared-copy owner through completion. The descriptor grants no request, source or completion authority.


Original native operation banks accept either an exact AR role or an exact
Embedded role through a private tagged carrier. Registry equality, completed
submission errors and bank retirement retain that same tag/account; an AR role
never compares equal to an Embedded role and no schedule conversion occurs.
Their source constructor bank, neural-bank claim and account-only slot custody
still come from the existing shared admission worker. The actual tag and its
retained failure envelope are included in the existing constructor controls.

SelectedOriginalOperationPlan binds an EmbeddedEquationRecipe through the same
ResidentNativeRecipe source/neural boundary worker. Its Embedded entry compares
the exact plan, invocation coordinate and workspace geometry before spending the
one-use bank claim. An Embedded prefill claim already denotes one physical span;
there is no AR span object or inferred multiplication by requested proposal width.
Resident and bounded paths use the same prepared neural/storage/registry workers,
selected unit layout, exact source windows and current Scope authentication.
Source/stream checks, failure-prefix custody and completion retirement are unchanged.

Typed session mechanism entry points expose this binding and bank preparation
without opening an executor or interpreting a model family. The enclosing
Embedded source/role compiler must still supply the actual equation/source and
native completion consumer. This bank producer neither creates a numerical Scope
nor treats polling errors as completion; public original Embedded execution is
not enabled by this factoring alone.

The Embedded native invocation mechanism consumes one exact admitted equation
role and reuses prepared native domains, token-validation storage and submission
recovery. A lexical construction guard closes graph and validation bookkeeping
before bank teardown. Actual closing state, scores and hidden captures are visited
into prepared completion roots; source publication happens only after terminal
completion and Record retirement. The enclosing adapter remains responsible for
authenticating actual state/parameter sources and pricing input, copy and transport
producers before admission; this scope mechanism alone does not enable a public
Embedded execution path.

Prediction workspace parameter binding consumes the retained native module source,
not its unloaded inner placeholders. The backend snapshots actual resident manager
array owners through a fixed nonblocking source loan, or uses the existing retained
layerwise parameter rows for host/disk output geometry, capacity and canonical
owner lifetime. Replacement arrays take the same source path. One native projection
inventory preserves backing aliases across physical modules; paid metadata records
keep dense construction order separate from architecture physical ordinals and
residency unit IDs. Binding authenticates retained tasks/local layout and current
native backing identities, then uses the shared finite parameter prepublication
worker. A final source callback rejects unconsumed module tails. These source facts
and retained witnesses authorize no native operation; the consumed invocation still
validates execution/source revision, selected equation, stream and actual domains.

The common speculative source owner retains an alias of the exact target
inference blueprint alongside its native source epoch and request identity.
Embedded equation construction consumes that retained selection and prepared
source graph; it does not reopen an artifact or accept an unrelated blueprint
whose geometry happens to match. The alias shares source storage and retires
before its source metadata funding.

Embedded prediction uses the same native backend `Error` domain as original
autoregressive execution. The typed executor and erased type bundle move existing
retained failures into `BackendFailure` without constructing a native `Exception`
wrapper. Native `Exception` values remain concrete sources through `Error::from`.
The original completion/quarantine worker is unchanged; its existing typed adapter
is shared by both executor types. This does not make an ordinary completion an
original completion witness.

The shared architecture prediction driver carries the complete execution context
through operation, observation and captured-prefill error boundaries. Its ordinary
error methods retain ordinary formatting. Original context methods reserve the
actual transport and use the existing metadata string/source workers before any
new diagnostic allocation. Neural bridge sources retain that same funding through
the closed neural error owner; observation markers keep the concrete failure in
the existing bridge. Architecture-owned fixed output/commit/type errors are inline
typed values. This boundary creates no new native or request authority.

Typed replicated prediction strategies accept a backend phase mechanism after
architecture pairing. The ordinary default invokes the same transaction without
adding validation or completion. A native phase mechanism can bind actual state,
parameter sources and request accounting before that transaction and retain its
native scope through completion. The same hook covers directly invoked and
captured-prefill seed equations; captured prefill keeps its forced observation
transaction, exact seed-span coordinates and carry-root completion. Native
adapters receive typed session mechanisms without adding family dispatch or
constraining unrelated portable session implementations to MLX.

The typed prediction phase handoff exposes an allocation-free visitor over the
shared driver's actual closing tensor and logits values. Concrete completion
adapters combine those borrowed roots with the current target and prediction
state. Output geometry and cloned root inventories do not grant source authority.

Prediction invocation adapters receive the existing shared scheduler's fixed
prefix provenance independently of optional activation observation. The normal
scheduler guard clears it on success, failure and unwind; no backend reconstructs
committed history or installs an observation engine to obtain these coordinates.

The MLX Embedded source owner retains the same exact original request and
runtime occurrence cursor outside target/prediction snapshots. Runtime normalizes
shared scheduler prefix coordinates and actual prefill spans; native binding
consumes each attempt before source-dependent quoting and admission. The source
owner grants no model equation or completion authority by itself.


Prediction workspace construction borrows the immutable declaration inventory retained
by successful ordinary extension materialization on the same prepared source graph.
The initial DeepSeek-V3 producer retains typed MTP, block, MLA, router and expert
construction specifications together with the exact selected task rows, source
layout, local placement, parameter description and component coordinates. Request
quotation validates that retained topology and task selection, aliases immutable
rows and coordinates, and copies only the closed neural declarations through
`WorkspaceContext`'s concrete metadata-copy producers before using the same typed
module builders. It does not clone configuration maps, rebuild model descriptors,
or treat equal byte counts as source identity. Native parameter and current-state
binders still authenticate the actual execution sources independently.

The source inventory is built once by ordinary loaded preparation, before it is
published in the existing placement slot. It contains no request or native grant
and has no edge back to the source graph. Request modules and failures retain
metadata funding through their enclosing workspace owners. Other prediction
families keep their ordinary constructors and require their own retained declaration
producer before this request-time source entry can qualify them; this is remaining
integration work, not a family limitation. Standalone checked V3 template creation
without that retained source is rejected before unpriced declarations are made.

The embedded prediction equation quote consumes the retained prediction declaration
and exact current lane through the same typed profile dispatcher and
`PredictionEquation` worker used by execution. The prepared state layout is lent
once to the native projector; its source owner remains external while the quote
retains metadata aliases. Parameter materialization consumes the same immutable
task rows and checks its entire source inventory. A proposal reads only its
selected depth/group frontier; seed and replay require the complete lane frontier.
Scalar input and immediate readout tails are explicit mechanism companions, and
all raw outputs, actual row views, target/prediction state and observation aliases
remain in the completed trace. The report owns metadata custody and escaping
errors retain that custody. Neither the equation descriptor nor its quote grants
native scope, occurrence, source publication or completion authority. Fused raw
scores remain raw here; later lazily requested rows require their own admitted
native producer.

The complete target inspection is retained from its actual source-preparation
validation inside the existing selected-source owner. Routed and partitioned
construction borrow this immutable artifact/catalog/target pairing; repeated
quotes do not copy or reconstruct it. Equation-only construction also omits the
extension materialization key set that only ordinary materialization consumes.

The concrete MLX embedded-prediction input and observer installation contracts use
the backend `Error` domain alongside the embedded executor. Native `Exception`
values move into its source-preserving variant; composite input failures retain
their typed backend or neural cause. This low-level callback error type does not
change the portable facade error contract or qualify arbitrary installed callbacks
for original-account execution.

The typed phase callback can shorten the ordinary execution context to the
lifetime of its actual native invocation. Scalar prediction input consumes that
borrowed prepared producer; no global registry or unscoped native pointer carries
the binding. The source/cursor lifetime is erased through a narrow borrowed
request interface, while the same concrete owner retains all issuance state.

A prediction phase borrows the enclosing cache branch's state and its exact
prepared evidence destination together. Successful native completion publishes
through that branch's existing paid copy provider; failure or allocation refusal
leaves the previous witness intact. Forks retain independent witness slots, and
neither the materialized predictor nor a shared backend adapter owns their latest
completion evidence.

Qwen hybrid prediction now uses the same retained construction source mechanism.
The private factory retains exact full-attention unit declarations, dense or
routed/shared MLP specifications, one canonical shared fusion/normalization
declaration, actual task rows, expert coordinates and the selected prediction
state layout. Ordinary preparation and retained reconstruction share typed
operator builders; request construction copies names/format companions through
the closed neural metadata census and copies state through the existing exact
StateLayout workspace producer. It does not recreate model configurations,
RoPE maps, task descriptions or placement. Native source and state authentication
remain separate. Checked source-template constructors require that retained
source rather than allocating new unpriced declarations. Remaining prediction
families still require their corresponding retained factory increments.

Native Embedded prediction equation quoting borrows the actual resolved target
session, current typed prediction lane and input tensors. A single input alias
collector, architecture-selected state projection and retained parameter binder
feed the existing architecture equation quote and resident native reducer. The
returned owner keeps the exact source witnesses, layerwise source, report and
cumulative metadata funding through subsequent registration and admission.

The scalar token companion uses the same eager original token-upload worker for
I32 and U32, with an exact signed source value, separately quoted Graph/backing
contributions and one physical birth. It prepares a paid final clone handle
before execution and retains the uploaded scalar through the actual completion
root visitor. Immediate sequential readout uses the existing static Slice/Squeeze
index. Fused output remains whole; later row extraction retains the existing lazy
consumer boundary and requires its own admitted producer. The native scope/role
and publication adapter remains a separate consuming join; the quote grants no
execution authority and does not relax the public Embedded gate.

The same typed invocation adapter wraps target prefill/verification/replay and
prediction equations. Target state remains installed in its ordinary session;
a separate borrowed evidence slot publishes completion to the correct enclosing
cache. Captured prefill preserves its one shared chunk driver, input/failure
agreement and output demand. Original target/seed invocations use their prepared
validation collectors; ordinary captured spans keep their existing collector.

Inkling MTP uses the same retained prediction factory. Its once-owned source
contains each depth's dense decoder, learned-relative attention parameters,
causal convolution declarations and exact full/sliding attention policy. The
optional chain normalization remains a distinct shared physical owner, so its
absence does not renumber the actual module inventory. Ordinary and retained
construction share the typed dense layer and attention builders. Concrete
ParameterSpec and causal-convolution declaration copies use the existing
Workspace metadata census; the selected state layout uses the shared exact
state-copy producer. Request reconstruction does not clone TextArgs or regenerate
parameter names. This source inventory conveys no native binding or phase grant.

The native embedded target and prediction quotes project current target state,
selected parameter representations, and layerwise source metadata through one
immutable session inspection helper. Target prefill and verification retain their
actual token backing separately from the portable equation's explicit token
placeholder; that placeholder grants no native source credit. The exact dtype
and span geometry are checked before quote reduction. Both quote forms keep
owned source witnesses and metadata funding through subsequent native binding.

The native speculative logits carrier also has a private model-phase pending
destination. Its actual shared shell, completed-value destination and immutable
stream copy are charged to the authenticated request before native entry. A
returned pending row owns its array, originating budget, role and host custody
through Recovery retirement. Only the exact completed resident source can seal
it for the existing numerical compiler; allocation identity and capacity are
rechecked against that source's retained native budget. This is per-output
evidence, not a mutable latest-source slot. Unknown/unsealed rows cannot enter
sampling. The generic numerical compiler and lazy fused-row caller remain the
execution mechanisms; this carrier by itself does not enable an Embedded lane.

Embedded native execution and its erased executor now use the same opaque
ordinary/original logits carrier as independent speculation. The public native
Array observer installer keeps its existing callback types through a borrowed
outer-row adapter; arbitrary installed callback ownership stays ordinary and
refuses original rows. The empty original observer set acts directly on the
closed carrier. Immediate sequential readout is injected through the actual
invocation binding and reuses the ordinary static Slice/Squeeze worker. A
missing invocation/output proof rejects before that worker; later verification
and fused row selection require their own retained per-output source join.

Nemotron-H prediction preparation retains the exact source and rank-local neural
declarations, physical-unit task rows, expert coordinate owners, and state layout.
Workspace construction borrows that retained source instead of rebuilding model
configuration or checkpoint-format maps. Pattern groups preserve their physical
attention and ReLU-squared expert units, with fusion on the first member and
final normalization on the last; state membership remains per physical unit.

Supplementary prediction source windows use a separate immutable inventory built
by the existing admitted residency-manager initializer. Its IDs are the actual
loaded unit declarations outside the retained target selection. The inventory
preserves physical IDs (including optional-module gaps); each window describes
the shared singleton module-acquire protocol and its real canonical alias closure.
Repeated and nested calls remain separate occurrences in the consuming invocation
bank. The source inventory is not an architecture execution schedule or a grant.

Ready-host snapshots and foreground descriptors share their existing constructors,
with the supplementary declarations, source-ID copies, identities, closure scratch
and window rows included in the same source-account census before construction.
A request projects these owners through a counted WorkspaceContext; it neither
reopens a checkpoint nor adopts the target policy identity. Source qualification
checks the exact manager and matching copy-witness/window pair. Source and weak
manager aliases retain their original initialization custody, while native role,
actual module/task/layout and invocation-order validation remain responsibilities
of the consuming prepared bank. Ordinary residency and target selection checks
are unchanged.

Prediction completion borrows the architecture executor's exact lane-value
iterator. The shared driver declares each actual observed-equation, captured-seed,
or carry-only completion point and passes the complete native execution context.
Carry-only completion additionally lends prior lane and target-output evidence;
a stream or current scope cannot substitute for those source witnesses. Ordinary
execution uses the same iterator and existing materializer completion worker.

Lazy Embedded logit selection is an additional fixed program in the existing
original numerical compiler. It consumes an exact completed model array and
its recorded completion stream, qualifies an inspection handle before birth,
and runs the same native static row worker. The completed row keeps both the
new numerical phase custody and its original backing source. No fused rows
are prepared eagerly. Selected prefill logits move through the same completed
source/stream binding without an extra numerical operation. Cache-copy source
validation remains unchanged; importing a model value into sampling requires
the stronger explicit completed-stream fact.

Embedded prediction completion recipes retain the quote-funded root-list
inventory for actual module/state completion calls, separately from fixed-width
native internal producers. Graph and Record accounting sums the exact per-call
root distribution and synchronization constructors; only reusable traversal
scratch uses the maximum root capacity. Materialization copy/wait producers keep
their separate source-derived populations. Binding consumes the immutable
inventory once and does not confer source or execution authority.

The retained prediction-construction inventory also covers sequential DeepSeek-V4
and fused DSpark. Both use the existing ordinary pooling attention, compressor,
indexer, low-rank projection, routed/shared expert and Hyper builders through
immutable typed declarations. Rotary buffers retain the existing fixed scalar
initializer and its exact floating-point expression order. Source and local
declarations are compiled from the actual model geometry at loading, including
selected expert-bank replacement, then reused without per-request Args, format
map, task-name or local-layout construction.

Sequential depth modules and DSpark's distinct pinned projections/Markov and
confidence heads retain their exact unit/shared roles, tasks and parameter source
layouts. The retained factory copies pooling policies through the existing
exhaustive state-policy census and copies DSpark's ordered target-capture policy
through a paid boxed-slice clone. Hyper and embedding specification copies extend
the common recursive metadata producer. Original source/config/task matching and
native parameter/state authorization remain separate; no family branch is added
to native execution.

Originally admitted speculative lane preparation and the one-lane driver consume
the common numerical source owner. The typed executor supplies its own cache and
occurrence schedule; target/draft source pairing and embedded prediction source
binding remain with their respective composition adapters. Sampling, text policy,
cancellation and controlled advancement continue through the same driver.

Embedded verification now keeps its completed source in the verification output,
so later row selection never consults a replacement branch's current state.
Fused prediction returns a fixed immutable tensor/source owner. Original draft
copies share its paid descriptor and evidence without cloning the native tensor;
ordinary drafts preserve their existing tensor-copy behavior. The temporary
observed proposal keeps that owner before its cache retires. Only the requested
fused row enters the existing source-bound numerical compiler.

The native binding authenticates each actual array against the completed source,
its recorded stream and the exact speculative request before constructing these
owners. Already settled target verification retains that proof instead of
submitting an ordinary event or allocating an ordinary completion root vector.
This does not certify an arbitrary source, input, or callback. Capture-row and
accepted-prefix tensor operations, token-vector preparation, and their saved-state
source joins remain separate producers needed before complete Embedded original
execution can be enabled.


Original supplementary eviction borrows the actual module identifier under the
source-bound call bank. The core residency ledger shares explicit pin/policy and
accounting checks plus the committed removal with ordinary eviction; its borrowed
entry additionally rejects unresolved transfers and allocates no identifier or
error message. The MLX manager validates the cached supplementary source, current
scope, and original operation custody and uses its non-reaping lock. The module
bank calls only after exact lease completion and retains failures with its
original source/account. Eviction updates residency telemetry, not cumulative
operation admission or observation allowances.

The Embedded outer tensor observer now has a structurally empty default slot.
Original execution validates that slot and the full source context before any
caller capability query or callback, then moves the already owned tensor through
a source-funded fixed transport. No native handle is cloned. Caller-installed
observers remain ordinary until their own state/source contract exists. Ordinary
execution still runs the shared begin-span, observe and intervene worker and
preserves its unchanged-value Clone behavior, including for the empty default.
This move hands off an existing value; it creates no completed-source evidence
and grants no numerical or model invocation.

Embedded request composition captures immutable numerical prerequisites from the
actual executable before lending its disjoint retained selection and mutable
session. The move-only preparation retains the existing blueprint, exact
execution identity, runtime facts, pool and paying metadata source. Binding
consumes it only after the selected schedule opens the matching request, with
the same pool/execution checks used by independent speculation. It supplies no
replacement selection or invocation permission and creates no second account.


The bounded chat renderer admits built-in length/count over represented borrowed
text and collection values through the shared MiniJinja length primitive. The
ordinary Value entry retains its exact custom-object length callback and error
behavior. Measured and actual bounded execution keep Unicode character counts
and trim-edge counts beside byte ranges in the existing paid operand record;
concatenation and trimming create no extra buffer or retained input reference.
The same source/compiler/render accounts price those actual record sizes and
worker controls. Scalar and missing-value length remain typed failures; dynamic
loop-object enumeration, arbitrary structured iteration and tool/reasoning
controllers are separate profiles and are not authorized by this filter.

Completed native tensor sources retain an exact Model or Numerical allocation
account tag per full backing. The existing completed-root constructor performs
the same unique-root, capacity, account and pool checks for both tags, and the
existing isolated-copy admission revalidates every original account. Model-only
constructor and readout APIs remain strict model projections. A numerical phase
never becomes a model role merely because its output later feeds a model.

Native publication accepts a finite lexical list of prior state/input sources.
Repeated declarations of one backing must agree on capacity and exact account;
current native budget inspection still authenticates every retained entry.
Views keep the backing's original account. These inventories contain account
custody and allocation facts, not tensor aliases or a mutable request-wide source
registry. They are the source prerequisite for later owned token/capture tensor
packets; the account generalization alone does not enable those producers.

The original embedded request entry consumes a prepared prediction lane and the
actual retained selection through the existing typed continuation. It preserves
the lane's architecture-reported initial prediction frontier, uses the shared
prefill geometry, and supplies the same request to cache preparation, phases,
sampling and the common lane driver. Typed adapter construction is charged before
its values are built. Initial source preparation currently requires a fresh
target frontier; populated target resume needs its exact retained completed state
and schedule source. Native phase and tensor-source qualification still determine
which executions can proceed; request wiring alone is not complete support.


Bounded chat default/d uses the same lazy primary-value selection primitive as
the ordinary MiniJinja filter. Positional fallback arguments are evaluated in
ordinary order before selection, and the optional flag uses the existing actual
truth rule. The compiler accounts for the emit plus three operand continuations
at maximum arity; render execution reuses the existing three paid operand slots.
The selected borrowed value is rebound before slot reuse, with no reference
stored in output or error buffers. An empty list fallback uses the existing
empty-sequence value, without a per-render list allocation. Arbitrary list
construction, keyword/splat arguments and tool/reasoning controllers remain
separate profiles; the filter does not authorize those operations.

The MLX Embedded prediction module bank consumes the architecture workspace
recorder's actual module entry and completion order. It maps dense entries to
the retained manager's distinct supplementary source inventory, preserving
repeated and nested calls. Each accepted role owns the existing transfer and
lease workers plus prepaid retained-root destinations; the weak module binding
checks that exact bank, selected stream, physical source and current scope.
Nested shared calls keep the outer lease and foreground source capacity until
its own completion. Failure prefixes stay with the same recovery owner, and
post-completion eviction uses the source-qualified manager operation. The
portable invocation carrier may move an existing root destination into this
worker; that move grants no source or submission authority.

The completed-root account bundle erases its existing shared handle behind a
private custody interface. The concrete Model/Numerical account vector remains
unchanged and each original account still validates against the current pool
usage. Safe Arc coercion checks Send and Sync at construction; no unsafe trait
implementation, extra owner allocation or recursion-limit change is involved.
Final retirement dispatches back to the concrete Arc, releasing its allocation
before its account vector and paying host authority. The constructor prices the
actual fat-pointer and query/retirement transport frames alongside that same
account shell. This boundary limits type expansion through pool/pin custody; it
creates no new source evidence, registration or execution permission.

The existing immutable fused-output owner also carries general prediction
tensors. Its ordinary branch preserves the original Clone behavior; its prepared
branch shares a paid immutable descriptor without cloning the native handle.
An explicit snapshot copy uses the retained prepared-copy provider and installs
that producer's returned evidence, never the old completion receipt. Value and
evidence retire before their copy provider and host custody. The former fused
logit-block name remains an alias of this same owner.

MLX execution contexts can lend a finite slice of those exact per-value completed
inventories for one outer model call. Binding validates every account against the
same request and the actual completed stream before entering a native invocation;
unknown evidence rejects. The phase binder still authenticates each actual full
backing against those inventories and its native budget. This borrowed transport
does not manufacture tensor provenance or enable the remaining token-upload and
capture-view numerical producers. Registered copies continue to require their
actual canonical pins; no unchecked registered-source marker is introduced.


Bounded chat plain `join` shares MiniJinja's ordinary separator/iteration worker
and scalar formatter. Its admitted inputs are borrowed scalar JSON arrays,
borrowed Unicode text and the ordinary empty None/undefined/empty-list cases,
with zero or one literal/borrowed text separator. Actual rendered bytes, Unicode
counts and trim boundaries are measured from that same input and worker before
reservation; execution fills the existing paid context-text destination and
one retained concat atom per call. Generated text carries inline measured
metadata through concatenation, trimming and length, so neither measurement nor
output relies on a reused borrowed-value register. Buffers escaping success or
partial reservation failure retain the existing host custody. Dynamic objects,
nested-value formatting, generated-text iteration, attribute projection,
autoescape and tool/reasoning policy remain separate profiles; `join` does not
implicitly authorize them.

The native Embedded target-phase adapter now consumes the portable occurrence
claim and the actual installed target state through the existing target equation
quote. It binds completed or registered input/state storage, prepares the selected
resident or bounded neural bank, and enters the same native recovery driver as
prediction equations. Closing state and output roots are borrowed; their source
evidence is published only after terminal completion and observer retirement.
The ordinary path continues through the same session callback. Both concrete
strategy construction sites select this adapter and account for its actual type.

The target and prediction adapters share finite source-prior binding, borrowed
state traversal and callback control sizing. Neither reconstructs a family
equation or claims authority from tensor shape. Public Embedded integration is
still being validated: populated target resumption, exact internal observation
programs, input-span numerical preparation and the complete controlled/residency
matrix remain integration work, not architectural restrictions.

The original numerical compiler also owns exact eager U32 token inputs. Their
closed program has zero tensor sources and retains the actual [1,N] geometry.
The shared native eager-upload facts supply its physical backing and Graph
extents; the ordinary resident completion reducer supplies the same collector,
Record and settlement protocol. The metadata trace uses an existing source,
not an Initialize/full equation or a signed conversion. Host input is borrowed
only through the eager copy; no caller token slice survives the invocation.

After numerical completion and exact Record retirement, the unique token value
moves into the existing immutable prediction-tensor owner. Its completed source
records the actual originating Numerical budget/account and stream. The retained
cache-copy context authenticates that source and prepares the same generic copy
provider used by cache states. Explicit tensor copies use the existing isolated
completed-source copy/publication worker and retain its registered Q/H custody
inside the payload authority; stale completion evidence is cleared. These
producers do not relabel token input as logits or as a model role. Their shared
caller hooks and token/capture view consumers remain required before public
Embedded execution can rely on this new tensor producer.

The immutable token constructor keeps its consumed native value and completed
source in a single value-first provisional transport. The numerical caller pays
that fixed transport before opening the completed value. After exact backing
validation, a cheap budget/account alias stays in the provisional owner while
source-evidence erasure can still fail. A failure therefore retires the native
value before its last local source/custody alias; success moves it into the
same immutable packet. This adds no array clone, new account or source grant.

Registered inputs to speculative numerical programs retain a distinct provenance
tag. The runtime associates an existing copy account with the exact request;
this association grants no model/numerical birth credit or native permission.
The MLX importer accepts only the closed published RegisteredArrayCopy, validates
its publication stream and completed integer backing, and retains its copy and
host custody through numerical source use. The existing whole prepared-input
copy is reusable before admitted token-span views. Raw arrays plus a pool
identity cannot enter through this importer, and completed model/numerical
allocation tags remain distinct from registered copy storage.

The original numerical stream wrapper retains a private exact source tag for completed model/numerical accounts or an authenticated registered-copy source. Both use the same prepaid stream-copy worker and deferred retirement owner; registered copies retain their independent copy account and are never relabelled as model or numerical allocations. The wrapper prices its actual tagged owner and control frames before native handle construction.

Original capture host construction accepts an explicit independent invocation
through the existing `CaptureRunHostPlan`, fixed claim table, frame builders,
transformation claims and funded observer. Its physical phase, shape and scope
mask remain separate from the logical prediction coordinate; no text origin is
created. The scope mask is copied into the same paid bank before use, skipped
records retain the ordinary Schedule/NotInvoked distinction, and all transform
claims use the actual invocation dimensions. Same-bank attempts remain one-use;
finished shared payloads retain destination custody after teardown. Fixed bounds
validation and ordinary diagnostic mapping share one semantic worker. This is a
neutral host producer: native source authentication, model-role capture custody,
workspace/transform quotation and the original Embedded observer hookup remain
separate required consumers. The native phase gates are unchanged by this unit.


Original Embedded prefill source preparation preserves the full native execution
context until the existing architecture input lowerer is called. The native
adapter authenticates the canonical original I/B input, cache identity and pool,
then shares its existing immutable `PreparedModelInputOwner`; it does not recreate
native handles, part vectors, fingerprints or admission configuration with the
ordinary constructor. Architecture-owned text and composite lowering use the
same geometry, processor validation and admission workers with the request's
paid metadata destinations. The neutral span-operation hook also preserves this
context through chunk preparation. These source controls grant no native
Slice/Concat permission. For an actual original single-part token input, the
existing isolated prepared-source copy worker completes one whole I32/U32 copy;
its closed registered importer and numerical range producer create each span.
The ordinary text/composite chunk builders consume a paid inspection alias of
that completed tensor, retain its immutable packet after the alias, and lend the
packet's exact account/source evidence to the same target phase. Source/chunk
geometry is checked before numerical construction, and repeated spans retain
cumulative accounting. Multipart and media input programs still require their
own complete source/view producer and reject before native lowering; this is an
input-producer integration dependency, not a model-family restriction. Ordinary
span preparation keeps its existing worker.

The original speculative eager token-input producer uses its own checked
OriginalPromptInputFacts storage within the admitted Graph and buffer budget.
It does not install the lazy equation constructor bank, whose population contains
no eager input slots. The same numerical recovery, prepared root completion and
source publication still settle the uploaded tensor before it escapes.

An explicit Embedded capture host plan can now accompany the existing model-role
admission. It binds the exact originally compiled C source, actual invocation
workspace and scheduler origin, and returns a move-only constructor beside that
same role. The constructor creates the existing funded observer bank under
account-only model custody. Request-owned cumulative lineage remains outside
model checkpoints; accepted roles and failed attempts retain prior spending.
An equivalent copied declaration cannot replace the retained physical source.
Model capture claims validate their actual paying role independently of native
source/scope/completion, and completed shared host payloads retain that custody.
This neutral destination producer does not install an internal native observer:
the prepared workspace source, quoted native transformations, callback lifetime
and exact completion/delivery join remain required at the same phase boundary.

Original embedded tensor views use the existing numerical phase compiler for static token and capture ranges. The view retains its actual native buffer/Graph budget and numerical account, while the immutable tensor owner also keeps its predecessor's source custody. Completed model/numerical backings retain their exact completion source; a registered-copy backing instead carries a closed array-free proof of its actual copy account, request, completed stream, allocation identity and full capacity. Both target and prediction input binding compare registered evidence to the actual projected native root before the existing canonical pin binder; registered roots receive no completed-model credit. Signed I32 and unsigned U32 token views preserve their source representation.

The same isolated array-copy worker accepts an exact prepared-B source without token normalization. Its account-only custody may be shared without copying arrays or refunding usage. The shared prepared-copy dispatcher lends its own closed evidence owner to providers which must publish fresh copy evidence; ordinary providers retain their existing default callback. Tensor copies use that loan to attach the new registered allocation's proof, never the predecessor's completion receipt. A failed evidence allocation keeps the still-closed copied Array and its original custody together. Public embedded invocation/caller integration remains a separate join; these producers do not authorize a model phase.

Internal speculative activation envelopes now use the same CapturedStepDelivery
owner as prediction captures. Legacy collectors move their ordinary frame;
original collectors move a SharedCapturedStep with its existing C/Q/H custody.
The shared controlled driver retains this owner through its existing bounded
buffer, and serialization preserves the previous record shape. Metadata remains
separately owned by the envelope; original constructors must prepay its identity
and reduction payloads. Caller clones share the funded frame and copy only their
ordinary envelope metadata; deserialization never creates funded ownership.

The Embedded prediction equation quote now receives an explicit logical observation coordinate and invokes the same observer span lifecycle around the retained architecture equation. Independent model-capture quoting uses the existing capture transformation worker with the actual physical phase, sequence/context shape, and borrowed applicability mask; the logical prediction count is never used as a cache extent. The quote retains all emitted capture roots until its equation report is fixed and remains separate from C-source validation, model-role admission, and native completion.

Native tensor-view buffer budgets are deliberately not Send/Sync and stay in array-free native-local PreparedEmbeddedEvidence: the completed-source wrapper or registered-copy proof. HostPreparationAuthority retains only the thread-safe numerical account and metadata funding. Constructor guards hold both the actual backing budget and view-operation budget until evidence publication succeeds or the native Array retires on failure.

Speculative activation source authentication compares the already admitted
artifact, selected execution/overlay tuple and realized session using a fixed
borrowed serializer sink. It creates no discovery DTO, plan clone or admission.
Architecture-owned declaration and scope validation remain separately required
before the backend compiles the exact original capture source.
