The shared summary trace identifies its real eager `Array::try_from_f32`
constructor as the closed zero-input `scalar_f32` equation. Both CPU and Metal
facts require exactly one rank-zero F32 output and price one native seed plus
the borrowed scalar/result transports. Generic initialization retains its
separate fill/copy contract; it supplies no eager-scalar evidence. CPU `where`
facts preserve the ordinary Bool/F32/F32 promotion and actual scalar broadcast
followed by the existing Select worker. A full cold summary trace combines these
with classification and rank-one reduction sources; native summary completion
and public capture admission remain independent consumer requirements.


The ordinary recognizer and retained-record reconstruction now use one fallible
slice-tree constructor. Its prepared entry reserves exact child tables, string
payloads and masks from the actual record, plus a finite failed-parent table
sized by that tree's actual depth. Every filtered trie is checked against the
actual full vocabulary's conservative constructor envelope before construction;
there is no caller-supplied/default arena or refund from scalar progress.
Completed child trees and leaf failure prefixes stay owned on later refusal.
The resulting immutable SlicerProgram has no tokenizer callback or compiler;
its enclosing runtime owner must still retain registered recipe/trie custody.
This closes immutable slicer construction only. Original Auto/Active admission
still awaits mutable lexer/parser storage, callback tokenization, per-step
scratch/mask construction and their controlled copy/commit consumers.

The original native text operation now installs a payload-free partition capture
source beside its existing model/control owner. It authenticates loaded discovery,
architecture output ownership, exact request/source identity and recorded scalar
precision, then lends the same paid runtime receipt program to the shared funded
observer. Complete logits transforms use producer hooks before publication; peers
receive canonical framed tensors through independently admitted native child roles.
The transport/frame owner remains in ordinary Recovery until enclosing completion.


Original tokenizer ID encoding now admits the actual bare ByteLevel component
when add_prefix_space and use_regex are both false. Its source selects the same
whole-span ByteLevel transformations and BPE scratch worker already used by
compiled regex spans. The mapped UTF-8 destination is still paid at twice the
actual normalized input-byte extent; there is no regex workspace or delegate to
invent for this path. Prefixing and other unsupported pipeline shapes retain
their typed profile refusal. This closes the reached normalized grammar-source
fixture's encode callback without changing its tokenizer or relaxing validation.

The numerical CPU capture source can now compose Summary with the existing raw
transforms. Admission still requires a complete CPU equation trace, exact source
representation and no intervention source; other readout families remain explicit
refusals. The native summary adapter borrows that installed recipe's exact CPU
stream and original observer through CpuCaptureLoan. It reuses the ordinary
selection/flatten/chunk worker, the same scalar read completion, source retention
and claimed host record; no replacement equation or completion account is created.
The quoted population retains source, selected, flat and all possible chunk
outputs, plus one flatten completion and every possible scalar frontier. Actual
zero-finite/zero-scale branches can omit work without refunding issued allowances.
Public support is not inferred from this join; its native behavior is validated
through the existing numerical source/copy/capture producer before any broader
capability claim.


The facade's original grammar source now consumes that constructor under its
existing WorkspaceMetadataFunding authority. Fixed inspection frames are funded
before reading the tree; the complete source-derived envelope is reserved before
any slice destination. OriginalGrammarSlicer stores its actual immutable program
before the exact OriginalGrammarVocabulary/registered-recipe owner, so all
program allocations retire before H/C. Typed failures retain the actual failed
tree before those same owners. This uses the existing neutral paid-host contract
and keeps llguidance grammar policy out of the backend and eredu-runtime. It
still does not admit a mutable grammar parser, Auto/Active controller or dynamic
mask callback; those consumers require their own complete construction and copy.

Managed parallel capture passes its retained `PreparedCaptureSelection` through
the existing funded parallel quote entry. The same planning account binds the
actual capture geometry and records its transforms beside the selected model
and publication equations. The shared native recipe and receipt program still
require exact source, role, transport, and completion producers; the outer entry
does not substitute a separate resident quote or create native permission.


External target prefill/verification quotation now borrows its exact retained
prepared token tensor through the shared architecture span driver. It validates
the invocation geometry and integer dtype, preserving context/storage identity
and recording no synthetic input allocation. The external trace callback carries
an optional input-operation index; None means every recorded equation is real
and none may be skipped. Ordinary token construction retains Some(index).
Native parameter/state binding, source admission, output demand and actual input
copy/preparation remain unchanged and keep their separate original owners.

Layerwise combined TP/PP construction reuses the tensor-wave owner from its
earlier same-selection, same-rank completed partition source. Final native
mechanism binding therefore seals the exact semantic source consumed by later
cold quotes. A different selection or published owner is rejected; no topology
inference supplies the native participation fact and no binding is reset.

### Completed native stride projection

The native descriptor loan exposes signed element strides only for its certified
completed allocation, while retaining the same source and runtime guard. Backend
projection consumes that evidence for ordinary, prepared and owning imports:
final-axis unit stride and a dense axis permutation are proved from actual
strides, including repeated extents and singleton axes. Negative, broadcast,
gapped or unknown strides receive no dense-layout claim. The fixed eight-axis
inspection frame is included in the common import reservation before inspection.
This adds descriptive layout evidence without evaluation, allocation, new
storage credit, or portable family policy in the backend.

Parallel capture receipt sizing uses each actual producer fragment's existing
pre-admitted complete-record encoding allowance and the canonical borrowed
wire envelope counter before quoting transport and receiver storage. The receipt
digest seals that derived bound, capped by the caller's per-record maximum;
all-rank work still consumes the separate nonrefundable step/run ledger. Repeated
source precision is covered by the same complete-record allowance. Empty
producers without such a fragment source retain their explicit bound. The native
transform, child transport role and physical metadata permissions are unchanged.

Shared readout retains the existing hidden tensor directly when its declared
sequence axis already contains one position. This removes a redundant index from
cached decode and one-position final prefill chunks without changing vocabulary
demand, geometry, state, observation attribution or the projection equation.
Multi-position selection continues to retain the complete declared axis policy.

Managed partition capture revalidation borrows the private loaded report that
ordinary capture built from the retained architecture placement, actual hook
coverage and native collector facts. It authenticates that report's execution
and communication setup against the current session before validating the
immutable admitted plan. The causal path binder, continuation and saved-copy
checks use this same report; no unrefined ordinary support table can silently
replace the partition source, and no discovery payload is reconstructed.

Parallel managed Summary capture uses the same retained complete-logits owner
and ordinary fixed Summary producer. Each reached prompt fragment uses the
existing finite F64 accumulator; receivers advance the same announced hooks
without a numerical transform. At shared post-forward delivery the canonical
receipt parser fills the original scalar claim, validates source identity,
shape, charge, counts and aggregates, and participates in the existing final
receipt vote before commit. Tensor and Summary payloads share envelope parsing
and transport; neither receipt arrival nor host parsing proves native completion.

CPU histogram capture uses the same immutable admitted edge source and ordinary
fixed-edge chunk program. Its floating comparisons, Bool predicates, scalar
broadcasts and count reductions each consume the existing native CPU worker
facts. The trace describes exact static intervals and eager F32 scalars, with
no generic initialization/source inference. The native adapter borrows the
installed CpuCaptureLoan and retains the existing claimed histogram destination
through inclusive-final-bin counting and exact partition validation. The complete
trace, source representation, root population and scalar completion count remain
mandatory before numerical admission; other capture families and interventions
remain independently qualified. No public support claim follows from cold facts
alone.

The original CPU scalar-overwrite source authenticates the existing rank-one
F32 `SliceUpdate::None` branch, including complete contiguous row backing and
one in-range singleton update. Its full-row copy and shaped overwrite share the
ordinary copy dispatch, with two actual task/weak-owner populations and one
output backing birth. Reduction updates, other ranks, dtypes, strides and
incomplete backing remain outside this source. Naming the shaped-copy callable
exposes its storage layout without replacing its numerical body. This source
alone grants no capture request, selected input, completion or host-output role.

CPU selected-token capture borrows the qualified numerical recipe and the same
original observer used by raw, Summary and Histogram capture. Its ordinary
TokenScoreProgram remains the sole finite-check, full-vocabulary partition,
competition-rank and strongest-alternative implementation. Exact static
Slice/Reshape metadata, eager scalar facts, composed ArgReduce/Squeeze and the
rank-one scalar overwrite describe its actual CPU workers. Each scalar read
retains its existing nested completion and paid claim destination; requested
IDs or sampling-domain membership never narrow normalization. Missing source
representations still refuse the entire recipe. TopCandidates and intervention
sources remain separate work; this does not widen public capture capabilities.

The CPU ArgSort source qualifies the existing rank-one F32 row worker and its
independent U32 output. The exact same comparator, sift and traversal loops
retain stable ascending IDs for equal scores and NaNs. Named callable factories
expose their actual control types and the queued task layout; they introduce no
second sorting engine or temporary heap. Native source validation checks the
actual primitive, axis, dtype, output geometry and input stride span. Other
ArgSort workers retain their existing unqualified status.

The CPU TopCandidates consumer uses the ordinary CandidateExtraction worker
under its qualified numerical capture loan. Its two-output quote reuses shared
geometry validation and the existing finite-classification/count sources, then
prices the full U32 ArgSort result, possible K-entry contiguity copy and K-F32
Gather/Squeeze result independently. All nine intermediate handles and the
three finite-count/IDs/scores completions remain in the original recovery and
completion owner. Host records consume the existing paid candidate destination;
mask/domain evidence does not change raw score ordering. Native source, capture
and cumulative budgets remain mandatory; no public capability is inferred from
this producer alone.

The shared llguidance slicer step now derives its mask and maximum simultaneous
child-match flags from the actual immutable slice tree. Ordinary bias computation
and the prepared borrowed step use one traversal, preserving lexer subsumption
order, the single-child complement and multiple-child fallback tries, prefix
filtering and mask sentinel storage. The prepared step reuses its exact mask and
flag allocations, and a failed second destination retains the completed mask.
This is the slicer-local destination contract only: recognizer lexer/parser
allocations, parser mask caches, callback tokenization and original Auto/Active
controller admission still require their own qualified producers.

The facade's prepared slicer step reserves its fixed inspection frames and actual
mask/traversal destinations through the same retained vocabulary funding. Both
success and failed destination prefixes borrow that exact immutable owner until
their storage retires. Step construction does not grant authority for the separate
recognizer supplied to the shared traversal.

Lexer precomputation now uses one source-derived state-stack and mask constructor
in both ordinary and prepared entry points. Its state capacity is the actual trie
maximum token depth plus the initial state, replacing the old growing 300-entry
estimate. The same trie walker, start-state selection, DFA transitions and error
checks remain authoritative. Prepared failures retain completed local destinations;
ordinary failures tear those buffers down before returning the original typed DFA
cause. This local traversal bound does not certify mutable derivative/DFA storage
or the remaining original parser/controller construction.

TokTrie callback segmentation now has shared allocation-free visitors for exact
UTF-8/greedy fallback spans, special spellings and marked/numeric tokens, plus the
same borrowed greedy iterator. Ordinary tokenizer environments immediately use
these workers and keep their original callback boundaries and fixed-token count.
Prepared consumers can supply original encoding outputs and paid destinations
without impersonating an allocating TokEnv callback; the visitors themselves
provide no tokenizer, parser, result-storage or account admission.

Original grammar tokenization consumes those same UTF-8, special and marker
visitors. Every text segment uses the originally retained tokenizer's existing E
admission/compiler; greedy and explicit-token rows use its actual trie. A finite
row destination is reserved before any E result, then an exact contiguous scalar
ID destination is reserved after the actual counts are known. Source comparison
rejects equal-vocabulary outputs from a different tokenizer owner while retaining
the completed E prefixes. Outputs/errors retain the exact trie, historical recipe
and H until all scalar/chunk storage retires. This closes callback tokenization
without adding an ordinary TokEnv adapter; mutable grammar/DFA/parser construction
and Auto/Active controller admission remain separate required work.

The derivre hash-cons owner now provides a fallible source-bound copy constructor
shared by ordinary Clone. It uses the actual initialized backing/entry lengths,
actual owning hash-table capacity/allocation and retained hasher; it preserves
committed IDs and legacy pending-insertion state. Every destination is reserved
and checked before publication, and failure retains its real vector/table prefix.
This is a local copy source, not authority for subsequent growing insertion or
complete expression-set, DFA, lexer, Earley or controller storage.

Compiled grammar expression sources have one fallible copy path shared with
ordinary Clone: actual hash-cons vectors/table, weight rows, pretty-printer
mapping, Unicode memo keys/table, JSON quote memo/table and inline parser-builder
configuration. The two private memo tables use the existing hashbrown owner so
admission reads their real allocation size; public std-map traversal callers keep
the same interface and share the original mapping equations through a storage-only
adapter. No source syntax parsing or new expression transformation runs in a copy.
Partial failures retain actual child destinations, including failed keys/mappings.
These sources still do not authorize future derivative/cache/Earley growth;
mutable parser and Auto/Active controller admission require that separate join.

The original CPU numerical capture path lends its already accepted CPU recipe to
the shared static activation worker and to pre/post Preview and Summary evidence.
Cold activation traces preserve explicit slice coordinates and identify the
actual eager F32 scalar constructor. A complete positive-stride F32 replacement
uses MLX's existing SliceUpdate identity branch: the selected replacement remains
the output owner, with one C result handle and no new copy or Eval task. Partial
F32 rectangles use their exact copy/overwrite source and one complete output
backing. A full
positive-stride slice likewise prices the existing identity return. Source
claims, scheduled intervention receipts, cumulative capture use, escaped evidence
and native completion remain with the same ordinary/controlled shared drivers;
this producer does not broaden public intervention admission.

Direct tensor-parallel capture quotation binds the same prepared observation
paths to its actual retained local runtime and uses the ordinary parallel
traversal with a borrowed hook. Unit input/output and internal callbacks now
reach the cold observer in the same order as native observed execution; path
construction and shared-observer allocation are absent from forward. Exact
per-selection placement, native transform and transport sources remain separate
admission requirements, including for intermediate activations.

Managed complete-point capture borrows the exact loaded architecture placement
table during cold quotation. Its allocation-free complete-source projection
uses the ordinary collector's lowest exporting replica and rejects partial or
additive axes. The native frame copies one paid producer ordinal per selected
point from that same retained table; it retains the original shared capture
source and never reconstructs an owner from a path or family name. Complete
unit observations executed by every rank use the existing native capture hook
and receipt path. Final publication preserves its separate architecture-declared
owner; absent PP unit hooks still require a remote source producer before grant.

Regex AST source copying now shares ordinary Clone's constructor with a finite
source-derived traversal and partial-destination stack. The quote includes actual
nested byte/word/child arrays, each boxed unary child, JSON escape strings and
maximum live traversal depth. No regex recognition or syntax parsing occurs in
this copy. Failed child construction retains completed siblings and unfinished
parent destinations; borrowed traversal scratch safely retires before the error
escapes. Actual source-inspection custody is still required before walking a tree,
and this constructor grants no parser/derivative growth authority.

Lexer declaration source copies compose those exact AST/expression constructors
with actual lexeme names, match sets, token ranges, JSON options, skip-class memo,
warning strings and scalar flags. Ordinary LexemeSpec/LexerSpec Clone immediately
uses the same constructor; the class memo uses derivre's existing owning source
map and retained hasher, without a new storage or lexer engine. Late failures keep
completed lexemes, builder, memo and warning siblings. No new lexemes, derivatives
or token states are compiled in this copy. The compiled grammar/parser mutable
state and actual paid source owner still must be joined before Auto/Active opens.

`Tensor::narrow_axis` declares one exact nonnegative, half-open interval while
retaining its axis. Shared neutral geometry validates the source and supplies
the default existing-index fallback. Workspace execution records the exact
StaticSlice coordinates; MLX calls the same native Slice directly. Its three
coordinate arrays stay inline through four axes and use exactly the input rank
above that, with both fixed frames and out-of-line coordinate bytes charged to
the StaticSlice source. CPU qualification still requires its known physical
representation and supported nonempty Slice geometry; shape alone does not
qualify a generic Index. Architecture readout can use this shared contract for
multiple-position LastPosition without changing model equations or capture.

Multi-position shared readout uses the neutral rank-preserving narrow_axis
contract with its declared sequence axis and exact final-position bounds.
Portable tensor implementations retain the ordinary index fallback. The MLX
realization and workspace trace preserve the exact Slice coordinates and their
source accounting; selection policy remains in architectures.

Parallel capture scalar facts are indexed by the immutable admitted selection,
not shared across unrelated observation points. Each actual hook fills its paid
cell; the completed span report copies those facts into a paid immutable row.
An issued operation merges only its own reports, checking scalar consistency
within each selection across prefill fragments. Its native receipt source owns
the resulting paid table, so skipped hooks stay absent and mixed physical
precisions at different declared points never inherit one another's source.

Compiled grammar source copies now compose the retained lexer declaration with
actual symbol/rule indices, RHS parameter expressions, nullable/rule conditions,
capture/stop metadata and nested-grammar references. Parameter-condition copying
uses the same ordinary constructor and actual boxed topology; no predicate is
reinterpreted and no grammar rule is recompiled. A failed symbol allocation keeps
completed lexer/symbol/condition prefixes. This supplies an exact immutable source
constructor, not a parser admission claim: production recipes must still provide
its independent immutable source after ordinary compiler retirement, and mutable parser/DFA
storage and callback/controller custody remain required joins.

Saved parallel capture quotation lends the copied checkpoint, causal selection
and exact cached placement into the same observed partition span driver and
populated sampler used by ordinary resume. The shared capture observer restores
its absolute prediction frontier and inherited usage; it receives newly paid
per-selection source cells and records the existing native capture populations.
The copied source, retained communicator and separately admitted copy/request
roles remain distinct. Restore or fork does not reset observation, receipt or
copy spending, and absent native hook/source producers remain explicit refusals.

The CPU static SliceUpdate source generalizes the existing singleton overwrite
by exact rank, source elements and replacement elements. For nonempty partial
unit-stride F32 rectangles at ranks one through four, native inspection requires
complete row sources, matching physical precision, exact coordinates and the
ordinary `SliceUpdate::None` primitive. The same full vector copy and shaped
overwrite retain four weak aliases and two tasks, with one output allocation.
Only the shaped task needs collapse/iterator workspace; rank-three work includes
its two zero-prefix iterator controls. Copy loops, output values, source
ownership and completion are unchanged. Whole replacement remains its separate
identity branch, and this source conveys no half conversion or reduction mode.

Immutable declaration registration uses a distinct retained-destination receipt.
AST traversal/partial stacks are real constructor peaks but retire before success;
lexeme, lexer and compiled-grammar constructors propagate that distinction. Only
verified completed destination buffers enter persistent source/residency capacity.
Full constructor buffers and controls remain required for fresh original copies.

CPU partial static activation traces now consume the same qualified SliceUpdate
source as the native ordinary worker. They retain the original tensor, exact
selected coordinates, replacement tensor and complete new output through the
same capture loan and final completion. F32 scalar arithmetic on selected row
gaps uses the existing generic binary worker and its original collapse/iterator
source, with no inserted copy or alternate arithmetic. The selected last axis
must remain contiguous and wider than one; physical precision and native backing
validation remain mandatory. Rank-three batched rectangles and ordinary sampler
partial Scale share this path. Before/after Preview and Summary evidence keep
the selected region and cumulative capture/copy obligations; unknown precision,
unsupported strides and mismatched source declarations remain typed refusals.

The CPU-target/GPU-assistant public observation fixture uses the same retained
placement, model artifacts and greedy settings as the validated reverse-placement
generation fixture. It passes configured resources into the existing public
capture driver, not another scheduler. Selected TokenScores and TopCandidates
are compared with each role's nonzero raw row through cached decode. Ordered
partial Scale requests use the existing controlled setup callback in ordinary,
managed and controlled modes; pre/post Preview and Summary evidence is checked
against a host coordinate oracle. Source models are dropped before escaped
record inspection. These checks remain pending until the linked native runs
establish public parity; lower-level CPU source checks alone do not establish it.


Partition session preparation now asks the selected neutral strategy for its
ordinary immutable observation source. The direct tensor-parallel adapter binds
the actual LayerwiseRuntime source and retains it through the existing session
publication and saved-state source owners. A prepared observation token is lent
through the same partition pass to the existing borrowed parallel hook; the
partition scheduler, communication roles, output publication, and completion
remain shared. Executors without that exact producer retain an absent source.
This source authenticates paths only: global producer ownership, scalar layout,
capture receipt storage, and transport admission remain independent requirements.

Neutral shared-controller accounting also supports independently constructed
immutable declarations. A trusted composition producer reports only its verified
completed owned allocation capacity; it may retain no compiler/factory/parser/DFA
aliases or mutable execution state. The closed typed/erased owner exposes borrowed
access only and reuses the existing per-domain attachment worker, releasing its
Arc shell and payload before accounting custody. Declaration capacity remains a
distinct inventory kind and grants neither tokenizer provenance nor execution.
Cold backend preparation acquires the same exclusion as byte sources, registers
actual capacity before publication, and keeps failed factory prefixes under that
exclusion until their typed error retires. Original request construction still
requires separately paid source constructors; cold registration is no substitute.


The facade now retains an independent immutable compiled grammar declaration
alongside each validated grammar recipe. The ordinary compiler exposes the same
compiled input through a narrow constructor callback, then destroys its Matcher,
ParserFactory, TokEnv, DFA and parser products as before. The declaration copy
contains only copied symbols, rules, conditions and lexer/regex configuration;
it has no aliases of those ordinary execution products. A source-copy failure
remains distinct from a grammar-validation failure, so resource failures do not
trigger the schema-syntax fallback.

Before registration, the independent declaration retains the compiler's cold
preparation exclusion. `GenerationRuntimePlan::register_sources` independently
copies it under the backend's shared declaration factory, validates matching
recipe bytes, and binds the destination to the newly registered recipe identity.
Only the checked completed declaration capacity enters source/residency
accounting; constructor scratch is excluded. The registered owner retains that
shared-storage charge and no eager compiler authority. This replaces the earlier
byte-only declaration boundary; serializing and reparsing equivalent immutable
grammar data is unnecessary and does not supply execution authority.

The original grammar vocabulary constructor now first constructs its independent
compiled declaration. It reserves fixed adapter controls and the stored actual
source inspection frames before walking the historical declaration, verifies the
same worker's requirements, and reserves all destination buffers/constructor
frames before copying. Successful inputs and typed failures retain their exact
historical declaration, recipe and funding until their actual payloads retire.
The vocabulary/slicer owner therefore carries the complete immutable grammar
input into the next constructor. Mutable lexer/DFA growth, Earley parser state,
controller mask/commit/copy and semantic tool payload admission remain unfinished;
this input owner does not enable Auto/Active execution by itself.


The derivative engine's byte-alphabet construction now has one shared finite
worker, consumed by ordinary `AlphabetInfo::from_exprset` and its original
source-copy plan. The exact expression graph and root list bound the traversal
stack, visited flags, byte-set references, multiword signatures and independent
root/printer destinations. Byte-set equivalence uses fixed representatives from
the 256-byte alphabet, preserving first-seen literal order and ascending order
for the remaining equivalence classes. It does not allocate a signature hash
map or duplicate the returned root vector. Original callers must reserve its
source/child inspection frames and complete constructor requirements first.
Failures retain the independently copied expression set and actual scratch/
output prefix. Expression derivatives and mutable DFA/cache growth remain
separate consumers; an alphabet owner alone admits no parser.

Assignment state is now distinct from its u8 class value. Previously `0xff`
served both as an unassigned sentinel and as the valid 256th alphabet class,
which could reassign that byte or produce a 257th class. The shared worker keeps
all 256 literal classes distinct, including a repeated root assigned class 255.


Lexer scalar/root extraction now has an exact source plan over the existing
`LexerSpec` rows. Ordinary lexer construction immediately consumes that plan and
hands the result through the same alphabet/root/special-occurrence worker used
by original construction. The regex-vector constructor accepts that completed
input without reconstructing root policy or repeating alphabet compression;
its subsequent relevance, derivative and DFA work is unchanged and remains
separately unqualified for original execution.

The original slicer owner can now reserve and build its real lexer roots, then
reserve the existing expression-source inspection frames and the alphabet
constructor's complete population. The resulting original lexer-input owner
keeps the same CGrammar, exact historical recipe/declaration, tokenizer/trie,
slicer and metadata funding through success or actual partial failure. It owns
the constructed expression set, alpha mapping, lexical flags and root order;
it is an input to the next mutable lexer constructor, not a parser capability.


Expression mapping now has one fallible traversal shared by ordinary derivative,
relevance and expression-rewrite consumers. Its cache lookup, node/value buffer
writes, value copies, processing callback and memo publication remain distinct
operations. The ordinary adapter preserves its prior allocation sizes, cloned
values, nullable/byte-concat short-circuit policy and traversal order. A cache hit
still performs only its value copy. Storage failure propagates before the next
operation; completed memo entries and caller-owned traversal/value destinations
remain owned, and typed copy/publication failures may retain their own partial
payloads. No rollback or budget refund is inferred.

This internal fallible seam supplies no original allocation authority. The
concrete paid derivative/relevance stores must still qualify every value clone,
container growth and expression-processing allocation before parser admission;
using a fallible callback alone does not make those ordinary allocations paid.


Expression mapping's traversal/value slots now have an actual source-bound
constructor. A mutable loan of the reached expression arena supplies its finite
node count, all current child edges and maximum arity; the checked plan allocates
those exact scratch capacities. The shared traversal writes within them through
its fallible memory adapter. Callers must supply the actual value-copy, memo and
processing producers; this constructor supplies no implicit `Clone`, growing
map, derivative work or original authority for those operations.

The loan permits separately qualified processing to append expressions, while
rejecting those new nodes as roots of its captured source. A later operation
must obtain a fresh source-derived workspace. Failure retains the actual scratch
and completed source/memo mutations, marks that workspace failed, and prevents
reentry; it does not reset spending or roll back source state. This closes only
the traversal population of derivative/relevance work, with concrete expression
and memo-growth producers still required before grammar-controller admission.

The derivative node worker now shares its equations and constructor order between
ordinary evaluation and fallible prepared construction. Its interface separates
source reads, byte-suffix copies, scalar expression constructors, child-vector
simplification, and the two-branch nullable-concatenation destination. Ordinary
derivative evaluation consumes this worker immediately and retains its existing
memoization and simplifiers. A constructor refusal leaves earlier source mutations
and child destinations intact; the interface supplies no allocation permission.
Original derivative admission still requires paid arena, simplifier, memo, and
value-copy producers at these concrete boundaries.

Derivative storage now has a source-bound constructor for every existing
expression/alphabet-byte memo slot, the largest actual byte-suffix destination,
two nullable alternatives, and the shared traversal destinations. It retains an
exclusive loan of that expression owner. Byte copies and memo publication use
these finite destinations without growth; repeated hits and immediate no-match
results use the same ordinary selection worker. Newly appended expressions
cannot become roots until a new source scope is prepared. A failed arena
constructor fences the scope while retaining completed memo rows, byte scratch,
and expression mutations; it does not erase work or refund funding.

This constructor does not price or authorize expression/simplifier growth. Its
production adapter requires a separate fallible arena producer at every shared
node-construction boundary and has no ordinary fallback. Generic mapping-call
transport, arena controls, and any arena-owned child-vector growth remain part of
the enclosing original operation quote. Consequently this concrete storage
producer does not open Auto/Active controller admission on its own.

The checked hash-cons destination can now be constructed from an actual
quiescent source table. It reuses the ordinary source-copy worker, preserving
all vector IDs, the source hasher and the table's exact owning layout. Its
finite entry allowance is the source table's usable capacity; its payload
allowance is the source's initialized backing, with the largest actual source
encoding priced again as scratch. Element slots and scratch are independently
allocated and quoted before copying. No load-factor estimate or speculative
capacity stands in for the owning table layout.

The resulting owner uses the existing fixed insertion/duplicate/cancellation
worker and retains actual partial copy storage on failure. This raw container
does not validate expression references, predefined arena seeds or parser
execution. It also does not solve requests needing larger extents than the
actual source supplies; that remains an explicit destination-producer gap,
not an architectural grammar limitation or permission to grow ordinary tables.

Expression storage now has ordinary and finite variants behind the same ExprSet
read representation. The prepared source constructor copies the complete exact
metadata, Unicode map, printer, IDs and fixed hash-cons destination through the
same ordinary copy worker. It checks the actual predefined seeds, alphabet and
topological child references before accepting the source. A late metadata failure
retains the already constructed finite table and all completed metadata. The
public prepared owner exposes only immutable source access; ordinary mutable
arena growth is unavailable through that owner.

Byte, repetition, complement, lookahead and byte-concatenation constructors share
one set of equations with ordinary execution. Their checked emission validates
the same arena's children and uses the existing fixed encoding/insertion worker.
Actual consumed cost and completed earlier chunks survive a later refusal; a
duplicate remains usable when unique destinations are exhausted. Copying an
already prepared table preserves its original committed, entry and scratch
limits, so staging scratch never becomes extra committed capacity during copy.
These scalar constructors do not qualify n-ary simplification, concatenation
flattening, symbolic relevance, weight growth or whole parser/controller work.
Those producers and their operation controls remain required before original
Auto/Active admission; the shared immutable source alone supplies no execution
authority.

N-ary construction now shares one flattening, normalization, byte-set merging
and lookahead-selection worker between ordinary execution and a finite workspace
loan of a prepared expression owner. The workspace derives its input and
one-level expansion bounds from that owner's actual encoding limit, plus its
actual alphabet words. It constructs all argument, suffix, byte and lookahead
destinations before use. Ordinary temporaries retire at their former semantic
block boundaries; the prepared workspace retains its already paid storage.

Lookahead selection uses an allocation-free sort whose expression-ID tie-break
preserves the former stable key order because the incoming IDs were already
sorted. A failed constructor retains normalized arguments, populated scratch,
consumed cost and earlier arena mutations in the fenced source scope. The exact
source's optimization flag is preserved. The reached ordinary AlphabetInfo
worker already disables prefix-tree optimization for lexer execution; optimized
source requests still require their separate prefix-tree producer and are never
silently redirected to an unoptimized path. N-ary workspace construction does
not by itself qualify enclosing derivative, relevance or parser operation
controls, nor open original Auto/Active controller admission.

Concatenation now uses one shared recursive flatten/fold worker for ordinary and
finite expression storage. Byte-group appending, identity/no-match handling,
right-to-left fold order, scalar emission and consumed cost follow the same
worker; existing ordinary vector entry points delegate to it. Per-frame ordinary
owned parts retire when that frame finishes. The finite scope instead retains
its already constructed frame, part and byte destinations for reuse.

The prepared source's actual entry bound and the shared encoded-byte maximum
bound simultaneous recursive frames, iterator parts and copied bytes, including
repeated byte sources on different concat edges. No canonical-left shortcut or
resident-concat substitute is introduced. A later emission failure retains all
active nested frames, copied byte groups and previous arena results in the
fenced scope. These are conservative finite workspace extents; a larger or
more economical destination producer remains possible without changing concat
semantics. Enclosing recursive operation controls and the remaining grammar
constructors still require admission before this source can run as an original
Auto/Active controller.

Remainder construction now shares its branch equations and digit mapping between
ordinary and checked expression emission. Decimal forcing uses a fixed mapped
u32 digit buffer instead of an intermediate formatted String and copied byte
vector. Its width bound follows the actual nonzero u32 power branch, including
the ordinary wrapping build's widths; no decimal text is reinterpreted by a
second formatter. The ordinary arithmetic policy is unchanged. The checked
producer reports nonrepresentable powers as a typed source failure after the
already consumed operation cost, before committing a new expression.

The decimal buffer and local typed control census are available to the enclosing
original arena quote. General derivative arithmetic qualification and the
remaining lexer/relevance/parser state producers remain required; this scalar
constructor alone supplies no controller execution authority.


The prepared derivative scope now assembles the shared n-ary, concatenation,
scalar and remainder workers under the same mutable expression-source loan.
Its memo and traversal destinations include only the entry and encoding extents
of that actual finite arena. Valid expressions emitted by the scope can become
subsequent derivative roots; unused numeric slots, foreign IDs and plain-source
workspaces do not gain mutation authority. Ordinary derivation uses the same
node equations and keeps its existing arithmetic behavior, while the finite
consumer refuses arithmetic overflow before evaluating an invalid native
integer operation. Completed expressions, memo entries, cost and temporary
prefixes remain owned after refusal, and the scope cannot be reused.

N-ary and concatenation geometry receipts now prepare their existing buffer
workers independently of a temporary call borrow, so the derivative scope can
retain both beside its expression loan. These receipts are sizes, not source
or execution authority. No ordinary simplifier fallback is installed. The
constructor quote includes the actual buffers and constructor frames; enclosing
recursive operation frames, mutable DFA/relevance state and Earley parser
construction remain required before original Auto/Active controller admission.
The source-template arena still has only its inspected table/word capacity;
a larger independently priced expression-destination producer is separate
unfinished work, not a grammar-family limitation.


Symbolic relevance now evaluates each derivative node through one fallible
construction worker, immediately used by the ordinary relevance cache. It
preserves selector order, Cartesian-product order, nullable concatenation,
normalization points and expression cost. A reached-node list plan borrows the
actual immutable child lists, checks their source references, and prices the
direct result/intermediate list capacities before creating them. Its once-only
list bank preserves partial constructor allocations on failure and cannot grow
or retry an exhausted issue. Cartesian products use checked products of those
actual child lengths rather than treating parser fuel or arena-node count as
a byte bound. The list bank itself grants no expression or parser authority.

The byte-selector complement, union, intersection and subtraction operations
now share ordinary and prepared equation workers. Prepared scratch contains
exactly the eight words needed by the complete u8 selector domain, with the
source's actual alphabet and word count checked before mutation. Ordinary
large-alphabet behavior remains on its ordinary scratch destination. Existing
tail-bit treatment, same-source shortcuts, source cost and final encoding are
retained. Original symbolic memo/value copying, grouping and disjoint scratch,
relevance traversal and the enclosing controller's operation admission remain
required; this packet opens no Auto/Active controller gate.


Prepared symbolic simplification now consumes the same stable first-occurrence
grouping and two-pass worker as ordinary relevance. One scope retains the actual
mutable expression loan, a dense index bounded by that owner's finite entry
extent, group vectors derived from the reached input count and encoding width,
and one result vector. The second pass recycles the completed input vector;
it does not create a hidden result allocation. The shared n-ary workspace can
now price the reached group input count while its final expression encoder
keeps the same fixed word/entry/encoding limits. Derivative normalization uses
the same in-place normalized-prefix handoff.

First-pass regex unions and second-pass byte-selector unions consume those
actual prepared workers. Success preserves ordering and source cost; refusal
preserves emitted expressions, normalized groups and cost, and fences the
failed scope. An escaped completed list retains its own vector while the scope
retains its remaining buffers and expression source. These are local constructor
and buffer requirements; the original symbolic mapping/memo, disjoint-set
worker, relevance walk and full controller admission remain separate work.


The disjoint-selector loop now has one ordinary/prepared equation worker.
Its prepared consumer retains the actual expression owner, the same paid
n-ary union worker and byte-set intersection/subtraction worker, a finite
argument vector, and a result vector bounded by the complete stored selector
bit domain. Nonempty disjoint sets each consume at least one such bit; final
word padding is included because ordinary byte-set complements preserve it.
The bound is independent of parser fuel and does not replace the existing
overlap/split order with byte-by-byte enumeration.

Rows are updated in the original order. A failed later constructor leaves
previous row splits, actual expression mutations, normalized union arguments
and spending in the same source scope. Successful output takes the actual
result vector, and the scope is single-use on both success and failure. This
closes the local disjoint consumer; the symbolic value/memo owner, relevance
walk and original controller integration still require their own paid joins.


The finite expression source and derivative memo now have one move-only owning
machine. Its plan owns the prepared ExprSet before inspection, creates the same
scoped destinations, then keeps their storage parts beside that exact source.
Each call reborrows the retained fields; no self-reference, source substitution,
ordinary arena alias or fresh constructor fallback is needed. The derivative
memo survives calls and newly emitted roots retain the same finite arena IDs.

Constructor failure owns its actual destination prefix before the expression
source. Operation failure leaves the source, memo, cost and count in the machine
and fences reuse. If an unwind loses local parts, the diagnostic count becomes
unavailable rather than reporting a refunded zero. The new raw owner is a
mechanism/source boundary; original lexer/parser/controller admission still
requires the remaining symbolic memo, relevance, DFA and callback consumers.


The owning expression machine now also retains the symbolic traversal parts
and memo values. It uses the same symbolic-node worker and the actual prepared
scalar, n-ary, concatenation, grouping and disjoint consumers. Memo slots and
traversal shells are constructed from the same finite expression owner's entry
and encoding extents. Each reached node/group destination and each variable
value/selector copy is inspected and reserved through an explicit host-funding
callback before allocation; the facade's existing reserve_metadata mechanism
can supply that callback. There is no default allowance or alternate evaluator.

A memo hit still reserves and constructs its real independent output vector.
Completed memo entries and source mutations remain in the machine if a later
reservation or constructor fails. The common failure fence covers both scalar
and symbolic derivative calls, while counters and expression cost retain the
completed/attempted prefix. The original controller integration must retain
its enclosing H/source with these raw expression-ID results and errors. The
relevance walk, mutable DFA/Earley state, callback/copy/commit paths and final
Auto/Active admission remain to be joined; this mechanism is not that admission.


The PP executor uses the same layered observation binding producer as the
replicated and direct-TP runtimes. Its source records global architecture
addresses; the existing local address table selects borrowed unit hooks while
parameter mutation invalidates their generation. Cold PP quotation and native
execution consume the same explicit token and ordinary partition worker,
including the separate neural and control-only contexts. This does not certify
remote scalar facts or receipt transport: those remain required before a
partition capture record can be admitted or delivered.


Prepared partition capture resolves each scheduled row's physical floating
representation from its retained complete producer. Destinations and logical
source-frame credits are reserved before local preparation agreement. A fixed
canonical frame then authenticates the producer, receipt, selection, skip
decision, and spent ledger; every present replica witness must match. Only
then is the already-paid decoder bound to that dtype and the existing final
coordination vote performed. Missing producer facts remain a typed refusal;
geometry, family, and nonproducer absence never invent a floating format.
Native frames use the existing retained capture transport and child role.


Complete intermediate partition captures no longer require every rank to
execute the hook. The retained architecture table selects the complete producer
and explicitly identifies ranks absent from that invocation. Their cold prefill
progress uses the same admitted fragment worker without constructing a tensor
or inventing its scalar type; the prepared source exchange resolves the actual
producer dtype before runtime observation. Existing raw and Summary transform
sources, local address bindings, receipt resealing, and final delivery votes are
still required. Sharded, additive, and sparse points keep their distinct source
requirements rather than inheriting this complete-producer path.


Pipeline-wave execution names the same short observation-control lifetime as
its retained pass. The neutral method and concrete executors carry the existing
state-outlives-control requirement explicitly; neither prepared inputs nor the
state gain a static lifetime or a second observation owner.


CPU scalar multiplication and exact GELU retain the ordinary eager F32 scalar
promotion for F16/BF16 inputs. Their source plans name the actual half-to-F32
casts before arithmetic; GELU casts the original input independently before its
initial division and later multiplication. Erf and subsequent arithmetic use the
existing F32 workers, and the output representation is F32. Input storage keeps
its original half representation. Exact cast, scalar, temporary and output
populations use the shared CPU recorder; no whole-model conversion or output
rounding is introduced. Mixed-parameter dense/RMS and the remaining half model
consumers still need their own source joins before full half execution is claimed.


The finite expression machine now owns a weight/attribute cache and its exact
traversal scratch beside the same derivative and symbolic source. Ordinary
relevance and prepared queries execute one shared child traversal and the same
weight equations, including the large-DAG depth threshold and inherited repeat
flag. Ordinary cache padding is preserved as historical source data. Prepared
cache slots also cover the existing finite arena's future entries; operation
queries do not grow vectors or borrow an ordinary mutable arena.

The fixed cache is seeded under constructor funding. Its work stack derives
from that arena's entry and encoded-child limits, rather than a default fuel
allowance. Checked arithmetic or destination failure retains completed cache
entries and the exact source, and fences the whole owning machine. These raw
weight queries close the storage prerequisite for shared relevance sorting;
relevance traversal, DFA/parser state, and controller startup/copy/commit still
need their actual consumers before Auto/Active admission can be opened.


Routed partition observation now borrows the actual LayerwiseRuntime path
binding into its invocation and selected provider equation. The parallel
layerwise worker lends its existing traversal hook directly to that equation,
so prepared execution creates no ordinary path tables or shared observer shell.
The retained selection keeps its original provider, acquisition, dependency and
abort behavior. This traversal source does not authorize a dense cold quote for
a routed or composite constructor; their exact source variants remain required.


CPU dense source selection preserves the ordinary order of floating promotion:
matrix operands convert independently after any weight transpose and before
flattening; optional bias promotes only the completed matrix result. Each real
conversion retains its input/parameter and contributes its own full source extent
to the graph and physical envelope. The final output's dtype cannot select a
different matrix worker. Mixed F16/BF16/F32 operands that promote to F32 use the
retained F32 worker; same-F16 Matmul remains unqualified pending its native source.

Learned CPU RMS likewise converts its gain to the ordinary promoted dtype and
its input to F32 before the existing reduction. Constructed modules return that
promoted result. The tensor adapter retains its explicit final conversion back
to input dtype, including half rounding. Only equal half input/gain pairs take
the existing extra GPU-probe cast; mixed pairs do not inherit that population.
Weightless half RMS and unqualified native same-F16 fallback controls remain
explicit source refusals. No conversion changes source identity or stream.


Composite partition passes now bind the actual prepared composite architecture's
observation path owner. Group input/output hooks, dependency-only auxiliary
groups and local unit boundaries borrow that table through the same execution
loop. Removing the prepared input preserves the independent observation loan;
mutable parameter access invalidates its generation. Provider/media controls,
transport, local state addressing and the cold constructor source remain their
existing separate obligations.


The CPU Gather source descriptor includes the existing native Float16 copy
dispatch, with the same exact one-index geometry, signed-stride inspection,
iterator storage and retained task/weak-view population. Its byte extents use
the actual two-byte element size; no F32 table conversion occurs. Strict F16
embedding lookup consumes that source through the existing validation, safe-index
mask, Gather and Squeeze worker. Output representation remains F16 and the
validation root, five eager seeds and original source/account custody are
unchanged. This producer alone does not establish full half model admission.


CPU pointwise source selection also consumes exact stored floating parameter
representations. The existing binary promotion rule determines its result, and
each differing operand contributes its own real cast before broadcast. A stored
half layer scalar therefore converts only one element to F32 before the ordinary
full hidden-state multiplication. A half full operand converts its own extent;
these allocations remain distinct from the output and from an eager scalar seed.
The shared source recorder retains each input and existing CPU cast/binary task,
with no new native worker or altered arithmetic. Missing representation and
unsupported same-F16 output paths still refuse.

The existing Gemma target trace separately runs BF16 and F16 checkpoint parameter
representations through the same two-layer family, including ordinary prefill
chunks and multiple cached positions. It reports exact missing operations and
their input facts for the accumulated source implementation. This cold fixture
does not certify checkpoint provenance, native numerics, or public admission.


Ordinary relevance now invokes a shared DFS after its entry optimizations. The
finite expression machine consumes that same walk with its existing symbolic
and weight workers. Its persistent result cache covers exactly the retained
arena's entry slots. Each invocation reserves real visited/stack/root storage;
each reached child list reserves its actual filtered length. The stack bound is
one dummy root plus at most one frame per visited arena entry. Failed searches
retain their unfinished lists and existing cache/source prefix with the owner.

Weight memo entries are prepared before the infallible standard sort comparator;
both ordinary and prepared paths then sort by the same weight/expression-ID key.
The visited-set behavior, ancestor publication, expression cost and fuel check
order are shared. The raw prepared DFS is deliberately not full controller
admission: the existing concat/repeat entry optimizations, containment, mutable
DFA/parser state and startup/copy/commit consumers still require their joins.


The partitioned common decoder now supplies the same causal prefill-row
declarations as its ordinary model, from the retained configuration and actual
block factory fact. The declaration preserves global unit identities; separate
partition placement and prepared transport still select local hooks and remote
receipt delivery. No row equivalence is inferred from a capture path or rank.

External speculative lanes retain the loaded target session's intervention
declaration before the target and assistant are lent to the shared driver. Each
lane pays the declaration's existing identity-copy controls from its own metadata
funding, then attaches it while binding the external numerical request. The shared
binding checks the exact target origin, and every intervention still validates
the admitted plan against that retained declaration. This also applies to CPU
targets and controlled advancement; external source preparation grants no
replacement intervention authority.

CPU F16 lookup uses the existing Gather and Squeeze workers. The Squeeze source
accepts the canonical F16 input already validated by the shared alias geometry
inspector. Its exact singleton axes, output shape, unchanged dtype and backing
span checks remain mandatory; the worker aliases the existing data and adds no
backing birth or dtype conversion. Native coverage validates both descriptors
before executing the complete take, including signed-zero/NaN bits and escaped
source custody.


The full prepared non-emptiness entry now consumes the same ordinary concat
filtering, intersecting-repeat probes and DFS. Explicit repeat continuations
replace recursive entry calls in both paths. Their finite prepared stack comes
from the actual arena-entry bound; filtered lists reserve their reached length.
The existing concat frame/fold worker consumes those expression-only lists, and
the existing n-ary worker constructs each repeat-child intersection.

Nested probes retain the original top-level expression-cost ceiling. The
ordinary recoverable fuel failure retires only its temporary search buffers
before the enclosing repeat resumes; completed expression/memo work and host
spending remain intact. Allocation, source and equation failures never take
that recovery path. The owning source remains required across every success or
failure. Containment and the actual regex-vector DFA/state/controller handoff
remain separate unfinished callers; no Auto/Active admission is claimed here.

The parameterized public half CPU-target fixture writes real BF16 or F16
SafeTensors payloads for every floating target parameter, preserving nonzero
values and exact checkpoint shapes. Its Metal assistant uses the existing F32
checkpoint. Each dtype uses the same ordinary, managed and controlled external
driver in fresh processes, compares committed IDs/text, and requires at least
two verification rounds. Loaded models and original sources leave scope before
escaped output checks. This fixture is staged coverage, not a support claim: the
full dtype-specific source trace and public native run must both pass.


The architecture-owned routed partition constructor now retains one immutable
resident provider table containing the selected bank equations, per-unit route
cardinality and partition observation coordinates. Ordinary provider erasure
retains aliases to that exact table. The neutral routed-bank dispatcher can lend
the same table without copying map nodes or plans; this loan exists only when the
provider implements the existing contract through an immutable reference. Stateful
addressable providers retain their existing mutable path. Resident owned and
borrowed providers call the same grouped workers, with the new forwarding control
frames charged to checked construction metadata. This source custody is a
prerequisite for routed partition cold quotation; it does not qualify the dense
partition source, expert exchange, or an absent native capture producer.


Routed partition execution handoffs retain their immutable realization table,
collective-wave schedule and neutral execution plan once. Rebinding a local or
pipeline executor lends those exact owners through the existing constructors,
rather than cloning their map nodes and vectors during checked quotation. The
ordinary owned constructors delegate to the same workers; expert coordinate
validation compares the retained entries directly without allocating a temporary
set. This metadata sharing grants no mutable bank, native transport or completion
authority.


Resident routed tables are created exactly once during the existing routed or
composite bank constructor's preparation. Subsequent source loans only read the
retained owner and return `ResidentSourceUnavailable` when it is absent; there is
no lazy allocation or concurrent initialization on a quote path. The actual shared
`construct_partition_bank_providers` WithLayer branch consumes aliases of this
constructor-owned table. Independent-cache banks keep their separate mutable
mechanism construction and do not receive a resident source.

The original grammar expression owner now consumes the ordinary conservative
prefix-containment worker, including its forced-byte rewind, ordered branch
search, repeat bounds, exception lengths and suffix handling. Ordinary and
prepared paths share scalar And construction, concatenation iteration and an
iterative simple-length worker. The prepared branch destination counts then
fills the same immutable source traversal, reserves each reached pair-cache
entry before publication, and retains source, memo and accepted funding through
partial failure. Only expression-fuel exhaustion is recoverable for the existing
subsumption caller; its requested false-cache behavior is preserved. Allocation,
source and equation failures fence the owner. This supplies the containment
mechanism; grammar DFA state construction and controller admission still require
their own exact source and destination joins.

CPU Softmax source inspection selects the exact floating dtype and precision.
The existing precise F16 and BF16 workers retain F32 accumulation, the shared SIMD
exponential polynomial, and half output storage. Their task and local controls
are measured from those actual template instantiations; optional contiguous-copy
Data, descriptors and worker storage reuse the original copy source. The native
descriptor requires the actual precise primitive, unchanged dtype/shape and
completed nonempty rank-two through rank-five input geometry. Nonprecise half
Softmax remains a separate unqualified worker.

The typed query is a source fact only. It does not qualify an attention equation
or change the selected F32 tiled, BF16 or F16 Matmul mechanism. The focused native
cases compare ordinary and admitted half outputs bit-for-bit, scalar and SIMD
tail rows against an independent scalar reference, and escaped backing retirement.

The CPU BF16 plain-Matmul source covers the existing row worker through rank
five, requiring inline Shape/Strides capacity and checked signed batch, matrix
and backing-span products. It shares the actual zero/one/two General-copy source
with the selected F32 tiled path: each required copy contributes its exact
backing, descriptors, cleanup and worker terms, and all copies share the one
existing retained temporary batch. Native inspection counts copies from each
actual matrix interior rather than the output shape. The row worker remains
selected only for the existing plain BF16 Matmul primitive and retained kernel
choices; AddMM, opaque BLAS and different dtypes gain no authority.

This source extension precedes the complete half-attention consumer join. The
focused rank-five native case exercises both copied operands, exact BF16 row
rounding, independent batch coordinates and escaped output retirement. Mixed
operand casts remain separate actual conversion populations.

The CPU matrix contract also retains `Float32AndFloat16Tiles`, an immutable
model-independent choice of the bundled SIMD worker for F32 and F16 inputs with
F32 accumulation. F16 uses the same 16-by-16 tiles, partial-lane order and final
half conversion as `simd_fp16.cpp`; it does not call BNNS. The native build also
reports whether its ordinary F16 platform branch is already that exact worker
(non-Accelerate builds). That concrete fact can qualify F16 under the existing
platform/F32-only selector without asserting any bound for platform F32 BLAS.
Accelerate builds require the explicit combined choice for source-qualified F16.

The retained selection is copied through the same paid stream owner and native
primitive. Its Matmul source covers nonempty normalized ranks two through five,
checked signed indexing, and the actual zero, one or two ordinary General copies
for matrix interiors; it preserves separate F32 tile, F16 tile and BF16 row task
layouts, completion controls and backing births. Dense projection consumes the
actual matrix promotion before any subsequent bias cast. AddMM and full half
attention admission remain separate source joins; these matrix facts alone do
not admit a model or bypass an input/source guard.

The original grammar source now constructs the actual lexical root and initial
DFA state owner under its retained funding. Ordinary and prepared constructors
share root non-emptiness/fuel accounting, lazy and repeat classification, selected
root ordering, nullable/lowest-match descriptors and next-byte analysis. The
prepared owner uses independent expression mechanisms, source-layout intern
storage, paid masks and reached transition/descriptor destinations; it preserves
the DEAD/MISSING payloads and IDs without cloning an ordinary execution object.
The raw empty intern-table plan derives its table allocation and committed-word
limits from the retained source, with separately quoted encoding scratch; it
supplies no semantic IDs. Larger destination growth, transition-driven state
construction and complete parser/controller admission remain separate required
joins. A failed constructor owns every allocated prefix before its grammar/H
source; a failed state publication fences further work and retains the inserted
state and any incomplete descriptor until the actual owner retires.


Managed partition capture completes each reached local replica dependency before
its peer transforms the selected producer's tensor. The funded observer forwards
the ordinary replica hook and spends one receiver source attempt per coordinated
selection/epoch; absent PP ranks and skipped/empty fragments add no local work.
The backend retains that input in the same admitted model recovery owner and uses
its authenticated nested completion, with no new transform or host receipt.
Cold observation traces the same pre-publication replica hook, its one retained
root and exact completion/control census. Post-publication remote progression is
reserved for ranks without a local source, so a replica does not advance twice.


Resident routed direct partitions retain their checked bank plans once during
ordinary architecture construction. Both native provider handles and cold
workspace execution borrow that same immutable table; repeated constructor
handoffs reuse its canonical source rather than lazily rebuilding a quote table.
The common decoder constructor installs the routed source only after exact
selection, checkpoint, local state, TP and bank-residency validation. Workspace
execution uses the existing prepared routed/provider traversal, retained paths,
parameter loan, and shared output publication worker. Actual provider phase
agreements carry the same explicit parallel/control context as the enclosing
invocation. This join covers resident-bank local TP constructors; routed PP/EP,
other architecture constructors and mutable addressable-bank cold sources still
require their corresponding source/consumer joins.

CPU SDPA now quotes the shared fallback from the actual Q/K/V promotion, including
F16 and BF16 precise Softmax and the corresponding selected matrix source. The
scale scalar stays in the promoted input dtype, as in the ordinary native worker;
there is no implicit conversion of the whole attention equation to F32. Mixed
inputs retain each real AsType source and its input extent. A converted strided
value becomes a contiguous cast result; an unchanged strided value retains its
actual matrix-interior copy source.

The optional Boolean-mask path uses the same Select worker over stored/broadcast
F32, F16 or BF16 values. Its exact dtype, readable spans, collapse storage and
prefix iterator controls are qualified through the existing CPU bank. This does
not admit additive masks, causal aranges inside SDPA, sinks, softcaps or foreign
layout variants: those retain their existing independent source requirements.
Shared capture/completion and ordinary/controlled drivers are unchanged.

Prepared lexical vectors now consume the shared ordinary transition and
subsumption loops. Each uncached edge reserves a candidate from the actual
predecessor-state width, then calls the existing paid derivative/relevance
mechanisms and the same descriptor/publication worker. Memo hits preserve IDs;
actual expression cost reduces the same fuel allowance. Only containment fuel
refusal is recoverable during subsumption; source, funding, expression and state
capacity failures retain their prefixes and stop the owner. Facade operation
errors keep the funding account even when they escape after the lexical owner
retires. Complete lexer/parser construction, copy and controller startup remain
required; no Auto/Active admission is enabled by these lexical mechanisms.


CPU and Metal parallel quotation retain the actual model execution mechanism
through direct admission, saved-state quotation and numerical collective/pipeline
children. The shared collective census consumes exact native occurrences; CPU
model workers, native transport workers and completed child stages keep distinct
Graph, Record and backing populations. CPU quotation does not borrow GPU kernel
authority. Each native child replays the same numerical equations using its
retained stream implementation and compares against the prepared capacity before
submission. Frame decode quotes both header and payload output roots. This
implementation still requires focused CPU parallel/native validation; missing
individual CPU operation sources remain typed unknown bounds until implemented.

The explicit native distributed constructor can now select CPU or GPU streams
at device index zero. Its stream/mechanism selection is shared with the
execution-plan factory, so CPU parallel loading and CPU external assistants use
the same cold choice and actual source owners. Existing default native
distributed construction continues to select GPU.

The same lexical descriptor worker now supplies next-byte, hidden/lookahead
length and restricted-state queries to ordinary and prepared vectors. Prepared
queries use actual interned state rows and source roots, reserve newly reached
next-byte cache slots and candidate storage before construction, and retain
failed state through the same operation fence. The facade forwards these through
the existing grammar funding/error owner. These are the actual queries required
by lexer warm-up and large-lexeme precomputation; the enclosing lexer/parser
startup remains a separate required consumer.


The completed routed decoder constructor also retains its exact pipeline unit
addresses and local state realization beside the immutable provider table. Its
workspace quote passes the ordinary provider-backed unit strategy to the same
pipeline executor and span driver as dense construction, preserving prepared
observation paths, boundary transport, output publication and the independent
control context. Quotes borrow the table and plan; they cannot initialize them.
Tensor-only routed pipelines bind the existing architecture-derived inactive
sum/gather schedule to the actual native group participation fact, then lend that
same sealed schedule to the cold quote. Canonical source publication retains the
same schedule across repeated constructor preparation. This source currently
requires resident bank ownership without expert exchange; expert-parallel row
movement and mutable addressable-bank sources remain implementation work and
receive no new native admission from this handoff.

CPU boundary byte reinterpretation consumes the existing closed byte-view dtype
and shape relation. Its native View source validates the actual destination,
complete input span and exact alias/copy predicate, then enters the shared CPU
copy bank. The copying branch adds one actual General-copy temporary, with its
own descriptor, Data and backing inside the same Eval/cleanup occurrence; the
alias branch adds none. Neither branch performs a numerical cast.

Cold integer layouts carry no invented floating precision or row-order evidence.
Where their actual layout is not proved, the quote reserves the View worker's
possible copy. Native inspection still chooses the actual branch. A widening
View produces row-major storage either by requiring its ordinary row alias or
by its actual contiguous temporary; same-width aliases never establish new row
order. Byte framing's remaining concatenation, range and packing equations keep
their independent sources and are not admitted by this descriptor alone.


The routed pipeline handoff exposes its exact provider-only unit strategy
separately from its expert-exchange strategy. Both call the same ordinary local
provider worker. A checked workspace quote therefore needs only the grouped
operators and failure agreement that this branch reaches; it does not claim
variable all-to-all or routed row movement support to satisfy unused generic
bounds. The retained handoff rejects a local borrow of an expert-exchange plan.


The original grammar lexer now consumes its paid owning regex vector through
ordinary Lexer's shared first-byte warm-up and greedy, lazy, special-token,
forced-end and next-byte decisions. Its finite selection and first-byte masks
are reserved before construction, and a failed warm-up keeps the actual vector
and every reached mask. The facade keeps the same independently copied grammar,
vocabulary, slicer and funding after those mutable destinations; it does not
clone a second LexerSpec or inherit an ordinary parser. Escaped operation errors
retain their funding, and failed mutable owners cannot resume spending. This
closes lexer construction/advancement only: prepared trie precompute, Earley
parser state, and source-qualified growth beyond historical expression/intern
capacity remain concrete producer work before Auto/Active controller admission.


Dense CPU vocabulary-parallel lookup shares the strict lookup's global token
validation, local parameter gather and typed source accounting. It separately
quotes the actual local-ID subtraction, scalar-zero integer selection, expanded
ownership mask and dtype-preserving zero/selection output. Negative sentinel
policy adds its real equality/or validation work and scalar source; it never
permits arbitrary out-of-vocabulary IDs. The rank Sum remains a separate retained
collective occurrence. F16 Full and broadcast I32 Select require their actual
native source companions before their cold plans can become complete.

The shared boundary byte worker preserves header/payload slice coordinates in both native and workspace execution. Its CPU source joins U8 reshape (actual alias or one General copy), two-input concatenation, exact unit-stride Slice, and the existing U8 Add with one scalar broadcast for misaligned payloads. The eager zero byte has a closed `scalar_u8` declaration; generic initialization is not inferred as that source. Integer layouts do not invent floating precision or row-order evidence. Each actual native descriptor still validates dtype, dimensions, strides and backing; the common recorder, completion and selected per-side source remain responsible for admission.


Prepared lexer precomputation now consumes the original vocabulary's exact trie
through ordinary Lexer's shared TokTrie walker and fixed-depth stack/mask
constructor. Its callback uses the same paid derivative and lexical decision
worker; source inspection, callback frames and local destinations are reserved
before execution. A typed callback failure stops further lexical calls while
the trie balances the stack, and the error owns completed stack/mask storage
before the facade's retained funding. Ordinary DFA error downcasts and completion
checks are preserved. Parser large-lexeme scheduling and Earley row/scratch
construction remain the next callers; this does not grant controller admission.

The CPU shard lookup's existing native producers also accept exact F16 scalar Full and I32 stored/broadcast Select. F16 Full retains its actual one-element source and ordinary scalar copy; this does not add half per-row Full. I32 Select uses the same templated task, dtype-sized scalar controls, four-stride collapse and prefix iterators as the other exact typed broadcast sources. Full/Select validate the actual input dimensions, item sizes, nonnegative strides and backing before entry. The backend lookup planner retains responsibility for composing the real zero, Boolean condition, local indexes and final value mask.

Managed raw capture now publishes the completion state of every descriptor retained
by its actual selection invocation. The shared Full/Slice/Preview/half-conversion
worker first completes its existing final nested event, then validates the retained
source and intermediate descriptors through that same original observer. This
removes completed matching events before later pure backing inventory queries; it
never evaluates a missing descriptor or treats a foreign/pending event as complete.
