The borrowed iteration and refusal controls are included in the original capture
census, and all selected roots remain with the existing recovery owner on failure.


ParserState startup and the original lexer now share the actual large-lexeme
precompute schedule: the same enabled flag, remaining initial fuel, source row
order and weight threshold select calls to the same trie walker. Each original
selected mask is paid before creation and remains attached to the lexical owner
if precomputation fails. Ordinary timing/error context stays at its existing
parser boundary. This join consumes the retained original vocabulary, rather
than accepting a replacement trie or treating precompute limits as an execution
permit; Earley scratch/row construction remains separate pending work.

Composite partition preparation now retains its complete executor structure before
backend binding: local unit addresses, route schemas, group transport kinds,
publication ownership, and routed wave/provider plans. Ordinary execution and
the checked workspace adapter can borrow the same immutable tables through the
architecture-owned plan; repeated binding clones only source handles and does not
reconstruct maps or rerun semantic planning. This constructor handoff alone does
not qualify a composite native workspace or data-dependent expert movement. Those
consumers must still supply the exact parameter/provider source, observer, selected
transport recipe, and admitted metadata before execution.

Logical paired/packed collectives use the same ordinary zero constructor with a closed dtype-specific cold declaration. Its CPU plan counts one eager typed zero, the actual rank-dependent Broadcast, one scalar Full, and both seed/output storage. Generic initialization remains unqualified. Packed member extraction now exposes its actual unit-stride leading-axis slice and reshape in both Native and Workspace adapters; the existing static-slice caller source covers the inline or rank-derived coordinate destinations. The shared peer arithmetic, placement, selected membership, completion and cumulative budgets are unchanged. N-member Stack and dtype-specific partial-update mechanisms retain their own independent source requirements.


The originally copied immutable CGrammar now resides in an exactly prepaid
shared shell, allowing actual Earley Scratch to retain that same declaration
without another deep copy. Ordinary and original constructors share Scratch
field initialization, item/parameter uniqueness and mutation, the root grammar
stack node, and start-rule prediction order. Original destinations grow only
after each reached vector/mask reservation; a failed constructor retains its
actual scratch and source. The facade keeps this seed beside the warmed lexer
and original vocabulary/funding until their real retirement. This seed remains
distinct from a Parser: initial Earley row closure, scan/commit, captures, masks
and snapshot copying still require their production joins before admission.

Partition capture evidence now matches the final payload to the exact admitted
transform: raw Full/Slice/Preview records require the paid shared tensor, while
Summary requires its decoded fixed statistics. The existing single-producer,
source identity, epoch, metadata-account, and charged-contribution checks still
precede evidence publication; other payload kinds remain unqualified here.

Saved token continuation installs an explicit empty borrowed-storage selection
before its first copied-state/sampler span. The same prepared equation observer
therefore receives a complete residual report with no excluded roots in both
resident and partitioned capture. Copied state, key, pending input and all future
equation storage remain fully priced; only the existing sealed copy proof can
credit old source storage. Completed media keeps its exact immutable B selection.
The empty selection's actual constructor and iterator are funded before creation,
and a missing selection still fails the native recorder's source requirement.

CPU ordered member stacking already uses the ordinary ExpandDims then Concatenate equations. The Concatenate source now counts the actual N input leases, N destination slice descriptors, 2N weak copy owners, N existing GeneralGeneral jobs, and one output backing/cleanup. The ordinary CPU copy loop keeps its ordered prefix offset in one scalar instead of allocating a prefix-size vector; copy arithmetic and order are unchanged. Equal F32/F16/BF16 operands require no AsType primitive or extra cast backing. The native descriptor checks every actual input span and the full joined geometry before using the source, and the shared recorder retains the complete multi-input completion.


Reached original lexer warm-up now grows hash-cons payload and encoding backing
through the existing insertion/publication worker under a closed paid account.
The growth request comes from the actual complete encoding, with its original
ID, hash, staged words, semantic cost and derivative memo preserved; no derivative
is retried and no constant capacity slack is introduced. Ordinary and prepared
paths share backing initialization, while their allocation policies remain
explicit. New physical Vec allocations are charged in full before growth and
partial failures retain the actual table/backing. The funded callback's fixed
first-error slot preserves the concrete source error and source/H until its last
alias frees the shared shell. Copies do not inherit growth authority. Existing
hash-table entry capacity and other operation workspaces remain checked; larger
entry tables need their own exact allocation producer rather than a load-factor
estimate or ordinary fallback.


The composite cold partition consumer borrows the executor plan and canonical
prepared model source published by the same architecture constructor. Its dense
Gemma text TP path retains exact local geometry, parameter addresses, state
slice, and observer binding. It uses the ordinary composite partition executor
and existing checked resident or layerwise policy. Shared serial/parallel Gemma
ingress now owns the same metadata account and finite publication table; only
the selected embedding mechanism differs. Group tables, collective shapes,
borrowed dependencies and completion roots are constructed in paid destinations.

This source does not qualify ordinary-only producers: composite PP still needs
its typed boundary publisher table and receiver metadata source; media module
construction and routed EP movement need their own exact retained producers.
These are implementation gaps, not architecture restrictions. Their absence
remains a typed cold refusal before the ordinary allocating path can execute.

The original Earley seed now closes its initial chart through the same agenda as
ordinary parsing. Completion, ordered prediction, parametric conditions, nested
grammar stack entries and nullable captures use one worker; the original context
reserves each reached item, parameter, stack and capture destination before its
mutation. Failed construction retains the actual partial chart and declaration.
Initial captures have empty token bytes and retain exact source-name references
in that independently paid immutable declaration; their overwrite/list-append
selection uses the ordinary capture predicate. This closes initial agenda
inference, not row publication or the remaining byte/token parser controller.

Hash-cons entry growth consumes the pinned hashbrown 0.17.1 table's exact prospective allocator layout. The safe query and ordinary reservation share the source-owned choice between unchanged capacity, in-place tombstone rehash and a new table; the existing `TableLayout` supplies the requested bytes/alignment, including control groups. It invokes no allocator or hasher and grants no admission. The pinned external dependency keeps its upstream unsafe implementation outside workspace membership; the new quote/test modules forbid unsafe, and no portable Eredu crate gains an exception. Callers retain their actual funding and old allocation through any paid new allocation; requested layout is distinct from allocator-private overhead or excess capacity.

The original chart then publishes its actual initial Row, RowInfo and LexerState
through the same skip-selection and row-storage workers. Composition supplies the
prepared lexer from the same retained grammar-source chain. Disabling initial
skip copies the actual first-row lexical mask under funding and invokes the
existing initial-state interner again, preserving both state construction order
and partial failure custody. These are parser construction mechanisms; token
scanning, history, final controller admission and copy/commit remain distinct
required consumers.


Composite partition boundary metadata now follows the same selected typed
architecture schema as ordinary transport. Gemma's publisher geometry, role
strings, encoded vectors and decoded K/V slots are paid before allocation.
Transported publications use the existing finite publication owner and retain
its metadata custody through receiver-cache installation and resumed execution.
The receiver iteration borrows the same attention-cache ownership calculation
used by ordinary local state construction. The composite executor lends its
pass metadata to the existing boundary schema, framing and acceptance workers;
received vectors are moved through these workers without a fresh tensor copy.
This closes the dense Gemma PP metadata producer previously refused by the
composite cold consumer. Media factories and routed/EP provider movement remain
separate exact source joins.


Raw parser capture decoding now uses one token-expansion worker for ordinary
TokTrie decoding and inspected destinations. The worker preserves numeric-token
parsing, special-token stripping, absent-token decimal spelling and malformed
marker bytes, without nested decoded-token allocations. Its original plan borrows
the actual trie and raw bytes, counts the reached output with that same worker,
and constructs one exact output allocation after reservation. Output and failure
prefix custody remain with the enclosing parser/source funding owner.


The Gemma composite static media factory now borrows vision and audio configuration
members from the same immutable family source retained by initial construction.
The existing paid `SharedConfig::project` owns each child loan; no quantization
map, rotary map or channel table is copied during checked reconstruction. Static
patch, position, standardization, audio subsampling and modality/output projection
parameter names, format companions and constructor controls use the same
`ModuleMetadata` destinations as the ordinary module worker. Parameter owners
retire before their retained child configuration and its funding. Initial owned
construction validates those children; checked reconstruction requires the retained
source. This closes static media-module construction for a text-selected composite
quote without qualifying raw image/audio ingress, encoder-layer temporary storage,
or dynamic expert movement. Those remain separate actual producer joins.


The same retained composite factory also uses paid module destinations for the
vision/audio encoder layers: clipped projections, attention and feed-forward
projections, learned normalization weights, convolution parameters and exact
resident layer tables. Ordinary and checked construction share the same loops
and scalar geometry. This extends constructor metadata coverage only; raw media
admission and forward-time rotary, masks, relative embeddings and pooling
scratch still require their existing independent producer source before a
managed media request can be admitted.


Gemma media forward workers now borrow the enclosing pass metadata destination
through both ordinary and tensor-parallel execution-group calls. Vision uses the
existing prepared rotary-frequency worker, paid two-axis and pooling vectors,
and a shared immutable grid owner that keeps its account through state aliases.
Audio uses the existing generated-F32 producer for the same relative-position
and attention-mask scalar equations, with exact chunk/row/column destinations
and paid valid-frame/crop tables. Generated values are skipped by cold execution;
the shared initialization plan separately prices their fixed host payload and
the selected backend retains responsibility for native seed/copy storage. The
existing forward failure wrapper retains the account through rejected work.
These worker sources do not replace the remaining raw media-ingress admission,
plan/copy and transport sources; the raw-ingress refusal stays at that boundary.


Original Earley construction now continues through definitive byte history.
Ordinary and prepared contexts consume shared lexical routing, scan-item
selection/copy, grammar-stack return, greedy transition, single-byte follow-up,
and hidden-byte handoff workers. The prepared context owns its actual byte and
lexer stacks, rows and raw/decoded capture destinations, pricing reached storage
before mutation and each recursive handoff frame before entry. Capture names
remain source references under the immutable declaration; byte values and pending
publication are independent paid buffers. The facade forwards through the same
retained lexer/trie/source chain and retains failed chart and lexical prefixes.
This is a concrete byte/parser consumer, not complete Matcher/controller
admission: token application and max-token progression, speculative trie mask
walking, snapshot copies and final controller binding still require their shared
original consumers.

The shared MLX GELU and tanh-GELU workspace producers retain the scalar fact
established by their actual eager F32 scalar arrays. Known F16, BF16, and F32
inputs produce F32; an absent input scalar source remains unqualified. This
allows the existing architecture-selected dense projection and parallel
collective source to consume the same worker without inferring a dtype from a
family name, parameter format, or logical workspace layout. Layout contiguity
remains conservative and the existing native activation receipts are unchanged.

Processed speculative logits retain the native buffer-budget handle produced
by their completed numerical invocation. Cross-device verification consumes
that exact handle with its request account through the existing independent-copy
worker. The move creates no additional buffer, changes no sampling equation,
and does not weaken source, stream, request, or completion validation.

Gemma prepared raw-media admission now shares its ordinary part geometry and
media equations with the counted diagnostic destination. The same retained
input identity and metadata descriptors must pass the existing inspector and
admission recheck. Counted I32/bool metadata reads remain a required source;
inspectors without that exact evaluated source keep their typed refusal.
The admitted ingress consumer pays its finite part, padding, grid, and valid
length tables, and uses borrowed batch layouts to generate the canonical
vision/audio masks through the shared fixed-buffer F32 initializer. Ordinary
batch plans use the same scalar mask equations. Tensor copies and transforms
continue through the existing prepared-input, encoder, and native source
contracts, with the input funding retained through construction and failure.
This supplies the neutral raw-media producer and consumer; it does not claim a
native Gemma raw metadata source where only the text inspector is installed.

The shared uneven-axis gather workspace adapter preserves the native worker's
exact Slice coordinates for peer rows and trimmed vocabulary columns. It uses
the existing typed zero-fill declaration for padded shards. That declaration
now lives on the neutral WorkspaceTensor contract and is reused by backend
logical collectives; concrete backends still own scalar seeds, fills, copies
and completion. CPU planning therefore consumes the same precise sources as
the unchanged native gather equation, including uneven peer widths.

Original grammar constructors retain their complete failed prefixes in owning
construction errors. Mutable DFA and lexer operations now use separate typed
operation errors, because their existing source owners already retain all reached
storage after failure. Constructor-only expression payloads and optional full
lexer/vector owners therefore do not cross every parser/agenda result temporary.
This removes the measured large stack frames without heap allocation, a raised
stack limit, or loss of the original typed cause. The facade keeps the operation
error and its failed lexical source under the same retained authority.

The original Earley owner now consumes the actual TokTrie byte-mask walk. Ordinary
and original paths share speculative-history begin/end, row-cache predicates,
pending-byte and accepting-row queries, and the same lexical/agenda workers. The
forced-prefix recognizer borrows its exact input instead of allocating a second
copy. The original operation reserves the real trie control frames and token-mask
destination before traversal; callback errors remain typed, retain the partial
mask/chart and source account, and never expose a mask as a completed decision.
Successful walks restore committed bytes, captures and lexical/grammar stack
boundaries while retaining paid reusable chart/lexer storage. The facade binds
this worker only to the lexer, trie and immutable declaration already held by one
original source owner. This is the byte-compatibility stage; numeric-range/EOS
policy, token commitment and full Auto/Active controller admission remain separate
unfinished producer joins.

The CPU publication workspace description follows its actual settled contribution
and native Sum worker. Multi-rank publication retains the worker's dense output
layout through the shared architecture sampling handoff; one-member publication
preserves the actual input alias layout. These facts add no storage credit or
communication authority. Uneven gather's cold fixture uses the same selected
collective layout description before checking exact slice and padding sources.

Composite parameter representation sources use the same immutable runtime fence
and paid descriptor collector as ordinary replicated text sessions. The completed
execution lends its exact static modules and selected unit policy before cold
workspace construction; an unavailable unit source can retain only the complete
static source. Parameter identity and local shape must still match before native
floating or layout evidence reaches lookup, projection, or collective quotation.
This table supplies descriptive facts only, with no additional storage or native
submission authority.


The original grammar expression machine now extends derivative, symbolic,
weight and relevance memo destinations from the same committed expression
source after paid hash-cons growth. Each replacement vector charges its entire
actual allocation request through that source's retained funding owner before
allocation, while preserving prior memo entries and failed prefixes. Traversal
geometry comes from the committed graph; fixed detached sources acquire no
growth authority. This closes the stale constructor-time node limit reached by
the facade's JSON grammar after trie precomputation. The shared ordinary
expression equations, token history and parser state remain unchanged; complete
numeric/EOS token commitment and controller admission are still being joined.

Original Gemma media admission uses the shared ordinary validation worker over
borrowed host-slot views, and compiles its fixed decoder spans into the existing
neutral semantic records. Binding still authenticates the retained constructor,
selected blueprint, source identity, and current session. The Gemma ingress
consumer projects only fixed scalar geometry from those records; masks, encoder
execution, continuation geometry, and decoder spans use the ordinary workers
with their retained metadata destination. No source metadata requires native
evaluation or readback.

The original prepared-input owner now lends its complete B custody independently
of optional architecture-specific encoder tables. Existing table consumers still
require a checked conversion to the same owner's completed table projection.
Gemma plans retain the general B owner, original semantic source, workspace
source, and funding through success or failure. This does not add a materialize
attempt or a native submission permission.

Boolean original host slots now have a dedicated exact-sized value destination,
canonical content encoding, and copied metadata identities. The native prepared
input leaf uses the same source arena, descriptor/Data construction, page-rounded
allocator and retirement path for Boolean values, pricing the actual one-byte
scalar storage before construction. The public adapter lends the typed mask
slice directly; no cast graph, evaluation, readback or late authority is added.
Audio masks therefore retain their actual Boolean payload through the existing
original model-input compiler and Gemma ingress worker.

Sparse routed receipt validation has one shared allocation-free worker. Ordinary
callers allocate its exact row-identity scratch; a funded capture producer lends
prepaid scratch and receives typed failures without allocating diagnostics.
Duplicate detection and final ordering use in-place unstable sorting after row
identity validation. This preserves original token/slot/expert semantics and
does not infer missing route ownership, source coverage, or funding authority.


Original grammar token application now consumes the same ordinary token worker
for previously forced bytes, actual numeric-token ranges, row/token ordinals,
lexeme and grammar token limits, hidden-stop backtracking, acceptance flushes
and EOS. The original chart keeps paid token-history and filter destinations;
failed mutations retain their actual prefix. Its facade lexer stores the exact
selected ParserLimits through lexical preparation and chart handoff, and no
ordinary tokenizer or parser alias supplies original execution authority. The
shared byte-mask walker remains a separate raw compatibility result; complete
controller mask finalization, token forcing and saved-controller copy are still
being integrated before Auto/Active admission.

The original routed capture geometry now resolves the same admitted token,
route and unit axes as the ordinary capture worker through one shared resolver.
Its typed sparse wrapper retains the actual bank and source selection, validates
exact source bank extents, and exposes selected sparse row/scalar capacity without
expert-dense expansion. Borrowed-axis validation is also used by ordinary routed
receipts. These cold facts do not supply source backing or execution authority;
the funded host/native producer and distributed route receipt joins remain
separate integration work.

Original sparse capture host construction now prices fixed selected-row banks,
one shape/value destination per selected route, bounded source-chunk evidence,
and duplicate-validation scratch in the existing original run hold. The same
claim table issues each destination once. Filling never grows a buffer; row
completion moves values into the ordinary sparse receipt and its shared validator
checks coordinates and full source coverage. Failed partial destinations and
completed output aliases retain the original paying custody. The native worker,
canonical prefill fragments and distributed route-exchange joins are not claimed
complete by this host constructor.


Prepared grammar masks now apply the ordinary marker-token exclusion, numeric
range flush and EOS rules after the same paid trie traversal. Exact current
lexer state, row and pending-byte facts qualify reuse of the owner-borrowed
complete mask. Selected lexer fuel/state and Earley item limits precede each
uncached step; reached limit failures retain the actual chart and mask prefix.
The facade forwards its retained ParserLimits and trie/declaration owner.
Mask reuse does not claim an independent returned or snapshot copy. Token
forcing, saved-parser copy and Auto/Active controller admission remain the next
required joins.

Managed prepared-input text delivery uses the same facade original tokenizer,
stop-source, retained decoder/sequence and `OriginalPlainSession` as managed
plain text. `ManagedPreparedInputRequest` moves an already completed original
prompt into core admission. A neutral original-tokenizer hook checks canonical
host token slots against the retained domain before startup; MLX borrows the
actual original source and never evaluates or adopts ordinary arrays. Core still
checks exact input, selected session and current revision. Both automatic and
controlled entry points use the same advancement and saved-state workers, and
public errors retain the existing neutral `BackendFailure` chain. The ordinary
owned-event prepared-control surface retains its independent custody contract.

Loaded original-media preparation borrows the existing inference blueprint's
exact prepared source graph. It delegates semantic compilation to the same
architecture source worker and does not reopen or copy a model source. A missing
empty-state revision is initialized by the existing paid revision producer before
B binding; the actual state retains that metadata account. Frontier, idle/fence,
and original source matching remain required. This source setup performs no
neural operation and leaves the one-use completed B binder unchanged.

`LoadedModel::prepare_managed_model_input` accepts borrowed neutral host parts and
one capacity, then uses `OriginalModelInputBackend` to compile exact original
host, semantic and native sources against the loaded blueprint. The resulting
move-only `OriginalModelInput` retains source-preparation funding until handed to
`ManagedPreparedInputRequest::from_original` and then the shared core admission.
Native source/binding failures enter existing storage retirement while preserving
their original host source, payload-free B account and funded diagnostic. This is
independent of neural request permission; no ordinary input is adopted and no
processor family is selected inside the backend.


Deterministic grammar bytes now use one ordinary/prepared forcing loop and one
quick-hint/256-byte speculative uniqueness probe. The selected Earley item
limit bounds that phase, and each reached original byte/history destination
spends its existing source funding before allocation. Unique numeric token
ranges use the same fixed 13-byte maximum decimal spelling in both paths.
Original pending bytes stay borrowed from their chart through token application;
failed probes retain actual speculative and committed prefixes. The facade
invokes this worker with its retained source and limits. Saved-parser copying
and the complete Auto/Active controller owner remain the next required joins.

The native sparse collector now resolves original expert IDs by slicing the
provider group table to the actual native chunk and gathering with its existing
selection indices. The same equation applies to ordinary and exchanged rows;
validation still checks the token/selection relationship before any gather.
This removes the temporary host index vector and duplicate index upload from
the shared collector. It is a mechanism simplification, not native budget
authority; original routed capture source qualification remains separate.

The original grammar chart also invokes the ordinary noncommitting token
validation worker. Numeric-token flushes, forced raw marker spellings, EOS and
byte probes use the same order and restore boundary; a funding failure retains
its actual speculative prefix. Committed extension checks inspect the same
Earley row as the ordinary parser. These are source-owned parser operations;
Auto/Active controller publication, canonical forced-token processing and
mutable snapshot copies still require their enclosing owner joins.


Expert-route packing now borrows its immutable global-owner and owner-local
numbering from the selected architecture constructor. Native and ordinary
partition providers consume this same retained source; no backend reconstructs
expert placement. The shared packer uses fixed finite destination arrays derived
from the actual row/route cardinality and selected peer count, preserving stable
route order and zero-work peers. Its original i32 readout is borrowed directly,
without an intermediate converted ID vector.

A move-only paid packing result retains the metadata account after construction;
refused attempts retain the same cumulative reservations in their error. This
account pays only the exact host destinations and controls. It grants neither
native selection readout nor count consensus, variable exchange, or numerical
storage. Dynamic expert-parallel managed qualification remains closed until
those actual producers use their retained invocation sources; a cold quote does
not invent routing IDs or treat static ownership as a completed routing decision.

Original distributed publication uses its retained CPU Sum communication worker
even when model equations execute on Metal. Cold publication representation
therefore preserves the worker's complete contiguous output row independently
of compute-device selection. One-member aliases retain the input's actual
strides. The same actual CPU source/binding remains mandatory; this shape fact
does not grant a collective or generalize other Metal collective layouts.


Prepared media processors expose an architecture-owned retained-storage
classification. The current normalized policies consist entirely of inline
scalar fields: every plan and nested source is destructured exhaustively and
checked through a private scalar-only contract. Native enclosing-session
inventory consumes this declaration rather than treating every processor as an
unknown payload owner. The policy remains part of the enclosing metadata object;
processed host input, native input leaves, feature buffers and completion owners
retain their separate original preparation accounts. This declaration performs
no processing, allocation, readback, or source-identity substitution.

The original token-session owner now contains the actual mutable Earley chart,
committed token IDs and visible raw byte history. It shares ordinary Matcher's
validate/consume/stop driver and the exact token-span backtrack conversion.
Startup reads the original request's max-token scalar from its checked retained
recipe descriptor; no grammar JSON parsing or ordinary matcher alias supplies
execution authority. Both control-reservation and worker failures retain their
actual input or changed prefix before the lexer, immutable sources and funding
retire. Canonical forced-token mask production, mutable copy/rollback and
Auto/Active controller registration remain separate unfinished consumers.

Routed capture's fixed host payload now owns its source-token extent and receipt
identity independently of the temporary plan borrow. Ordinary scheduled writers
use that same owner, allowing subsequent prefill frame composition to retain
partial sparse rows without a self-referential plan. Real source intervals may
arrive in batch/chunk order; overlap and capacity are checked before insertion,
and the shared ordinary validator sorts and proves full logical coverage at
sealing. This does not manufacture coverage for an unvisited source interval.

Canonical forcing's token-suffix chop now walks a borrowed raw-token byte
iterator in both ordinary and original paths. The same four-token lookback,
max-token suffix, trie extension and whole-token removal workers run without a
second decoded suffix allocation. Numeric marker spelling is shared with raw
decoding and deterministic forcing. Original traversal reserves the actual
fixed iterator/recognizer frames and retains failed speculative rows under the
same chart/source owner; this supplies the chop consumer for the remaining
canonical forced-token mask join.

Canonical forced-token selection now has one ordinary/original driver: append
the actual last-token/raw forced bytes, tokenize with the retained normalized
source, retry without the prior token only when that exact encoding differs,
and run the shared stable-prefix/suffix chop. The original result borrows
ranges from its own completed encoding and byte buffer, retaining both through
consumer use or failure. Tokenizer canonicality is captured from the actual
historical normalized environment in the checked recipe descriptor. A failed
second encoding or parser chop retains its new failure beside earlier outputs;
no ordinary TokEnv, default canonicality or independent tokenization authority
is borrowed. Final mask publication and mutable snapshot/controller joins remain
required before Auto/Active original admission.

The workspace integer-scalar maximum records the same I32 operand as the native
operator. Coordinate sanitation therefore preserves integer gather indices through
padding, concatenation and views. Its native graph, scalar storage and host census
reuse the existing binary-scalar producer; mixed U32/I32 remains unqualified where
its wider promotion has no workspace representation. This declaration changes no
prepared media identity and grants no input evaluation.

Sparse RoutedUnits prefill now uses a source-bound flattened batch/token
projection alongside the existing shared chunk progression. Its private frame
slot owns one fixed destination across all provider spans, including chunks
with no selected rows. Short writers translate physical tokens through the
bound original prompt geometry, split visited source ranges at batch boundaries,
and poison dropped attempts without refunding charges. Complete sealing uses
the ordinary sparse validator. Native quotation/producer binding and distributed
sparse receipt assembly still require their exact source joins before activation.

The Metal sampler representation adapter now preserves a proven F32 input
through the existing TokenFilter, optional filter, TopK, TopP and MinP workers.
This is the scalar type already used by their mask, threshold, gather and scatter
equations, including disabled-filter aliases. Unknown/reduced input types and
output strides remain unclaimed. Distributed publication therefore feeds the
same actual F32 sampling program without losing source type during cold tracing.

A routed prefill chunk may contain several native/provider batches. Each short
writer commits only its real disjoint source intervals into the persistent
target. The chunk remains incomplete until their physical token count is exact;
the shared canonical advance resets only that chunk counter. Sparse rows and
the original host charge remain owned across every provider batch and chunk.

Partitioned expert execution lends the retained request source directly through
the existing group and wave calls, separately from neural tensor parallelism.
The routed provider consumes that lexical context when it prepares actual route
IDs. MLX uses the ordinary I32 conversion, the existing model dependency
completion and its completed signed-stride host reader; one exact source-sized
host destination is paid before construction. The shared stable route packer
then borrows those IDs and retains the same cumulative metadata account with
its output or failure. No pass stores a new context or changes TP policy, and
ordinary calls retain the original readout path. Managed dynamic expert exchange
still requires the separate retained count/exchange and cold native producer
chain; this input source alone does not qualify those operations.

The canonical forcing result now feeds the complete original token-session
mask: a forced singleton, an independently copied Earley result finalized with
all exact EOS aliases, or the stopped session's EOS mask. The finalizer is
shared with ordinary TokenParser and preserves the Earley cache separately.
Grammar no-forcing policy uses the same collected raw prefix without invoking
canonical encoding. Every failure retains forcing outputs and its actual parser
prefix; no source-only mask grants controller admission. Mutable copies/rollback
and the Auto/Active controller authentication/startup consumers remain open.

The neutral sampling trace retains each split-key row as `SelectRandomKey { index }`.
The shared workspace random-state worker and native random-state worker keep the
same first-axis Slice/Reshape operation. CPU and Metal source plans consume this
exact coordinate; generic same-shaped Index descriptors do not acquire key-row
authority. CPU resident sampling uses the existing source-visible random, argmax
and final scalar completion workers, with split views counted separately from
the explicit-key draw and both advanced-key/token roots retained.

Partition group execution names the independent control lifetime and requires
only that the current state outlive that loan. Concrete and borrowed-state
executors implement the same contract. Routed linear projections pay for the
sole output-shape vector whose final extent changes; unchanged input shapes
remain borrowed from the actual tensor descriptor.

Composite partition execution forwards the same lexical request control source
through the existing selected unit strategy to the routed expert provider. Dense
strategies preserve their ordinary behavior. Active composite pipeline waves
retain the loan without installing a neural context on control-only partitions;
no source is reconstructed from family names, membership or current native TLS.

The original no-prompt grammar session now consumes the ordinary token-history and byte-chart rollback workers directly. Both preserve EOS byte accounting, normal-stop reopening, request token-limit restoration, lexer-stack and row-history truncation, and acceptance/forcing cache invalidation. Prepared rollback reserves its fixed operation frames before mutation and retains the actual changed chart/history on refusal; it never refunds funding. Reset delegates the same operation. The shared LexerSpec predicate retains the ordinary restriction for stop/max-token lexemes. Paid independent mutable lexer/DFA/chart copies and Auto/Active controller registration remain separate required producers.

The prepared grammar chart/token copy now uses independent exact vector and mask destinations for all initialized scratch items, row/lexer histories, nested lexeme bytes, captures, token IDs, session bytes and cached masks. Fixed structural rows are Copy-only data, preventing hidden heap cloning through the common vector worker; nested owners use the existing Lexeme/Scratch and token-mask constructors after reservation. Failure retains each completed destination in the copied prefix while the borrowed original remains untouched. The immutable grammar declaration remains shared. A runnable snapshot still requires the independent mutable lexer/DFA owner and explicit new growth funding; this chart copy neither aliases that mutable state nor opens controller admission.

### Explicit sparse prefill row declarations

The architecture's causal block declaration now carries sparse routed-unit
coordinates separately from ordinary Sequence axes. Shared decoder families
derive these declarations from the same Config bank points used by their
observed provider calls. Runtime requires a RoutedUnits value/transform and
TokenRows followed by two known sparse extents, then binds the existing
CaptureRoutedPrefillPlan before quoting. Its fixed descriptor is included in
the selection control peak. A Sequence declaration cannot authorize sparse
flattening, and a sparse declaration cannot authorize a dense observation.
This adds semantic candidate binding; original native source/completion,
distributed receipt and final admission integration remain required.

Expert peer-count consensus consumes the selected opaque group descriptor and
actual local count row. One shared constructor forms ordinary and funded count
plans; the funded result retains its matrix and four peer vectors with their
cumulative account. The native source uses the existing initialized I32 leaf,
completed Gather constructor, signed-word destination and request child-role
worker. Each reached gather spends the live request cursor before source or
role admission and lends its completed matrix only for the shared constructor.
No model-family policy moves into the transport adapter. Logical subgroup count
sources and variable exchange still require their corresponding retained
iteration/route producers; this physical-group source does not qualify them or
replace them with a world collective.

Independent prepared expression-machine copies now construct the exact copied graph through the existing ExprSet/HashCons and derivative/symbolic/weight/relevance constructors, then copy the actual persistent memo, traversal, simplifier, search and containment state into those owned destinations. Each replacement allocation reserves its complete request while the initialized target remains live; nested symbolic/search values publish into retained parent slots before further allocation. The old growth account is omitted by the shared source-copy policy. Future growth requires an explicitly supplied new PreparedHashConsFunding owner; None leaves a fixed independent source. Errors retain all constructed source/plan/machine prefixes and that new account. Lexer/DFA state assembly and controller snapshot composition remain the next consumers.

### Borrowed native sparse coordinate lookup

The native wrapper exposes checked logical random access on an already evaluated
array through the same signed-stride reader as ordinary host iteration. Sparse
capture can read original route/group/scalar coordinates without uploading a
second index tensor or allocating a host index vector. The borrow retains the
actual completed source, supports reversed/broadcast/unaligned layouts, and
returns typed dtype/layout errors or None for an absent element. Its fixed
control population is explicit; callers still supply original source retention,
completion and host/native admission before using it.


The retained expert count consensus also supplies variable transport's borrowed
source-major matrix. The runtime validates every entry against the selected
opaque group and both local directions, and reverse exchanges borrow the
transpose. This matrix carries geometry, not native authority: an authenticated
original context must provide its exact transport producer and completion; a
missing producer is retained as a typed failure, never ordinary fallback. The
original mechanical checks borrow tensor shapes and funded scalar metadata,
without allocating shape vectors or formatting native errors. Active routed
providers carry the same context through dispatch, return, and the existing
ordered TP/EP/pipeline provider votes. Logical count, native variable transport,
metadata movement and inactive-wave loans remain explicit producer work; this
contract does not open the dynamic expert-parallel source gate.

Prepared lexer copies now pair the independent expression-machine copy with the actual DFA intern table, exact state IDs/descriptors, lazy/possible/accepting masks, cached transitions/lookahead decisions, source alphabet/configuration, fuel and transition counters. The shared finite table-copy plan omits the old growth owner and accepts only explicit new funding. Every nested accepting-list and mask destination stays in its copied parent on failure. The completed lexer copies its first-byte mask without rerunning warm-up. The existing token-session conformance case now advances a copied chart with a separately copied lexer, preserving the original pair. The next facade join must retain this pair with copied session histories and exact immutable declaration/tokenizer custody before controller snapshot admission.


Generated F32 initialization uses the existing shared fixed-buffer worker for
raw media masks and relative embeddings as well as other architecture scalar
sources. Its native recipe now follows the actual MLX realization: one eager
F32 source and one Copy, with their existing graph/record/backing classes. The
shared source supplies fixed initializer frames; its host fact separately
prices the one F32 vector through native construction. Scalar expressions and
their captured architecture plans retain their existing caller-owned contract.
No scalar is executed during quotation, and no model-family branch or alternate
initialization worker is introduced.

### Completed routed source to original prefill destination

The MLX sparse source reader borrows the exact five completed native descriptors,
validates route/token/group geometry, resolves the retained compact-bank map, and
copies selected scalars directly into CaptureRoutedPrefillWriter. Signed-stride
host lookup reads F32/F16/BF16 and I32/U32 without an index tensor, numerical
compaction, per-row DTO or conversion buffer. It validates the original writer's
native account first, and failures retain partial host storage in the frame.
Its fixed control census does not include or authorize source completion: the
native scheduled observer and cold recipe must still supply exact source
registration, five-root completion and the complete invocation/receipt coupling.
Partitioned unit/origin maps remain a separate source binding.

The original grammar token session now copies the actual populated lexer/DFA and
Earley/token chart together through their paid copy workers. Copies share only
the immutable declaration, tokenizer/trie and slicer source; their mutable
operation and future expression/table growth use an explicitly supplied new
metadata account. Canonical forcing uses that same new account for its byte and
ID destinations, while each tokenizer encode still admits its existing exact E
operation against the retained tokenizer source. Construction errors retain the
completed copied lexer/chart prefix and both source and destination custody.
The historical source account remains live while any source alias exists.
This closes the mutable pair producer; Auto/Active controller registration,
request startup and saved-controller handoff remain required before admission.


Inactive routed pipeline waves now receive the same explicit request-source
loan as active units through additive strategy companions. Their zero count
row is allocated only after exact selected peer geometry and metadata funding
are checked, then consumed by the shared count consensus worker. Dispatch and
return borrow the same count plan and context, and provider votes retain their
existing TP/EP/wave order. This does not change neural tensor-parallel selection
or make missing native/logical transport and metadata-movement sources complete.
The ordinary wave path and default no-op strategies remain shared.

Canonical capture record encoding also accepts borrowed fields from the retained
neutral admission and completed paid fragment payload. Owning and borrowed records
use the same core serializer, including nonfinite tensor spellings. The runtime's
contiguous fragment bank authenticates its local rank, exact ordinal, source dtype,
geometry and charge before lending zero or one record to the existing counted
transport writer. This grants no native completion, remote-rank vote or final
assembly authority; additive nonlinear captures retain their raw F32 terms.

The direct sparse copy also requires the existing CaptureSourceSegment. Runtime
checks the same immutable source owner, inference geometry and exact announced
chunk before the native reader can fill the destination. The original scope and
stamp are borrowed; matching byte counts or equal plan contents cannot substitute.

The facade's originally constructed active grammar state now assembles the
retained tokenizer/trie, immutable slicer, paid DFA/lexer, initial Earley chart
and token session through their existing constructors. Active commitment,
secondary EOS-alias acceptance and complete-versus-terminal decisions use the
same policy worker as ordinary GrammarState. Its copied state preserves the
terminal alias bit alongside the independently copied mutable pair. Failed
startup retains the reached source or constructor prefix, and failed semantic
operations retain the actual changed state and funding. This is the active
semantic producer; prepared-controller registration, dynamic decision/source
authentication, automatic trigger activation and public startup remain separate
consumer joins before the managed grammar gate can open.

The shared host-metadata account now lives in `eredu-core` as
`HostMetadataFunding` and `HostMetadataAccount`. `eredu-nn` preserves its existing
`WorkspaceMetadataAccount` alias and an allocation-free transparent
`WorkspaceMetadataFunding` compatibility handle. All callers
retain the same account, exact constructor/control sizing and shell-before-account
retirement. This lets neutral controller contracts receive the existing finite
per-constructor funding without depending on neural workspaces or creating a
second account mechanism. Funding remains distinct from source authentication,
execution permission and host lifetime-only custody.


Saved text admission assembles its accepted native owner in a separately paid
helper after recursive cold quotation returns. The helper consumes the same
move-only diagnostic, source pins and pending control exchange; its failures
remain under the enclosing planning and host-preparation custody. This keeps
owner-construction transports off the active media-module construction stack
without changing stack limits, snapshot semantics or native copy authority.

Workspace's existing counted vector, UTF-8 and neural-error constructors remain
in `eredu-nn`; the transparent funding handle preserves those inherent methods.
Its conversions and dereference expose the same core account without a new
allocation or account, while preventing core from depending on neural errors.

Original active grammar decisions now loan the actual paid parser's LSB-first
u32 mask words as a neutral `PackedTokenFilter`, intersected with the retained
tokenizer validity. Core capture and runtime's existing invalid-Boolean mask
expansion consume that same loan, including output truncation/padding and
prospective forcing. The borrower cannot overlap parser mutation; no extra
ordinary Boolean mask is constructed or adopted. This representation carries
no execution or source-registration authority: the exact grammar controller and
its original source/account still require their separate admission handoff.

Sparse prefill source transfer binds the five actual provider arrays to the same
stamped capture segment as dense fragments. The native carrier retains every
graph before settlement, publishes each completed backing, pins the complete
source set, then lends its paid sparse writer through the neutral source-bound
transfer. Failed copies leave partial rows and native recovery on their existing
owners. Borrowed geometry validation precedes completion. This mechanism requires
its actual five-source population and does not itself enable a capture route;
the observer quotation and provider invocation policy must admit that population.

The original active grammar keeps its complete parser and owning failure slots
in one fixed paid cell. Startup and independent copy reserve that cell before
allocating it. Semantic operations move failed worker prefixes into its existing
slot, so their returned error retains the same cell and account without allocating
at refusal or multiplying the entire parser through caller stack frames. A cold
constructor refusal retains the unboxed parser separately. The shared grammar
commit, EOS and terminal workers and their source identity remain unchanged.

The architecture's text-span driver declares its prepared I32/U32 matrix with a
specific neutral input equation and retains its exact operation ordinal. CPU and
Metal facts price that completed matrix and no additional model-owned host
payload; the existing prepared-input producer owns construction and native copy
controls. The resident recorder replaces only the driver-authenticated ordinal
with that input receipt. Generic initialization keeps its own source requirements;
the declaration is not an independent CPU initializer or a native allocation grant.

The scheduled routed prefill observer uses the same source-bound logical row
progression and original capture ledger as dense fragments. A row is charged
once before its first physical provider batch, accepts only nonoverlapping
source intervals through the fixed sparse writer, and completes its hook only
when the provider invocation finishes. Original/effective timing comes from the
admitted point. Callback failures retain the native owner's custody through the
neutral retained error. This consumer still requires the cold actual-source
population, and does not grant ordinary/decode or partitioned sparse authority.

Prepared collective completion accepts the actual full borrowed value frontier.
One/two roots retain the existing inline worker; larger frontiers use the existing
paid PreparedNestedRoots destination and the same synchronous completion worker.
Cold resident quotation records the largest actual ValueCompletion frontier in
each trace and includes it in nested traversal, Graph and Record bounds. No
family-specific root count or smaller substitute frontier is declared. Failed
preparation retains its original metadata owner, and unresolved native work
remains in the existing submission owner.

The backend's variable-frontier completion owns its preparation failure locally,
retaining the original metadata account with the native cause. It does not call
composition policy to keep that failure alive; the exact local error owner is
included in the same completion control census.

Cold routed prefill consumes actual provider callbacks and the same borrowed
five-source layout validator as native extraction. Each accepted callback keeps
its exact source roots and records five publications and completions, without
inventing a conversion tensor or expanding experts into a dense activation.
The shared logical row policy supplies charge and chunk completion. Cold source
coverage is diagnostic; the native fixed writer remains the authority for exact
route identity, disjoint provider ranges and complete payload validation.

The prepared grammar controller is a distinct neutral contract from fixed plain
and forbidden token filters. Its source loan includes the exact historical
recipe and declaration, the actual original tokenizer/trie object, canonical
history, validity and mutable metadata account. Source equality supplies no
native admission. The facade composes the actual paid active parser with an
independent paid canonical history: accepting a secondary EOS alias can complete
the grammar without appending a parser token, but still commits that canonical ID.
The runtime provisional branch copies both mutable owners, validates the same
borrowed history suffix as the ordinary controller, advances the shared grammar
workers, and loans the actual completed packed mask. Nested failures retain their
changed parser and completed history before funding retirement. Native source
registration, dynamic sampler/copy authentication and Auto trigger activation
remain separate joins; this contract does not open their public admission gates.

The existing speculative token-controller contract now names its typed prepared
grammar owner explicitly. Fixed controllers use an uninhabited association;
facade and token-choice wrappers forward the actual owner and paid replacement
worker. Prepared facade grammar clones retain one immutable shared source through
the existing closed SharedStorageOwner retirement mechanism. A successor is
independently copied and published under its own metadata account, with immutable
recipe/declaration/tokenizer/validity identity checked before replacement. Ordinary
grammar callbacks do not authorize these operations; the remaining shared sampler
and native authentication joins must consume this typed source before public
Active or Auto admission can open.


Native variable Ring exchange has a complete-matrix source for its existing
row-exchange worker. Checked geometry binds every count and orientation to the
actual physical communicator and tensor row size; each reached forwarding hop
validates its expected source, destination and bytes before payload allocation.
The lazy primitive and asynchronous dispatch own separate counted matrix copies.
Their CPU callback, optional contiguous copy, output backing, socket tasks and
payload vectors are quoted by the same native producers. The existing strict
resident constructor loan and single-source completion/Record worker supply
construction and retirement; scalar-only queries cannot qualify this operation.
The safe wrapper retains the borrowed matrix through constructor acceptance and
uses the existing operation/completion owners. Original expert routing remains
closed until its selected-group consumer, idle-row sentinel and logical subgroup
count sources are connected; this native producer alone does not declare that
whole distributed path supported.


The prepared variable-exchange consumer retains the completed peer-count matrix
and the exact selected physical communicator under the request cursor. Its
existing model dependency completion runs before the independently admitted
communication child. The child borrows the canonical Ring variable worker's
constructor, dispatch, payload, graph, backing and terminal-completion sources;
accepted recovery owns both its immutable original matrix and its derived
transport matrix until completion or safe failure. Each idle rank receives the
ordinary self-directed one-row sentinel, created by the shared prepared-input
leaf allocator with an exact physical dtype and zero initialization. The public
result keeps its original zero-row shape. The original count consensus remains
unchanged, and sentinel derivation only changes idle diagonal entries. Completed
count gathers and variable operations retain their selected group, including
subworld groups, rather than a lookalike control-world handle.

The leading-axis physical Ring source is now connected to the shared neutral
variable-exchange callback. Logical subgroup iteration and axis relocation still
require their own exact existing worker source before original execution can use
those paths; no geometry-only or ordinary fallback opens these source gates.


Completed expert peer-count rows now reuse the same retained logical collective
quotation and selected pair/packed-world execution stages as neural collectives.
The selected communication descriptor supplies the group; a count group is not
reconstructed as a tensor-parallel model occurrence. The initialized input
producer preserves a typed completed-leaf witness, so this source does not spend
an unrelated model completion root. Every reached transport/arithmetic stage
consumes its original request cursor claim and retains its exact quote, matrices,
stream and recovery custody. The final actual numerical child fills the existing
paid word destination under its own completion observer through the shared word
decoder. No additional Eval, completion event or ordinary host readout is created.
Logical plans that select explicit routed itineraries remain subject to their
exact producer gate until that distinct ordinary itinerary is joined.


Prepared peer-count consensus now has an additive move-only source loan. The
loan lends the checked local matrix and moves an optional existing core closed
shared-storage owner into the funded architecture count plan. Both forward and
reverse exchange borrow that exact owner through CommunicationPeerMatrix. The
backend must authenticate its concrete source against the retained request,
selected group and completed values; type matching alone grants no authority.
The ordinary consensus API and backends without an extended source keep their
existing worker. This handoff creates no native dependency in portable crates
and no ambient latest-table state.

The common precommit capture delivery seal accepts completed sparse routed
payloads and validates their actual wire encoding through the same bounded
serializer as dense/reduction records. The original source/coverage and duplicate
checks remain in the routed receipt constructor; final publication still waits
for the ordinary transaction vote.

The remaining causal target families now declare sparse original/effective bank
rows beside their existing ordinary prefill equations. Qwen hybrid and conditional,
Qwen VL, Kimi, LFM2, V3/V4, Gemma, Muse, Inkling and Nemotron use their actual target
group, sparse layer schedule and routing invocation identity. Inkling preserves
its distinct shared-bank invocation. Existing Config routing points are reused
where available. No prediction/media encoder hook, backend family branch, native
source grant or observation capability is inferred from these declarations.

Composite pipeline wave completion now forwards the retained parallel source
context for both media and primary decoder groups. The shared dependency worker
therefore completes the actual output and retained context values under the same
admitted native model role. Ordinary execution continues through that worker's
ordinary branch; no composite family or fixed root count is selected by a backend.

The speculative sampler contract now forwards the typed prepared grammar through
its existing ConstrainedSampler. The dynamic decision owns an independently copied
parser/history and pairs its completed packed mask with the same borrowed logit
policy used by ordinary sampling. Copy and commit use the exact source-checked
branch worker; adaptive commitment retains the actual observed probability and
uses the shared policy-before-controller sequence. Failure tears down local policy
copies before their funding while preserving escaped grammar prefixes. Controlled
force and clear use the existing pending/domain/grammar validation rules and
publish only an independent successor. Prefix completion uses the ordinary
terminal worker without introducing a mask computation. Fixed policies explicitly
associate an uninhabited grammar type. Native source registration, processed-value
authentication, per-operation funding and Auto trigger startup remain required
consumers; this typed handoff itself opens no original public admission gate.


The original peer-count loan carries a closed completed scalar source through the
same neutral expert route-count owner and both forward/reverse movement calls.
For a logical group, the existing gather transports an explicit physical source
header and destination/count pairs. The accepted packed-world completion exposes
its already-completed value to a funded word destination before normal local
extraction. All physical rows must be present, including rows whose counts are
zero; missing unrelated rows are never reconstructed as idle participants.
The resulting source retains the exact local matrix, selected member order,
request cursor identity and complete physical table when that worker produced
one. Its payload has no native array or ambient lookup, and closed Arc retirement
releases the allocation before source/account custody. Direct-pair gathers retain
only the exact local source they produced. The native variable consumer must
select the corresponding actual transport source before the logical gate opens.


Logical variable transport selection now has one borrowed plan shared by the
ordinary collective and original source query. It lends the retained physical
world, logical member order and the existing input/output block permutations.
The original query authenticates that world against the selected group's actual
participation wave and queries the same matrix-bearing native worker with its
world persistent owner. This source query does not itself authorize logical
execution or invent the complete physical matrix; the completed count-source
loan and exact permutation producers remain required at the consumer.


Variable leading-block permutation is one shared worker for ordinary and cold
execution. The selected member order determines interval extraction and final
concatenation; the native adapter uses the existing exact axis-range Slice
producer, and the workspace adapter declares those same intervals. Exact counts
fund offset, value and borrowed-value destinations before the worker. Empty and
single-block paths retain the existing zero/alias semantics, and no caller can
grow beyond the admitted per-member block destination.

### Retained-media sparse decoder declarations

Gemma, Inkling, Qwen VL, conditional Qwen hybrid, and Muse derive sparse
retained-media decoder declarations from the same architecture-owned routed
bank declarations used by their ordinary target. Their validated media ingress
retains positions, masks, and embeddings before those row-local expert
equations. Only explicit flattened routed declarations are carried over;
encoder, readout, and prediction hooks retain their separate contracts.
This changes semantic source discovery; native execution, exact capture
admission, and distributed source ownership still require their existing joins.

Original grammar numerical processing now enters the existing mask/policy/capture
worker with the owned grammar decision. Before invoking it, the native adapter
authenticates the actual originally compiled trie in its source pool and the
registered recipe, declaration and validity owners through the same shared
attachment lookup used for filters. The completed provisional branch must use
the actual numerical metadata account. The existing processed-value choice witness
now also retains a prepared canonical-history identity and its immutable sources;
new history allocations, changed forced state and fixed/grammar source substitution
are rejected by the shared choice validator. That witness retains no parser and
supplies no tokenizer execution authority. Original sampler startup, saved-copy
funding and dynamic control publication still need their actual owner handoff
before public Active or Auto admission can open.


Original logical variable exchange authenticates its completed count-source owner
against the retained request cursor, selected group and exact local matrix. A
physical-world operation consumes only the complete world table produced by that
source. Input/output member permutations execute the shared leading-block worker
under separately admitted child roles, each quoted from its actual completed
input, counts and stream. Native recovery retains the scalar owner through
completion/failure, and the same matrix-bearing worker supplies graph, record and
backing populations. Idle physical rows use the existing typed zero sentinel and
return their original empty result only after the actual transport completes.
A logical source without its complete world table still refuses precisely; direct
route movement needs its own actual itinerary rather than a full-world substitute.


Explicit logical collectives lend their retained route/value/exchange itinerary
through one allocation-free plan. Ordinary execution and original source lookup
consume the same ordered fold, skipping only actual no-op positions. Each reached
step obtains the existing accepted paired Send/Receive source with complementary
physical submission order; its cold owner retains the actual group and selected
native peer geometry. This adds source coverage without substituting a guessed
packed-world schedule for explicit routes.

### Routed ordinary invocation host retention

Ordinary and decode routed invocations retain one original-account sparse
destination in the existing capture record sidecar. Short provider-batch writers
borrow that destination; final receipt validation uses the existing sparse
coverage and duplicate rules. Dropped or failed writers poison their destination,
and failed finalization retains initialized payloads with the same frame custody.
The sidecar and writer controls are priced by the existing step and routed host
plans. This does not grant native source or completion authority; the actual
native carrier must bind its independently admitted source before writing.


Count-source wire rows have one exact physical-world width with explicit unused
slots, so different selected subgroup widths cannot truncate the world source.
If the ordinary pair/route gather produced only local rows and the selected
variable plan requires the physical world, the same accepted Gather worker
acquires every physical row before the count loan is published. That actual
operation consumes its own request claim and finite destination; it is skipped
when the preceding packed-world completion already produced the full table.
The immutable local source is compared against the full table before its paid
successor is published, with no cursor reset or reservation refund.

### Ordinary and decode routed observation driver

The funded observer now uses one shared ordinary invocation policy for routed
geometry, metadata, logical quota and provider-batch delivery. All actual
provider batches write to the existing frame's single sparse target; sealing
uses the existing coverage/duplicate validator. Prefill chunk mapping retains
its architecture-bound companion, and distributed placement remains separately
authenticated. Source validation precedes quota, native transformation is an
explicit backend method, and aborts preserve the frame's failed destination.

### Shared native sparse capture producer

Chunked prefill and ordinary/decode sparse destinations share the same five-source
native completion, registered backing retention, and direct scalar-copy worker.
A static destination adapter selects only coordinate mapping and short writer
ownership. All five graphs are retained before any fallible settlement, and
ordinary invocation writers bind the same original native scope and source bank.
No second tensor collector, intermediate row array, or family dispatch is added.

### Ordinary sparse native quotation

The cold observer now applies the same ordinary/decode routed geometry and
once-only logical quota as the funded observer, retaining five actual source
roots for every provider batch. Cold and native capture share layout validation
and the same publication population. Completion requires complete physical
token coverage for each original/effective hook; selected empty batches still
supply their real source extent. No device, stream, or native tensor is needed
to select or quote this path.

The native original sampler now prepares a supplied typed grammar only when its
source metadata account is the actual request account, then makes an independent
paid copy before placing it in the existing immutable sampler owner. Commitment
reuses the processed-value check and native probability observation before the
shared policy/controller transaction; only the complete successor replaces the
source. Forced-choice changes and terminal queries use that same authenticated
owner/account and preserve the ordinary validation order. These consumers do not
adopt an ordinary parser or change public grammar admission. Saved sampler copies
still require the source-derived complete lexer/chart copy bound and their own
snapshot funding before that path can be admitted.


Original explicit-route peer-count consensus now executes the same retained route
fold through existing accepted Pair and dependency-arithmetic roles. Each reached
step has a peer-only cold quote and a funded completed-word readout. Exact host
slots assemble every route source once in logical-rank order, validating native
headers before publishing the scalar source. Host-only count delivery needs no
invented model-output Stack recipe. The subsequent world-source completion runs
only when the selected variable transport needs physical rows absent from that
local itinerary; all claims and temporary receipt reservations remain spent.


The focused native variable-exchange fixture reuses the original Ring authority,
Graph/Record/backing owners and process launcher. Four ranks compare ordinary and
accepted Int32/Float32 forward/reverse exchanges with nonuniform counts and an
idle participant, then all-zero sentinel transport. It checks cold/accepted
allocation classes, incomplete-matrix refusal without output mutation, accepted
work after a terminal source fence, and output custody beyond its enclosing role.
The exact request-token identity and logical empty-result behavior remain covered
by the backend consumer/public itinerary rather than inferred from this C ABI case.


Variable exchange along a non-leading axis uses one shared ordinary permutation
plan and transpose/inverse-transpose worker. The existing paid transformation
role quotes each actual input/stream and retains the same count-source owner;
transport still receives the exact leading-axis source and completed matrix.
Idle sentinel construction uses the selected original axis, while its public
empty result retains the original geometry. No second variable-exchange driver
or inferred output precision is introduced.


The local logical variable-exchange branch now borrows its actual route itinerary
from the selected Group. Ordinary execution and counted source preparation share
source rank, destination block and reached exchange ordering without cloning the
route table. Physical-world participation remains an earlier separate choice;
a local route cannot manufacture a world wave. The native asymmetric payload
source and its counted consumer are still required before managed local variable
exchange can be admitted.


Prepared expression snapshot copies inspect the retained arena/table and every
mutable cache capacity without invoking a constructor or a funding callback.
The existing source-copy constructor still creates the independent expression
arena. Empty derivative, symbolic, weight and relevance destinations then consume
the existing paid storage-copy workers; they do not construct scratch from fresh
expression bounds only to overwrite it. The same frame and allocation-layout
functions supply prospective copy payment and actual spending, including nested
symbolic values and reached relevance/containment stacks. Copy failure retains
the independent arena and completed mutable prefix under the explicitly supplied
new funding; the old growth authority never transfers. This prospective source
is the lower-level producer for grammar snapshot admission, which remains closed
until the lexer, chart and controller totals are joined.


The saved lexer and Earley token-session producers now extend that prospective
copy total through the actual DFA masks, intern table, nested matching lists,
chart rows, capture buffers and committed history. Their copy workers and
inspection share exact layout and fixed-frame functions. DFA vectors preserve
retained capacities; chart/session slices preserve initialized lengths, matching
the existing copy behavior. Funding callbacks remain borrowed during copy, so
the copy frame counts the reference rather than adopting a caller closure.
No parser or funding operation runs during this source inspection. The actual
copy still reserves each reached destination before allocation and retains the
completed independent prefix on refusal.


The neutral prepared-grammar controller contract exposes its complete prospective
copy payment for a requested canonical-history capacity. The facade's concrete
owner joins its paid active-state cell, lexer/chart/session copies, canonical
history and actual retained hash-cons callback constructor through the same
control functions consumed during execution. Inspection constructs no mutable
parser and reserves no account; its callback descriptor is the same concrete
captured-funding representation used by the copy worker. Unknown or incomplete
sources and undersized history remain unavailable. The complete controller
fixture checks exact payment, one-byte-short refusal and retirement of both
successful and failed independent owners before native snapshot composition.


Prepared grammar snapshot quotation now composes the concrete grammar copy with
the existing constrained policy copy, committed-history branch and every typed
controller-publication wrapper. Neutral controllers report their actual
replacement destination payment separately from the mutable parser copy. The
runtime sampler retains a source-bound copy query beside its existing copy
callback; no proposed-history or mask execution is priced as a committed copy.
Both facade and token-choice wrappers consume the same fixed forwarding controls
used by quotation, while the facade shared-owner publisher retains its actual
source/account comparison and final-owner retirement.


The saved paged-cache and grammar sampler now share a neutral finite host-metadata
partition extracted from the existing saved-cache counter. It consumes only the
caller's already admitted total, including its exact counter/funding constructor;
it never reserves the outer pool, refunds individual operations or supplies
native authority. The final funding alias destroys the counter and shells before
releasing the retained HostPreparationAuthority. Native grammar snapshot quotation
joins that constructor with the complete shared sampler copy and actual native
owner/error controls. Snapshot execution preserves the existing independent RNG
copy order, then copies the actual grammar through its typed shared worker into
that finite new account. Restored copies retain their own account and the exact
immutable source identities; later mutations still require their newly admitted
operation account. Public grammar startup admission remains a separate join.


An asymmetric paired native source retains separate Send and Receive prototypes
on the identical physical Group. Both prototypes must be completed and their
scalar representations must match; each constructor is recomputed from its own
retained layout. The Receive prototype supplies geometry without becoming a DAG
input. The existing paired completion worker and accepted native constructors
remain shared, and the older same-input joins keep their pointer-identity check.
Control census includes both source inspections and binding transports. This
source supports the existing logical variable payload itinerary without borrowing
a physical-world collective or a caller-provided byte allowance.


The local variable route source borrows each reached exchange from the same
ordinary Group itinerary. Send and Receive layouts remain separate through the
retained native source and actual-input binding, with their exact persistent
communicator pins, Graph/Record/backing census and source-before-funding custody.
Complementary submission order comes from those physical endpoints. A no-op route
step produces no native operation; no world participation proof is inferred.


Local variable routing shares one route/slice/row-check/assembly worker across
ordinary and source-funded mechanisms. It preserves the retained source order,
actual reached exchanges and source-rank concatenation, while each mechanism owns
its native completion and paid destinations. The scalar row-count wire is I32,
matching the native Array dimension domain; neither path narrows a wider runtime
shape. The managed consumer still requires the complete count-source identity
and actual per-stage native sources before entering this shared worker.


Variable route assembly uses the existing paid numerical transformation role for
its final concatenation. The role retains every actual completed source array,
projects all of them into the same cold equation recorder, and executes the
